```text
1	# marvin HDMI → BGR888 Capture Pipeline
2	
3	Authoritative configuration reference for the 720p60 HDMI capture path on SAM9X75. Every stage, every register bit that matters, with datasheet citations. When something breaks, start here before grepping code.
4	
5	**Status:** working as of 2026-05-02. Validated at **1280×720p60** and **720×480p60**, native BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel) in DDR, no CPU post-processing. The pipeline is resolution-agnostic — PFE crop, DMA size, and framebuffer offsets all scale from the TC358743-detected `{width, height}` automatically.
6	
7	Datasheet references are to **SAM9X7 Series DS60001813** (sections 48 = MIPI CSI / D-PHY, 49 = CSI2DC, 50 = ISC). TC358743 refs are to the Toshiba datasheet + mainline Linux `drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c`.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Pipeline overview
12	
13	```
14	HDMI source (Pi 720p60 RGB)
15	        │
16	        ▼
17	TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
18	  DT=0x24 RGB888, 2 lanes, 972 Mbps/lane, continuous-clock mode
19	        │
20	        ▼                          <── MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY
21	SAM9X75 DWC D-PHY RX Gen3
22	  HSFREQRANGE=0x0A (950–1000 Mbps band)
23	        │
24	        ▼                          <── 40-bit isc_data bus
25	CSI2DC (Demultiplexer Controller)
26	  VPCFGR: DT=0x24, VC=0, PA=0, RMS=1  (byte-stream mode)
27	  → 4 BGR pixels packed into 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27)
28	        │
29	        ▼                          <── byte-stream on vp_data bus
30	ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
31	  PFE_CFG0: MIPI=1, BPS=FORTY, MODE=PROGRESSIVE, CONT=1, COLEN=1, ROWEN=1
32	  PFE_CFG1: COLMIN=0, COLMAX=(W×3/4)-1   (e.g. 959 at 1280px)
33	  PFE_CFG2: ROWMIN=0, ROWMAX=H-1   (719)
34	        │
35	        ▼                          <── sub420_data[39:0]
36	ISC — Rounding/Limiting/Packing (RLP)
37	  RLP_CFG: MODE=BYPASS (15)
38	  → rlp_data[31:0] = sub420_data[31:0] (pass-through)
39	        │
40	        ▼                          <── rlp_data[31:0]
41	ISC — DMA Host
42	  DCFG: IMODE=PACKED32, YMBSIZE=BEATS32, CMBSIZE=BEATS32
43	  → stores 32-bit words to DDR; RMS=1 byte-stream → dense BGR888
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	DDR3 framebuffer  (1280 × 720 × 3 = 2,764,800 B/frame)
47	  B G R  B G R  B G R  ...  (dense, no padding byte)
48	```
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 2. Stage-by-stage configuration
53	
54	### 2.1 HDMI source
55	
56	- 1280×720p @ 60 Hz, RGB (not YCbCr), progressive.
57	- Any stable DVI/HDMI source works. Raspberry Pi with `/boot/firmware/config.txt` forced to `hdmi_group=1 hdmi_mode=4 hdmi_force_hotplug=1 hdmi_drive=2` is the known-good reference.
58	- Pixel rate: 74.25 MHz (standard CEA-861 VIC 4 / 720p60).
59	
60	Full-range vs limited-range is sender-controlled. TC358743's AVI InfoFrame carries whatever the source advertises; currently Pi sends limited-range, so peak values in DDR are `0xFE` not `0xFF`. EDID colorimetry overrides are a separate future task.
61	
62	### 2.2 TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
63	
64	Driver: `firmware/marvin/default/src/tc358743.c`. Register values derived from mainline Linux `tc358743.c`.
65	
66	| Register | Value | Meaning |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `PLLCTL` PRD=4, FBD=144 | PLL out = 972 MHz | `hsck = (27 MHz / PRD) × FBD` |
69	| `CSI_CONFW` lanes | 2 | 2 data lanes × 972 Mbps = 1.944 Gbps total (plenty for 720p60 RGB888's ~1.33 Gbps) |
70	| `CONFCTL` | 0x0007 | PCLK divider off, 3-byte pixel pack, no audio |
71	| `FIFOCTL` | 0x0176 | FIFO level 374 (kernel hardcodes at all rates) |
72	| `VI_MODE` | 0xE6 | RGB888 input, 16-bit HDMI RX side |
73	| `VI_REP`  | 0x00 | **No pixel replication / doubling** (critical — was 0x80 in earlier 480p test and caused 16-row phase drift) |
74	| `VOUT_SET2` / `VOUT_SET3` | 0x01 / 0x08 | Output color format / range handling |
75	| CSI-2 DT | 0x24 | RGB888 per CSI-2 spec |
76	
77	D-PHY timing (for 972 Mbps):
78	```
79	LINEINITCNT  = 0x1B58
80	LPTXTIMECNT  = 0x0007
81	TCLK_HEADER  = 0x2806    TCLK_TRAIL  = 0x0000    TCLK_POST = 0x0008
82	THS_HEADER   = 0x0806    THS_TRAIL   = 0x0005
83	TWAKEUP      = 0x4268    HSTXVREGCNT = 0x0000
84	```
85	
86	Operating mode: **continuous clock** (`TXOPTIONCNTRL = CONTCLKMODE`). This is the required-match with the SAM9X75 RX side — if RX expects gated but TX sends continuous (or vice versa), `CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP` hangs permanently.
87	
88	### 2.3 SAM9X75 MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY RX
89	
90	Driver: `firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi/` (MCC-generated, slightly tweaked).
91	
92	Key setting — **the one parameter that took us the longest to get right**:
93	
94	```c
95	// isc_capture.c:25
96	#define ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE  0x0Au
97	```
98	
99	This is the `HSFREQRANGE` DWC D-PHY test-mode value. SAM9X75 is **DWC Gen3** (verified from Linux DT: `snps,dw-dphy-rx` with `snps,phy_type=<0>`). The Gen3 table entry for the 950–1000 Mbps band is `0x0A`.
100	
101	- **Wrong** (used during earlier debug): `0x1A` — that's a Gen2 value. At 972 Mbps Gen2 bands diverge from Gen3, symptom is persistent `PHY_FATAL.SOT_SYNC_ERR = 0x3`.
102	- **Correct** for 972 Mbps Gen3: `0x0A`.
103	- Changes with bitrate. If bitrate moves, look up Gen3 table (DesignWare MIPI D-PHY RX Gen3 Databook), don't copy values from other SoC examples.
104	
105	Other CSI settings:
106	- `CSI_NUM_LANES = 2` (matches TC358743).
107	- `csiObj->csiFps = 60u` (informational; drives some timing in the driver).
108	
109	### 2.4 CSI2DC — the RMS=1 lever
110	
111	**This is the key decision that enables in-pipeline BGR888 packed.** DS60001813 §49.6.54:
112	
113	| VPCFGR Field | Value | Reason |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| DT (bits 5:0) | 0x24 | RGB888 (matches TC358743 emission) |
116	| VC (bits 7:6) | 0 | Virtual channel 0 |
117	| PA (bit 14) | **0** | LSB-aligned. PA=1 is for 10/12-bit Bayer sensors being packed onto ISC's 12-bit internal bus. Irrelevant for MIPI RGB888 bypass. |
118	| **RMS (bit 13)** | **1** | **Critical.** See below. |
119	| RGB36MAP (bit 15) | 0 | Use Table 49.27 pixel mapping |
120	
121	`RMS` (Recommended Memory Storage) per datasheet:
122	
123	- `RMS=0` — "CSI2DC outputs 1 pixel per component per clock cycle, compliant with the ISC processing engine." → Table 49.25: `demux_data[39:24]=0`, `[23:16]=R`, `[15:8]=G`, `[7:0]=B`. One pixel per 40-bit VP word — gives BGRX32 (4 B/pixel, 25% extra DDR bandwidth, X byte always 0x00).
124	- `RMS=1` — "CSI2DC generates a byte stream compliant with the CSI-2 specification memory format." → Table 49.27: 4 BGR pixels packed into 12 bytes. Results in **dense 3 B/pixel BGR888** — 25% less DDR bandwidth, and XLCDC HEO reads natively in `RGB_888_PACKED` mode.
125	
126	**MCC's default omits RMS=1.** We add it (re-apply patch #3):
127	
128	```c
129	// firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi2dc/plib_csi2dc.c
130	void CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe(uint32_t dt, uint32_t vc, uint32_t align_isc) {
131	    CSI2DC_REGS->CSI2DC_VPCFGR = CSI2DC_VPCFGR_DT(dt)
132	                               | CSI2DC_VPCFGR_VC(vc)
133	                               | (align_isc ? CSI2DC_VPCFGR_PA_1 : 0)
134	                               | CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1;  /* PATCH #3: byte-stream mode */
135	}
136	```
137	
138	Other CSI2DC config:
139	- `GCFGR.MIPIFRN = 0` (free-running, matches TC358743's continuous-clock mode). MCC default is gated (`MIPIFRN=1`); mismatch leaves `CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP` stuck on reset. Override via `csi2dcObj->enableMIPIFreeRun = true;` in `isc_capture.c`.
140	- `VPER = 1` (video pipe enabled).
141	
142	### 2.5 ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
143	
144	DS60001813 §50.6.6, §50.7.4–50.7.6.
145	
146	Key settings configured by `DRV_ISC_Configure()`:
147	
148	| PFE_CFG0 field | Value | Why |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| REP | 0 | N/A for BPS=FORTY |
151	| BPS (30:28) | 5 = FORTY | "40-bit input (used for MIPI formats up to forty bits per pixel)." Matches CSI2DC's 40-bit VP bus. |
152	| MIPI (bit 14) | 1 | Input from MIPI interface |
153	| GATED (bit 8) | 0 | Free-running clock |
154	| CCIR656 (bit 9) | 0 | Not embedded-sync — using MIPI |
155	| CONT (bit 7) | 1 | Continuous acquisition (vs single shot) |
156	| MODE (6:4) | 0 = PROGRESSIVE | Source is progressive |
157	| VPOL / HPOL | 0 | Active-high sync (standard) |
158	
159	**Two bits that MCC leaves OFF but we must set:**
160	
161	| PFE_CFG0 field | Value | Why MCC misses it |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| **COLEN (bit 12)** | **1** | Enables the column crop window |
164	| **ROWEN (bit 13)** | **1** | Enables the row crop window |
165	
166	MCC's `ISC_PFE_Crop_Area()` function is defined in `plib_isc.c` but **never called**. Without COLEN+ROWEN and valid COLMAX/ROWMAX, the PFE expects a 1×1 frame and fires HDTO (Horizontal Detection Timeout) on the first real line. The Linux `mchp-isc` driver sets both bits; we match that.
167	
168	We program these directly after `DRV_ISC_Configure()`. With RMS=1, COLMAX is in ISC sample units (32-bit byte-stream words), so the formula is `(width × 3 / 4) - 1`:
169	
170	```c
171	// isc_capture.c
172	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG1 = ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMIN(0u)
173	                       | ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMAX((width * 3u / 4u) - 1u);  // 959 at 1280px
174	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG2 = ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMIN(0u)
175	                       | ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMAX((uint32_t)height - 1u);   // 719 at 720p
176	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG0 |= ISC_PFE_CFG0_COLEN_1 | ISC_PFE_CFG0_ROWEN_1;
177	```
178	
179	With RMS=1, COLMAX is in **byte-stream word units** (4 bytes per ISC sample), so COLMAX = `(W × 3) / 4 - 1`. Under the previous RMS=0 path, COLMAX was in pixel units (`W - 1`).
180	
181	### 2.6 ISC — Rounding, Limiting, Packing (RLP)
182	
183	DS60001813 §50.6.19, §50.7.67.
184	
185	| RLP_CFG field | Value | Reason |
186	|---|---|---|
187	| **MODE (3:0)** | **15 = BYPASS** | "32-bit input is sampled and written to the rlp output port. Select this mode for MIPI RMS mode." Passes `sub420_data[31:0]` through unchanged. With our RMS=0 input that's `0x00RRGGBB`. |
188	| ALPHA (15:8) | — | Ignored in BYPASS mode (only used by ARGB444/ARGB555/ARGB32 modes) |
189	| YMODE / LSH / REP | 0 | Not applicable to BYPASS |
190	
191	**Why not ARGB32 RLP (Mode 10)?** Per §50.6.19 Table row for RGB32/ARGB32:
192	```
193	rlp_data[31:24] = A = ALPHA[7:0]       (register)
194	rlp_data[23:16] = R = sub420_data[29:22]
195	rlp_data[15:8]  = G = sub420_data[19:12]
196	rlp_data[7:0]   = B = sub420_data[9:2]
197	```
198	
199	These bit positions are the output format of the ISC **CSC module** (Color Space Conversion, §50.6.15), not raw MIPI RGB888. On our bypass path, R/G/B sit at `[23:16]/[15:8]/[7:0]` — a 6/4/2-bit shift off what ARGB32 RLP wants. Attempting it yields mangled 3-shifted-copies-of-garbage per 12 bytes. **ARGB32 RLP is structurally unusable for MIPI RGB888 bypass;** it would require enabling the full demosaic pipeline (for Bayer sources) or CSC (for YCbCr).
200	
201	Consequence: we cannot get `alpha = 0xFF` in-pipeline for free. We get `alpha = 0x00` because CSI2DC zeros the upper 16 bits of each 40-bit VP word. If `0xFF` alpha matters, a one-shot CPU pass to set `buf[3::4] = 0xFF` does it cheaply, or stamp 0xFF into the framebuffer once at init (DMA writes never touch byte 3 if pixel stride matches — need to verify that assumption before relying on it).
202	
203	**Driver hint:** `iscObj->rlpMode = ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_BYPASS` (value 15 in the MCC enum). `drv_isc.c` writes this into RLP_CFG during `DRV_ISC_Configure`.
204	
205	### 2.7 ISC — DMA Host
206	
207	DS60001813 §50.6.20, §50.7.70.
208	
209	| DCFG field | Value | Reason |
210	|---|---|---|
211	| **IMODE (2:0)** | **2 = PACKED32** | "32 bits, single channel packed." Stores each `rlp_data[31:0]` as 4 contiguous bytes in memory. With RMS=1 byte-stream, this writes dense BGR888 — every 3rd byte is the start of the next pixel, no padding. |
212	| YMBSIZE (6:4) | 4 = BEATS32 | 32-beat AXI burst (sama7g5 / SAM9X7 — MCC's PACKED8 default is BEATS8 which is the sama5d2 value, undersized for this SoC). |
213	| CMBSIZE (10:8) | 4 = BEATS32 | Same rationale as YMBSIZE. |
214	| ARQOS / AWQOS | 0 | Dynamic QoS based on FIFO level (recommended default) |
215	
216	MCC's `DRV_ISC_Configure` sets PACKED8 + BEATS8 if `iscObj->layout = ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED8`. We override after `DRV_ISC_Configure`:
217	
218	```c
219	// isc_capture.c:219-221
220	ISC_REGS->ISC_DCFG = ISC_DCFG_IMODE_PACKED32
221	                   | ISC_DCFG_YMBSIZE_BEATS32
222	                   | ISC_DCFG_CMBSIZE_BEATS32;
223	```
224	
225	The write is safe because nothing in MCC writes DCFG again after this point (the redundant-call to `DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA` was removed). `DRV_ISC_Configure` already calls it internally at `drv_isc.c:381` — don't add a second call.
226	
227	**Descriptor view:** `DCTRL.DVIEW = 0` (PACKED / single channel). `DAD0` holds the current buffer base address. `DST0` = 0 (contiguous frame, no row stride gap).
228	
229	### 2.8 Framebuffer layout in DDR
230	
231	```c
232	// isc_capture.c
233	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_W        1280u
234	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_H        720u
235	#define ISC_CAP_BPP          3u      /* BGR888 packed */
236	#define ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS  4u
237	
238	static __attribute__((__section__(".region_nocache")))
239	       __attribute__((__aligned__(32)))
240	       uint8_t g_framebuffer[ISC_CAP_MAX_W * ISC_CAP_MAX_H * ISC_CAP_BPP * ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS];
241	```
242	
243	- Pool size: 1280×720×3×4 = ~11 MB, in the **uncached** DDR region (`.region_nocache`).
244	- Uncached so CPU vision consumers (cv_marvin_v1) see DMA-fresh bytes without D-cache invalidation.
245	- 32-byte aligned (cache line boundary).
246	- At 480p: only 720×480×3×4 = ~4.1 MB actually used.
247	- 4-deep ring gives slow consumers up to ~50 ms read window before lapping.
248	
249	Pixel access pattern (0-indexed, little-endian):
250	
251	```c
252	uint8_t *px = &g_framebuffer[(y * W + x) * 4];
253	uint8_t B = px[0];
254	uint8_t G = px[1];
255	uint8_t R = px[2];
256	// px[3] = 0x00 (X / unused)
257	```
258	
259	As a 32-bit word: `*(uint32_t*)px == 0x00RRGGBB` (native little-endian).
260	
261	### Sizing strategy
262	
263	The buffer pool is statically allocated for the **maximum supported resolution** (`ISC_CAP_MAX_W × ISC_CAP_MAX_H × ISC_CAP_BPP × ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS` = 1920 × 1080 × 4 × 2 = 15.8 MB), reserved once at link time in `.region_cache_aligned`. Per-capture the ISC DMA descriptor is programmed for only `width × height × 4` bytes; the rest of the pool sits idle.
264	
265	| Resolution | In use / frame | 2-buffer total | Idle |
266	|---|---|---|---|
267	| 480p60 | 1.32 MB | 2.64 MB | 13.2 MB |
268	| 720p60 | 3.69 MB | 7.37 MB | 8.4 MB |
269	| 1080p60 | 7.90 MB | 15.8 MB | 0 |
270	
271	Trade-off: idle DDR at low resolutions (trivial on this 256 MB platform) in exchange for zero reallocation on source-resolution change — buffer base pointers stay constant, the consumer never needs to re-bind. `ISC_Capture_Configure` rejects any `width > MAX_W || height > MAX_H` so the guarantee is enforced.
272	
273	---
274	
275	## 3. Verified output — color sweep
276	
277	Pi source, 720p60 RGB limited-range (so peak = 0xFE). Probe reports memory at representative points across the frame:
278	
279	| Source color | Memory (`b0 b1 b2 b3`) | Decode |
280	|---|---|---|
281	| Red   | `00 00 FE 00` | B=0, G=0, R=0xFE, X=0 |
282	| Green | `00 FE 00 00` | B=0, G=0xFE, R=0, X=0 |
283	| Blue  | `FE 00 00 00` | B=0xFE, G=0, R=0, X=0 |
284	| White | `FE FE FE 00` | B=G=R=0xFE, X=0 |
285	| Black | `00 00 00 00` | — |
286	
287	All five match expectation across the full 1280×720 extent (rows 0..719 completely written, no cliff). Framerate sustained at 70 fps probe-window average (≈60 fps real + diagnostic ticks).
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 4. Where each override lives in code
292	
293	| Stage | File | Line | Change |
294	|---|---|---|---|
295	| TC358743 D-PHY timing | `default/src/tc358743.c` | 25–33 | 972 Mbps timing constants (kernel-derived) |
296	| TC358743 PLL | `default/src/tc358743.c` | 14–20 | `PLL_PRD=4`, `PLL_FBD=144` |
297	| CSI HSFREQRANGE | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 23 | `0x0A` for DWC Gen3 @ 972 Mbps |
298	| CSI bitrate override | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 83 | `csiObj->csiBitRate = ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE` (MCC default is `0x16`) |
299	| CSI2DC RMS=0 | `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi2dc/plib_csi2dc.c` | 71–78 | dropped `CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1` from VPCFGR write |
300	| CSI2DC free-run | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 88 | `enableMIPIFreeRun = true` |
301	| ISC PFE crop | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 195–202 | direct `PFE_CFG1/2` + `COLEN`/`ROWEN` writes |
302	| ISC DMA config | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 209–211 | direct `DCFG` write (PACKED32 + BEATS32×2) |
303	| Framebuffer BPP | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 17 | `ISC_CAP_BPP = 4` |
304	
305	---
306	
307	## 5. Debug / diagnostics
308	
309	Runtime log is intentionally quiet — initialization, format detection, and a one-shot pre-start register snapshot only. No periodic dump.
310	
311	What lands on the DBGU during normal operation:
312	
313	1. **TC358743 init + lock sequence** — I2C presence, init, SYS_STATUS transitions as HDMI negotiates, final `detected WxH @ FPS, RGB ...` with raster dimensions.
314	2. **`ISC_Capture: configured WxH BGRX32 (N bytes/frame)`** — called by `app_coordinate_capture` when TC358743 reports a locked format.
315	3. **`ISC_Capture diag (pre-start):` block** — one-shot register snapshot printed from `diag_dump_rx()` right before `DRV_ISC_Start_Capture`. Contains CSI / CSI2DC / ISC state at the moment capture is armed. When diagnosing new sources or regressions, this is the first place to look.
316	4. **`ISC_Capture: capture started`** — green light. Quiet from here.
317	5. **TC358743 format-change events** — if the source switches resolution mid-run, the watcher prints a new detection line and the capture module re-configures.
318	
319	If deeper inspection is needed (byte-level probes, phase scanners, content bounding box), resurrect `ISC_Capture_ProbeFrame()` from git history (commit `29a21bf` has the last full version) and wire it into a temporary 1-Hz tick.
320	
321	---
322	
323	## 6. Known carry-forwards
324	
325	- **`INTSR.HDTO` always set** after capture start — informational-only residual, not a stop signal. Also present under working RMS=1 config. Safe to ignore.
326	- **DDONE interrupt unreliable** — `iscObj->frameIndex` advances rarely or not at all; `g_frame_count` (incremented from the frame-done callback, driven by VD) counts correctly. DMA itself works (buffers update on schedule). Investigate before building consumer logic that relies on DDONE firing per frame.
327	- **Pixel range 0x00–0xFE** because TC358743 passes through source's limited-range signaling. EDID overrides or TC358743 colorimetry registers can force full-range; deferred until display stage forces the issue.
328	- **Alpha channel = 0x00** — not 0xFF. Acceptable for display framebuffers that ignore alpha; requires CPU fix-up if alpha is semantic.
329	
330	---
331	
332	## 7. Datasheet-anchored reasoning for ARGB/RGBA aspirations
333	
334	If someone revisits this and asks "can we get ARGB32 directly in-pipeline?":
335	
336	1. **ARGB32 RLP mode** requires upstream data at `sub420_data[29:22]/[19:12]/[9:2]`. That's the CSC output format (§50.6.15). CSC is a module for converting to/from YCbCr — it's not a pass-through. Routing RGB888 through CSC would work only if CSC has an identity-RGB mode, which per §50.6.15 it doesn't (the CSC input is YCbCr by design).
337	2. **Demosaic pipeline** (WB → CFA → CC → GAM → …) expects 10/12-bit Bayer mosaic input, not 24-bit RGB.
338	3. **CSI2DC has no alpha-insertion register** — only RMS mode and the RGB36MAP packing variant. Neither affects the upper byte.
339	
340	Therefore the cleanest path to ARGB32 is:
341	- **Software post-pass:** single `memset` of byte 3 at framebuffer init (if DMA stride matches) or a per-frame byte-smearing pass (expensive).
342	- **GFX2D blit:** use the 2D graphics engine to copy BGRX32 → ARGB32 with alpha fill. Zero CPU cost if the engine supports it.
343	- **Display IP native BGRX support:** SAM9X75 LCDC supports multiple BGRX/ARGB layouts — pick one that doesn't care about alpha. Probably the right answer.
344
```

 `./firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md`

```text
1	# marvin BGR888 → LCD Display Path
2	
3	How the captured video (documented in [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md)) lands on the 10.1" 1280×800 LVDS panel. Implementation: BGR888 packed from DDR → SAM9X75 XLCDC HEO layer → LVDSC → panel. Zero CPU, zero scaling, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap on ISC frame-done ISR.
4	
5	**Status:** working. Pi 480p (720×480) and Wii/ElectronWarp 480p (720×480) display centered on the 1280×800 panel with 280 px black pillarbox each side and 160 px black letterbox top + bottom. Pi 720p (1280×720) display works too — full panel width, 40 px letterbox top + bottom.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Path overview
10	
11	```
12	DDR framebuffer (g_framebuffer in isc_capture.c)
13	  BGR888 packed, 32-byte aligned, in .region_nocache
14	        │                     <── XLCDC DMA reads
15	        ▼
16	XLCDC HEO layer (High-End Overlay, with hardware scaler)
17	  RGB_888_PACKED color mode (memory order B, G, R per pixel)
18	  src_w × src_h window, centered on the 1280×800 panel via lcd_bind()
19	  alpha=255 global; pointer re-set to just-completed buffer on every ISC ISR
20	        │
21	        ▼
22	XLCDC timing engine  (1280×800 @ 60 Hz, 10.1" panel timings from MCC)
23	        │
24	        ▼
25	LVDSC  (LVDS serializer)
26	        │
27	        ▼
28	10.1" 1280×800 LVDS panel
29	```
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Key decisions, with rationale
34	
35	### 2.1 HEO, not OVR1 or BASE
36	
37	The SAM9X75 XLCDC BASE layer has **no window position or size registers** — its window is always the full configured display size. Pointing BASE at a 720-wide framebuffer while the display is 800 wide produces an 80 px/row skew.
38	
39	Overlays (OVR1, OVR2, HEO) have position/size registers so their window can be smaller than the panel and positioned anywhere. **We use HEO** (High-End Overlay) because:
40	- It has a built-in hardware scaler (`HEOCFG3`/`HEOCFG4` separate display vs. memory rect) — used when we later need to scale a source smaller than 720p up to fit the panel.
41	- It natively supports `RGB_888_PACKED` color mode, which matches our BGR888 capture format exactly.
42	- OVR1 lacks a scaler; adding one later would require migrating the bind call anyway.
43	
44	### 2.2 `XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED`
45	
46	Our capture format is BGR888 packed — memory byte order per pixel is `B, G, R` (low address to high), dense with no padding byte.
47	
48	The XLCDC `RGB_888_PACKED` mode reads memory in this byte order (per SAM9X75 LCDC datasheet Table 44.26). Setting this mode on the HEO layer lets LCDC DMA read the capture buffer directly with zero conversion.
49	
50	### 2.3 Global alpha via `XLCDC_SetLayerOpts(layer, 255, true, false)`
51	
52	HEO's layer opts take a global alpha (0–255) and an `enable_dma` flag. We pass `alpha = 255` + `enable_dma = true`:
53	- `enable_dma = true` → pixel data comes from the framebuffer via DMA.
54	- `alpha = 255` → the layer is fully opaque.
55	
56	### 2.4 Pillarbox, not scale
57	
58	Panel is 1280×800. Source dimensions vary; `lcd_bind_capture(w, h)` centers the source via `xpos = (1280-w)/2`, `ypos = (800-h)/2`. Common cases:
59	
60	| Source | Window | Pillarbox L+R | Letterbox T+B |
61	|---|---|---|---|
62	| 720×480 (Wii / Pi 480p) | 720×480 at (280, 160) | 280 px each | 160 px each |
63	| 1280×720 (Pi 720p) | 1280×720 at (0, 40) | 0 (fills width) | 40 px each |
64	
65	No scaling engine needed for either source yet. BASE layer (below HEO in z-order) paints the surrounding black region — it's still the MCC-auto-allocated 1280×800 buffer of zeroes.
66	
67	If the source is larger than 1280×800 (e.g. 1080p), `lcd_bind` bails with a log error and the bind step is skipped (capture pipeline still runs into DDR, just nothing on screen). Downscaling uses the HEO hardware scaler — `HEOCFG3`/`HEOCFG4` set the display rect vs. source-memory rect independently.
68	
69	### 2.5 Per-frame pointer swap
70	
71	On every ISC frame-done ISR, `video.c` calls `XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, just_completed_addr, true)`. The `update=true` flag latches the new address at the next panel VSYNC, so LCDC never reads mid-frame and the display tracks every captured frame at the full 60 Hz ISC rate. With a 4-deep capture ring, there is no buffer aliasing — ISC is never writing the same buffer the display is reading.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. Cache coherency
76	
77	`g_framebuffer` lives in `.region_nocache` (uncached DDR). All DMA consumers (ISC write, LCDC read, CPU vision reads) see the same bytes directly from DDR — no cache flush or invalidate calls needed. This is the simplest correct choice for a buffer written by DMA and read by multiple consumers including the CPU.
78	
79	---
80	
81	## 4. Call sequence
82	
83	All wiring is in `firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c`:
84	
85	### 4.1 Boot-time (`APP_Initialize`)
86	
87	```c
88	XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
89	```
90	
91	MCC's auto-initialization (`SYS_Initialize`) already ran:
92	- `XLCDC_Initialize()` — clocks, timing engine, all 4 layers (BASE/OVR1/HEO/OVR2) set up at 1280×800 with auto-allocated buffers in `.region_nocache` (now in RGB565, ~2 MB per layer).
93	- `XLCDC_Start()` — panel clock, sync, disp enable, SD enable (all called from inside `Initialize`).
94	- `LVDSC_Initialize()` — LVDS serializer.
95	- `DRV_GFX2D_Initialize()` — 2D graphics engine (available for later work).
96	
97	Backlight is *not* turned on by auto-init. We do it ourselves.
98	
99	### 4.2 Per-capture (`app_coordinate_capture` → `lcd_bind`)
100	
101	Runs once when TC358743 reports a lock and `ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)` succeeds. See `video.c` `lcd_bind()` for the current implementation. Key settings:
102	
103	- `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, ...)`
104	- `XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, ...)` — centered: `x = (1280-w)/2`, `y = (800-h)/2`
105	- `XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize` and `HEOCFG3`/`HEOCFG4` for display and source-memory rects respectively
106	- All `update=false` until the final `SetLayerEnable(true, true)` which commits atomically
107	
108	`XStride = 0` means no padding bytes between rows — source memory is tightly packed at `width × 3 B/row` for BGR888.
109	
110	---
111	
112	## 5. Current limitations / next steps
113	
114	- **Panel-exceeding sources aren't displayed.** Pi 720p (1280×720) fits the 1280×800 panel; only 1080p and beyond need the HEO scaler enabled.
115	- **BASE layer is still the MCC-auto-allocated 1280×800 black buffer.** ~2 MB of `.region_nocache` DDR (RGB565) permanently displaying black around our overlay. Low priority; could reclaim by dropping `XLCDC_BUF_PER_LAYER` to 0 for BASE.
116	- **Limited→full range expansion — not yet done.** TC358743 reports RGB limited-range (16–235) for both Wii and Pi sources, so bytes in DDR reflect that range. Vision consumers deliberately see unexpanded bytes (linear rescale carries no new signal). The expansion is cosmetic, needed only because the panel expects 0–255 and renders limited-range data with muted blacks/whites.
117	  - **Planned path:** HEO layer Color Space Conversion matrix (`HEOCFG14..17`). Programmable `out = M × in + offset` configured as identity RGB→RGB with the 219-step limited→full gain/offset. Zero CPU, display-only, capture framebuffer unchanged.
118
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Yellow-Tinge / Left-Half Artifact — Complete Analysis
2	
3	Working document collecting every test we've run against the yellow-tinge / left-half-of-overlay artifact on the SAM9X75 + 10.1" NVDI 1280×800 LVDS panel. Goal of this doc: avoid re-treading any of the tested ground; record the empirical results; identify the root cause; document the resolution.
4	
5	**Status (2026-06-09): production refresh raised to 55 Hz on the SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid board.** The board port (Curiosity → Curiosity Hybrid, same 10.1″ panel + LVDS cable) widened the signal-integrity margin: the cliff moved up from the original board's 52–54 Hz window to ~57–58 Hz. 60 Hz now shows only *mild* overlay yellow (vs *severe* before), 57 Hz is clean at rest but still cable-handling-sensitive (right at the new edge), and **55 Hz is clean and handling-robust → new production setting** (~3.5% margin under the 57 Hz edge, +5 Hz over the original board's 50 Hz). Same root cause and overlay-only signature as before — only the transmit-side margin improved. Full Hybrid sweep in §9. The original-board investigation and root-cause analysis below (§1–§8) stand as the historical record.
6	
7	**Status (2026-05-15, original SAM9X75 Curiosity board): RESOLVED at 50 Hz.** Yellow is gone at **40, 45, 50, and 52 Hz**, present at 54 Hz, severe at 60 Hz. Threshold sits in the **razor-thin 52–54 Hz window** (427 → 444 MHz LVDS bit clock — only ~4% bit-rate gap separates clean from failing). Confirms the hypothesis: at 444 MHz the LVDS receiver was right at the edge of its eye-margin budget for this cable; modest EMI from overlay-layer DMA tipped it over. Backing off bit rate restores margin. **Production setting: 50 Hz** (~8% margin under the cliff, comfortable headroom without sacrificing visible refresh quality).
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Symptom
12	
13	- White pixels in **overlay layer content** (OVR1 or HEO) display with a yellow tinge.
14	- The tinge is concentrated on the **left half** of the overlay window with a **sharp vertical divide** near the window's horizontal midpoint. The right half of the same window is clean.
15	- The artifact is **modulated by physical handling of the LVDS cable** at the panel-side connector end — touching, twisting, or repositioning the cable changes the strength of the artifact and can fully clear it in a "right" position.
16	- Yellow ≈ blue channel attenuated, red+green normal. White = `0xFE 0xFE 0xFE` per channel; yellow tinge looks like blue dropping to ~50% while R+G stay full.
17	- Frame rate / sustained display look fine — no flicker, sync, or timing instability. Just the per-pixel color shift on the left half of overlay content.
18	
19	## 2. Key finding: artifact is **overlay-layer-only**
20	
21	BASE layer **never** shows the artifact, regardless of what we put in it or at what bandwidth. The instant any overlay layer (OVR1 or HEO) is bound to display non-zero content over BASE, yellow appears in that overlay's left half.
22	
23	This is the strongest single clue. It rules out:
24	- LVDS cable being globally bad — both halves of the LVDS bit stream serve all panel pixels; if a lane were degraded uniformly, BASE pixels would also corrupt
25	- LVDS clock / serializer marginal — same reasoning
26	- DDR / panel timing — both paths use the same pixel clock and panel timing
27	- Total LCDC read bandwidth — BASE alone at 123 MB/s ARGB_8888 reads is clean; OVR1 at 62 MB/s RGB_888_PACKED reads is yellow
28	
29	What's different about overlays that BASE doesn't share:
30	- Overlays have **per-pixel alpha-blend logic** between layers
31	- Overlays have a **scaler / CSC / gamma / brightness-contrast / chroma-key / replication** pipeline that BASE lacks
32	- Overlay DMA is **windowed within a scanline** (active only during the overlay's x-range), so its bus activity is **clumped** rather than spread across the line
33	- Overlays are configurable for **VIDPRI** (elevated AHB priority); BASE is not
34	
35	The bandwidth, blend factors, and color format have all been varied without changing the artifact. That points away from those as the root cause and toward something structural in the overlay's data path.
36	
37	## 3. Tests performed
38	
39	Across the `lcd` and `bigteninch` branches.
40	
41	### 3.1 BASE layer alone tests (no overlay active)
42	
43	| Test | BASE format | BASE content | BASE BW | Yellow? |
44	|---|---|---|---|---|
45	| MCC default boot, BASE-only | RGB_565 | auto-zero black | 122 MB/s | **clean** |
46	| BASE white fill (lcd `mode 1`) | RGB_565 | 0xFFFF white | 122 MB/s | **clean** |
47	| BASE white at 32-bit (today) | ARGB_8888 | 0x00FFFFFF white | 123 MB/s | **clean** |
48	
49	### 3.2 BASE + ISC capture writes, no overlay reads
50	
51	| Test | BASE format | BASE content | ISC writing? | OVR/HEO reading? | Yellow? |
52	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
53	| `lcd` mode 2 | RGB_565 | white | yes | no | **clean** |
54	
55	This rules out ISC's DMA writes as a cause. ISC + BASE active simultaneously → no yellow.
56	
57	### 3.3 BASE + Overlay (OVR1 or HEO) bound to capture
58	
59	| Test | BASE | Overlay layer | Overlay format | Capture src | Yellow on overlay? |
60	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
61	| `lcd` initial config | RGB_565 black | OVR1 | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | **yes, left half** |
62	| `lcd` after MCC regen → broken blend | RGB_565 black | OVR1 | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | OVR1 invisible (separate bug) |
63	| `lcd` after blend fix | RGB_565 black | OVR1 | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | **yes** |
64	| `lcd` post-HEO migration | RGB_565 black | HEO | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | **yes** |
65	| `lcd` HEO with scaler 1.667× | RGB_565 black | HEO scaled | ARGB_8888 | 720×480→1200×800 | **yes** (in scaled output) |
66	| `lcd` mode 3 (HEO + BASE white) | RGB_565 white | HEO | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | **yes (HEO area only); BASE pillarbox stays clean white** |
67	| `lcd` mode 4 (HEO, BASE *disabled*) | DMA off | HEO | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | **yes** |
68	| `bigteninch` (post LVDSPLL fix, OVR1) | RGB_565 black | OVR1 | ARGB_8888 | 720×480 BGRX32 | **yes** |
69	| `bigteninch` RGB888 packed | RGB_565 black | OVR1 | RGB_888_PACKED | 720×480 BGR888 | **yes (same intensity)** |
70	| `bigteninch` BASE white (32-bit) | ARGB_8888 white | OVR1 | RGB_888_PACKED | 720×480 BGR888 | **yes (BASE pillarbox stays clean white)** |
71	| `bigteninch` BASE white (16-bit) | RGB_565 white | OVR1 | RGB_888_PACKED | 720×480 BGR888 | **yes; possibly slightly worse** |
72	
73	**Pattern:** every overlay configuration exhibits yellow on its left half. BASE never does. Format, blend mode, scaler, layer choice (OVR1 vs HEO), and total bandwidth are all independently varied without affecting the symptom.
74	
75	### 3.4 Software config tweaks (all on `lcd` branch except where noted)
76	
77	| Lever changed | Direction tried | Effect on yellow |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| HEO `BLEN` | INCR32 → INCR4 (smaller bursts) | none |
80	| HEO `VIDPRI` | 1 → 0 (lower priority) | broke display (BASE also corrupted) |
81	| HEO `HEOCFG4 XMEMSIZE` in 1:1 mode | skip the write in bypass | none |
82	| HEO scaler taps | nearest → bilinear | unchanged at 1.667× |
83	| LVDS `PREEMP` (all lanes + clock) | 0 → 1 | slight improvement |
84	| LVDS `PREEMP` | 1 → 2 | no further improvement |
85	| LVDS `DC_BAL` | UNBALANCED → BALANCED | garbage (panel doesn't speak it) |
86	| OVR1 / HEO blend `SFACTC` | various | doesn't change yellow; affects layer visibility only |
87	| LCDC layer count | 4 → 2 (drop OVR2 + HEO when not used) | enables clean display, but doesn't affect yellow when OVR1 is active |
88	| Overlay color depth | ARGB_8888 → RGB_888_PACKED (4 B/pixel → 3 B/pixel) | none (same intensity) |
89	| BASE color depth (today) | ARGB_8888 → RGB_565 (4 B/pixel → 2 B/pixel) | slightly worse |
90	| Total LCDC read BW | 185 → 124 MB/s | none (or slightly worse) |
91	| Capture path | RMS=0/PACKED32/BGRX32 ↔ RMS=1/PACKED32/BGR888 | none |
92	
93	### 3.5 Hardware tests
94	
95	| Action | Effect |
96	|---|---|
97	| Wiggle / reseat LVDS cable at panel end | Yellow strength changes; can sometimes find a position that nearly clears it |
98	| Wiggle cable at SoC end | Less effect |
99	
100	The cable-handling sensitivity is the strongest evidence that this is a **signal-integrity margin** issue, not a bus-arbitration / bandwidth issue.
101	
102	## 4. Hypothesis
103	
104	The artifact is **EMI / signal-integrity coupling between overlay-layer DMA activity and the LVDS pairs**, manifesting only when an overlay's data path is active.
105	
106	Why overlays only:
107	- Overlays have substantially more **combinatorial logic** in their data path (scaler, CSC, alpha blender, chroma key, gamma/contrast/brightness, replication). All of these blocks toggle on every pixel, even when "disabled" — gates still switch based on inputs and remain in the data path. BASE has none of this. So overlay rendering generates more switching activity per pixel inside the SoC, which radiates more high-frequency noise.
108	- Overlays are **windowed** — DMA bursts are clumped within the overlay's x-range rather than spread across the scanline. Same total bandwidth concentrated in a shorter window means higher peak switching rate, more concentrated EMI energy.
109	- Overlays are typically configured with **`VIDPRI=1`** for video priority, which lets them preempt other masters — promotes burst-chaining and longer continuous bus-busy windows.
110	
111	Why left-half-only:
112	- The LCDC has internal line-buffer / FIFO logic that fills at the start of a scanline and drains as it's displayed. The first portion of the overlay's window has the highest **input-side switching rate** (FIFO filling at peak rate while output is just starting). By mid-window, the steady state is reached and EMI evens out. The first half is where the noise is concentrated.
113	
114	Why white pixels worst:
115	- White = `0xFE 0xFE 0xFE` per channel = `0x00FEFEFE` (BGRX) or `0xFEFEFE` (BGR888 packed). These pixel patterns produce the highest ratio of `1`-bits per LVDS lane symbol. Long runs of high-density `1`-bits push the LVDS receiver's input common-mode bias off-center, eroding the eye margin most aggressively. With slightly more EMI than the LVDS receiver can tolerate at marginal cable SI, the most off-balance bit positions (which carry blue components in VESA mapping) flip wrong, dropping blue → yellow tinge.
116	
117	Why cable handling matters:
118	- LVDS pairs are differential; the cable shielding determines impedance and EMI rejection. Touching the cable changes the parasitic capacitance to ground, which shifts the impedance, the reflection profile, and the EMI pickup pattern. At marginal SI, those shifts can put the receiver above or below the bit-error threshold.
119	
120	Together: at the LVDSPLL bit clock (~444 MHz over 4 lanes carrying full 24-bit color × 60 Hz), we're operating at the edge of the cable's signal-integrity envelope. SoC internal noise from overlay rendering tips us over the edge for the left half of overlay regions specifically, and the cable's positioning determines how far over.
121	
122	## 5. Resolution: lower LVDSPLL → 40 Hz refresh
123	
124	The "long shot" of reducing LVDSPLL turned out to be the actual fix. We swept frame rates 30 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 / 60 (each computed to keep the LVDSPLL VCO above the 600 MHz minimum) and observed:
125	
126	| Refresh | LVDSPLL | Bit clock per LVDS lane | Result |
127	|---|---|---|---|
128	| 30 Hz | 246.5 MHz | ~246 Mbps | Yellow gone, subtle flicker on bright content |
129	| 40 Hz | 328.6 MHz | ~329 Mbps | Yellow gone, no flicker |
130	| 45 Hz | 369.7 MHz | ~370 Mbps | Yellow gone, no flicker |
131	| **50 Hz** ← chosen | **410.8 MHz** | **~411 Mbps** | **Yellow gone, no flicker — production setting** |
132	| 52 Hz | 427.2 MHz | ~427 Mbps | Yellow gone, no flicker (closest clean) |
133	| 54 Hz (was) | 444.5 MHz | ~444 Mbps | Yellow on overlay left half |
134	| 60 Hz | 492.9 MHz | ~493 Mbps | **Significant yellow, much worse than 54 Hz** |
135	
136	The yellow threshold is bracketed in the **razor-thin 52–54 Hz window** — only ~4% bit-rate spread separates clean from failing. Textbook signature of a marginal SI link operating right at its eye-budget cliff: until the eye closes past the receiver's threshold there's no visible degradation, then it falls off rapidly. Past the cliff, severity scales with how far over you push:
137	
138	- 52 Hz @ 427 Mbps = clean → ~4% margin under threshold (closest tested clean)
139	- 50 Hz @ 411 Mbps = clean → ~8% margin (chosen production setting)
140	- 45 Hz @ 370 Mbps = clean → ~17% margin
141	- 40 Hz @ 329 Mbps = clean → ~26% margin
142	- 30 Hz @ 246 Mbps = clean → ~45% margin (but slight flicker)
143	- 54 Hz @ 444 Mbps = visible yellow → ~0% margin (just over the cliff)
144	- **60 Hz @ 493 Mbps = severe yellow** → ~−10% margin (well past)
145	
146	The 60 Hz observation confirms the SI cliff is one-directional: pushing further past the threshold makes things worse fast. Beyond simple bit errors, the LVDS receiver may also be dropping into a degraded lock state where it's not fully recovering between symbols.
147	
148	Cable swap or hardware mitigations would push the ceiling up — but at 50 Hz with ~8% margin, we're comfortably below the cliff and haven't seen any new artifacts in extended testing. No further hardware work needed for this panel.
149	
150	### Production MCC values: 50 Hz (original Curiosity board — superseded on the Hybrid; see §9)
151	
152	Set in the **XLCDC Driver** MCC component (`le_gfx_driver_xlcdc.yml`):
153	
154	```
155	LVDSClockMul       = 34
156	LVDSClockFrac      = 964690
157	LVDSClockDivPMC    = 2
158	XLCDCPixClockHint  = 58680000
159	LVDSClockOutHint   = 410760000
160	```
161	
162	Verify: `24 × (34 + 964690/2²²) / 2 = 24 × 34.230 / 2 = 410.76 MHz` ✓
163	- VCO `24 × 34.230 = 821.5 MHz` (above 600 MHz floor) ✓
164	- LVDSPLL output `410.76 MHz`
165	- Pixel clock `410.76 / 7 = 58.68 MHz`
166	- Frame rate `58,680,000 / (1440 × 815) = 50.00 Hz` exactly
167	
168	### Alternative settings
169	
170	For reference if you ever want to back further off the cliff (slower refresh, more SI margin) — both confirmed clean:
171	
172	**45 Hz** — `Mul=30, Frac=3384800, DivPMC=2` → 369.68 MHz output, 17% margin
173	**40 Hz** — `Mul=27, Frac=1610613, DivPMC=2` → 328.61 MHz output, 26% margin
174	**30 Hz** — `Mul=41, Frac=318768, DivPMC=4` → 246.46 MHz output, 45% margin (subtle flicker on bright content)
175	
176	## 6. Why the panel + cable can't handle 444 MHz cleanly
177	
178	This is the actual root cause:
179	
180	- **Cable SI margin too tight at ~444 Mbps/lane.** Confirmed by physical-handling sensitivity — touching/repositioning the cable changes the artifact, which is the textbook signature of a marginally-failing differential pair. Likely the cable wasn't qualified for this rate, or the connector seating is slightly off.
181	- **Overlay-layer rendering pushes EMI floor higher than BASE-only does.** Overlay's data path has scaler/CSC/blender combinatorial logic that toggles on every pixel, plus its DMA bursts are clumped within the overlay's x-window rather than spread across the line. Both increase peak switching activity and EMI relative to BASE.
182	- **At 444 MHz bit clock, the marginal cable + elevated EMI floor combine to cross the bit-error threshold** specifically on the worst-case data patterns (long runs of high-density 1-bits, i.e. white pixels), and specifically on the bits that carry blue components (LVDS lane A2 in VESA mapping). That's the yellow tinge.
183	- **At 328 MHz bit clock**, the eye opens by ~35% (proportional to bit period). The receiver gets enough margin to recover all bits cleanly, including the worst-case patterns. Yellow disappears.
184	
185	## 7. Future work (optional, not blocking)
186	
187	1. **Hardware: better cable** — would let us run higher refresh rates if needed. 60 Hz would be possible with a properly-rated cable. Not currently necessary.
188	2. **Hardware: ferrite or shielding** — same goal. Not necessary at 40 Hz.
189	3. **Software: reduce overlay EMI floor** — long shots if we want to push refresh higher without fixing the cable: move overlay buffer to `.region_nocache`, disable any HEO blocks we haven't yet, etc. None of these promise more than a small SI improvement.
190	
191	## 8. Why 40 Hz is fine
192	
193	- Panel locks cleanly with no visible flicker at this rate on our content (live camera feed + static UI elements).
194	- Camera input is 60 fps, but display only needs to show "current frame" — 40 Hz LCDC refresh just means each captured frame is shown for at most 25 ms before the next refresh starts. Worst-case input-to-output latency is unchanged (the limiter is ISC writing into DDR at 60 fps).
195	- DDR bandwidth needed by LCDC drops 33% (from `BASE + OVR1 read at 60 Hz` to `at 40 Hz`), freeing it for vision workloads.
196	- 40 Hz is well above the 24 Hz cinema-rate baseline humans tolerate easily.
197	
198	## 9. Board port re-test: SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid — ceiling raised, production → 55 Hz
199	
200	Re-ran the frame-rate sweep after porting marvin to the SAM9X75 **Curiosity Hybrid** board (2026-06-09), reusing the same 10.1″ panel and its LVDS cable. The board change swaps everything on the **transmit** side — PCB routing from the LVDSC pins to the panel connector, the connector itself, power/ground integrity — and removes the on-board USB host as an EMI aggressor. The receiver side (panel + cable) is unchanged.
201	
202	Result: **the SI margin widened and the cliff moved up ~5 Hz.**
203	
204	| Refresh | Mul / Frac (DivPMC=2) | LVDS clock | Result on Hybrid |
205	|---|---|---|---|
206	| 60 Hz | 41 / 318768 | 492.9 MHz | **mild** overlay yellow (was *severe* on the original board) |
207	| 57 Hz | 39 / 93114 | 468.3 MHz | clean at rest; slight yellow inducible by handling the cable at the connector (right at the new edge) |
208	| **55 Hz** ← chosen | **37 / 2738881** | **451.8 MHz** | **clean and handling-robust → production** |
209	| 50 Hz | 34 / 964690 | 410.8 MHz | clean (original-board production) |
210	
211	Reading: the new cliff edge sits at ~57–58 Hz (vs the original board's 52–54 Hz). 57 Hz is the new "closest clean" — clean undisturbed but handling-sensitive, the same marginal-SI signature the original board showed at 52 Hz. Backing off to **55 Hz** gives ~3.5% margin under that edge and stays clean even under deliberate cable handling, so it's the production setting — a net +5 Hz over the original board's 50 Hz.
212	
213	The improvement is entirely transmit-side: same overlay-only artifact, same yellow-on-white signature, same cable-handling sensitivity — only the eye margin at a given bit rate improved. A better-rated panel cable (§7) would still be the lever to reach a robust 60 Hz; not pursued — 55 Hz is comfortable.
214	
215	### Production MCC values: 55 Hz
216	
217	Set in the **XLCDC Driver** MCC component (`le_gfx_driver_xlcdc.yml`):
218	
219	```
220	LVDSClockMul       = 37
221	LVDSClockFrac      = 2738881
222	LVDSClockDivPMC    = 2
223	XLCDCPixClockHint  = 64548000
224	LVDSClockOutHint   = 451836000
225	```
226	
227	Verify: `24 × (37 + 2738881/2²²) / 2 = 24 × 37.653 / 2 = 451.84 MHz` ✓
228	- VCO `24 × 37.653 = 903.7 MHz` (above 600 MHz floor) ✓
229	- LVDSPLL output `451.84 MHz`
230	- Pixel clock `451.84 / 7 = 64.55 MHz`
231	- Frame rate `64,548,000 / (1440 × 815) = 55.00 Hz` exactly
232

1	# marvin — UI architecture (canvas compositor + per-screen modules)
2	
3	How marvin's operator UI is structured: independently-authored panels (dashboard, nav,
4	dialogs) each render into their own **canvas surface** in RAM, the compositor maps surfaces
5	onto the scarce **LCDC hardware layers**, and — with the MGS screen state machine disabled —
6	the application owns screen orchestration so multiple panels coexist **live and interactive
7	at once** instead of one-screen-at-a-time switching.
8	
9	Read [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.5 (operator UI) and §4.1 (video/display) first. Decisions in
10	[`journal.md`](journal.md) (2026-06-25, 2026-06-29). **Status: migrated to the MGS layer-screen
11	model and confirmed on hardware** — one master `Marvin` screen with dashboard (BASE), nav
12	(OVR1), and song-select dialog (OVR2) as layer-screens; the model and the canonical mental
13	picture are in §0.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 0. The mental model (read this first) — three concepts, not two
18	
19	These are distinct and must not be collapsed (this has been a recurring source of confusion):
20	
21	1. **Legato layer ("layer-screen")** — a logical screen / dialog / overlay. Bounded by
22	   `LE_LAYER_COUNT` = the number of layer-screens.
23	2. **GFX canvas** — the RAM framebuffer backing a layer-screen. **Coupled 1:1 to its Legato
24	   layer:** the renderer writes Legato layer *i* into `canvas[baseCanvasID + i]` (base 0 →
25	   layer *i* ↔ `canvas[i]`), and `leAddRootWidget(root, layerIdx)` rejects
26	   `layerIdx >= LE_LAYER_COUNT`. So a canvas id is **not** free of its Legato layer.
27	3. **XLCDC hardware layer** (`BASE`/`OVR1`/`OVR2`; `HEO` = camera) — where a canvas is
28	   composited for scanout. Bound at **display time, at runtime, and reassignable** via
29	   `gfxcSetLayer(canvasID, hwLayer)` (`ui_manager.c` `bind_canvas`).
30	
31	**"canvas ≠ layer" is true only for the *hardware* layer (3), not for the *Legato* layer (2).**
32	A panel never *owns* a HW layer — two canvases never shown together can share one; the same
33	canvas can be on `OVR1` in one situation and `OVR2` in another. The 8-slot canvas pool
34	(`CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ = 8`) means up to 8 layer-screens may be **defined**
35	(`LE_LAYER_COUNT` ≤ 8, canvases 0–7); the LCDC then composites **any 3** of them onto its 3
36	usable HW layers at once — *define many, show a few.*
37	
38	### 0.1 Direction (decided 2026-06-29): adopt MGS's single-master-screen / layer-screen model
39	
40	Per Microchip's GFX-canvas layer-screen guide¹, MGS is meant to be **one master screen whose
41	*layers* are the logical screens** ("layer-screens"), each auto-associated with its own canvas.
42	marvin **adopted this model on 2026-06-29** (confirmed on hardware). It previously *emulated*
43	it by hand — each panel a **separate 1-layer MGS Screen**, built on layer 0 then manually
44	disconnected and re-hosted by `ui_manager`, with `LE_LAYER_COUNT` pinned at 3 by a never-shown
45	`LayerBudget` screen. Now there is **one master screen named `Marvin`, one layer per panel**:
46	layer 0 dashboard (BASE), layer 1 nav (OVR1), layer 2 song-select dialog (OVR2). MGS derives
47	`LE_LAYER_COUNT` and associates each layer-screen with `canvas[i]`, so the `LayerBudget` hack
48	and the disconnect/re-host dance are gone — `ui_manager` calls `screenInit_Marvin()` +
49	`screenShow_Marvin()` once (the latter builds the tree and attaches each root to its Legato
50	layer), then per-panel `*_Setup()` wiring, and binds canvases to HW layers at display time.
51	**The splash is separate and fully manual** (pre-Legato RGBA8888 scanout): it is *not* a
52	canvas at all — it owns a static framebuffer and drives its XLCDC hardware layer directly via
53	the PLIB (`splash.c` `Splash_Show`/`Splash_Hide`, mirroring `video.c`'s HEO setup), so the
54	canvas pool is exactly the three layer-screens (0/1/2).
55	
56	> **§1–§7 below were written for the previous per-screen-Factory + manual-re-host design** and
57	> are kept for history; where they conflict with §0, §0 wins. `screenInit_X` is now a one-time
58	> flag only — the widget tree is constructed in **`screenShow_X`** (a gotcha worth remembering).
59	
60	¹ developerhelp.microchip.com → MGS Harmony guide → how-to → gfx-canvas → layer-screen.
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 1. The core idea
65	
66	Content geometry was welded to hardware 1:1:1 — one Legato layer → one framebuffer → one LCDC
67	layer. There are only **4 LCDC layers** (`BASE`, `OVR1`, `HEO`, `OVR2`); `HEO` is the live
68	camera. The compositor breaks the welding:
69	
70	- A **surface** is a RAM framebuffer (a GFX Canvas object) holding a panel's pixels.
71	- A **layer** is a hardware compositor window. The LCDC blends them every scan with zero CPU.
72	- Showing a panel = point a layer at its surface + enable (register writes, no re-render).
73	  Hiding = disable/move the layer. Sliding = animate the layer's window position.
74	
75	**GFX Canvas** is the substrate: `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` redirects Legato's render target to a
76	canvas object, and `gfxcSetLayer`/`ShowCanvas`/`SetWindowPosition` map/show/move that surface
77	on an LCDC layer. (Why canvas and not a hand-rolled retarget or direct-layer-only: see the
78	2026-06-25 journal entry — canvas is the only thing that gets Legato content *into* an
79	arbitrary off-screen surface; direct layer control still does the show/move.)
80	
81	## 2. The enabling change — MGS screen state machine OFF
82	
83	Legato's stock "screen state machine" (`le_gen_init.c`) shows **one screen at a time** —
84	`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing screen's widget tree. That is fatal to a compositor
85	that wants several panels live simultaneously. So it is **disabled** ("Generate Screen State
86	Machine" off; `le_gen_init.{c,h}` no longer generated — see the 2026-06-25 journal entry and
87	the `compat/` stub that works around the resulting MGS include bug).
88	
89	Two confirmed facts make this work (verified in `legato_state.c` / `legato_renderer.c` /
90	`legato_input.c`):
91	
92	1. **`_state.layerList` is global and `leUpdate` renders/updates *every* attached layer each
93	   frame.** There is no "active screen" render gate. Attach roots to multiple layers → they all
94	   render live.
95	2. **Touch picks across all attached layers, top-to-bottom** (`leInput` iterates `layerList`
96	   from the top). So an attached overlay is interactive wherever it sits; the layer below
97	   receives touches elsewhere. *(This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable /
98	   reveal-then-promote" idea — that was a consequence of the state machine, which is now gone.)*
99	
100	So the model is simply: **attach a panel's root to a layer → it is live and interactive;
101	detach (or move off-screen) → it is gone.** No freeze, no promotion dance.
102	
103	## 3. MGS Screen = widget-tree factory
104	
105	With the state machine off, the generated per-screen functions are ours to call directly
106	(MGS even relabels them `// call to show this screen`). We treat each **MGS Screen as a
107	widget-tree factory**, decoupled from display:
108	
109	- `screenInit_X()` — builds the widget tree (+ registers any MGS-wired events).
110	- `screenShow_X()` — attaches its root(s) to layer(s) and raises the `X_OnShow` hook.
111	- `leAddRootWidget(wgt, layer)` / `leRemoveRootWidget(wgt, layer)` — **re-host** a root onto
112	  whatever Legato layer we want, independent of the index MGS authored it on.
113	- `screenGetRoot_X(lyrIdx)` — fetch a root to re-host or toggle visibility.
114	
115	So each panel is authored in its own clean MGS Screen, then the compositor assembles the
116	trees onto the layer set it manages. The screen's `OnShow` hook is that panel's
117	**composition root** — where it runtime-registers its widget event callbacks (the DI pattern;
118	see the 2026-06-25 journal entry on widget events being runtime-registerable while screen
119	lifecycle events are direct calls).
120	
121	## 4. Hardware layer budget
122	
123	| Legato layer | LCDC | Content | Lifecycle |
124	|---|---|---|---|
125	| 0 | BASE | active full-screen view (dashboard, …) | swappable (replace) |
126	| 1 | OVR1 | **nav drawer** | resident — attach once, persists across base-view swaps |
127	| 2 | OVR2 | **modal dialog** (song/mode select), sized to the dialog | shown/hidden; background stays live |
128	| — | HEO | camera | `video.c`, **outside Legato** |
129	
130	- **Nav on its own resident layer ⇒ "same nav over every view" for free** — it is independent
131	  of layer 0, so swapping the base view leaves it untouched.
132	- **Modal dialog on OVR2 sized to the dialog ⇒ uncovered dashboard telemetry keeps updating**
133	  (layer 0 renders live behind it). The dialog is invoked only from the dashboard.
134	- **Ceiling:** dashboard + nav + dialog + camera = **all 4 LCDC layers**. A 4th simultaneous UI
135	  surface needs canvas multiplexing (`gfxcSetBaseCanvasID`) or giving up a layer.
136	
137	> **Current HW-layer map (supersedes the table above; see §16):** BASE = dashboard, HEO = video,
138	> **OVR1 = video frame overlay / song-select dialog**, **OVR2 = nav drawer / album-art strip**.
139	> Z-order `OVR2 > OVR1 > HEO > BASE`. Nav moved to OVR2 so it sits *above* the OVR1 video frame
140	> (an open drawer covers the frame's left edge). The pairs on each overlay are time-exclusive:
141	> frame ⇎ dialog (frame hidden whenever video is), nav ⇎ album-art (nav closed during song-select).
142	
143	### 4.1 Two layer counts — don't conflate them
144	- **`LE_LAYER_COUNT`** (Legato, `legato_config.h`) = how many canvases / Legato layers the global
145	  `layerList` manages = **3**. MGS derives it as the **max layer count across all screens** in the
146	  design; there is no explicit knob.
147	- **`XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS`** (XLCDC driver, "Total Layers" in `le_gfx_driver_xlcdc.yml`) = enumerated
148	  hardware layers = **4** (`layerOrder` = {BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2, OVR2 3}).
149	
150	They differ on purpose: Legato manages 3 canvases, each mapped onto **3 of the 4** hardware layers.
151	
152	### 4.2 Pinning `LE_LAYER_COUNT` = 3 (the LayerBudget screen)
153	Each panel is authored as its own **1-layer** MGS screen, so nothing reaches 3 layers on its own —
154	and there's no direct setting. A dedicated, **never-shown `LayerBudget` screen with 3 layers** pins
155	the count (regen-safe; no `legato_config.h` patch). Keep it un-shown: its roots then never attach,
156	so Legato layer 2 stays an empty internal root. **Caveat:** `LE_LAYER_COUNT` 3 lets Legato render
157	into `canvas[2]`, whose buffer is still the generated `NULL` until the dialog assigns one — safe
158	**only** while layer 2 has no attached root / no damage (i.e. LayerBudget is never shown and no panel
159	re-hosts onto layer 2 yet).
160	
161	### 4.3 Why HEO is safe (and stays enabled)
162	Layer targeting is **explicit, not positional**: Legato layer *i* → `canvas[i]` →
163	`gfxcSetLayer(i, hwLayer)`, where `hwLayer` indexes `layerOrder`. We map canvases only to hw layers
164	**0 / 2 / 3** (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) and **never to 1 (HEO)**, so the canvas framework never issues an
165	IOCTL to HEO regardless of enumeration order. The only GFX-side touch of HEO is
166	`DRV_XLCDC_Initialize` disabling all enumerated layers once at init — before `video.c` configures it
167	(post-scheduler), so video is the last writer. So **HEO stays enabled** and `video.c` keeps full
168	runtime control via the XLCDC PLIB, including the `HEOCFG12` blender + `VIDPRI` z-order that
169	`XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer` provides (`video.c` does not set those itself — which is exactly why disabling
170	HEO in MCC would break compositing, and why we don't).
171	
172	## 5. Live coexistence vs. replacement
173	
174	The compositor offers two verbs, chosen per interaction — you do **not** pick one global mode:
175	
176	- **Coexist (overlay-as-layer)** — the panel is its own layer over a still-live background.
177	  Used for the **nav drawer** (dashboard keeps updating behind it) and the **modal dialog**
178	  (telemetry keeps updating around it). No freeze.
179	- **Replace (switch base view)** — a full-screen view replaces another on layer 0; the
180	  outgoing one detaches (its surface can hold the last frame, or it is rebuilt on return).
181	  Used when a view genuinely supersedes the dashboard and live background isn't needed.
182	
183	Because the compositor owns layer placement and attach/detach, moving an interaction between
184	these is a compositor-level change, not a per-module rewrite — the reversibility we wanted.
185	
186	## 6. Module structure
187	
188	```
189	            ┌──────────────────────── ui_manager ─────────────────────────┐
190	            │ string-table init · screen init/show · root re-host onto     │
191	            │ layers · layer/canvas pool · visibility · verbs:             │
192	            │   show_view(X) · push_overlay(nav|dialog) · hide_overlay(…)   │
193	            └───────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────┘
194	              ┌─────▼─────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐
195	              │  dashboard │         │ screens/nav │          │ song_select  │
196	              │ (BASE,lyr0)│         │ (OVR1,lyr1) │          │ (OVR2,lyr2)  │
197	              └────────────┘         └─────────────┘          └──────────────┘
198	   each: owns its widgets + interactions; composition root = its screen OnShow hook
199	```
200	
201	- **`ui_manager`** (promoted from today's `compositor.c`) owns the *mechanism*: string-table
202	  setup, calling `screenInit_/screenShow_`, re-hosting roots onto the right layer, the canvas
203	  buffer pool, layer visibility, and the coexist/replace verbs. It is the "top-level module
204	  that ties everything together."
205	- **Per-screen/overlay modules** own only their panel's content + event wiring, registered
206	  from their own `OnShow` composition root. They never call `legato_*`/canvas APIs directly —
207	  they go through `ui_manager`, which is what keeps the layer mechanics swappable.
208	
209	### 6.1 Source layout (`default/src/ui/`)
210	
211	The UI tree is grouped by role; module files carry an explicit `screen_`/`widget_` prefix so
212	a flat editor tab list reads unambiguously:
213	
214	```
215	ui/
216	  ui_manager.{c,h}                          orchestrator (mechanism; stays at root)
217	  manual_input.c                            input shim for the future manual-input screen
218	  screens/<name>/   screen_<name>.{c,h}     one folder per panel (+ panel-specific helpers)
219	  widgets/<name>/   widget_<name>.{c,h}     reusable widgets, one folder each
220	```
221	
222	Current contents: `screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard`, `screens/video/screen_video`,
223	`screens/navigation/screen_navigation`, `screens/song_select/screen_song_select`,
224	`screens/splash/screen_splash`, `widgets/song_list/widget_song_list`,
225	`widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa`.
226	
227	`screen_video` is a screen module without its own canvas: the live video is on the
228	HEO hardware layer (compositor-owned), so this module owns only the *interaction* —
229	a tap handler on `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD` that toggles the HEO window between the
230	windowed rect and fullscreen via `UiManager_VideoShow`. See §14.
231	
232	**Naming convention:** a screen module's file is `screens/<name>/screen_<name>.{c,h}` and its
233	public functions are prefixed `Screen<Name>_` (PascalCase of the file basename) — e.g.
234	`screen_song_select.c` → `ScreenSongSelect_Setup`. This matches the project's `Module_Method`
235	style (`UiManager_*`, `ButtonAA_*`) and stays clear of the MGS-generated entry points
236	(lowercase `screenInit_Marvin`, `event_Marvin_*`). Each panel module exposes
237	`Screen<Name>_InitSurface()` (assign its canvas buffer, pre-scheduler) and `Screen<Name>_Setup()`
238	(set its canvas window + wire content/events on the widgets `screenShow_Marvin` already built);
239	`ui_manager` calls these — the modules never bind HW layers themselves. The splash is the one
240	exception: it is not a canvas, so it exposes `ScreenSplash_Load`/`Show`/`Hide` instead. Headers
241	are included from the `default/src` root, e.g. `#include "ui/screens/navigation/screen_navigation.h"`.
242	New panels add a `screens/<name>/` folder; new widgets a `widgets/<name>/` folder — each wired
243	into `user.cmake`
244	(no MCC involvement).

264	## 8. Static-allocation, cache & priority rules
265	
266	- **Static non-cached surfaces.** Each canvas surface is a file-scope static array in
267	  `.region_nocache` (no malloc), passed via `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`. They are CPU-rendered then
268	  read by the 2D engine / LCDC DMA, so non-cached is required (same policy as `FB_CACHE_NC`
269	  and the Legato scratch — 2026-06-24 cache-coherency fix). RGB565 to match the panel.
270	- **`GFX_CANVAS_Task`** is at UI-band priority 2 (set in the gfx_canvas yml), required even
271	  with FX off (drives `INIT→RUNNING`). It's a dynamic MCC task on heap_1 like the others.
272	- **Heap.** The canvas component pushed `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang via the
273	  malloc-failed hook; heap is now 65536 and the fault hooks emit a DBGU marker (2026-06-25).
274	
275	## 9. Memory budget
276	
277	`.region_nocache` is 32 MB, shared with the ISC capture pool (~10.5 MB) + Legato scratch
278	(0.5 MB). Full-screen RGB565 surface ≈ 2.0 MB; overlays sized to content are far less (nav
279	~320×800 ≈ 0.5 MB; a modal dialog smaller still). ~19 MB free after BASE + capture + scratch,
280	so **memory is not the binding constraint — the 3 UI layers are.**
281

300	## 10a. Anti-aliased rounded button corners (done)
301	
302	The nav buttons use the widget `cornerRadius` (set in code — not exposed in MGS), but the
303	classic skin's rounded-rect fill draws corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard, stepped
304	edges). Smoothing is done **without touching Legato/MCC code** (`config/default/` is
305	off-limits), via a per-instance vtable re-point in `src/ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`:
306	
307	- `leWidget.fn` is a writable per-instance pointer to a `const` vtable. `ButtonAA_Enable`
308	  makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points
309	  the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (not an MCC knob; unguarded
310	  `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h`), no global RAM cost — scoped to re-pointed
311	  buttons.
312	- The wrapper runs the original paint (bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with the
313	  supported radius overdraws the four corners: sample the backdrop from each corner's
314	  extreme pixel (left untouched by the rounded fill), then blend a 1px transition band from
315	  a precomputed coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill is read from
316	  the live scheme each paint, so highlight (selected/unselected) and pressed states track.
317	- Runs **in-pass** (damage → repaint → AA in one paint), so no timing/flicker window.
318	- Wired from `nav_buttons_init()`; currently nav-only. Extending app-wide is just calling
319	  `ButtonAA_Enable` from other screens' button init. Single radius (`BUTTON_AA_RADIUS`);
320	  other radii pass through unsmoothed.
