322	## 12. Boot splash (done — code-complete, pending hardware test)
323	
324	A full-screen photo splash is the first thing on the panel: the loader reads it off the SD card
325	into RAM, gets it onto BASE, and only then lights the backlight, so the panel never shows a
326	pre-splash/garbage frame. It's also the first real use of the **replace** verb (§5) and proves
327	the runtime-image path the album-art pre-load will reuse.
328	
329	- **Splash on its own OVR2 layer/canvas, drawn over the dashboard.** The `Splash` MGS screen
330	  (`le_gen_screen_Splash.c`: full-screen `Splash_Panel_0`, solid scheme fill) is kept as the base
331	  for the "every base view has an MGS component" convention; its only real content — the photo — is
332	  loaded, not authored, so `screens/splash/screen_splash.c` adds one `leImageWidget` onto
333	  `Splash_Panel_0` in code and points it at the in-memory JPEG (solid fill = fallback when there's
334	  no card/image). `ui_manager` re-hosts the splash onto **Legato layer 2 / canvas 2 / OVR2** (32bpp
335	  XRGB8888, full screen, topmost overlay) so it covers the BASE dashboard while the dashboard paints
336	  underneath; dropping OVR2 reveals the finished dashboard.
337	- **Runtime JPEG from SD.** The loader reads `/<card>/ui/splash.jpg` (≤1 MB, **baseline** JPEG —
338	  the decoder is baseline-only) into a static cache-aligned buffer; `Splash_SetImageJpeg` builds a
339	  runtime `leImage` (format `JPEG`, mode `RGB_888`, buffer = compressed bytes + length, mirroring a
340	  generated `leImage`) and sets it on the image widget. Legato's enabled JPEG decoder decodes on
341	  paint into the 32bpp canvas. The compressed buffer stays resident while the splash is shown.
342	- **OVR2 must be set to 32bpp by hand (driver gotcha).** The GFX-XLCDC driver
343	  (`drv_gfx_xlcdc.c`) assumes **every** layer is the project framebuffer format (`FB_COL_MODE` =
344	  RGB565, `FB_TYPE_SZ` = 2): its canvas commit path (`SET_LAYER_UNLOCK`) writes address/alpha/
345	  position/size/stride/enable but **never `RGBMODE`**, so a canvas's `GFX_IOCTL_SET_LAYER_COLOR_MODE`
346	  is captured in `drvLayer.pixelformat` and silently dropped. An RGBA8888 splash buffer therefore
347	  gets read by a still-RGB565 OVR2 → garbled. `ui_manager` fixes this with a direct
348	  `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR2, RGBA_8888, true)` after binding the splash canvas;
349	  the driver never rewrites RGBMODE, so it sticks (same runtime XLCDC poke `video.c` uses for HEO).
350	  BASE/OVR1 stay RGB565 = the default, so they need no poke. Full-screen ⇒ XSTRIDE gap is 0, so the
351	  driver's `FB_TYPE_SZ`-based stride calc is harmless here.
352	- **Backlight gating.** The backlight is a **GPIO** (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN` / PC18), *not* the LCDC
353	  PWM — `XLCDC_EnableBacklight()` only enables the LCDC's `LCD_PWM` dimming output, which isn't
354	  wired to this board's backlight (so calling it does nothing visible). `UiManager_EnableBacklight()`
355	  drives PC18 directly (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set()`, active-high assumed). The pin starts low at
356	  boot (MCC PIO config — the old "set high on start" that made the panel light too early is gone),
357	  so the panel stays dark until the loader calls this after the splash is painted. Video go-live
358	  (`Video_SetWindow`/`CaptureEnable`/`DisplayShow`) also moved into the loader, post-handoff, so the
359	  camera doesn't pop in over the splash.
360	- **Asset:** seed at `data/ui/splash.jpg` (1280×800), copied to the card's `/ui/splash.jpg`
361	  (mirrors the catalog `data/` convention).
362	
363	## 13. Pre-rendered, persistent per-screen canvases (done — code-complete, pending hardware test)
364	
365	Fixes the reveal-before-paint flash (§10): a screen used to be shown while Legato incrementally
366	painted its freshly-rebuilt tree, so unpainted regions flashed uninitialized-DRAM noise (~1–2 s for
367	the Dashboard's ~200-widget tree). The model is now the §1 ideal — **paint into an off-screen
368	surface, then reveal**:
369	
370	- **Every screen is persistent + owns a canvas.** MGS screens are set **persistent** (built once in
371	  `screenInit_*`, never torn down — `screenHide_*` no longer deletes), each re-hosted onto its own
372	  Legato layer → canvas → HW layer: Dashboard 0/0/BASE (RGB565), Nav 1/1/OVR1 (RGB565), Splash
373	  2/2/OVR2 (RGBA8888). `CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ` (8, expandable) gives room per screen; no
374	  `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` multiplexing needed.
375	- **Build pre-scheduler, then let the render task paint; the loader just waits.** All screens are
376	  built + hosted on their layers in `UiManager_Initialize` (pre-scheduler → no concurrency). Once
377	  the scheduler is up, the normal `LEGATO_Tasks` + `GFX_CANVAS_Task` pair paints them — a full-screen
378	  surface spans several scratch tiles (`LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1`, 512 KB ⇒ ~131 072 px @ 32bpp),
379	  and the scratch is freed by the canvas commit *between* render passes, which only happens when
380	  those tasks actually run. So the loader does **not** drive `leUpdate` or touch the scheduler — it
381	  yields and polls the public `leRenderer_IsIdle()`. Important: `leRenderer_IsIdle()` is just
382	  `frameState == LE_FRAME_READY`, which is **also true in the gaps between `leUpdate` calls** (which
383	  tick only every ~10 ms), so a single sample reads "done" mid-paint; `wait_render_idle` requires
384	  idle to hold **continuously for ≥120 ms** before trusting it. Boot sequence: load JPEG (retried —
385	  SDMMC isn't ready this early) → `Splash_SetImageJpeg` → `wait_render_idle`
386	  (splash + dashboard + nav all painted; idle = every layer's frame complete) →
387	  `UiManager_EnableBacklight` (first lit frame = complete splash, dashboard finished behind the OVR2
388	  splash) → *(asset pre-load — none yet)* → min on-screen hold → `UiManager_RevealDashboard`
389	  (hide OVR2 → finished dashboard) → video go-live → self-delete.
390	  - *Earlier mistake (corrected):* the loader first suspended `LEGATO_Tasks` and drove `leUpdate`
391	    itself. That fought the scheduler and was wrong twice over — one `leUpdate(0)` only fills one
392	    scratch tile (the rest bail on the locked scratch), and calling `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` in a tight
393	    loop doesn't free it (the commit completes between real task runs). Letting the normal tasks run
394	    and pending on idle is both correct and simpler.
395	  - **Scratch buffer sized for a full-screen tile.** With the stock 512 KB scratch a full-screen
396	    32bpp surface is ~8 tiles, and a JPEG re-decodes per tile (~8×) → slow. Bumped
397	    `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE_KB` 512 → **4096** (MGS Graphics setting) so `maxScratchPixels` ≈
398	    1.05 M ≥ 1280×800 → one tile = whole screen, one decode, one render pass. Cost: a single 4 MB
399	    nocache scratch (`LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1`, widget buffer disabled) — fits the headroom; also
400	    makes the RGB565 dashboard one pass.
401	- **Open:** the splash stays attached to layer 2 after reveal (just hidden); the future modal dialog
402	  (also OVR2/layer 2) will need to detach it first.
403	
404	## 14. Tap-to-fullscreen live video (`screen_video`)
405	
406	Tap the live video to blow it up to fullscreen; tap again to shrink it back to the
407	windowed rect. The video is on **HEO**, which Legato cannot pick, so the tap is
408	caught on a Legato widget and the interaction is expressed purely as HEO geometry:
409	
410	- **Catch on `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`.** It's the full-screen (1280×800) pickable
411	  layer-0 panel under the IGNOREPICK/IGNOREEVENTS `root0`. Legato **bubbles** a
412	  touch up the parent chain until a widget calls `leWidgetEvent_Accept`
413	  (`legato_input.c`), and plain panels (VIDEO_STREAM, BASE_*) never accept — so a
414	  tap on the video region bubbles up to the dashboard panel. `screen_video`
415	  re-points that panel's `touchDownEvent` (the shared-vtable-copy idiom from
416	  `screen_dashboard.c`'s header tap).
417	- **Windowed → fullscreen:** a tap whose (x,y) is inside the windowed video rect
418	  calls `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,BASE_W,BASE_H)`. The HEO bilinear/bicubic scaler
419	  stretches the source to fill (stretch-to-fit; slight aspect change vs the window).
420	  `base_discard_reconcile` follows the video rect, so BASE DMA is discarded across
421	  the whole panel while fullscreen — a free bandwidth win.
422	- **Fullscreen → windowed:** while fullscreen, `screen_video` gates picking off on
423	  `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP` + `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM` (the two subtrees holding
424	  every interactive dashboard widget) by clearing `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` — flag-only,
425	  no repaint, same gate as `ui_manager`'s `panel_set_pickable`. So **every** tap
426	  then resolves to the dashboard panel and exits fullscreen, restoring the windowed
427	  rect and re-enabling input.
428	- **Windowed state is re-established** by `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`, which
429	  `ui_manager` also calls at reveal and on song-select close, so the video always
430	  returns to a known windowed state.
431	
432	## 15. Active-picture detection + HEO source-crop
433	
434	The Wii's component→HDMI conversion frames the active raster with dead black bars
435	(measured ≈ **716×448 @ (0,15)** in a 720×480 capture — top 15 / bottom 17 / right
436	4 / left 0), and the thickness varies by console/converter, so it's **detected at
437	runtime**, not hardcoded. The bars aren't black=0 — they sit at the same ~13
438	pedestal as in-video black — so detection keys on a **fixed luma threshold**
439	(`max(B,G,R) > 40`, well above the ≤14 border and below the ≥145 content), not on
440	zero.
441	
442	- **Detector lives in `video.c`** (`Video_GetActiveRect`): it owns the frame,
443	  format, and ring, and the capture buffer is in `.region_nocache` so CPU reads
444	  are coherent. It scans inward from each edge (bounded to the deepest border the
445	  ≥700×420 min-size gate allows, so a dark loading frame stays cheap), unions the
446	  bright bounds over 16 *bright* frames (dark frames find no content and are
447	  skipped — a loading screen at capture start just defers the lock), then locks if
448	  the union clears 700×420. One-shot per capture arm; reset on re-arm/source-size
449	  change; **full-frame fallback** (`x=y=0`, `w/h`=full) until locked.
450	- **`ui_manager` `heo_bind` consumes it as the HEO source crop:** offset the frame
451	  base by `y*stride + x*bpp`, size `HEOCFG4` (source memory rect) to the active
452	  w/h, and skip the cropped columns each line via `XSTRIDE=(src_w-active_w)*bpp`
453	  (same formula the GFX driver uses, `FB_TYPE_SZ*(resx-sizex)`). The bicubic
454	  scaler then maps the active rect onto the window/fullscreen dst — the console's
455	  dead bars never reach the panel. `heo_frame_latch` (ISC IRQ) adds the same crop
456	  offset per ring slot; `heo_reconcile` rebinds when the rect changes (detection
457	  flipping full→cropped). Applies to both windowed and fullscreen; bonus: active
458	  716×448 ≈ 1.60 = 1280×800, so fullscreen is essentially aspect-correct.
459	
460	### 15.1 HEO video levels expansion (gamma CLUT)
461	
462	The source is mildly range-compressed against the panel's full 0..255 — measured
463	black cluster ~5 (the dead-border pedestal ~13 is cropped out by §15), white ceiling
464	~233. The HEO **CBHS** limited-range black-level block is **YCbCr-only** (SAM9X7 DS
465	§6.2.6.7), so it can't touch our RGB888 HEO input. The HEO's **per-component gamma
466	CLUT** *does* operate on true RGB (`HEOCFG1.GAM`, four 256-entry LUTs), so `ui_manager`
467	loads it with a linear levels-expansion curve (`out = clamp((in−5)·255/228)`;
468	`VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK/WHITE`) — deepening near-black to true black and lifting whites.
469	
470	- **Display-only:** the DDR capture is untouched, so the detector/gameplay read raw
471	  pixels; the expansion is applied by the LCDC at scanout (zero runtime cost).
472	- **Load timing:** the CLUT (`LCDC_HEOCLUT[256]`) must be written with `GAM`/`CLUTEN`
473	  clear, so it's loaded in `UiManager_Initialize` (post `XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer`, pre any
474	  bind). `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode` rewrites `HEOCFG1` with `GAM(0)` each bind, so
475	  `heo_bind` re-asserts `GAM` after it.
476	- **Fixed curve.** The ~5/233 pedestal/ceiling may vary by Wii/converter — retune the
477	  `VIDEO_LEVELS_*` constants (same per-hardware caveat as §15's detection).
478	
479	## 16. Rounded AA video frame (OVR1 overlay)
480	
481	A 1px rounded frame with anti-aliased corners around the windowed video, matching
482	the dashboard panels (`0x404040` = `SCHEME_PANEL` `LE_SCHM_SHADOWDARK`, radius 6).
483	The video is on HEO (a hard rectangle, not a canvas), so `PanelAA`'s backdrop-blend
484	can't reach it; instead a per-pixel-alpha overlay *above* HEO composites the frame.
485	
486	- **Direct-driven ARGB_4444 layer on OVR1.** The GFX canvas framework has no 4444
487	  mode (`gfxColorMode` = 5551/8888 only), so the frame is a static framebuffer
488	  driven straight through the XLCDC PLIB (splash/HEO-style), not a canvas.
489	  ARGB_4444's 16 alpha levels give smooth AA at half the bandwidth of 8888
490	  (ARGB_1555's 1 alpha bit cannot AA). Register writes live in `ui_manager`
491	  (`UiManager_VideoOverlayShow/Hide`); the buffer + fill live in `screen_video.c`.
492	- **Fill** (once, from a rounded-rect SDF): corner-cut = opaque black (the dashboard
493	  backdrop, so the video's square corners read as rounded), a 1px stroke, and a
494	  transparent interior (video shows through). Alpha AA on the stroke→video edge is
495	  what smooths the corner. `alpha = 1 − innerCoverage`; opaque colour = stroke
496	  scaled by its share of the opaque part (remainder is the black cut).
497	- **Nav moved OVR1 → OVR2** so the drawer sits above the frame and covers its left
498	  edge when open (z-order `OVR2 > OVR1 > HEO > BASE`). Nav binds via
499	  `UiManager_ShowNavLayer` (`bind_canvas` → RGB565, re-poked each open because
500	  album-art leaves OVR2 in RGBA8888).
501	- **Lifecycle = windowed video visible:** shown by `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed`,
502	  hidden on fullscreen enter (edge-to-edge) and song-select open (video hidden).
503	- **Bandwidth:** an always-on full-rect OVR1 read while windowed (~720×480
504	  ARGB_4444 ≈ 41 MB/s) on top of BASE+HEO — watch for CSI-2 D-PHY capture stalls.
505	
506	### 16.1 Future: per-frame gameplay overlay on this layer
507	
508	This OVR1 overlay (above HEO, aligned to the video window) is also the natural home
509	for a **frame-by-frame gameplay HUD** drawn over the live video — note-highway
510	markers, hit/miss annotations, detected-note boxes, timing cues, etc. It would
511	compose with (or replace) the static frame in the same surface.
512	
513	Design implications when we build it:
514	- **Direct buffer draw, no Legato.** Same as the frame: the canvas framework can't
515	  own this layer (no ARGB_4444 mode, and per-frame Legato repaint is too heavy), so
516	  the HUD is rasterised straight into the overlay framebuffer (CPU and/or the GFX2D
517	  engine) and the LCDC composites it. Must be **fast / minimal overhead** — it runs
518	  every gameplay tick, so favour incremental redraw (clear+draw only changed
519	  regions) over full-surface clears.
520	- **Double-buffer to avoid tearing.** The static frame is written once so a single
521	  buffer is fine; a per-frame HUD redrawn while the LCDC scans it would tear. Use
522	  two overlay buffers and flip the layer base address at vsync (mirrors the HEO
523	  ring / `heo_frame_latch` non-blocking address update).
524	- **Format.** ARGB_4444 keeps bandwidth down and is enough for solid markers/AA
525	  edges; bump to ARGB_8888 only if the HUD needs finer gradients.
526	- **Geometry.** Overlay coords map 1:1 to the *displayed* video window; if the HUD
527	  is derived from source-pixel positions, apply the active-area crop + scale
528	  (§15) to place markers correctly on the scaled video.
529	
530	## 11. Relationship to spec §4.5 / Q5
531	
532	This answers spec **Q5** (Legato vs. custom UI) for the *presentation* layer: **Legato is the
533	renderer; a marvin `ui_manager` over GFX Canvas owns surface/layer composition and screen
534	orchestration.** Per-screen *authoring* stays in MGS (one Screen per panel); the compositor
535	assembles their trees onto hardware layers.
536
```

1	# GH3 (Wii) — Navigation Model
2	
3	Working model of Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock (Wii) screens and the menu
4	graph between them. This is the source artifact for the §4.8 game-state work:
5	the **observer** (M9) classifies the current screen and reads the highlighted
6	selection; the **controller** (M10) plans button sequences along the graph
7	edges below. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.8.3 (game catalog & menu metadata).
8	
9	Screen text is transcribed from operator narration; the referenced screens live
10	as a renamed corpus in [`gh3_screens/`](gh3_screens/) (see its README for the
11	name ↔ original-snapshot mapping). Raw `marvin-perf snapshot` captures land in
12	the gitignored `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/`. Native capture is 720×480.
13	
14	**Scope now:** the navigation *structure* — screens, their items, and the edges
15	between them. The **vision** side (per-screen classifier regions, highlight
16	readout) is deferred until the observer (M9) is built; screen snapshots are
17	recorded here now so that work has its corpus ready.
18	
19	Status: **in progress** — populated screen-by-screen. `TBD` = not yet captured.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Conventions
24	
25	### Inputs
26	- **Strum up / strum down** — move the selection within a list.
27	- **GREEN** — confirm / enter the selected item.
28	- **RED** — back up one level.
29	
30	(Bit names on the wire are the gameplay fret/strum masks; the controller emits
31	the same bits for menu navigation — the fretboard MCU doesn't distinguish menu
32	from gameplay. §4.8.4.) Some menus also use the `+` button (pause) and possibly
33	others beyond fret/strum; the full controller is actuatable in principle —
34	fauxmote emulates the complete guitar extension incl. `+`/`−` — the actuator
35	command protocol just needs to carry those inputs.
36	
37	### Highlight paradigms
38	How "selected" is presented drives what the observer reads. Two kinds so far:
39	
40	- **static-list** — the list is painted at fixed screen positions; a highlight
41	  moves between rows. Observer reads *which row is lit*. (e.g. `main_menu`)
42	- **fixed-slot** — the selected item sits in a fixed, highlighted slot and the
43	  list scrolls underneath it. Observer reads *what occupies the highlight slot*.
44	  (e.g. `song_select`)
45	
46	### Edge notation
47	An edge is `from → to : [inputs]`. `STRUM_DN×n` means n strum-downs. Moving to
48	list index `i` from the top (index 0) on a static list is `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN`.
49

340	## Menu graph (edges)
341	
342	| from | to | inputs | notes |
343	|------|----|--------|-------|
344	| main_menu | _(per item)_ | `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` | static list, index per catalog above |
345	| main_menu | training_menu | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | TRAINING (index 4) |
346	| training_menu | song_select | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | PRACTICE (index 1) |
347	| song_select | part_select | `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` | song at list index i; shared node. May skip part_select for some songs |
348	| song_select | bonus list | `BLUE` (back: `YELLOW`) | toggles the song list, not a screen change |
349	| part_select | difficulty_select | LEAD `GREEN` / 2nd `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | items song-dependent |
350	| difficulty_select | section_select | `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` | EASY 0 / MEDIUM 1 / HARD 2 / EXPERT 3 |
351	| section_select | speed_select | `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` | FULL SONG = top (idx 0); strum up to saturate |
352	| speed_select | loading | `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` | FULL SPEED = top (idx 0); strum up to saturate |
353	| loading | in_song | _(none — wait)_ | transient; auto-advances |
354	| in_song | pause_menu | `+` (guitar plus) | not a fret/strum bit — see caveat |
355	| in_song | practice_end_menu | _(none — song ends)_ | gameplay completes |
356	| pause_menu | in_song | `GREEN` | RESUME (idx 0) |
357	| pause_menu | loading | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | RESTART (idx 1) → replay |
358	| pause_menu | speed_select | `STRUM_DN×3, GREEN` | CHANGE SPEED (idx 3) |
359	| pause_menu | section_select | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | CHANGE SECTION (idx 4) |
360	| pause_menu | song_select | `STRUM_DN×5, GREEN` | NEW SONG (idx 5) |
361	| pause_menu | quit_confirm | `STRUM_DN×6, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 6) → confirm dialog |
362	| quit_confirm | pause_menu | `GREEN` | CANCEL (idx 0) |
363	| quit_confirm | main_menu | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 1) — confirm |
364	| practice_end_menu | song_select | `GREEN` | CONTINUE (idx 0) |
365	| practice_end_menu | loading | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | RESTART (idx 1) → replay |
366	| practice_end_menu | speed_select | `STRUM_DN×2, GREEN` | CHANGE SPEED (idx 2) |
367	| practice_end_menu | section_select | `STRUM_DN×3, GREEN` | CHANGE SECTION (idx 3) |
368	| practice_end_menu | main_menu | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 4) |
369	| _any_ | _(parent)_ | `RED` | back up one level |
370	
371	_(filled in as destinations are confirmed)_

373	---
374	
375	## Navigator notes (implementation)
376	
377	> **Implemented (2026-07-02):** the on-device controller is
378	> `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/game_controller.c` — a port of the offline
379	> `tools/gameplay` `NavController`. Triggered by the dashboard START button or the
380	> console `play` command; reads the committed `Selection`; drives the worked path
381	> below closed-loop and hands off to the CV detector at `in_song`. v1 covers the
382	> practice path from a menu anchor (RED→`main_menu`); mid-song `+`/pause recovery is
383	> not wired (the T1S mask path carries no `+`). See the marvin journal 2026-07-02.
384	
385	How the controller (M10) uses this map. Unmapped paths don't need modeling —
386	they're handled by recovery, not enumeration.
387	
388	- **Closed-loop — verify every screen (not a blind macro).** Before issuing a
389	  step's inputs, confirm the observer reports the expected screen; after issuing
390	  them, confirm the expected destination before proceeding. On mismatch, recover
391	  (see below) and re-plan. Never fire a button sequence open-loop and *assume* we
392	  landed where we hoped — drift, sticky defaults, variable/absent screens, and
393	  load times all break that. This is why the observer (M9) gates the controller
394	  (M10). (spec §4.8.1.)
395	- **Stubs / unknown destinations.** Edges marked `TBD` simply have no plan; the
396	  navigator never routes through them. Out-of-scope nodes (`tutorials_menu`) and
397	  any screen the observer doesn't recognize are treated as "unknown state."
398	- **Recovery from unknown state.** RED backs up one level from any menu, so the
399	  generic recovery is *"press RED until a recognized screen appears, then
400	  re-plan."* This gets us un-stuck from a wrong branch without mapping it.
401	- **Top-item selection (`STRUM_UP×N`).** For steps where we always want the top
402	  item (FULL SONG, FULL SPEED), strum up to saturate at the top, then GREEN,
403	  rather than trusting the entry highlight. (Depends on no wrap-around — open.)
404	
405	### Worked path — training run (main-setlist song `i`, difficulty `d`, LEAD)
406	The nominal input plan. Each step runs **gated on a screen check** (verify the
407	expected screen before, confirm arrival after) per the closed-loop rule above —
408	it is not executed as one blind burst. From `main_menu` (if not there, recover
409	with RED first):
410	
411	1. `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` → TRAINING → `training_menu`
412	2. `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` → PRACTICE → `song_select`
413	3. `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` → song at catalog index `i` (Song catalog) → `part_select`
414	4. select LEAD, then GREEN → `difficulty_select`  *(see caveat)*
415	5. `STRUM_DN×d, GREEN` → difficulty `d` (EASY 0 … EXPERT 3) → `section_select`
416	6. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SONG → `speed_select`
417	7. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SPEED → `loading` (wait) → `in_song` (gameplay)
418	
419	**Caveat (step 4):** `part_select` items vary per song and the screen may be
420	absent — exactly the case the closed-loop rule handles: after step 3's GREEN,
421	check which screen actually appeared. If it's `part_select`, pick LEAD (read the
422	offered items) and GREEN; if it's already `difficulty_select`, skip step 4. A
423	purely open-loop macro can't do this safely (extra inputs would mis-fire), so
424	until the observer exists, restrict to songs known to show LEAD-at-top. Per-song
425	`parts` metadata lets the planner pre-know the layout either way.
426

```text
1	# marvin boot binaries — what they are and how to (re)build them
2	
3	at91bootstrap is marvin's first-stage boot: RomBOOT loads it, it brings up the
4	266 MHz clocks + the in-package DDR3L (Winbond `W632GU6NB12I`), then either hands
5	off to the application or — for the JTAG dev loop — stops and waits.
6	
7	All bootstraps here are built from at91bootstrap **v4.0.13** source (recipes
8	below), so their provenance is known.
9	
10	| File | Medium / use | Built from defconfig |
11	|------|--------------|----------------------|
12	| `sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf` | **JTAG load-to-RAM** (init-and-stop). Used by `../openocd/load-ram.sh`. | `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone` |
13	| `sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin` | **NAND** boot (SAM-BA `writeboot`) | `sam9x75_curiosity_pronf_uboot` |
14	| `sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin` | **NAND** boot via the macOS u-boot/JTAG path (`../openocd/program-nand.sh`) | as above + PMECC header prepended (`make-pmecchead.sh`) |
15	| `sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin` | **NAND flasher**, RAM-loaded over JTAG by `../openocd/program-nand.sh` (drives `nand erase`/`nand write`; not itself flashed to the board) | u-boot `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash` (recipe below) |
16	| `sam9x7-dataflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin` | **QSPI** boot (SAM-BA `writeboot`) | `sam9x75_curiosity_prodf_qspi_uboot` |
17	| `sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin` | **microSD** boot (copied to FAT as `boot.bin`) | `sam9x75_curiosity_prosd_uboot` + `IMAGE_NAME=harmony.bin` |
18	| `make-pmecchead.sh` | Prepend the SAM9X7 ROM PMECC header to a NAND bootstrap (so a plain `nand write` is RomBOOT-bootable; SAM-BA's `writeboot` does this itself) | — |
19	| `nand_flash.bat`, `qspi_flash.bat` | SAM-BA flashing scripts (Linux/Windows host) | — |
20	
21	The media bootstraps all jump to **`0x23F00000`** (`CONFIG_JUMP_ADDR`) — exactly
22	where marvin links and runs — so marvin (`out/harmony.bin`) is the second stage.
23	
24	## Boot order (SAM9X75 ROM)
25	
26	The ROM tries NVM in a fixed sequential fall-through (first valid image wins);
27	order is customizable only via the OTP Boot Configuration Packet:
28	
29	> **SD/eMMC (SDMMC0) → SD/eMMC (SDMMC1) → QSPI → NAND (SMC) → SPI (FLEXCOM5)**
30	
31	So **SD outranks NAND, and QSPI sits between them.** Useful consequences:
32	- NAND = resident firmware; **SD = override/recovery** (a valid card boots first,
33	  no jumper change; remove it to fall back to NAND).
34	- For NAND to boot, **QSPI must hold no valid image** (erase it or keep JP4/QSPI-CS
35	  out) — otherwise QSPI boots before NAND.
36	- For the JTAG dev loop we pull JP3 (NAND) + JP4 (QSPI) and use no card, so the
37	  ROM falls all the way through to the SAM-BA monitor.
38	
39	## Board ↔ defconfig
40	
41	The **SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid (cHybrid)** maps to the at91bootstrap
42	**`sam9x75_curiosity_pro_*`** defconfigs (confirmed by the on-board red LED on
43	PIOC 14 — `curiosity_pro` uses PC14, plain `curiosity` uses PC19; DDR is identical
44	across both). All variants here use the in-package `W632GU6NB12I` DDR3L.
45	
46	## Marvin customization: blue LED channel → PC18, output low
47	
48	at91bootstrap's only LED action is a one-shot `at91_leds_init()` in `hw_init()`
49	(`driver/led.c`): it drives up to three Kconfig-defined pins (R/G/B) to fixed
50	levels and never touches them again. The blue channel carries no status meaning,
51	so we **repurpose it to hold PC18 low at boot** — a generic "init this pin output
52	low" with no source edits. (`pio_set_gpio_output(pin, 0)` = output enable, pull-up
53	off, drive low.) Stock blue is PC20; our binaries move it to **PC18, value 0**,
54	leaving red (PC14) and green (PC21) as-is.
55	
56	This is applied at build time so the at91bootstrap clone stays vanilla. After
57	`make <defconfig>` and **before** the final `make`, run:
58	
59	```sh
60	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=18|' .config      # macOS sed
61	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=0|' .config
62	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- oldconfig </dev/null               # see note
63	```
64	
65	> **The `oldconfig` step is mandatory.** `CONFIG_LED_B_PIN` reaches the code via
66	> the generated C header `config/at91bootstrap-config/autoconf.h`, and a plain
67	> `make` does **not** regenerate that header after a hand-edit of `.config` — only
68	> a kconfig target (`oldconfig`) does. Skip it and the build silently keeps PC20.
69	> (Contrast `CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME` below, which the Makefile reads from `.config`
70	> directly as a `-D` flag, so it needs no `oldconfig`.) Verify with:
71	> `arm-none-eabi-objdump -d <elf> | grep -A8 at91_leds_init` — the blue call
72	> should load `r0, #82` (0x52 = PIOC·32+18) with `r1, #0`.
73	
74	## Marvin customization: app copy window (`CONFIG_IMG_SIZE`) → 4 MiB
75	
76	The **raw-offset** media bootstraps (NAND, QSPI) copy a fixed `CONFIG_IMG_SIZE`
77	bytes from `CONFIG_IMG_ADDRESS` (`0x40000`) to `0x23F00000` and jump — there is no
78	size header, so the window is a compile-time constant. Stock is `0x100000` (1 MiB,
79	sized for u-boot); marvin (`harmony.bin`) has outgrown that, so we build these
80	with **`CONFIG_IMG_SIZE=0x00400000`** (4 MiB) — enough headroom for marvin to keep
81	growing. Reading past the app into erased pages is safe (at91bootstrap detects
82	all-`0xff` pages), it just costs a little boot-time NAND read. The SD bootstrap has
83	no `CONFIG_IMG_SIZE` (it loads the whole file by name from FAT), so it is immune.
84	
85	This window is **coupled** to two things that must stay consistent:
86	- **`../openocd/program-nand.sh` `NAND_IMG_SIZE`** — a guard that refuses to flash a
87	  `harmony.bin` larger than the window (which would boot truncated). Bump it to
88	  match if you rebuild with a different `CONFIG_IMG_SIZE`.
89	- **The flasher chip-erases** (`../openocd/nand_console.py`, program mode) so every
90	  page in the copy window is clean `0xff` before the write — otherwise the
91	  bootstrap's read of that window hits stale/half-written pages and PMECC fails.
92	
93	Like the LED override, it's applied to `.config` after `make <defconfig>` (it is a
94	`-D` flag so it needs no `oldconfig`, but the LED override's `oldconfig` covers it):
95	
96	```sh
97	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_IMG_SIZE=.*|CONFIG_IMG_SIZE="0x00400000"|' .config   # macOS sed
98	```
99	
100	## Prerequisites
101	
102	- **at91bootstrap source** (this was built from `v4.0.13`):
103	  ```sh
104	  git clone https://github.com/linux4sam/at91bootstrap
105	  # in-use clone for this project: ~/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap
106	  ```
107	- **ARM bare-metal toolchain** — Arm GNU Toolchain (this build used 15.2.Rel1).
108	  It is installed but not on `PATH`; add its `bin` dir:
109	  ```sh
110	  export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
111	  ```
112	  (Any `arm-none-eabi-` cross-gcc works; XC32 is *not* used for at91bootstrap.)
113	
114	## Build the JTAG load-to-RAM bootstrap (`sam9x7-boot-none-*.elf`)
115	
116	This is the `bkptnone` defconfig — `CONFIG_INIT_AND_STOP=y`: it inits clocks + DDR
117	and then **loops**, leaving MMU/caches off, so a debugger can load a binary into
118	the freshly-initialized DDR. (It does *not* issue a `bkpt`, so it is harmless with
119	no debugger attached.)
120	
121	```sh
122	cd ~/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap
123	export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
124	
125	make mrproper
126	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone_defconfig
127	# blue LED channel -> PC18, output low (see "Marvin customization" above)
128	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=18|' .config
129	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=0|' .config
130	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- oldconfig </dev/null
131	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
132	```
133	
134	Output lands in `build/binaries/`:
135	
136	```
137	build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf   <- copy this here
138	build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.bin   (raw image; not needed for JTAG load)
139	build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.map
140	```
141	
142	Copy the ELF into this folder (the `.elf` is what `load_image` consumes; it
143	carries the entry point, `0x300000`):
144	
145	```sh
146	cp build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf \
147	   <repo>/firmware/marvin/binaries/
148	```
149	
150	If the version string in the filename changes (newer at91bootstrap), update the
151	`BOOTSTRAP_ELF` default in `../openocd/load-ram.sh` to match.
152	
153	The `..._bkptnone_defconfig` contents (for reference):
154	
155	```
156	CONFIG_INIT_AND_STOP=y
157	CONFIG_SAM9X7=y
158	CONFIG_DDR_SET_BY_DEVICE=y
159	CONFIG_DDR_W632GU6NB12I=y
160	CONFIG_BOARD_QUIRK_SAM9X75_CURIOSITY=y
161	CONFIG_LED_*    # red PC14, green PC21, blue PC20 (curiosity_pro);
162	                # we override blue -> PC18 value 0 at build time (see above)
163	```
164	
165	## Build the production (standalone-boot) bootstraps
166	
167	These configs are named `*_uboot_*` by convention but are **not** u-boot-specific
168	— they load the next-stage binary from flash into DRAM (`0x23F00000`) and jump.
169	No actual u-boot / Linux is involved; marvin (`harmony.bin`) is the second stage.
170	
171	- **NAND / QSPI** load the app from a **raw flash offset** (`CONFIG_IMG_ADDRESS`,
172	  `0x40000`) — the filename is irrelevant on-device, so these keep their stock
173	  `-uboot-` build-name suffix.
174	- **SD** loads the app from **FAT by filename** (`CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME`). The stock
175	  default is `u-boot.bin`; we override it to **`harmony.bin`** (the Harmony MPU
176	  convention, and consistent with the NAND/QSPI host files). at91bootstrap then
177	  auto-names the output `...-sdcardboot-harmony-...`.
178	
179	```sh
180	cd ~/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap
181	export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
182	
183	# Each build inserts the marvin overrides (see "Marvin customization" above)
184	# between `make <defconfig>` and the final `make`: blue-LED -> PC18, and the app
185	# copy window -> 4 MiB. IMG_SIZE only exists in the raw-offset (NAND/QSPI) configs,
186	# so its sed is a harmless no-op on the SD build (which loads by filename).
187	marvin_cfg() {   # run from the at91bootstrap dir, after `make <defconfig>`
188	  sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=18|' .config
189	  sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=0|' .config
190	  sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_IMG_SIZE=.*|CONFIG_IMG_SIZE="0x00400000"|' .config
191	  make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- oldconfig </dev/null
192	}
193	
194	# NAND  (raw offset; filename unused)
195	make mrproper && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pronf_uboot_defconfig
196	marvin_cfg && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
197	# QSPI  (raw offset; filename unused)
198	make mrproper && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_prodf_qspi_uboot_defconfig
199	marvin_cfg && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
200	# microSD — override the FAT second-stage filename to harmony.bin
201	make mrproper && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_prosd_uboot_defconfig
202	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME=.*|CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME="harmony.bin"|' .config   # macOS sed
203	marvin_cfg && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
204	# artifacts: build/binaries/sam9x7-{nandflashboot,dataflashboot}-uboot-4.0.13.bin
205	#            build/binaries/sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin
206	# (mrproper wipes build/, so copy each .bin out before the next build.)
207	```
208	
209	### Flashing
210	
211	- **NAND (macOS, no SAM-BA)** — `../openocd/program-nand.sh` RAM-loads the u-boot
212	  flasher over JTAG and `nand write`s the boot region + marvin. The boot region
213	  uses the PMECC-headed bootstrap (`*-pmecchead.bin`); see
214	  `../openocd/program-nand.md`. **Validated** booting marvin standalone from NAND.
215	- **NAND / QSPI (Linux/Windows)** — SAM-BA. See `nand_flash.bat` / `qspi_flash.bat`:
216	  bootstrap via `writeboot`, marvin via `write harmony.bin:0x40000`. (SAM-BA's
217	  `nandflash` applet writes the PMECC/boot header the ROM expects — the same header
218	  `make-pmecchead.sh` prepends for the macOS path.)
219	- **microSD** — `../openocd/make-sdcard.sh` on macOS. It writes the SD bootstrap as
220	  `boot.bin` (what the ROM looks for) and marvin as **`harmony.bin`** (the SD
221	  bootstrap's `CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME`).
222	
223	> **QSPI over JTAG from macOS** is still open R&D — OpenOCD has no SAM9X7 QSPI
224	> driver and the u-boot QSPI-boot flasher path isn't wired up here (u-boot's `sf`
225	> could drive it; check whether QSPI boot needs an analogous header). BOSSA is
226	> **not** applicable (it programs Cortex-M on-chip flash over the SAM-BA protocol,
227	> not SAM9 external NVM, and not over JTAG).
228	
229	## Build the NAND flasher u-boot (`sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-*.bin`)
230	
231	This is **not** a boot stage — it's u-boot RAM-loaded over JTAG to drive NAND (see
232	`../openocd/program-nand.md`). Source: the linux4microchip u-boot fork,
233	<https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp> (branch `linux4microchip-2026.04`,
234	v2025.07 base), built with `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig`. Any
235	`arm-none-eabi-` cross toolchain works. macOS specifics: use Homebrew `gmake`
236	(stock make 3.81 can't parse u-boot's Makefile) and pass OpenSSL via the
237	**environment** (command-line `HOST_EXTRACFLAGS` clobbers the bundled-dtc include
238	path); adjust the OpenSSL prefix for your host.
239	
240	```sh
241	git clone -b linux4microchip-2026.04 https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp.git
242	cd u-boot-mchp
243	# ensure an arm-none-eabi- cross-gcc is on PATH (e.g. the Arm GNU Toolchain)
244	export HOST_EXTRACFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"   # macOS host-tool deps
245	export HOSTLDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
246	gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig
247	gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- -j8
248	cp u-boot.bin <repo>/firmware/marvin/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin
249	```
250
```

```text
1	# SAM9X75 cHybrid — JTAG debug with OpenOCD
2	
3	Debug the SAM9X75 (ARM926EJ-S) over JTAG using the board's onboard **FTDI
4	FT4232H**, whose **channel A** is wired to the JTAG bus (TCK/TDI/TDO/TMS on
5	ADBUS0–3). No special FTDI driver is required.
6	
7	> The FT4232H also has a configuration EEPROM; tooling to program board
8	> identity/serials lives in [`../ftdi/`](../ftdi/). It's independent of this
9	> debug config, but the serial numbers it writes are what `FTDI_SERIAL` (below)
10	> selects on.
11	
12	## Prerequisites
13	
14	```sh
15	# macOS (Homebrew)
16	brew install openocd libftdi libusb
17	
18	# Debian/Ubuntu
19	sudo apt install openocd libftdi1-2 libusb-1.0-0
20	```
21	
22	On macOS the built-in `AppleUSBFTDI` driver creates `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` nodes
23	for the FT4232H channels — that is normal and does **not** interfere; libusb
24	still claims channel A for JTAG. Just don't open the channel-A serial node in a
25	terminal while debugging.
26	
27	## Files
28	
29	| File | Purpose |
30	|------|---------|
31	| `sam9x75-chybrid.cfg` | OpenOCD config: FTDI channel A + ARM926EJ-S target + reset/WDT |
32	| `load-ram.cfg` | OpenOCD proc that loads marvin into DDR via at91bootstrap (`marvin_load_ram`) |
33	| `load-ram.sh` | Load + run marvin over JTAG — the dev loop, repeatable with no power-cycle |
34	| `make-sdcard.sh` | Prepare a bootable microSD on macOS (standalone boot, no JTAG) |
35	| `program-nand.{sh,cfg}` | Program marvin into on-board NAND from macOS (u-boot RAM-loaded over JTAG as a PMECC flasher) — see `program-nand.md` |
36	| `erase-nand.{sh,cfg}` | Erase NAND over JTAG to make the board non-bootable — return to RAM dev without touching jumpers (e.g. board in an enclosure) |
37	| `nand_console.py` | Shared u-boot-console driver (pre-flight port check, erase, program+verify) used by `program-nand.sh` / `erase-nand.sh` |
38	
39	## Usage
40	
41	```sh
42	openocd -f sam9x75-chybrid.cfg
43	```
44	
45	Expected output (gdb server on port 3333):
46	
47	```
48	Info : JTAG tap: sam9x75.cpu tap/device found: 0x0792603f (mfg: 0x01f (Atmel), part: 0x7926, ver: 0x0)
49	Info : Embedded ICE version 6
50	Info : sam9x75.cpu: hardware has 2 breakpoint/watchpoint units
51	Info : starting gdb server for sam9x75.cpu on 3333
52	Info : Listening on port 3333 for gdb connections
53	```
54	
55	Attach a debugger:
56	
57	```sh
58	arm-none-eabi-gdb -ex 'target remote :3333'
59	```
60	
61	`reset`, `reset halt`, and `reset init` reset the SoC over the nRST line (AD5) —
62	including a *running* marvin — and `reset init` additionally disables the watchdog
63	and MMU/caches. This relies on driving nSRST push-pull (`-data`/`-oe`) with a
64	500 ms pulse and `srst_pulls_trst`; a too-short pulse or `-oe`-only definition
65	does **not** actually reset the chip. (Config follows the Microchip class-material
66	example for this board.)
67	
68	A `Warn : libusb_detach_kernel_driver() failed with LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS` line on
69	macOS is harmless — OpenOCD claims the interface anyway.
70	
71	## Load marvin into RAM over JTAG (no SD card)
72	
73	`load-ram.sh` boots marvin entirely over JTAG — no microSD required. It reuses a
74	purpose-built **"init-and-stop" at91bootstrap**
75	(`../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf`, built from the
76	`sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone_defconfig` — `CONFIG_INIT_AND_STOP`) to bring up
77	the 266 MHz clocks and initialize the in-package DDR3L, then loads marvin's ELF
78	into DDR and jumps to it. (Reusing at91bootstrap avoids re-implementing the
79	SAM9X75D2G DDR3L init by hand — see `load-ram.cfg` and the journal.) To rebuild
80	the bootstrap from source, see [`../binaries/README.md`](../binaries/README.md).
81	
82	```sh
83	./load-ram.sh                            # ../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf + ../out/marvin/default.elf
84	FTDI_SERIAL=W16-2026-413 ./load-ram.sh   # target a specific board
85	```
86	
87	It is **repeatable with no physical power-cycle** — edit, rebuild, re-run:
88	
89	```sh
90	./load-ram.sh        # reset init → at91bootstrap (DDR) → load + run marvin
91	# ... edit, rebuild marvin ...
92	./load-ram.sh        # again, from the running marvin — no power-cycle
93	```
94	
95	**Prerequisites:**
96	
97	1. **No bootable medium present:** both memory CS jumpers OUT (JP3 = NAND,
98	   JP4 = QSPI) **and remove any bootable microSD.** A present medium boots before
99	   `reset init`'s early-halt can catch the core (SD is highest boot priority), and
100	   the load then fails on the dirty state. With nothing bootable, RomBOOT sits in
101	   the SAM-BA monitor.
102	2. Nothing else may hold the FT4232H — kill any debug OpenOCD server first.
103	
104	Mechanism (`marvin_load_ram`, also the by-hand recipe):
105	
106	`reset init` (resets the SoC from any state via the 500 ms nSRST pulse, then
107	disables the watchdog + MMU/caches) → `adapter speed 0` (RTCK adaptive clocking —
108	**required**; at fixed TCK, OpenOCD loses JTAG sync when at91bootstrap switches
109	the master clock) → load the init-and-stop at91bootstrap → resume → brief wait →
110	halt (clocks + DDR now up, MMU/caches off; the bootstrap just loops) → load
111	marvin → resume at `0x23f00000`. An I-cache invalidate (`arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0`)
112	follows each `load_image`. The reset re-initializes the MPDDRC, so the bootstrap
113	brings DDR3L up fresh each run — that is what makes the loop repeatable without a
114	power-cycle. (An `INIT_AND_STOP` bootstrap halts itself after DDR init, so no
115	breakpoint or disassembly is needed.)
116	
117	**Headless note:** with no display/maXTouch panel connected, marvin's maXTouch
118	driver init fails gracefully (driver → ERROR) and the rest of the system runs.
119	This relies on the bounded-retry fix in `drv_maxtouch.c` (journal re-apply patch
120	#10) — without it, an absent panel hangs the system at the FreeRTOS malloc-fail
121	hook.
122	
123	## Debugging in VS Code (or gdb CLI)
124	
125	`arm-none-eabi-gdb` (Arm GNU Toolchain) attaches to OpenOCD's gdb server on
126	`:3333`. marvin is **loaded** by `load-ram.sh`; the debugger only **attaches** (it
127	does not reflash), so the loop is: *load → attach → debug*.
128	
129	**VS Code** — `.vscode/launch.json` + `.vscode/tasks.json` (repo root) provide:
130	
131	- a background task `openocd: sam9x75 gdb server` that starts the server, and
132	- two attach configs (pick whichever extension you have installed):
133	  - **marvin: attach over JTAG (cppdbg)** — Microsoft C/C++ (`ms-vscode.cpptools`)
134	  - **marvin: attach over JTAG (Native Debug)** — `webfreak.debug`
135	
136	Both auto-start the server (`preLaunchTask`), attach, load symbols from
137	`out/marvin/default.elf`, and stop the server on exit (`postDebugTask`). Set a
138	breakpoint, run the config, and step/inspect. (cortex-debug is Cortex-M-centric
139	and is intentionally not used for this ARM926 target.)
140	
141	**gdb CLI** equivalent:
142	
143	```sh
144	openocd -f sam9x75-chybrid.cfg &                       # gdb server on :3333
145	arm-none-eabi-gdb firmware/marvin/out/marvin/default.elf \
146	    -ex 'set architecture arm' -ex 'target remote :3333'
147	```
148	
149	## Bootable microSD (standalone, no JTAG) — `make-sdcard.sh`
150	
151	For a board that boots on its own (no debugger), `make-sdcard.sh` prepares a card
152	on macOS: it FAT-formats the card and writes the SD bootstrap
153	(`../binaries/sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin`) as **`boot.bin`** (what the
154	ROM looks for) and marvin (`../out/harmony.bin`) as **`harmony.bin`** (the
155	bootstrap's `CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME`) — the layout the SAM9X75 ROM SD-boot path expects.
156	
157	```sh
158	diskutil list                  # find the card, e.g. /dev/disk4
159	./make-sdcard.sh /dev/disk4    # ERASES the card (asks you to confirm the id)
160	```
161	
162	It refuses a fixed internal disk and requires you to retype the disk identifier
163	before erasing. Then insert the card and power-cycle. SD is the highest-priority
164	boot source (see `../binaries/README.md`), so a valid card boots ahead of
165	NAND/QSPI — no jumper change needed. **Validated:** boots marvin standalone from
166	SD on this board (DBGU banner, no JTAG).
167	
168	## Program / erase on-board NAND from macOS — `program-nand.sh` / `erase-nand.sh`
169	
170	`program-nand.sh` writes marvin into NAND so the board boots standalone (full
171	runbook in [`program-nand.md`](program-nand.md)). `erase-nand.sh` is the inverse:
172	it erases NAND over JTAG, which matters once marvin is resident.
173	
174	**Returning to RAM dev with no jumper access (e.g. enclosure).** `load-ram.sh`
175	requires no valid boot medium so `reset init` can catch the core. With marvin in
176	NAND and JP3 (NAND-CS) unreachable, the ROM boots NAND on every power-on and the
177	RAM loop is unreliable. `erase-nand.sh` removes the boot image — the ROM then
178	falls through to the SAM-BA monitor and `load-ram.sh` works again, no jumper
179	change:
180	
181	```sh
182	./erase-nand.sh          # erase boot+app region (0x0..0x100000)
183	./erase-nand.sh chip     # full-chip erase
184	./load-ram.sh            # back to the RAM dev loop
185	```
186	
187	Both are one-shot and fully automated: they RAM-load u-boot over JTAG and drive its
188	`atmel_nand` driver from the DBGU console (`nand_console.py`), erasing/writing and
189	verifying with no manual console steps. Each **pre-flight checks the console port
190	is free** and bails with a clear error if it's held elsewhere (screen/minicom)
191	*before* touching the board. They need OpenOCD + `uv` (for `pyserial`) and must run
192	outside the Claude command sandbox (libusb USB access). Override the DBGU node with
193	`CONSOLE=/dev/cu.usbserial-...` (auto-detected as the 3rd `cu.usbserial-*` = channel
194	C otherwise).
195	
196	**Reflashing a board that already boots marvin from NAND** (e.g. in an enclosure):
197	erase first — `./erase-nand.sh && ./program-nand.sh`. `program-nand.sh` stages
198	firmware into low DDR, which a *running* marvin's capture DMA can corrupt, so it
199	refuses if it catches the core booting from NAND. `erase-nand.sh` is the robust one
200	(it recovers a booting/wedged board: `reset init`, then forces MMU/caches off so
201	the load isn't under marvin's page tables); once NAND is erased the board is
202	non-bootable and `program-nand.sh` runs its clean ROM-monitor path.
203	
204	## Selecting a specific board
205	
206	When several boards are connected at once, pick one by its FT4232H serial
207	(requires the EEPROM to have been flashed — see [`../ftdi/`](../ftdi/)):
208	
209	```sh
210	openocd -c "set FTDI_SERIAL W16-2026-413" -f sam9x75-chybrid.cfg
211	```
212	
213	Leave `FTDI_SERIAL` unset to use the first FT4232H found.
214	
215	## Channel A reset / clock pinout
216	
217	| Signal | FT4232H pin | Notes |
218	|--------|-------------|-------|
219	| nSRST  | AD5 | system reset, push-pull `-data 0x20 -oe 0x20`; 500 ms pulse; `srst_pulls_trst` |
220	| RTCK   | AD7 | return clock; enables adaptive clocking via `adapter speed 0` |
221	| nTRST  | — | AD4 is N/C on this board; not defined (TAP re-validates via `srst_pulls_trst`) |
222	
223	## Scope / limitations
224	
225	This supports **attach, halt, resume, memory/register access, reset**
226	(`reset` / `reset halt` / `reset init` — resets a running marvin; `reset init`
227	also disables the watchdog + MMU/caches), **adaptive clocking** (`adapter speed 0`,
228	using RTCK), **loading + running marvin from DDR over JTAG, repeatable with no
229	power-cycle** (`load-ram.sh` — validated booting marvin headless and reloading
230	from a running marvin), **source-level debug** (gdb/VS Code on `:3333`), and a
231	**macOS microSD prep** for standalone boot (`make-sdcard.sh`).
232	
233	It **programs on-board NAND from macOS** via [`program-nand.sh`](program-nand.md)
234	— u-boot is RAM-loaded over JTAG (same mechanism as `load-ram`) and acts as a
235	PMECC-aware flasher; marvin then boots standalone from NAND. Validated on
236	hardware (2026-06-11). This replaces the SAM-BA `../binaries/nand_flash.bat` flow
237	on macOS. **QSPI** still needs SAM-BA (`../binaries/qspi_flash.bat`, Linux/Windows)
238	or MPLAB — OpenOCD has no SAM9X7 QSPI driver and the u-boot QSPI-boot path isn't
239	wired up here.
240

```text
1	# Program marvin into NAND over JTAG — no SD card, no SAM-BA (macOS)
2	
3	Writes the standalone NAND boot image (at91bootstrap + marvin) to the cHybrid's
4	on-board NAND from macOS, using **u-boot as a PMECC-aware flasher loaded over
5	JTAG**. The SAM9X75 ROM then boots NAND on its own: RomBOOT → at91bootstrap →
6	`harmony.bin` in DDR (the same chain as the SD path, just resident in NAND).
7	
8	This replaces the SAM-BA `nand_flash.bat` flow (`../binaries/nand_flash.bat`) on
9	hosts where SAM-BA isn't used. It reproduces exactly what SAM-BA does:
10	
11	| SAM-BA (`nand_flash.bat`)            | here (u-boot console)                       |
12	|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
13	| `erase::0x100000`                    | `nand erase 0x0 0x100000`                    |
14	| `writeboot:sam9x7-nandflashboot…bin` | `nand write 0x22000000 0x0 0x4000`           |
15	| `write:harmony.bin:0x40000`          | `nand write 0x22100000 0x40000 0x80000`      |
16	
17	## Why u-boot (and not OpenOCD's NAND driver)
18	
19	The boot region must be written with the **PMECC** (BCH) layout RomBOOT expects.
20	OpenOCD's `at91sam9` NAND driver does old-style hardware ECC, not PMECC, so it
21	can't produce a bootable boot region. u-boot's `atmel_nand` driver uses the same
22	PMECC IP, configured from the board DT (hw ECC, 8-bit strength, 512-byte step,
23	on-flash BBT) — the scheme RomBOOT reads — so `nand write` is RomBOOT-correct by
24	construction.
25	
26	## Build the u-boot flasher (one-time)
27	
28	A prebuilt flasher is committed at
29	`../binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin` (what `program-nand.sh`
30	uses by default) — you only need this section to regenerate it.
31	
32	Source: the linux4microchip u-boot fork,
33	<https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp> (branch `linux4microchip-2026.04`,
34	v2025.07 base), config `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig`. Any
35	`arm-none-eabi-` cross toolchain works. macOS quirks: use Homebrew **gmake** (the
36	stock `/usr/bin/make` 3.81 can't parse u-boot's Makefile), and pass OpenSSL to the
37	host-tool build via the **environment** (passing `HOST_EXTRACFLAGS` on the command
38	line clobbers the bundled-dtc include path); adjust the OpenSSL prefix for your host.
39	
40	```sh
41	git clone -b linux4microchip-2026.04 https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp.git
42	cd u-boot-mchp
43	# ensure an arm-none-eabi- cross-gcc is on PATH (e.g. the Arm GNU Toolchain)
44	export HOST_EXTRACFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"   # macOS host-tool deps
45	export HOSTLDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
46	gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig
47	gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- -j8       # -> u-boot.bin (links/enters at 0x23f00000)
48	cp u-boot.bin <repo>/firmware/marvin/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin
49	```
50	
51	## Stage + program
52	
53	1. **Prerequisites (physical):**
54	   - Remove any bootable microSD (SD outranks NAND in the ROM boot order).
55	   - QSPI must hold no valid image (QSPI outranks NAND) — keep **JP4 (QSPI-CS)
56	     OUT**, or erase QSPI.
57	   - **JP3 (NAND-CS)** may be either way for *programming* (we drive NAND from
58	     u-boot, not RomBOOT); it must be **IN** to boot from NAND afterwards.
59	   - Kill any debug OpenOCD server holding the FT4232H.
60	   - **The board must not already be booting marvin from NAND.** This flow stages
61	     firmware into low DDR, which a running marvin's capture DMA can corrupt — so
62	     `program-nand.sh` refuses (clear error) if it catches the core running in DDR.
63	     To reflash a board that already boots from NAND (e.g. in an enclosure, no
64	     jumper access), erase first: **`./erase-nand.sh && ./program-nand.sh`**.
65	     `erase-nand.sh` robustly handles a booting/wedged board; after it, NAND is
66	     non-bootable so `program-nand.sh` catches the clean ROM-monitor path.
67	
68	2. **Program** — one command does everything:
69	
70	   ```sh
71	   cd firmware/marvin/openocd
72	   ./program-nand.sh
73	   # FTDI_SERIAL=W16-2026-4300 ./program-nand.sh   # target a specific board
74	   # CONSOLE=/dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX2 ./program-nand.sh   # override DBGU node
75	   ```
76	
77	   It (a) **pre-flight checks the DBGU console** is free and bails with a clear
78	   error if it's held elsewhere (screen/minicom), *before* touching the board;
79	   (b) over one JTAG pass, brings up DDR via the init-and-stop at91bootstrap and
80	   stages at91bootstrap → `0x21100000`, `harmony.bin` → `0x21200000`, u-boot →
81	   `0x23f00000`, then jumps to u-boot; (c) drives the u-boot console
82	   (`nand_console.py`) to erase `0x0..0x100000`, `nand write` both blobs, and
83	   verify each region against its staged DDR copy (`cmp.b`). Exit status is
84	   non-zero unless both verifies pass.
85	
86	   Staging addresses sit outside the windows u-boot's default `bootcmd` reads
87	   into (`0x21000000-0x21080000`, `0x22000000-0x22600000`), and the console driver
88	   waits for a *stable* prompt, so a 3 s autoboot can't clobber the staged blobs
89	   or eat the commands.
90	
91	3. **Boot from NAND:** power off, set **JP3 (NAND) IN**, **JP4 (QSPI) OUT**, no SD,
92	   power on. marvin boots from NAND — DBGU banner, no JTAG.
93	
94	To program by hand instead (e.g. debugging), open the console
95	(`screen /dev/cu.usbserial-...2 115200`) after staging and run: `nand erase 0x0
96	0x100000`, `nand write 0x21100000 0x0 0x4000`, `nand write 0x21200000 0x40000
97	0x80000`.
98	
99	## Layout reference
100	
101	| NAND offset | Contents                          | DDR stage    | Size written            |
102	|-------------|-----------------------------------|--------------|-------------------------|
103	| `0x00000`   | at91bootstrap (boot region)       | `0x21100000` | file size, 4 KiB-rounded (`0x4000`) |
104	| `0x40000`   | `harmony.bin` (marvin app)        | `0x21200000` | file size, 4 KiB-rounded (`0x7f000`) |
105	
106	(`program-nand.sh` computes the write size from each file, rounded up to the 4 KiB
107	page; the values shown are for the current binaries.)
108	
109	The boot region must carry a **PMECC header** the ROM reads (page 0, no ECC): 52
110	copies of a 32-bit word encoding the NAND/PMECC params, with the bootstrap code
111	at offset `0xD0`. Prepend it with at91bootstrap's `scripts/addpmecchead.py` —
112	but generate the word from the **actual** chip params (`nand info`:
113	4096/256/8-bit/512 → word `0xc2605007`), *not* that script's SAM9X7 defaults
114	(2048/64/4), which don't match this board's NAND.
115	
116	The at91bootstrap reads the app from raw offset `0x40000` (`CONFIG_IMG_ADDRESS`,
117	`CONFIG_IMG_SIZE=0x100000`) and jumps to `0x23f00000` — where marvin links. See
118	`../binaries/README.md`.
119	
120	## Validation & caveats
121	
122	**Validated on hardware:** marvin boots standalone from NAND (RomBOOT →
123	at91bootstrap → harmony), and both regions read back bit-identical to the staged
124	images. The PMECC layout matches RomBOOT (the "something extra" SAM-BA `writeboot`
125	does is exactly the page-0 NAND header, which `make-pmecchead.sh` prepends).
126	
127	The one parameter that is **NAND-part-specific** is the header word: it encodes
128	this board's `4096/256/8-bit/512` geometry (→ `0xc2605007`, eccOffset 152). If the
129	populated NAND ever changes:
130	
131	1. read the real geometry from u-boot `nand info`,
132	2. regenerate the header: `make-pmecchead.sh <in> <out> <page> <oob> <ecc> <sector>`,
133	3. confirm the u-boot DT ECC (`nand-ecc-strength`/`-step-size`) still matches, so
134	   u-boot writes the ECC at the offset the header declares.
135	
136	If a future board ever fails to boot from a freshly programmed NAND, capture
137	`nand dump 0x0` and check the page-0 header word against the regenerated value.
138
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./firmware/marvin/openocd/program-qspi.md`

```text
1	# Program QSPI NOR (splash / UI assets) over JTAG — no SD card (macOS)
2	
3	Writes a blob (the raw splash framebuffer, or a UI-asset image) into the on-board
4	QSPI NOR (`SST26VF064B`, 8 MiB) from the host over JTAG, using **u-boot as an SF
5	flasher loaded over JTAG** — the same pattern as [`program-nand.md`](program-nand.md),
6	but with `sf` instead of `nand`, and **no PMECC/ECC/header** (NOR needs none). The
7	dev win over the SD path: assets reflash straight from the host, no card-swapping
8	each iteration.
9	
10	Region offsets come from [`../default/src/flash/qspi_layout.h`](../default/src/flash/qspi_layout.h):
11	
12	| Region   | QSPI offset | Size       | DDR stage    |
13	|----------|-------------|------------|--------------|
14	| splash   | `0x000000`  | 4 MiB      | `0x21100000` |
15	| assets   | `0x400000`  | ~3.98 MiB  | `0x21100000` |
16	| settings | `0x7FC000`  | 16 KiB     | **off-limits** (the tool refuses) |
17	
18	## Prerequisite: a u-boot with `sf` support
19	
20	The flasher u-boot must include the SPI-flash stack (`CONFIG_CMD_SF` + the SAM9X7
21	QSPI controller + `CONFIG_SPI_FLASH_SST`).
22	
23	**Resolved for this board: the committed NAND flasher
24	(`sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin`) already includes SF** — `sf probe 0`
25	detects the SST26 — so it is the **default `UBOOT_BIN`** and no separate qspiflash
26	build is needed. The steps below are only for re-verifying on a new board/u-boot.
27	
28	1. **Confirm SF in a u-boot** — the `shell` mode stages just the bootstrap + u-boot
29	   (no programming) and hands you the console:
30	
31	   ```sh
32	   cd firmware/marvin/openocd
33	   UBOOT_BIN=../binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin ./program-qspi.sh shell
34	   # then, in another terminal:
35	   screen /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX2 115200      # exit: Ctrl-A k
36	   U-Boot> sf probe 0
37	   ```
38	
39	   If it prints `SF: Detected sst26...`, you're done — set `UBOOT_BIN` to that
40	   binary for the real runs and skip the build. (Many Microchip u-boot configs
41	   enable SF regardless of boot medium.) `qspi_console.py` also bails with a clear
42	   message if `sf probe` isn't supported, so a real run can't silently half-flash.
43	
44	2. **Otherwise build the qspiflash variant** (one-time, same toolchain as the NAND
45	   flasher — see program-nand.md for the macOS gmake/OpenSSL notes):
46	
47	   ```sh
48	   git clone -b linux4microchip-2026.04 https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp.git
49	   cd u-boot-mchp
50	   export HOST_EXTRACFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"
51	   export HOSTLDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
52	   gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pro_qspiflash_defconfig
53	   gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- -j8       # -> u-boot.bin (entry 0x23f00000)
54	   cp u-boot.bin <repo>/firmware/marvin/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-qspiflash-flasher-2025.07.bin
55	   ```
56	
57	   Verify the entry/link address is still `0x23f00000` (`CONFIG_TEXT_BASE`); the
58	   scripts load u-boot there. If a `qspiflash` defconfig doesn't exist, start from
59	   the nandflash one and enable `CMD_SF` + the QSPI driver + SST flash.
60	
61	## Jumpers / physical prerequisites
62	
63	- **JP4 (QSPI-CS) IN** — the part must be connected for `sf` to reach it. Our QSPI
64	  holds no boot image (splash/assets/settings, no boot header), so RomBOOT inspects
65	  it and skips it; JP4 IN does **not** cause a QSPI boot.
66	- **JP3 (NAND-CS) OUT** and **no bootable microSD** — so nothing boots marvin and
67	  the core is caught cold (DDR off) in the ROM monitor. `program-qspi.cfg` refuses
68	  (clear error) if `reset init` finds the core running in DDR, because staging into
69	  low DDR would race a running marvin's capture DMA.
70	- Kill any debug OpenOCD server holding the FT4232H, and close any serial monitor
71	  on the DBGU console.
72	
73	> This jumper state (JP4 IN, JP3 OUT, no SD) is also fine for `load-ram.sh`: with no
74	> bootable image anywhere, RomBOOT falls through to the monitor either way — so the
75	> dev loop is **flash QSPI → load-ram marvin** without re-jumpering. (Verify on first
76	> use that RomBOOT skips the non-bootable QSPI with JP4 IN.)
77	
78	## Program
79	
80	```sh
81	cd firmware/marvin/openocd
82	./program-qspi.sh splash                      # ../out/splash.raw -> QSPI 0x000000
83	./program-qspi.sh splash path/to/splash.raw   # explicit file
84	./program-qspi.sh assets icons.bin            # -> QSPI 0x400000
85	./program-qspi.sh assets fonts.bin 0x80000    # -> QSPI 0x400000 + 0x80000
86	./program-qspi.sh raw 0x123000 blob.bin       # escape hatch: arbitrary offset
87	# UBOOT_BIN=../binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin ./program-qspi.sh splash
88	```
89	
90	It (a) pre-flight checks the DBGU console is free; (b) over one JTAG pass, brings up
91	DDR via the init-and-stop at91bootstrap, stages the blob → `0x21100000` and u-boot →
92	`0x23f00000`, then jumps to u-boot; (c) drives the u-boot console (`qspi_console.py`)
93	to `sf probe` / `sf erase` (4 KiB-rounded length) / `sf write` from DDR / verify by
94	reading back to scratch DDR (`0x21600000`) and `cmp.b`. Exit status is non-zero
95	unless the verify passes. The blob stages below u-boot's autoboot read window and the
96	console waits for a *stable* prompt, so autoboot can't clobber it or eat commands.
97	
98	To program by hand (debugging): after staging, open the console
99	(`screen /dev/cu.usbserial-...2 115200`) and run (all numbers **hex**, erase length
100	64 KiB-aligned) `sf probe 0`, `sf erase 0x0 0x3f0000`, `sf write 0x21100000 0x0
101	0x3e8000`, then `sf read 0x21600000 0x0 0x3e8000` + `cmp.b 0x21100000 0x21600000
102	0x3e8000` (expect `Total of ... were the same`, no `!=` line). `0x3e8000` =
103	4,096,000 = the splash size; `0x3f0000` is that rounded up to 64 KiB.
104	
105	## Caveats
106	
107	- **Settings region is protected:** the tool refuses any write whose end passes
108	  `0x7FC000`. (The `qspi`/`settings` *firmware* tools still scribble there — see the
109	  partition-map decision in the journal.)
110	- **Splash format** is raw RGBA8888 1280×800 = 4,096,000 bytes — the exact size
111	  `splash.c` expects (it rejects any other size). Asset blob formats are defined by
112	  whatever the firmware asset reader expects (compile-time offsets for now).
113	- **u-boot parses command args as hex** — the script passes all lengths/offsets in
114	  hex. `sf write` writes the file's exact byte count; `sf erase` rounds up to u-boot's
115	  **64 KiB** erase block for this part (a 4 KiB-aligned length gives `ERROR -22`). The
116	  64 KiB-rounded erase stays within the region (splash/assets are MiB-sized and
117	  64 KiB-aligned). The verify covers the written bytes.
118	- 100 MHz QSCK reads are integrity-clean (firmware `qspi verify`); u-boot's `sf`
119	  runs the QSPI at its own (lower) default rate, so programming is reliable
120	  regardless of the firmware clock setting.
121
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./firmware/marvin/ftdi/README.md`

```text
1	# SAM9X75 cHybrid — FT4232H EEPROM programming
2	
3	The SAM9X75 cHybrid board has an onboard **FTDI FT4232H** "USB to JTAG & UART
4	bridge" with a **93LC46B** configuration EEPROM. This folder contains tooling to
5	program that EEPROM so each board reports a proper product name and a **unique
6	serial number**.
7	
8	> JTAG debug of the SAM9X75 (which uses the same FT4232H, channel A) is
9	> configured separately in [`../openocd/`](../openocd/).
10	
11	## FT4232H channel map (this board)
12	
13	| Channel | USB interface | Function on cHybrid | EEPROM driver |
14	|---------|---------------|---------------------|---------------|
15	| A | 0 | JTAG (MPSSE) — TCK/TDI/TDO/TMS on ADBUS0–3 | D2XX |
16	| B | 1 | unused (bridge resistors DNP) | D2XX |
17	| C | 2 | DBGU console (UART, populated via R149/R151) | VCP |
18	| D | 3 | unused | D2XX |
19	
20	(See schematic `SAM9X75 cHybrid-REV1_SCH.PDF`, sheet 14.)
21	
22	## Prerequisites
23	
24	```sh
25	# macOS (Homebrew)
26	brew install libftdi libusb
27	
28	# Debian/Ubuntu
29	sudo apt install libftdi1-2 libftdi1-dev libusb-1.0-0
30	```
31	
32	## Files
33	
34	| File | Purpose |
35	|------|---------|
36	| `ft4232h-chybrid.conf` | FT4232H EEPROM image definition (`ftdi_eeprom` format) |
37	| `flash-eeprom.sh` | Flash one board's EEPROM with a given serial |
38	
39	## Why
40	
41	Boards ship with a **blank 93LC46B**, so the FT4232H falls back to internal
42	defaults: it enumerates as a generic "Quad RS232-HS" device with no serial
43	number, and the host names its ports arbitrarily. Flashing the EEPROM gives each
44	board:
45	
46	- a product string (`SAM9X75 cHybrid`) and a **unique serial number**, so the
47	  host names ports predictably (e.g. `/dev/cu.usbserial-W16_2026_4130..3`) and
48	  OpenOCD can target a specific board with `FTDI_SERIAL` (see `../openocd/`);
49	- per-channel driver flags (channel A/B/D = D2XX, C = VCP).
50	
51	## Procedure
52	
53	> Flash **one board at a time, with only that board connected.** `ftdi_eeprom`
54	> selects the device by USB VID/PID, so multiple unprogrammed FT4232Hs are
55	> ambiguous.
56	
57	1. Connect the target board (and only it) via USB.
58	2. Flash it with its serial number (use whatever scheme you like; we use the
59	   board's label, e.g. `W16-2026-413`):
60	   ```sh
61	   ./flash-eeprom.sh W16-2026-413
62	   ```
63	   Success prints `FTDI write eeprom: 0`. (A trailing `FTDI close: -1` is
64	   benign — the chip re-enumerates on write.)
65	3. Unplug/replug the board so the host reads the new descriptors.
66	4. Verify:
67	   ```sh
68	   # macOS
69	   ioreg -p IOUSB -l | grep -iE 'cHybrid|<your-serial>'
70	   ls /dev/cu.usbserial*
71	
72	   # Linux
73	   lsusb -v -d 0403:6011 | grep -iE 'iProduct|iSerial'
74	   ```
75	
76	`flash-eeprom.sh` uses `ft4232h-chybrid.conf` as the base image and overrides
77	only the `serial=` line, so you never have to edit the config per board.
78	
79	## Platform behaviour of the per-channel driver flag
80	
81	The EEPROM marks channels A/B/D as **D2XX** (no serial port) and C as **VCP**
82	(serial port). Whether the host honours that depends on the OS — the VCP/D2XX
83	flag is really a Windows-driver concept:
84	
85	| OS | Result |
86	|----|--------|
87	| Windows | Honoured — only channel C gets a COM port; A/B/D are D2XX (libusb) only. |
88	| Linux | **Not** honoured by default — `ftdi_sio` creates `/dev/ttyUSB*` for all four channels. Suppress per-interface with a udev rule or by unbinding `ftdi_sio`. |
89	| macOS | **Not** honoured — `AppleUSBFTDI` creates a `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` node for all four channels. |
90	
91	So only on Windows does the flag hide the unused channels. On Linux/macOS the
92	extra nodes are harmless — JTAG on channel A still works because libusb claims
93	the interface regardless of the serial node. The product string and unique
94	**serial number apply on every OS**, which is the portable benefit of flashing.
95	
96	## Reference: editing the EEPROM image
97	
98	`ft4232h-chybrid.conf` is in [libftdi `ftdi_eeprom`](https://www.intra2net.com/en/developer/libftdi/)
99	format. Key fields:
100	
101	```ini
102	manufacturer="Microchip"
103	product="SAM9X75 cHybrid"
104	use_serial=true
105	serial="W16-2026-359"      # overridden by flash-eeprom.sh
106	
107	cha_vcp=false   # channel A -> D2XX (JTAG)
108	chb_vcp=false   # channel B -> D2XX (unused)
109	chc_vcp=true    # channel C -> VCP  (DBGU console)
110	chd_vcp=false   # channel D -> D2XX (unused)
111	```
112	
113	Useful one-off commands (run with a single board connected):
114	
115	```sh
116	# Build the image without flashing (validates the config, writes the .bin)
117	ftdi_eeprom --device i:0x0403:0x6011 --build-eeprom ft4232h-chybrid.conf
118	
119	# Flash directly from the config (what flash-eeprom.sh wraps)
120	ftdi_eeprom --device i:0x0403:0x6011 --flash-eeprom ft4232h-chybrid.conf
121	
122	# Erase the EEPROM back to blank
123	ftdi_eeprom --device i:0x0403:0x6011 --erase-eeprom ft4232h-chybrid.conf
124	```
125	
126	The 93LC46B holds 128 bytes; the image above uses ~114, so keep the strings
127	short if you extend it.
128
```
</details></tool-use>

67	    # Frame Buffers" off, the framebuffer is non-cached but the Legato render

69	    # reads stale CPU-cached pixels -> streaky bleed. The #ifndef guard in

71	    "LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR=__attribute__((section(\".region_nocache\")))"
72	    # Fretboard link transport: default is FLEXCOM1 UART. Uncomment to route
73	    # the fretboard command/data over the 10BASE-T1S link (LAN8651) instead —

231	    /* Program PFE crop window to the configured image size. The MCC

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Load marvin into DDR over JTAG and run it, with no SD card. macOS/OpenOCD only.
3	# The dev iteration loop: repeatable with no power-cycle (edit, rebuild, re-run).
4	# See load-ram.cfg for the mechanism.
5	#
6	# PREREQUISITES:
7	#   * No bootable medium present: JP3/JP4 (NAND/QSPI CS) OUT and no bootable microSD
8	#     (else RomBOOT boots it before reset init catches the core).
9	#   * Nothing else holding the FT4232H (e.g. kill a running debug OpenOCD server).
10	#
11	# Usage:   ./load-ram.sh
12	# Env overrides:
13	#   BOOTSTRAP_ELF  at91bootstrap init-and-stop ELF
14	#                  (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf)
15	#   MARVIN_ELF     marvin ELF (default: ../out/marvin/default.elf)
16	#   FTDI_SERIAL    target a specific board by its FT4232H serial
17	set -euo pipefail
18	
19	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
20	root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"
21	
22	BOOTSTRAP_ELF="${BOOTSTRAP_ELF:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf}"
23	MARVIN_ELF="${MARVIN_ELF:-$root/out/marvin/default.elf}"
24	FTDI_SERIAL="${FTDI_SERIAL:-}"
25	
26	# XC32 ships binutils that read these ARM ELFs (just need the entry points).
27	xc32bin="$(ls -d /Applications/microchip/xc32/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
28	READELF="${READELF:-${xc32bin:+$xc32bin/}xc32-readelf}"
29	
30	[ -f "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" ] || { echo "missing bootstrap ELF: $BOOTSTRAP_ELF" >&2; exit 1; }
31	[ -f "$MARVIN_ELF" ]    || { echo "missing marvin ELF: $MARVIN_ELF (build marvin first)" >&2; exit 1; }
32	
33	boot_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"
34	marvin_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$MARVIN_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"
35	
36	echo "bootstrap : $BOOTSTRAP_ELF (entry $boot_entry)"
37	echo "marvin    : $MARVIN_ELF (entry $marvin_entry)"
38	
39	# Common args (never empty). A specific board serial, if given, must precede the
40	# config file that reads FTDI_SERIAL.
41	common=(-f "$here/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg" -f "$here/load-ram.cfg")
42	[ -n "$FTDI_SERIAL" ] && common=(-c "set FTDI_SERIAL $FTDI_SERIAL" "${common[@]}")
43	
44	# marvin_load_ram (load-ram.cfg): reset init -> run bootstrap to completion -> load
45	# + run marvin.
46	exec openocd "${common[@]}" -c "init" \
47	        -c "marvin_load_ram $BOOTSTRAP_ELF $boot_entry $MARVIN_ELF $marvin_entry" \
48	        -c "shutdown"
49

```text
1	# Load marvin into DDR over JTAG and run it — no SD card.
2	#
3	# Reuses a purpose-built "init-and-stop" at91bootstrap (the
4	# sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone build) to bring up the 266 MHz clocks + in-package
5	# DDR3L, then loads marvin into DDR and jumps to it. See ../binaries/README.md for
6	# the bootstrap and ../docs/journal.md for the rationale.
7	#
8	# PREREQUISITE: no bootable medium present — JP3/JP4 (NAND/QSPI CS) OUT and no
9	# bootable microSD. Otherwise RomBOOT boots that medium before `reset init` catches
10	# the core. `reset init` (sam9x75-chybrid.cfg) resets from any state, so loads are
11	# repeatable with no power-cycle. Driven by load-ram.sh.
12	
13	proc marvin_load_ram {bootstrap_elf boot_entry marvin_elf marvin_entry} {
14	    # `reset init` resets the SoC (500 ms nSRST pulse, srst_pulls_trst — see
15	    # sam9x75-chybrid.cfg) from ANY state, including a running marvin, then runs
16	    # reset-init to disable the watchdog + MMU/caches. Repeatable, no power-cycle.
17	    reset init
18	
19	    # Adaptive clocking (RTCK, AD7) is mandatory: at a fixed TCK, OpenOCD loses
20	    # JTAG sync when at91bootstrap's lowlevel_clock_init switches the master clock.
21	    adapter speed 0
22	
23	    # Enter the bootstrap in ARM / Supervisor with IRQ+FIQ masked (reset state).
24	    reg cpsr 0x000000d3
25	
26	    # Stage 1: run the bootstrap to completion — its main() does the full low-level
27	    # init, then crt0 hits its own `bkpt` (CONFIG_BKPT_NOTIFY_DONE), where we catch
28	    # it. (Stopping earlier, at hw_init, leaves init incomplete — see journal.)
29	    load_image $bootstrap_elf
30	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
31	    resume $boot_entry
32	    wait_halt 6000
33	    echo ">>> at91bootstrap init complete (BKPT_NOTIFY_DONE): clocks + DDR up"
34	
35	    # Stage 2: clocks are stable now → fast fixed TCK + DCC for the 517 KB transfer.
36	    # DCC keeps write-completion checks; fast_memory_access is intentionally left
37	    # off (it skips them — see journal).
38	    adapter speed 6000
39	    arm7_9 dcc_downloads enable
40	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
41	    echo ">>> loading marvin into DDR..."
42	    load_image $marvin_elf
43	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
44	    echo ">>> jumping to marvin at $marvin_entry"
45	    resume $marvin_entry
46	}
47
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./firmware/marvin/openocd/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg`

```text
1	# SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid — JTAG debug via the onboard FT4232H channel A.
2	#
3	# Channel A = JTAG (TCK=AD0 TDI=AD1 TDO=AD2 TMS=AD3 nSRST=AD5 RTCK=AD7; AD4/AD6 are
4	# N/C — no nTRST). Channel C = DBGU console. On macOS all four enumerate as
5	# /dev/cu.usbserial-*, but libusb still claims channel A for MPSSE (no driver swap).
6	#
7	# Usage:  openocd -f firmware/marvin/openocd/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg
8	#         then: arm-none-eabi-gdb -ex 'target remote :3333'
9	
10	adapter driver ftdi
11	ftdi vid_pid 0x0403 0x6011
12	ftdi channel 0
13	ftdi layout_init 0x0008 0x000b
14	# No nTRST: AD4 is N/C on this board (per schematic). Reset is driven entirely by
15	# nSRST (AD5); srst_pulls_trst below handles TAP re-validation after reset.
16	ftdi layout_signal nSRST -data 0x20 -oe 0x20
17	
18	# Select a specific board by its FT4232H serial when several are connected:
19	#   openocd -c "set FTDI_SERIAL W16-2026-359" -f sam9x75-chybrid.cfg
20	# Leave FTDI_SERIAL unset to use the first matching FT4232H.
21	if { [info exists FTDI_SERIAL] } {
22	    adapter serial $FTDI_SERIAL
23	}
24	
25	reset_config srst_only srst_pulls_trst
26	
27	transport select jtag
28	adapter speed 50
29	
30	adapter srst delay 500
31	adapter srst pulse_width 500
32	
33	set _CHIPNAME sam9x75
34	set _CPUTAPID 0x0792603f
35	
36	jtag newtap $_CHIPNAME cpu -irlen 4 -ircapture 0x1 -irmask 0xf -expected-id $_CPUTAPID
37	
38	set _TARGETNAME $_CHIPNAME.cpu
39	target create $_TARGETNAME arm926ejs -endian little -chain-position $_TARGETNAME
40	
41	# Work area in internal SRAM — lets load_image use the fast download path instead
42	# of slow word-by-word memory writes. -work-area-backup so it can be reused around
43	# code that lives in SRAM (e.g. at91bootstrap during load-ram).
44	$_TARGETNAME configure \
45	    -work-area-phys 0x00300000 \
46	    -work-area-size 0x10000 \
47	    -work-area-backup 1
48	
49	$_TARGETNAME configure -event reset-start {
50	    adapter speed 50
51	}
52	
53	# This board boots ROM/at91bootstrap immediately after reset, so a single post-
54	# reset halt is racy — retry until the core is caught.
55	$_TARGETNAME configure -event reset-deassert-post {
56	    for {set i 0} {$i < 50} {incr i} {
57	        if {[catch {halt 10}] == 0} break
58	        sleep 10
59	    }
60	}
61	
62	# reset-init (`reset init`): disable the watchdog (WDT_MR.WDDIS, bit 12) so the
63	# halted core isn't reset out from under the debugger, then raise the JTAG clock.
64	$_TARGETNAME configure -event reset-init {
65	    set WDT_MR 0xffffff84
66	    set val [lindex [mdw $WDT_MR 1] 1]
67	    mww $WDT_MR [expr {($val & 0x00FFFFFF) | (1 << 12)}]
68	
69	    adapter speed 1000
70	}
71
```
</details></tool-use>
