```text
1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	> **Re-scoped to a T1S sense+actuate node (2026-06-17):** the fretboard is a 10BASE-T1S
4	> PLCA follower (id 1) that infers actuator commands from the phototransistor data and drives the
5	> [`guitar`](../guitar/SPEC.md) node over T1S, while also streaming its data to marvin. The old UART
6	> link, the standalone Wii-guitar GPIO outputs (`cmd_receive.c`), and the `FRETBOARD_LINK`/`FRETBOARD_MODE`
7	> build flags are gone — one behaviour. Node-class model: top-level [`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) §2; link
8	> detail: [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
9	
10	## Overview
11	
12	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz). The fretboard is a 10BASE-T1S
13	node that both **senses** and **drives**. Each 240 Hz tick it samples five
14	phototransistors above the TV strike line; an on-device int8 neural net
15	(`model_infer.c`, weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) infers the Wii-guitar
16	button bitmask from the ADC window. Over T1S it then:
17	
18	- **streams** the 17-byte data frame (ADC scan + the driven bitmask) to the marvin
19	  coordinator — logging / edge-ai training; and
20	- **commands** the [`guitar`](../guitar/SPEC.md) node (id 2) directly with the
21	  inferred bitmask — peer-to-peer actuation; marvin coordinates/logs but is out of
22	  the command path.
23	
24	Inference runs in the main loop (it overruns the 240 Hz tick in the ISR); the ISR
25	only scans + stages the data frame. SW0 arms actuation, LED0 shows armed (boots
26	disarmed → commands 0/released). It has **no local Wii-guitar outputs** — those pins
27	are the LAN8651 SPI. See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md), edge-ai
28	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md), and
29	[`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
30	
31	## Hardware
32	
33	### Target
34	
35	| Spec | Value |
36	|------|-------|
37	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
38	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
39	| Clock | 24 MHz |
40	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
41	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
42	
43	### Pin Map
44	
45	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
46	
47	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
48	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
49	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
50	presence.
51	
52	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
53	|---------|-----------|-----|
54	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
55	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
56	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
57	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
58	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
59	
60	There are no button/strum outputs — those GPIOs are the LAN8651 SPI/CS/IRQ/RST
61	pins now. See [`t1s_detector.c`](t1s_detector.c).
62	
63	#### SERCOM0 SPI — LAN8651 (T1S)
64	
65	Mode 0 (CPOL=0/CPHA=0, MSB, 8-bit): MOSI=PA04, SCK=PA05, MISO=PA07; `T1S_CS`=PA15
66	(GPIO, held low across each TC6 chunk), `T1S_RST`=PA14, `T1S_IRQ_N`=PA13 (EIC
67	EXTINT13, falling).
68	
69	#### SERCOM1 — operator console
70	
71	Hosts the embedded-cli console + diagnostic log. TX PB00 / RX PB01, **500 000** 8N1,
72	ring-buffer mode (TX ring ≥ 512 B).
73	
74	## Software Architecture
75	
76	### Processing Loop
77	
78	`TC0` fires a periodic callback at **240 Hz** (≈4.17 ms). The ISR scans and stages
79	the data frame with the currently-driven command; the heavy work (inference, TC6
80	service, TX flush) runs in the `main()` service loop:
81	
82	```
83	TC0 ISR (240 Hz)                     main() service loop
84	  fret_scan_all()                      model_infer_* -> s_latest_cmd
85	  push sample to model queue           T1SDetector_SetCommand(cmd) -> guitar (T1S)
86	  cmd = armed ? s_latest_cmd : 0       T1SDetector_Tasks()  (service + flush data + HB)
87	  data_stream_send(cmd)  (stage)       CLI_Tasks()
88	```
89	
90	The ISR stays short (the model overruns the tick if run there — see the journal /
91	edge-ai `runtime.md` §3). `data_stream_send()` stages the frame; `T1SDetector_Tasks()`
92	flushes it (and the guitar command, and the heartbeat) from the main loop.
93	
94	### Module Descriptions
95	
96	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
97	
98	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
99	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
100	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
101	
102	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
103	the firmware:
104	
105	```
106	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
107	```
108	
109	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
110	
111	Builds one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick and stages it for TX to the marvin
112	coordinator over T1S (via `T1SDetector_SendFrame`):
113	
114	| Offset | Size | Field |
115	|-------:|-----:|-------|
116	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
117	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
118	| 3 | 2 | red |
119	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
120	| 7 | 2 | blue |
121	| 9 | 2 | orange |
122	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
123	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — the bitmask driven to the guitar this scan |
124	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
125	
126	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect dropped frames
127	(it advances per tick even when a send is skipped). `applied_mask` is the command
128	the node drove to the guitar this scan, paired atomically with the ADC scan for
129	edge-ai training-data export. The marvin RX side keys on this 17-byte layout.
130	
131	### T1S node ([t1s_detector.c](t1s_detector.c) / [.h](t1s_detector.h))
132	
133	PLCA follower **id 1**, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:01`, on the marvin-coordinated
134	(`02:..:00`) bus via a LAN8651 MAC-PHY over SERCOM0 SPI. Reuses the shared
135	`third_party/oa-tc6-lib` (OPEN Alliance TC6) + a local `tc6-conf.h`. All TC6 access
136	is serviced from the **main loop** (`T1SDetector_Tasks()`), never the 240 Hz ISR.
137	
138	- **Data → coordinator:** the 17-byte frame rides the Ethernet payload under
139	  ethertype `0x88B5`, dst = coordinator MAC. The ISR stages it
140	  (`T1SDetector_SendFrame()`, latest-wins); the main loop flushes it, one TX in
141	  flight. A frame dropped while busy shows as a `sample_seq` gap.
142	- **Command → guitar:** `T1SDetector_SetCommand()` (main loop) hands the inferred
143	  1-byte bitmask to the **guitar node** (id 2, MAC `02:..:02`, ethertype `0x88B5`).
144	  Sent edge-triggered + re-sent every 50 ms so a dropped command self-heals; the
145	  guitar applies latest-wins. Peer-to-peer — marvin is not in the command path.
146	- **Presence:** a 500 ms heartbeat (ethertype `0x88B6`, `node_type = 1` detector) so
147	  marvin's `nodes` command shows the node present.
148	- **Operator CLI:** SERCOM1 hosts an embedded-cli console ([cli.c](cli.c), vendored
149	  `third_party/embedded-cli/`): `t1s` (link / sync / chipRev / PLCA / data+command tx
150	  counts), `adc` (latest scan), `id` / `plca` (MAC-PHY register diagnostics).
151	  Bare-metal — `CLI_Tasks()` drains the RX ring each main-loop pass.
152	
153	**Coordination caveat:** there is no active-source arbitration yet — while the
154	fretboard is armed (SW0) it drives the guitar, and marvin must not also command the
155	guitar (both target `02:..:02`). marvin-side active-detector/active-guitar selection
156	is the follow-up. Link rationale, addressing, and the PoDL plan are in
157	[`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
158	
159	## Observability
160	
161	The data stream lands on **marvin** now (over T1S), so health is read there: the
162	`PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` rate via [`tools/marvin-perf`](../../tools/marvin-perf/) and
163	node presence via marvin's `nodes` console command. On the node itself, the SERCOM1
164	CLI (`t1s`, `adc`) shows link state, data/command TX counts, and the live scan.
165	([`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) was the UART-era serial monitor — no
166	longer applicable now that the stream is on the bus.)
167	
168	## Build System
169	
170	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
171	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
172	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
173	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
174	
175	## File Map
176	
177	| File | Purpose |
178	|------|---------|
179	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 scan/stage ISR + service loop (infer, drive guitar) |
180	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
181	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | 17-byte data frame builder (→ T1S) |
182	| [t1s_detector.c](t1s_detector.c) / [.h](t1s_detector.h) | T1S node: data→coordinator, command→guitar, heartbeat |
183	| [cli.c](cli.c) / [.h](cli.h) | Operator CLI on SERCOM1 (t1s/adc/id/plca) |
184	| [model_infer.c](model_infer.c) / [model_infer_stream.c](model_infer_stream.c) | On-device int8 model (ADC window → bitmask) |
185	| [tc6-conf.h](tc6-conf.h) | OA TC6 driver build config |
186	| `third_party/embedded-cli/` | Vendored embedded-cli (CLI engine, static-alloc) |
187	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
188

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Program marvin into on-board NAND from macOS over JTAG — no SD card, no SAM-BA.
3	# Stages at91bootstrap + harmony + u-boot into DDR over JTAG, starts u-boot, then
4	# erases + writes + verifies NAND from the DBGU console (all automated). macOS/
5	# OpenOCD only. See program-nand.md.
6	#
7	# PREREQUISITES:
8	#   * No higher-priority boot medium catching the core first: remove any bootable
9	#     microSD, and QSPI must hold no valid image (JP4/QSPI-CS OUT). JP3 (NAND) may
10	#     be IN or OUT for *programming* (we drive NAND from u-boot, not RomBOOT) but
11	#     must be IN to boot from NAND afterwards.
12	#   * The board must NOT already be booting marvin from NAND (staging into low DDR
13	#     would race a running marvin's capture DMA). program-nand.cfg refuses with a
14	#     clear error in that case — erase first: ./erase-nand.sh && ./program-nand.sh.
15	#   * Nothing else holding the FT4232H (kill any debug OpenOCD server first) or the
16	#     DBGU console serial node.
17	#
18	# Usage:   ./program-nand.sh
19	# Env overrides:
20	#   BOOTSTRAP_ELF  init-and-stop at91bootstrap ELF (brings up DDR over JTAG)
21	#                  (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf)
22	#   UBOOT_BIN      u-boot raw binary, the flasher (links/enters at 0x23f00000)
23	#                  (default: ../binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin)
24	#   NANDBOOT_BIN   at91bootstrap written to NAND offset 0x0 (the boot region) —
25	#                  MUST carry the SAM9X7 ROM PMECC header (the *-pmecchead.bin;
26	#                  regenerate with ../binaries/make-pmecchead.sh). The plain
27	#                  bootstrap has no header and RomBOOT will not load it.
28	#                  (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin)
29	#   HARMONY_BIN    marvin app written to NAND offset 0x40000
30	#                  (default: ../out/harmony.bin)
31	#   FTDI_SERIAL    target a specific board by its FT4232H serial
32	#   CONSOLE        DBGU console node (FT4232H channel C). Auto-detected as the 3rd
33	#                  /dev/cu.usbserial-* if unset; set explicitly with >1 board.
34	set -euo pipefail
35	
36	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
37	root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"
38	
39	BOOTSTRAP_ELF="${BOOTSTRAP_ELF:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf}"
40	UBOOT_BIN="${UBOOT_BIN:-$root/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin}"
41	NANDBOOT_BIN="${NANDBOOT_BIN:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin}"
42	HARMONY_BIN="${HARMONY_BIN:-$root/out/harmony.bin}"
43	FTDI_SERIAL="${FTDI_SERIAL:-}"
44	CONSOLE="${CONSOLE:-$(ls /dev/cu.usbserial-* 2>/dev/null | sort | sed -n '3p')}"
45	
46	# DDR staging addresses (must match program-nand.cfg) + NAND offsets.
47	BOOT_ADDR=0x21100000; BOOT_OFF=0x0
48	APP_ADDR=0x21200000;  APP_OFF=0x40000
49	
50	# The NAND boot bootstrap copies exactly this many bytes from APP_OFF to 0x23f00000
51	# at boot — its compiled-in CONFIG_IMG_SIZE (see binaries/README.md). harmony.bin
52	# must fit inside it or the bootstrap loads a truncated app. Keep in sync if the
53	# bootstrap is rebuilt with a different window.
54	NAND_IMG_SIZE="${NAND_IMG_SIZE:-0x400000}"
55	
56	xc32bin="$(ls -d /Applications/microchip/xc32/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
57	READELF="${READELF:-${xc32bin:+$xc32bin/}xc32-readelf}"
58	
59	for f in "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" "$UBOOT_BIN" "$NANDBOOT_BIN" "$HARMONY_BIN"; do
60	    [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "missing: $f" >&2; exit 1; }
61	done
62	[ -n "$CONSOLE" ] || { echo "no DBGU console found; set CONSOLE=/dev/cu.usbserial-... (channel C)" >&2; exit 1; }
63	
64	# nand-write sizes: file size rounded up to the 4 KiB page.
65	roundup() { printf '0x%x' $(( ( ($1 + 0xfff) / 0x1000 ) * 0x1000 )); }
66	BOOT_SZ=$(roundup "$(stat -f%z "$NANDBOOT_BIN")")
67	APP_SZ=$(roundup "$(stat -f%z "$HARMONY_BIN")")
68	
69	# Guard: the app must fit the bootstrap's copy window, else it boots truncated.
70	if [ "$((APP_SZ))" -gt "$((NAND_IMG_SIZE))" ]; then
71	    echo "marvin app $HARMONY_BIN ($APP_SZ rounded) exceeds the bootstrap copy window NAND_IMG_SIZE=$NAND_IMG_SIZE." >&2
72	    echo "The bootstrap would load a truncated app. Rebuild the NAND bootstrap with a larger" >&2
73	    echo "CONFIG_IMG_SIZE (see ../binaries/README.md) and set NAND_IMG_SIZE to match." >&2
74	    exit 1
75	fi
76	
77	boot_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"
78	
79	echo "bootstrap (DDR init) : $BOOTSTRAP_ELF (entry $boot_entry)"
80	echo "u-boot (flasher)     : $UBOOT_BIN -> 0x23f00000"
81	echo "NAND boot region     : $NANDBOOT_BIN -> NAND $BOOT_OFF ($BOOT_SZ)"
82	echo "marvin app           : $HARMONY_BIN -> NAND $APP_OFF ($APP_SZ)"
83	echo "console              : $CONSOLE"
84	
85	# Pre-flight: confirm the DBGU console is free BEFORE touching the board, so we
86	# don't stage everything over JTAG only to find the port busy.
87	uv run --with pyserial python "$here/nand_console.py" "$CONSOLE" probe
88	
89	# 1) Stage the three blobs into DDR over JTAG and start u-boot (JTAG released).
90	common=(-f "$here/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg" -f "$here/program-nand.cfg")
91	[ -n "$FTDI_SERIAL" ] && common=(-c "set FTDI_SERIAL $FTDI_SERIAL" "${common[@]}")
92	openocd "${common[@]}" -c "init" \
93	    -c "stage_for_nand $BOOTSTRAP_ELF $boot_entry $UBOOT_BIN $NANDBOOT_BIN $HARMONY_BIN" \
94	    -c "shutdown"
95	
96	# 2) Drive the erase + write + verify from the console.
97	uv run --with pyserial python "$here/nand_console.py" "$CONSOLE" program \
98	    "$BOOT_ADDR" "$BOOT_OFF" "$BOOT_SZ" "$APP_ADDR" "$APP_OFF" "$APP_SZ"
99	
100	echo
101	echo ">>> Done. Power off, set JP3 (NAND) IN / JP4 (QSPI) OUT, remove any SD, power on."
102	echo ">>> marvin boots from NAND (DBGU banner, no JTAG)."
103
```

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./firmware/marvin/openocd/program-nand.cfg`

```text
1	# Stage marvin's NAND images into DDR over JTAG, then start u-boot as a
2	# PMECC-aware NAND flasher. macOS/OpenOCD only. See program-nand.md.
3	#
4	# u-boot leaves low DDR untouched (it relocates to the top of RAM), so all three
5	# blobs are pre-staged in one JTAG pass and the NAND write is driven entirely
6	# from the u-boot console afterwards — no further JTAG interaction:
7	#
8	#   0x21100000  at91bootstrap (sam9x7-nandflashboot) -> NAND 0x0      (boot region)
9	#   0x21200000  harmony.bin   (marvin)               -> NAND 0x40000  (app)
10	#   0x23f00000  u-boot itself (entry) — the flasher; its atmel_nand driver
11	#               applies PMECC (8-bit/512, on-flash BBT per the board DT)
12	#
13	# Staging addresses avoid the regions u-boot's default bootcmd reads into
14	# (0x21000000-0x21080000 and 0x22000000-0x22600000) — otherwise a 3 s autoboot
15	# would overwrite the staged blobs with 0xff from the (empty) kernel partition
16	# before the console can program them.
17	#
18	# Mechanism mirrors load-ram.cfg: the init-and-stop at91bootstrap brings up the
19	# 266 MHz clocks + in-package DDR3L, then we load the blobs and jump to u-boot.
20	
21	proc stage_for_nand {bootstrap_elf boot_entry uboot_bin nandboot_bin harmony_bin} {
22	    # reset init resets the SoC from any state and disables the watchdog
23	    # (sam9x75-chybrid.cfg). Adaptive clocking (RTCK) is mandatory while
24	    # at91bootstrap switches the master clock.
25	    reset init
26	
27	    # Guard: this flow stages firmware into low DDR (0x211xxxxx/0x212xxxxx) and runs
28	    # the init-and-stop bootstrap, which must be the *only* DDR3L init — both require
29	    # a cold, non-booting board. Two ways the board can already be booting from NAND:
30	    # marvin (caught in DDR, MMU on — the PC tells us), or a valid boot-region
31	    # at91bootstrap looping on a corrupt app (caught in SRAM, MMU off, but DDR already
32	    # up — a PC test can't tell it from the cold ROM monitor, so probe DDR). Either
33	    # way, proceeding would stage into a live DMA region and re-init an already-trained
34	    # MPDDRC (mistrains it → reads shift a halfword → u-boot never runs). Bail; erasing
35	    # first makes NAND non-bootable so the next reset catches the ROM monitor, DDR cold.
36	    set _pc_out [capture {reg pc}]
37	    regexp {0x[0-9a-fA-F]+} $_pc_out _pc
38	    set _booting 0
39	    if {$_pc >= 0x20000000 && $_pc < 0x30000000} {
40	        set _booting 1
41	    } else {
42	        catch {
43	            write_memory 0x23f00000 32 {0xdeadbeef 0x12345678}
44	            set _rb [read_memory 0x23f00000 32 2]
45	            if {[lindex $_rb 0] == 0xdeadbeef && [lindex $_rb 1] == 0x12345678} { set _booting 1 }
46	        }
47	    }
48	    if {$_booting} {
49	        error "program-nand: board is already booting from NAND (marvin or a looping partial bootstrap). Run ./erase-nand.sh first, then re-run ./program-nand.sh."
50	    }
51	
52	    adapter speed 0
53	    reg cpsr 0x000000d3
54	
55	    # Run the bootstrap to completion (crt0 BKPT_NOTIFY_DONE) — clocks + DDR up.
56	    load_image $bootstrap_elf
57	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
58	    resume $boot_entry
59	    wait_halt 6000
60	    echo ">>> at91bootstrap init complete: clocks + DDR3L up, MMU/caches off"
61	
62	    # Clocks stable -> fast fixed TCK + DCC for the bulk transfers.
63	    adapter speed 6000
64	    arm7_9 dcc_downloads enable
65	
66	    echo ">>> staging at91bootstrap -> DDR 0x21100000"
67	    load_image $nandboot_bin 0x21100000 bin
68	    echo ">>> staging harmony.bin   -> DDR 0x21200000"
69	    load_image $harmony_bin 0x21200000 bin
70	    echo ">>> loading u-boot        -> DDR 0x23f00000"
71	    load_image $uboot_bin 0x23f00000 bin
72	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
73	
74	    echo ">>> starting u-boot — JTAG done; program NAND from the console"
75	    resume 0x23f00000
76	}
77
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Erase on-board NAND from macOS over JTAG, to make the board non-bootable and
3	# return to RAM development (load-ram.sh) WITHOUT touching the JP3/JP4 jumpers —
4	# e.g. when the board is sealed in an enclosure. macOS/OpenOCD only.
5	#
6	# Why this exists: load-ram.sh needs no valid boot medium so `reset init` can
7	# catch the core. Once marvin is resident in NAND (JP3 in), erasing NAND is the
8	# no-jumper way back to that state. It RAM-loads u-boot over JTAG (its atmel_nand
9	# driver does the erase), then drives the erase over the DBGU console.
10	#
11	# Usage:
12	#   ./erase-nand.sh            # erase the boot+app region (0x0..0x100000) — enough
13	#                              #   to make NAND non-bootable
14	#   ./erase-nand.sh chip       # full-chip erase
15	#
16	# Env overrides:
17	#   BOOTSTRAP_ELF  init-and-stop at91bootstrap ELF (brings up DDR over JTAG)
18	#   UBOOT_BIN      u-boot flasher (RAM-loaded; links/enters at 0x23f00000)
19	#   FTDI_SERIAL    target a specific board by its FT4232H serial
20	#   CONSOLE        DBGU console node (FT4232H channel C). Auto-detected as the 3rd
21	#                  /dev/cu.usbserial-* if unset; set explicitly with >1 board.
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25	root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"
26	
27	BOOTSTRAP_ELF="${BOOTSTRAP_ELF:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf}"
28	UBOOT_BIN="${UBOOT_BIN:-$root/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin}"
29	FTDI_SERIAL="${FTDI_SERIAL:-}"
30	CONSOLE="${CONSOLE:-$(ls /dev/cu.usbserial-* 2>/dev/null | sort | sed -n '3p')}"
31	
32	SCOPE="${1:-region}"
33	case "$SCOPE" in
34	    region|chip) ;;
35	    *) echo "usage: $0 [region|chip]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
36	esac
37	
38	xc32bin="$(ls -d /Applications/microchip/xc32/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
39	READELF="${READELF:-${xc32bin:+$xc32bin/}xc32-readelf}"
40	
41	for f in "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" "$UBOOT_BIN"; do
42	    [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "missing: $f" >&2; exit 1; }
43	done
44	[ -n "$CONSOLE" ] || { echo "no DBGU console found; set CONSOLE=/dev/cu.usbserial-... (channel C)" >&2; exit 1; }
45	
46	boot_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"
47	
48	echo "bootstrap (DDR init) : $BOOTSTRAP_ELF (entry $boot_entry)"
49	echo "u-boot (flasher)     : $UBOOT_BIN -> 0x23f00000"
50	echo "console              : $CONSOLE"
51	echo "erase                : $SCOPE"
52	
53	# Pre-flight: confirm the DBGU console is free BEFORE touching the board.
54	uv run --with pyserial python "$here/nand_console.py" "$CONSOLE" probe
55	
56	# 1) Bring u-boot up in DDR over JTAG (JTAG released afterwards).
57	common=(-f "$here/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg" -f "$here/erase-nand.cfg")
58	[ -n "$FTDI_SERIAL" ] && common=(-c "set FTDI_SERIAL $FTDI_SERIAL" "${common[@]}")
59	openocd "${common[@]}" -c "init" \
60	    -c "load_uboot $BOOTSTRAP_ELF $boot_entry $UBOOT_BIN" \
61	    -c "shutdown"
62	
63	# 2) Drive the erase + verify over the console.
64	uv run --with pyserial python "$here/nand_console.py" "$CONSOLE" erase "$SCOPE"
65	
66	echo
67	echo ">>> NAND erased. The ROM will now fall through to the SAM-BA monitor on boot,"
68	echo ">>> so ./load-ram.sh works again (no jumper change needed)."
69

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./firmware/marvin/openocd/erase-nand.cfg`

```text
1	# Load u-boot over JTAG so its atmel_nand driver can erase NAND — used to make
2	# the board non-bootable and return to RAM development without touching the
3	# JP3/JP4 jumpers. See erase-nand.sh and program-nand.md.
4	#
5	# Unlike load-ram (which assumes no bootable medium, so the core is caught in the
6	# ROM monitor with the MMU off), this runs against a board that IS booting from NAND
7	# — either marvin, or a valid boot-region at91bootstrap looping on a corrupt app.
8	# We therefore can't rely on `reset init` catching a clean state. So: halt, force a
9	# known state (MMU/caches off, IRQs masked, WDT off), then probe DDR. Whatever booted
10	# from NAND already brought up clocks + DDR3L, so if the probe round-trips we load
11	# u-boot straight into that DDR. Only a genuinely cold controller (erased NAND → ROM
12	# monitor) runs the init-and-stop bootstrap. Never init DDR twice: re-running the
13	# bootstrap's DDR3L init on a live MPDDRC mistrains it (reads shift by a halfword).
14	
15	proc load_uboot {bootstrap_elf boot_entry uboot_bin} {
16	    # reset init recovers from any state (incl. a board wedged by a prior failed
17	    # attempt) and disables the watchdog. NAND boots before the post-reset halt
18	    # lands, so the core is caught mid-marvin with MMU + caches ON.
19	    reset init
20	
21	    # Force MMU + I/D caches off so DDR + peripherals are physically addressable,
22	    # invalidate caches + TLBs, and mask IRQ/FIQ (SVC mode). Without this, the
23	    # bootstrap/u-boot load lands under marvin's virtual mapping and aborts.
24	    set sctlr [arm mrc 15 0 1 0 0]
25	    arm mcr 15 0 1 0 0 [expr {$sctlr & ~0x1005}]   ;# clear M(0), C(2), I(12)
26	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0     ;# invalidate I-cache
27	    arm mcr 15 0 7 6 0 0     ;# invalidate D-cache
28	    arm mcr 15 0 8 7 0 0     ;# invalidate TLBs
29	    reg cpsr 0x000000d3
30	
31	    # DDR up? Probe it directly rather than inferring from the PC. DDR is already
32	    # usable at catch time in every case except a genuinely cold controller: marvin
33	    # running from NAND, OR a valid boot-region at91bootstrap that brought DDR up and
34	    # is now looping on a corrupt app (JP3 in) — that bootstrap is caught in SRAM, so
35	    # a PC test would wrongly call it "cold". Only an erased NAND (ROM/SAM-BA monitor)
36	    # leaves DDR cold and needs bootstrap-none. Re-running bootstrap-none's DDR3L init
37	    # on an already-initialized MPDDRC mistrains it (reads come back shifted by a
38	    # halfword), so we must never init DDR twice. The u-boot load below overwrites
39	    # 0x23f00000, so clobbering it with the probe pattern is harmless.
40	    set ddr_ok 0
41	    catch {
42	        write_memory 0x23f00000 32 {0xdeadbeef 0x12345678}
43	        set rb [read_memory 0x23f00000 32 2]
44	        if {[lindex $rb 0] == 0xdeadbeef && [lindex $rb 1] == 0x12345678} { set ddr_ok 1 }
45	    }
46	    if {$ddr_ok} {
47	        echo ">>> DDR already initialized (probe ok) — loading u-boot directly"
48	    } else {
49	        echo ">>> DDR cold — running init-and-stop bootstrap first"
50	        # Adaptive clocking (RTCK) is mandatory while the bootstrap runs: at a fixed
51	        # TCK, OpenOCD loses JTAG sync when lowlevel_clock_init switches the master
52	        # clock and wait_halt catches a garbage state (see load-ram.cfg). Enter in
53	        # ARM/Supervisor with IRQ+FIQ masked, the reset state the bootstrap expects.
54	        adapter speed 0
55	        reg cpsr 0x000000d3
56	        load_image $bootstrap_elf
57	        arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
58	        resume $boot_entry
59	        wait_halt 6000
60	        echo ">>> at91bootstrap init complete: clocks + DDR up"
61	    }
62	
63	    adapter speed 6000
64	    arm7_9 dcc_downloads enable
65	    load_image $uboot_bin 0x23f00000 bin
66	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
67	
68	    echo ">>> starting u-boot — JTAG done; erasing NAND from the console"
69	    resume 0x23f00000
70	}
71
```

 `./firmware/marvin/openocd/nand_console.py`

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Drive the marvin u-boot console over the DBGU serial port for NAND ops.
3	
4	Shared by program-nand.sh and erase-nand.sh. Run via uv so pyserial is present:
5	    uv run --with pyserial python nand_console.py <port> <op> [args...]
6	
7	Ops:
8	    probe                       open the port exclusively and exit (pre-flight)
9	    erase   <region|chip>       erase boot+app region (0x0..0x100000) or whole chip
10	    program <ba> <bo> <bs>      erase 0x0..0x100000, then nand-write the boot region
11	            <aa> <ao> <as>      from DDR <ba> and the app from DDR <aa>, and verify
12	                                both against the staged DDR copies (cmp.b)
13	
14	All ops first wait for a STABLE U-Boot prompt (so commands aren't eaten by the
15	"Hit any key to stop autoboot" countdown). nand commands are retried once if their
16	expected keyword is missing. Exit status is 0 only on confirmed success.
17	"""
18	import sys, time
19	
20	try:
21	    import serial
22	except ImportError:
23	    sys.exit("nand_console: pyserial missing — run via: uv run --with pyserial python ...")
24	
25	BAUD = 115200
26	RB1 = "0x24000000"   # scratch DDR for boot-region read-back
27	RB2 = "0x24800000"   # scratch DDR for app read-back
28	
29	
30	def open_port(port):
31	    # macOS cu.* devices are exclusive: a second open fails with EBUSY, so this
32	    # cleanly detects a console already held by screen/minicom/etc.
33	    try:
34	        return serial.Serial(port, BAUD, timeout=0.3, exclusive=True)
35	    except Exception as e:
36	        sys.exit(f"nand_console: cannot open console {port}: {e}\n"
37	                 f"  In use elsewhere (screen/minicom)? Close it, or set CONSOLE=<node>.")
38	
39	
40	def wait_prompt(ser, timeout=12):
41	    end = time.time() + timeout
42	    while time.time() < end:
43	        ser.write(b"\r\n"); time.sleep(0.4)
44	        buf = ser.read(8192)
45	        if buf.rstrip().endswith(b"U-Boot>"):
46	            time.sleep(0.3)
47	            if not ser.read(8192):          # quiet → prompt settled (autoboot stopped)
48	                return True
49	    return False
50	
51	
52	def cmd(ser, c, t=120):
53	    ser.reset_input_buffer(); ser.write(c.encode() + b"\r\n")
54	    end = time.time() + t; buf = b""
55	    while time.time() < end:
56	        d = ser.read(4096)
57	        if d:
58	            buf += d
59	            if buf.rstrip().endswith(b"U-Boot>"): break
60	    txt = buf.decode("utf-8", "replace")
61	    print(f"\n=== $ {c} ===\n" + txt)
62	    return txt
63	
64	
65	def run(ser, c, expect, t=120):
66	    out = cmd(ser, c, t)
67	    if expect not in out:                   # raced the prompt — resync and retry once
68	        print(f">>> '{c}' missing '{expect}'; resyncing prompt and retrying")
69	        wait_prompt(ser); out = cmd(ser, c, t)
70	    return out
71	
72	
73	def main():
74	    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
75	        sys.exit("usage: nand_console.py <port> <probe|erase|program> [args...]")
76	    port, op = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
77	    ser = open_port(port)
78	
79	    if op == "probe":
80	        ser.close(); print(f"nand_console: {port} available"); return 0
81	
82	    print(">>> connecting to u-boot console (booting + stopping autoboot)...",
83	          flush=True)
84	    if not wait_prompt(ser):
85	        sys.exit(f"nand_console: no stable U-Boot prompt on {port} (is u-boot running?)")
86	
87	    if op == "erase":
88	        scope = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "region"
89	        ecmd = "nand erase.chip" if scope == "chip" else "nand erase 0x0 0x100000"
90	        run(ser, ecmd, "NAND erase")
91	        cmd(ser, f"nand read {RB1} 0x0 0x1000")
92	        chk = cmd(ser, f"md.l {RB1} 4")
93	        ser.close()
94	        ok = "ffffffff ffffffff" in chk
95	        print("\n>>> NAND erased (boot region all-0xff)." if ok
96	              else "\n>>> WARNING: erase not confirmed — check output above.")
97	        return 0 if ok else 1
98	
99	    if op == "program":
100	        ba, bo, bs, aa, ao, asz = sys.argv[3:9]
101	        # Chip-erase, not a fixed-size region erase. `nand write` needs erased
102	        # (0xff) pages, and the boot bootstrap reads a fixed CONFIG_IMG_SIZE window
103	        # (>= the app) from 0x40000 at boot — every page it writes AND every page
104	        # that window reads must be clean, or PMECC fails on a stale/half-written
105	        # page. A hardcoded region erase silently undershoots once the app grows
106	        # past it; chip-erase always covers both regardless of image or IMG_SIZE.
107	        run(ser, "nand erase.chip", "NAND erase")
108	        run(ser, f"nand write {ba} {bo} {bs}", "written")     # boot region
109	        run(ser, f"nand write {aa} {ao} {asz}", "written")    # app
110	        cmd(ser, f"nand read {RB1} {bo} {bs}")
111	        v1 = cmd(ser, f"cmp.b {ba} {RB1} {bs}")
112	        cmd(ser, f"nand read {RB2} {ao} {asz}")
113	        v2 = cmd(ser, f"cmp.b {aa} {RB2} {asz}")
114	        ser.close()
115	        ok = "were the same" in v1 and "were the same" in v2
116	        print("\n>>> NAND programmed and verified." if ok
117	              else "\n>>> WARNING: verify failed — check output above.")
118	        return 0 if ok else 1
119	
120	    ser.close()
121	    sys.exit(f"nand_console: unknown op '{op}'")
122	
123	
124	if __name__ == "__main__":
125	    sys.exit(main())
126
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# guitar — Specification
2	
3	> What guitar *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, firmware design, milestones).
4	> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.
5	
6	> **Status: working on hardware.** The T1S PLCA follower is up (chipRev read, link
7	> synced), receives marvin's command over T1S and actuates the Wii GPIOs, sends a
8	> presence heartbeat, and exposes a debug-UART CLI. Remaining work is the full
9	> multi-node system (G3) — see §6 and [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md).
10	
11	## 1. Purpose
12	
13	guitar is the **Wii-guitar actuator node** on the marvin T1S bus. It receives a 1-byte
14	button bitmask from [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md) over 10BASE-T1S and drives a real Wii
15	guitar controller's buttons via open-drain GPIO. It does **no sensing and no game logic** —
16	it is purely the actuation half of what today's [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) firmware
17	does, lifted onto its own node.
18	
19	This split lets sensing (detector nodes) and actuation (guitar nodes) live on separate nodes
20	of one PLCA bus, with marvin selecting the active one of each class (see top-level
21	[`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) §2 "Node classes"). Multiple guitar variants may coexist on the bus.
22	
23	The actuation logic is a direct port of fretboard's [`cmd_receive.c`](../fretboard/cmd_receive.c)
24	(bitmask → open-drain assert / tri-state release) — it has no detector dependencies. fretboard
25	keeps actuating until this node is proven; marvin flips its command target then.
26	
27	## 2. Hardware
28	
29	| Spec | Value |
30	|------|-------|
31	| Device | PIC32CM PL10 (same family as fretboard; Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) |
32	| Toolchain | XC32 |
33	| MAC-PHY | LAN8651 (10BASE-T1S), SPI Mode 0, ≤ ~12 MHz on the 24 MHz part |
34	
35	**To be fixed when the guitar MCC project is generated** (Greg, in MPLAB — same shape as
36	marvin's FLEXCOM4 setup):
37	
38	- One SERCOM in **SPI-master mode** (Mode 0: CPOL=0/CPHA=0, MSB first) for the LAN8651, plus
39	  GPIO for `CS_N` (hardware SS if held across a transaction, else bit-banged), `IRQ_N`
40	  (external-interrupt pin), and `RST`.
41	- Seven **open-drain** button-output GPIOs (assert = drive low, release = input/tri-state so the
42	  controller's pull-up restores idle), bit layout matching the wire command:
43	
44	  | Bit | Output |
45	  |----:|--------|
46	  | 0 | Green fret |
47	  | 1 | Red fret |
48	  | 2 | Yellow fret |
49	  | 3 | Blue fret |
50	  | 4 | Orange fret |
51	  | 5 | Strum down |
52	  | 6 | Strum up |
53	
54	- A periodic timer (TC) tick to service the bus / apply commands (no 240 Hz ADC scan — that's
55	  the detector's job).
56	
57	PoDL on the pair powers the node (transparent to firmware; see [T1S/PoDL link](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §6).
58	
59	## 3. The T1S link
60	
61	A **PLCA follower** — the mirror of marvin's coordinator glue, reusing the shared
62	[`third_party/oa-tc6-lib`](../../third_party/oa-tc6-lib) and the same L2 framing:
63	
64	- **Node id 2**, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:02` (addressing scheme: [T1S/PoDL link](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §7.1).
65	- `TC6_Init` + `TC6Regs_Init(enablePlca=true, nodeId=2, nodeCount=8, …)` — follower, **not**
66	  coordinator.
67	- Custom ethertype `0x88B5`; marvin's command rides as a 1-byte payload inside the 14-byte
68	  Ethernet header. The guitar accepts frames addressed to its MAC from the coordinator.
69	- **Bare-metal** (no FreeRTOS on PL10): the TC6 service loop runs from the main loop / timer
70	  tick, not a task; `IRQ_N` is wired to a SERCOM-EIC pin (not a PIO controller as on marvin).
71	
72	The marvin-side reference for all of this is [`firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c`](../marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c)
73	(coordinator) — the follower inverts the roles: RX the command, no detector-stream TX.
74	
75	## 4. Firmware design (to build)
76	
77	1. **Bring-up:** reset the LAN8651 (`RST` pulse), configure SPI (Mode 0), `TC6_Init` +
78	   `TC6Regs_Init` as follower id 2. Gate: read chip revision + PLCA *follower* status.
79	2. **RX path:** TC6 delivers the marvin command frame → validate ethertype `0x88B5` → take the
80	   1-byte payload as the button bitmask → apply to the 7 GPIOs (port fretboard's
81	   `cmd_receive_apply_mask` logic).
82	3. **TX path:** none required initially. Optional `applied_mask` telemetry back to marvin (for
83	   edge-ai zero-skew labels) is **deferred** with the edge-ai re-homing effort.
84	4. **Service:** call `TC6_Service` from the main loop / tick, woken by `IRQ_N`.
85	5. **CLI** (debug aid, on the SERCOM1 UART via embedded-cli, static allocation): `t1s` (link /
86	   sync / chipRev / PLCA / counters), `btn <mask>` and `tap <mask> [ms]` drive the button GPIOs
87	   directly — so the Wii-guitar wiring can be exercised before the T1S link is up.
88	
89	## 5. What this is *not*
90	
91	- **Not a sensor.** No phototransistors, no ADC — sensing is the detector node's job.
92	- **Not an on-device model.** The edge-ai MODEL_DRIVEN inference stays on fretboard for now;
93	  re-homing it (detector infers → T1S → guitar) is out of scope.
94	- **Not a game brain.** No chord/strum timing — marvin's timing pipeline owns that and sends
95	  the resulting bitmask.
96	- **Not the PLCA coordinator.** marvin (node 0) beacons the cycle; guitar is a follower.
97	
98	## 6. Milestones
99	
100	| Status | Item |
101	|---|---|
102	| ✅ | **G0** — guitar MCC project: SERCOM0 SPI (Mode 0), EIC EXTINT13 (falling) on `IRQ_N`=PA13, `CS`=PA15 / `RST`=PA14 GPIO, 7 button GPIOs, SERCOM1 debug UART (CS/IRQ_N reassigned to match wiring) |
103	| ✅ | **G1** — T1S follower bring-up on hardware: `LAN8651 up - chipRev=2 … PLCA follower id=2/8` |
104	| ✅ | **G2** — end-to-end: marvin's command over T1S → the addressed Wii GPIO asserts |
105	| ✅ | **CLI** — `t1s`/`btn`/`tap`/`id`/`plca` on the debug UART (embedded-cli). Drives the Wii-guitar GPIOs locally and reports T1S link/sync/PLCA status. |
106	| ✅ | **Heartbeat** — periodic presence frame (ethertype `0x88B6`) to the coordinator so marvin's `nodes` shows this node present |
107	| 🔭 | **G3** — full system: `fretboard` (detector) + `guitar` (actuator) both on the bus with marvin selecting the active of each (marvin already targets the guitar; needs the fretboard moved to T1S) |
108
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# T1S inter-node link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL
2	
3	Engineering detail for the marvin↔node link over **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet**
4	(with planned "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines). System-level summary and rationale live
5	in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) §2/§6; this document holds the detail.
6	
7	Status: **built and working between marvin (PLCA coordinator, node 0) and the
8	[`guitar`](../firmware/guitar/SPEC.md) actuator node (follower, node 2)** as of
9	2026-06-17. A LAN8651 MAC-PHY at each end over SPI + the OPEN Alliance TC6 driver
10	([`third_party/oa-tc6-lib`](../third_party/oa-tc6-lib)); a custom L2 header
11	(ethertype `0x88B5`) carries the existing 1-byte command bitmask; a presence
12	heartbeat (`0x88B6`, §7.2) plus link / `nodes` diagnostics run on both ends.
13	
14	The [`fretboard`](../firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) firmware to join as node 1 is
15	**written** (2026-06-17, `t1s_detector.{c,h}`), **T1S-only** (the old UART path +
16	build flags removed). It is a **sense+actuate** node: it streams its 17-byte data
17	frame to the coordinator (`0x88B5`, logging) **and** sends its on-device model's
18	inferred 1-byte command **directly to the guitar node** (`0x88B5`, dst `02:..:02`) —
19	peer-to-peer actuation — plus a `0x88B6` heartbeat. Its MCC config is done (SERCOM0
20	SPI + CS/RST/IRQ_N, mirror of guitar G0); remaining is the build-wiring + on-hardware
21	bring-up. marvin's RX side is already in place (node-table id 1 + `fretboard_link.c`
22	T1S frame handler); marvin keeps a `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` build flag
23	(§8). **PoDL is design-direction only** (not built) — the link is separately powered
24	during bring-up. Addressing in §7.1; the scope widened from a 2-node UART swap to
25	this multi-node PLCA bus on 2026-06-16.
26	
27	> **Command-plane note:** with the fretboard driving the guitar directly, two nodes
28	> can address the guitar (marvin and the fretboard). There is no active-source
29	> arbitration yet — the guitar applies whoever transmitted last, so only one should
30	> be armed at a time. marvin-side active-detector/active-guitar selection is the
31	> follow-up (it currently picks `node_for_type(GUITAR)`).
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 1. Why T1S here
36	
37	- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
38	  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
39	  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
40	- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
41	  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
42	- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
43	  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
44	- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
45	  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
46	  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
47	  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.
48	
49	## 2. The part: LAN8651B1
50	
51	A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
52	PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
53	TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
54	to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
55	over ~5 pins.
56	
57	Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):
58	
59	- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
60	- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
61	- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.
62	
63	SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
64	`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.
65	
66	**SPI mode — Mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first.** Mandated by the OA TC6
67	v1.1 spec the part conforms to, and confirmed in the LAN8650/1 datasheet
68	(DS60001734 §5.1 *SPI Format*, §9 timing): "on the rising edge of SCLK the data
69	is captured, while on the falling edge … the data will change … always
70	transferred most significant bit/byte first," and the `tcss` ("CS_N low to SCLK
71	rising") timing means **SCLK idles low** → CPOL = 0, sample-on-leading-edge →
72	CPHA = 0. Host SPI-master config: 8-bit words, MSB first, CPOL = 0 / CPHA = 0
73	(Harmony: *Clock Polarity = Idle Low*, *Clock Phase = Valid Leading Edge*),
74	`CS_N` active-low idling high. The same mode applies to the fretboard SERCOM.
75	
76	Bring-up watch items: if the device-ID read returns `0x00`/`0xFF`, flip the
77	Harmony phase setting first (the dropdown wording varies) — the target is Mode 0.
78	And a TC6 chunk transaction (header + 64-byte data) needs `CS_N` held low for the
79	*whole* transfer; if the FLEXCOM SPI PLib toggles hardware CS per byte, drive
80	`CS_N` as a plain GPIO instead.
81	
82	## 3. What the host MCU must implement
83	
84	No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:
85	
86	1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
87	   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
88	2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
89	   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
90	   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
91	   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
92	   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
93	   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference driver
94	   ([`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib),
95	   §References) small enough to run on an Arduino — the candidate base for both
96	   ends here.
97	3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
98	   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
99	   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
100	   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
101	   - detector (fretboard, id 1) → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
102	   - command source → guitar (id 2): the 1-byte button bitmask — sent by marvin
103	     (timing pipeline) and/or directly by the active detector (fretboard's model,
104	     peer-to-peer).
105	
106	   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
107	   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
108	   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
109	   transport changed.
110	
111	## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)
112	
113	Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.
114	
115	| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
118	| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
119	| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
120	| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
121	| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |
122	
123	SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
124	(`BAUD=0`; not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling). Irrelevant for *throughput* (the wire
125	is 10 Mbps) but it **dominates command latency** — see §4.1. Both nodes brought up
126	at `BAUD=11` ≈ 1 MHz (conservative); planned bump to 12 MHz.
127	
128	Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.
129	
130	### 4.1 Command latency (fretboard → guitar)
131	
132	End-to-end for the fretboard's inferred command to drive the guitar GPIO, by stage
133	(worst case):
134	
135	| Stage | Worst case | Notes |
136	|---|---|---|
137	| Command-ready quantization | ~4.2 ms | model output gated to the fretboard's 240 Hz tick — kept deliberately (the model is timing-fit to this grid; see fretboard journal 2026-06-17). |
138	| Fretboard SPI TX to MAC-PHY | ~0.5–1.1 ms | 1 TC6 chunk = 68 B; **0.55 ms @ 1 MHz**, ~45 µs @ 12 MHz. +1 chunk if a data frame is queued ahead. |
139	| PLCA media access | ~0.2–0.5 ms | wait for the node's transmit opportunity (8-slot cycle, 3 active); +1 cycle if behind the data frame. **Not** the bottleneck. |
140	| Wire (10 Mbps) | ~0.06 ms | 60-byte min frame. |
141	| Guitar SPI RX + apply | ~0.6 ms | 1 chunk read; **0.55 ms @ 1 MHz**, ~45 µs @ 12 MHz. GPIO assert instant. |
142	| **Total** | **~6–7 ms** (≈2–3 ms typical) | |
143	
144	The two off-wire terms dominate: the 240 Hz tick (firmware, intentionally kept) and
145	the **1 MHz host SPI** (~0.55 ms/chunk each end). Raising both nodes' SPI to 12 MHz
146	removes ~1 ms; PLCA media access is already sub-ms. The command is edge-triggered
147	(sent on change, not waiting for the 50 ms refresh), so a new note isn't delayed by
148	the refresh. Analytical estimate — validate by scoping fretboard `SetCommand` →
149	guitar GPIO apply.
150	
151	## 5. marvin side
152	
153	marvin runs **FreeRTOS + Harmony (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free
154	netdev — it needs its own TC6 driver. The TC6 service runs as a task woken by
155	the LAN8651 `IRQ_N` (a PIO external interrupt → `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`, the
156	same pattern as `fretboard_link.c`'s RX path). The plan **adapts
157	[`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib)** (its
158	hardware-agnostic core + thin Harmony FLEXCOM-SPI glue), rather than writing a
159	TC6 from scratch — proven chunk/credit logic, and a **single portable `oa_tc6`
160	layer shared between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)** is itself a
161	tidy demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family.
162	marvin resources are not a concern. Hand-authored T1S code lives in
163	`firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/`, kept out of the MCC-generated `config/`
164	tree and added via `user.cmake` (same discipline as `perf_log`/`console`).
165	
166	## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)
167	
168	PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
169	coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
170	firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):
171	
172	- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
173	  DC onto the pair.
174	- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
175	  the PIC32CM rail.
176	- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
177	  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
178	  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.
179	
180	Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
181	helps the demonstration story.
182	
183	## 7. Topology — PLCA multidrop, marvin as coordinator
184	
185	**Decided (2026-06-16): PLCA from the start, multi-node.** The system is expected
186	to grow several nodes on one pair — multiple guitars and phototransistor
187	fretboard-detector nodes coexisting — so PLCA multidrop is a requirement, not just
188	headroom. marvin is the **PLCA coordinator (ID 0)**; every other node is a
189	follower. The single marvin↔fretboard link is brought up first, but the
190	addressing and demux are designed for N from the start so a new node joins with a
191	table entry, not a transport rewrite.
192	
193	### 7.1 Addressing (static — no discovery, keeps the M0+ node dumb)
194	
195	Followers are typed by **node class** (top-level [`SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) §2): **detector**
196	nodes are RX sources (each maps to a marvin `detector_id`); **guitar** (actuator) nodes are
197	command TX targets. marvin selects the active node of each class.
198	
199	| Node | Class | PLCA ID | MAC (locally administered) | Notes |
200	|---|---|---|---|---|
201	| marvin | coordinator | 0 | `02:00:00:00:00:00` | beacons the PLCA cycle; selects active detector + guitar |
202	| fretboard | detector | 1 | `02:00:00:00:00:01` | photo-ADC stream → `detector_id` 1; also commands the guitar (id 2) directly |
203	| guitar | guitar (actuator) | 2 | `02:00:00:00:00:02` | receives the 1-byte command bitmask (from marvin or a detector) |
204	| node *k* | (either) | *k* | `02:00:00:00:00:0k` | future detector/guitar variants |
205	
206	- One **custom ethertype** `0x88B5` (IEEE local/experimental range; no
207	  registration needed for a private bus) carries the existing payloads verbatim.
208	- A static **node table** on marvin maps `{PLCA ID, MAC, node_type}` → the bus
209	  `detector_id` (and the actuator target for TX). The single fretboard keeps
210	  `detector_id = 1`, matching today's `adc_fretboard` bus slot. No discovery /
211	  enumeration protocol — the table is compiled in.
212	- The 17-byte fretboard→marvin frame and the 1-byte marvin→fretboard bitmask ride
213	  inside the Ethernet payload unchanged; marvin demuxes incoming frames by src MAC
214	  and addresses outgoing ones to a specific node.
215	
216	### 7.2 Presence heartbeat
217	
218	PLCA has **no node discovery**, so the coordinator can't enumerate who's on the
219	bus. A lightweight application heartbeat fills that gap: each follower
220	periodically (≈500 ms) sends a small frame to the coordinator
221	(`02:00:00:00:00:00`) under a **separate ethertype `0x88B6`** so marvin routes it
222	apart from data/command traffic (`0x88B5`). marvin stamps a per-node "last seen"
223	on receipt and reports it via the `nodes` console command (present = a heartbeat
224	within ~2 s).
225	
226	Payload (8 bytes): `version(1)`, `node_type(1)` (1=detector, 2=guitar), `node_id(1)`,
227	`flags(1)` (bit0 = follower synced), `seq(u32 LE)`. marvin derives the node from the
228	src MAC; the payload is informational (seq enables drop detection).
229	
230	## 8. Transport coexistence
231	
232	The marvin `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API is preserved; the
233	actuator command now targets the guitar node (`T1SLink_SendToGuitar`). UART and
234	T1S transports live behind a `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` **build flag**.
235	The `t1s` branch builds **T1S by default**; UART stays one (commented) line away in
236	`user.cmake` as a fallback during the fretboard's own transition.
237	
238	## 9. Decisions & open items
239	
240	**Built and working (2026-06-17):** marvin coordinator (id 0) ↔ guitar follower
241	(id 2) over T1S — command TX, presence heartbeat, and link/`nodes` diagnostics on
242	both ends. The earlier prerequisites (a FLEXCOM/SERCOM in SPI-master mode via MCC;
243	the `oa-tc6-lib` submodule) are resolved.
244	
245	Open / future:
246	
247	- **Fretboard node (id 1) — firmware written 2026-06-17** (`t1s_detector.{c,h}`,
248	  T1S-only). Sense+actuate: streams the 17-byte data frame to marvin (RX/detector path
249	  + node-table slot already in place) **and** sends its model's inferred command
250	  directly to the guitar (id 2). MCC config done. **Remaining:** build-wiring + on-
251	  hardware bring-up (banner `LAN8651 up … PLCA follower id=1/8`; confirm the
252	  `FRETBOARD_RAW` rate holds ≈240 Hz — data + command + heartbeat now share the node's
253	  PLCA TX).
254	- **Active-source arbitration.** Both marvin and the fretboard can address the guitar
255	  (`02:..:02`); the guitar applies whoever transmitted last. Need marvin-side
256	  active-detector/active-guitar selection so exactly one source drives at a time
257	  (today: single guitar → `node_for_type(GUITAR)`; the fretboard's SW0 is an interim
258	  manual arm).
259	- **PoDL** supply voltage + PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware) — not
260	  built; the link is separately powered for now.
261	- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.
262	
263	## References
264	
265	- **OA TC6 driver (candidate base, both ends):**
266	  [`MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib`](https://github.com/MicrochipTech/oa-tc6-lib) —
267	  Microchip's open-source OPEN Alliance TC6 (10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial
268	  Interface) library: SPI chunk protocol + control transactions, used as the
269	  shared portable layer (§3, §5).
270	- LAN8650/1 (LAN8651B1) datasheet — 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY Ethernet Controller with
271	  SPI, on [Microchip online docs](https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/) /
272	  the LAN8651 product page.
273	- OPEN Alliance *10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface* specification (TC6), v1.1.
274
```

```text
1	# marvin ↔ fauxmote command link
2	
3	> Protocol spec for the control link between **marvin** (SAM9X75 runtime brain) and
4	> **fauxmote** (ESP32 Wiimote/guitar emulator). marvin sends controller input;
5	> fauxmote reflects it to the real Wii. This is an alternative to the T1S
6	> `guitar` actuator node — fauxmote *becomes* the controller instead of pressing a
7	> real one.
8	>
9	> Companion docs: [`firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md`](../firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md),
10	> [`firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md`](../firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md), and the
11	> T1S bus link [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](t1s-podl-link.md) (the eventual second transport).
12	
13	**Protocol version:** 1. Both ends are compiled to a matching version for now
14	(no runtime negotiation); the version is reported in `STATUS` so a mismatch is
15	visible.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. Design goals
20	
21	1. **Low-latency gameplay control.** The hot path — frets, strum, whammy — is a
22	   single tiny fixed message fauxmote acts on immediately. No handshake, no ack,
23	   no per-message state machine.
24	2. **Absolute state, latest-wins.** Every input message carries the *complete
25	   current state* of its group, not deltas or events. Idempotent: a dropped or
26	   corrupt frame self-corrects on the next one. This matches both ends — marvin's
27	   existing 1-byte guitar bitmask is latest-wins, and fauxmote already streams the
28	   current state to the Wii every ~15 ms regardless of the command source.
29	3. **Transport-independent message layer.** The message bytes (§4) are identical
30	   over any physical layer. UART is the first transport (§3); 10BASE-T1S is the
31	   planned second (§6). Only the framing/binding changes.
32	4. **Fail safe.** If the command link goes quiet, fauxmote releases all inputs —
33	   a dropped link must never leave a note held.
34	
35	## 2. Layering
36	
37	```
38	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
39	  │  L3  Message layer   TYPE + fixed payload     │  ← identical on every transport
40	  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
41	  │  L2  Framing layer   delimit + integrity      │  ← UART: SOF/LEN/CRC (§3.2)
42	  │                                               │     T1S: none (Ethernet FCS) (§6)
43	  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
44	  │  L1  Physical        UART now / T1S later      │
45	  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
46	```
47	
48	Both firmwares implement the message layer against a thin transport seam
49	(`send(type, payload, len)` / `on_message(type, payload, len)`); UART and T1S are
50	two implementations of that seam (§7).
51	
52	## 3. UART transport (transport #1)
53	
54	### 3.1 Physical
55	
56	| Parameter | Value |
57	|---|---|
58	| Baud | **1 000 000** (1 Mbaud), 8-N-1, no flow control |
59	| Wiring | 3 wires: marvin TX → fauxmote RX, fauxmote TX → marvin RX, common GND |
60	| marvin port | a spare FLEXCOM in USART mode (TBD at integration; the legacy fretboard UART is freed as that path moves to T1S) |
61	| fauxmote port | **UART1** on the Feather V2's broken-out RX=`GPIO7` / TX=`GPIO8` (the board's second hardware UART, `Serial1`) — **not** UART0, which is the USB-CDC console/CLI |
62	
63	Baud is generous on purpose: a 7-byte hot frame is ~70 µs on the wire, negligible
64	against the Wii's ~15 ms report period, so the link adds no meaningful latency.
65	Baud is a compile-time constant on both ends and may be lowered if wiring
66	reliability requires it.
67	
68	### 3.2 Framing
69	
70	Each message is wrapped in a frame:
71	
72	```
73	  ┌──────┬──────┬──────┬───────────────┬──────┐
74	  │ SOF  │ TYPE │ LEN  │  payload[LEN]  │ CRC8 │
75	  │ 0x7E │      │      │                │      │
76	  └──────┴──────┴──────┴───────────────┴──────┘
77	```
78	
79	- `SOF` = `0x7E` — start-of-frame marker.
80	- `TYPE` — message type (§4).
81	- `LEN` — payload length in bytes (0..255). Fixed per type in v1; carried anyway
82	  for extensibility and to bound the frame during resync.
83	- `payload` — `LEN` bytes (§5).
84	- `CRC8` — over `TYPE`, `LEN`, and the payload bytes (not `SOF`).
85	  Polynomial `0x07` (CRC-8/CCITT), init `0x00`, no reflection.
86	
87	Framing overhead is 4 bytes; a 3-byte `GUITAR` payload is 7 bytes on the wire.
88	
89	**Receiver rules:**
90	- Scan for `SOF`, then read `TYPE`/`LEN`, then `LEN` payload bytes, then `CRC8`.
91	- If the CRC fails, or `LEN` disagrees with the known length for `TYPE`, **discard
92	  and rescan** from the next `0x7E`. (A `0x7E` inside a payload that causes a false
93	  frame is rejected by the CRC and the receiver re-syncs on the real boundary.)
94	- `TYPE = 0x00` is never valid — treat as noise and rescan.
95	- No ack on any message; corruption self-heals on the next state frame.
96	
97	## 4. Message types
98	
99	| TYPE | Name | Dir | LEN | Status | Purpose |
100	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
101	| `0x01` | `GUITAR` | m→f | 3 | v1 | Hot gameplay input (frets/strum/whammy/aux). |
102	| `0x02` | `WIIMOTE` | m→f | 4 | v1 | Menu-nav input (core buttons, D-pad, analog stick). |
103	| `0x03` | `LINK_CMD` | m→f | 1 | v1 | Bluetooth link management (pair/stop/reconnect/unlink/ext). |
104	| `0x04` | `ACCEL` | m→f | 3 | planned | Wiimote accelerometer state (tilt → star power, motion). |
105	| `0x05` | `POINTER` | m→f | 3 | planned | IR pointer position (bare-Wiimote menu nav). |
106	| `0x81` | `STATUS` | f→m | 4 | v1 | Link/connection/extension state + last-command result. |
107	
108	`0x00` reserved (invalid). `0x06`–`0x7F` reserved for future m→f; `0x82`–`0xFF`
109	for future f→m (telemetry). Each message updates one **independent slice** of the
110	latched controller state (§4.1) — new slices are added as new types without
111	touching existing ones.
112	
113	### 4.1 State model — independent slices, latched with timeout
114	
115	fauxmote holds a **single controller state** (buttons, whammy, stick, accelerometer,
116	IR pointer, extension bytes). Its report sender already assembles the Wii Bluetooth
117	report from that state every ~15 ms, independent of the command source.
118	
119	Each message type updates **one independent slice** of that state and nothing else —
120	`GUITAR` never touches the accel slice, `POINTER` never touches the frets, etc. So
121	the messages are fully independent: marvin sends whichever slices it needs, at
122	whatever rate each needs, in any order. fauxmote latches each slice and keeps
123	sending it to the Wii until a newer message for that slice replaces it.
124	
125	A **single link watchdog** (§6) guards the whole state: any control message
126	(`GUITAR`/`WIIMOTE`/`ACCEL`/`POINTER`) resets it. So long as fauxmote receives *any*
127	control message within the timeout, it holds all latched slices; if the link goes
128	fully quiet past the timeout, it reverts *all* slices to their safe defaults. This
129	is the core of the design — the wire protocol is a set of independent state-slice
130	updaters over one live link, not a single monolithic frame.
131	
132	## 5. Message payloads
133	
134	All fields are single bytes, so byte order is irrelevant. Bits are numbered
135	`bit0` = LSB. Reserved bits/bytes are sent `0` and ignored on receive.
136	
137	### 5.1 `GUITAR` (m→f, 3 bytes) — the hot path
138	
139	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| 0 | fret/strum mask | `bit0` Green, `bit1` Red, `bit2` Yellow, `bit3` Blue, `bit4` Orange, `bit5` Strum-Down, `bit6` Strum-Up, `bit7` reserved |
142	| 1 | whammy | raw 5-bit extension value `0..31`: rest ≈ `0x10`, fully pressed ≈ `0x1F` (upper bits 0) |
143	| 2 | aux | `bit0` Start (`+`), `bit1` Select (`−`), `bit2` Pedal, `bit3` Star-Power*, `bit4`–`7` reserved |
144	
145	Byte 0 is **bit-identical to marvin's existing guitar-node command bitmask** (the
146	[`T1SLink_SendToGuitar`](../firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.h) mask),
147	so marvin feeds the same computed mask to either actuation sink with no
148	translation.
149	
150	\* Star-Power is a semantic bit: fauxmote maps it to whatever mechanism activates
151	SP in-game (GH3 uses a Wiimote tilt, not a button — driven via the `ACCEL` slice,
152	§5.5). **Not implemented in fauxmote yet** (the emulator streams a fixed level
153	accel); a no-op until the `ACCEL` slice goes live.
154	
155	### 5.2 `WIIMOTE` (m→f, 4 bytes) — menu navigation
156	
157	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
158	|---|---|---|
159	| 0 | core buttons | `bit0` A, `bit1` B, `bit2` One, `bit3` Two, `bit4` Plus, `bit5` Minus, `bit6` Home, `bit7` reserved |
160	| 1 | D-pad | `bit0` Up, `bit1` Down, `bit2` Left, `bit3` Right, `bit4`–`7` reserved |
161	| 2 | stick X | `0..63`, center `32` (the guitar extension's 6-bit analog stick) |
162	| 3 | stick Y | `0..63`, center `32` |
163	
164	The analog stick is the guitar-mode Home-menu control (the IR pointer is
165	physically blocked when the Wiimote is seated in the guitar — see the fauxmote
166	journal). Bare-Wiimote menu nav uses the separate `POINTER` slice (§5.6).
167	
168	### 5.5 `ACCEL` (m→f, 3 bytes) — *planned*
169	
170	Wiimote accelerometer state, the same slice used to synthesize star-power tilt in
171	GH3 and general motion input. Independent of `GUITAR`.
172	
173	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
174	|---|---|---|
175	| 0 | accel X | `0..255`, center `128` (mapped to the Wiimote's accel range) |
176	| 1 | accel Y | `0..255`, center `128` |
177	| 2 | accel Z | `0..255`, center `128` (gravity ~+1 g at rest) |
178	
179	Default when the slice is stale/absent: **level** (all `128`, i.e. Z at +1 g). Not
180	consumed by fauxmote yet — the emulator currently streams a fixed level accel;
181	`ACCEL` goes live when fauxmote drives the accel field from this slice (which also
182	makes the `GUITAR` aux star-power bit meaningful). A finer 10-bit encoding can be
183	added later without changing the type.
184	
185	### 5.6 `POINTER` (m→f, 3 bytes) — *planned*
186	
187	IR pointer position, for bare-Wiimote menu navigation (feeds
188	`Wiimote_SetPointer`/`ClearPointer`). Independent of `WIIMOTE`. Moot while the
189	Wiimote is seated in the guitar (camera blocked) — use the analog stick there.
190	
191	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
192	|---|---|---|
193	| 0 | x | `0..255` → `0..1`, `0` = left edge |
194	| 1 | y | `0..255` → `0..1`, `0` = top edge |
195	| 2 | flags | `bit0` visible (`0` = pointer off / off-screen), `bit1`–`7` reserved |
196	
197	Default when the slice is stale/absent: **off** (pointer off-screen).
198	
199	### 5.3 `LINK_CMD` (m→f, 1 byte) — Bluetooth link management
200	
201	Mirrors the fauxmote CLI so marvin owns the whole link lifecycle. Fire-and-forget;
202	the result is reflected in the next `STATUS`.
203	
204	| Byte | Field | Values |
205	|---|---|---|
206	| 0 | opcode | `0x01` PAIR (enter sync/pairing) · `0x02` STOP (leave pairing) · `0x03` RECONNECT · `0x04` UNLINK (erase bond) · `0x05` EXT_ATTACH · `0x06` EXT_DETACH · `0x07` STATUS_REQ (send a `STATUS` now) |
207	
208	### 5.4 `STATUS` (f→m, 4 bytes) — the uplink
209	
210	Sent on any state change **and** as a heartbeat (~2 Hz) so marvin can tell the link
211	is alive and gate/annotate commands.
212	
213	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
214	|---|---|---|
215	| 0 | flags | `bit0` discoverable, `bit1` connected (HID data channel), `bit2` assigned (Wii gave a player slot), `bit3` ext-attached, `bit4` pairing-active, `bit5` bonded (bond in NVS), `bit6`–`7` reserved |
216	| 1 | player_slot | `0` = none, else `1..4` |
217	| 2 | report_mode | the Wii's last-requested report ID (e.g. `0x37`), `0` if unknown |
218	| 3 | last_result | result of the most recent `LINK_CMD`: `0` = ok/idle, nonzero = error code |
219	
220	## 6. Semantics & timing
221	
222	- **Absolute / latest-wins, per slice.** Every input message carries the full
223	  current state of *its slice* (§4.1). fauxmote latches the most recent message per
224	  slice and reflects all latched slices in its next Wii report. No history, no
225	  ordering requirement beyond last-writer-wins within a slice.
226	- **Send policy (marvin).** Send a slice on any change; additionally resend it at a
227	  floor rate (~10 Hz) so a dropped frame self-corrects. Bursting faster than the Wii
228	  report cadence (~15 ms) is wasted. marvin sends only the slices it needs —
229	  `GUITAR` continuously during gameplay, `WIIMOTE`/`POINTER` only while navigating.
230	- **Fail-safe (fauxmote), one watchdog.** A single **link timeout** (200 ms
231	  default) is reset by *any* control message. While it holds, all latched slices
232	  stay in effect. On expiry (the link has gone fully quiet) fauxmote reverts *all*
233	  slices to their safe defaults at once — `GUITAR` frets/strum released + whammy
234	  rest (≈ `0x10`), `WIIMOTE` buttons released / stick centered, `ACCEL` level, `POINTER`
235	  off. A dead link never holds a note. (marvin's ~10 Hz refresh of at least one
236	  slice keeps the watchdog alive during normal play.)
237	- **`STATUS` cadence (fauxmote).** On every state change, plus a ~500 ms heartbeat,
238	  plus immediately on `STATUS_REQ`.
239	- **`LINK_CMD`** is fire-and-forget; marvin reads the outcome in the following
240	  `STATUS`.
241	
242	## 7. Implementation seam (both ends)
243	
244	Keep the message layer transport-agnostic so the T1S move (§8) is a transport swap,
245	not a rewrite.
246	
247	**fauxmote** — a new `marvin_link.c` module:
248	- Owns the second UART, the §3.2 framing/CRC, and message parse/dispatch (FreeRTOS
249	  task).
250	- On `GUITAR`/`WIIMOTE`/`LINK_CMD`, calls the **same module APIs the CLI uses**
251	  (`Wiimote_SetButton`, `Guitar_SetWhammy`, `Wiimote_SetPointer`,
252	  `Fauxmote_EnterPairing`/`StopPairing`/`Reconnect`/`Unlink`, `Wiimote_SetExtension`),
253	  so the link is a second front-end over existing logic — no behavior duplicated.
254	- Emits `STATUS` from the existing `Wiimote_Is*` / `Fauxmote_*` state.
255	- The CLI stays for manual bring-up/debug.
256	
257	**marvin** — `net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c` (implemented 2026-07-02):
258	- Owns the **FLEXCOM1 USART (PA28/PA29)** — the fretboard UART-transport pins, free
259	  while the guitar node rides T1S — and the framing. Exposes
260	  `Fauxmote_SendGuitar(mask, whammy, aux)` / `SendGuitarMask(mask)`,
261	  `Fauxmote_SendNav(...)`, `Fauxmote_SendCmd(op)`, and `Fauxmote_GetStatus(...)`.
262	- A TX task re-sends the latched `GUITAR` slice on change (low latency) and at a
263	  50 ms floor; an RX task parses the `STATUS` uplink.
264	- **Mirror-to-both** (not a switched sink): `FretboardLink_Send()` — the one choke
265	  point both producers (timing pipeline + `manual_control`) call — also calls
266	  `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask()`, so the T1S guitar node and fauxmote move in lock-step.
267	  `GUITAR` byte 0 == the T1S 7-bit mask. Compile-guarded to the T1S guitar build
268	  (fauxmote owns FLEXCOM1, mutually exclusive with a `TRANSPORT=UART` guitar).
269	
270	## 8. T1S transport (transport #2, future)
271	
272	When fauxmote (or a successor node) joins the T1S bus, the **message layer (§4–§5)
273	travels unchanged as the payload of a T1S Ethernet frame**:
274	
275	- The UART framing layer (§3.2) is dropped — the Ethernet frame provides delimiting
276	  and an FCS; `TYPE` + payload become the frame payload.
277	- Addressed marvin ↔ fauxmote-node like the other T1S nodes (see
278	  [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](t1s-podl-link.md) §7 for the addressing/ethertype scheme).
279	- Only the transport seam (§7) changes; message handling and semantics are identical.
280	
281	**Caveat:** the current ESP32 Feather has no 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY, so this transport
282	is hardware-dependent and genuinely future work; UART is the working link.
283	
284	## 9. Open questions
285	
286	- ~~Exact marvin FLEXCOM instance + pins~~ **settled 2026-07-02:** marvin =
287	  **FLEXCOM1 / PA28 (TX) / PA29 (RX)** (the fretboard UART-transport pins, free while
288	  the guitar rides T1S); fauxmote = UART1 on Feather RX=`GPIO7` / TX=`GPIO8`. Wiring:
289	  marvin PA28 → ESP `GPIO7`, ESP `GPIO8` → marvin PA29, common GND.
290	- When to make the planned `ACCEL` slice live in fauxmote (drive the Wiimote accel
291	  field from it) — this is what makes GH3 star power (`GUITAR` aux `bit3`) work.
292	- Whether `ACCEL` needs finer than 8-bit-per-axis for smooth tilt; 10-bit can be
293	  added under the same type.
294	- Runtime version negotiation (a `HELLO` exchange) if the two ends ever ship
295	  independently; unnecessary while both are built from this repo.
296	</content>
297	</invoke>
298
```

1	# fauxmote — Specification
2	
3	> What fauxmote *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, success criteria, milestones).
4	> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose
7	
8	fauxmote is an **ESP32 firmware that emulates a Nintendo Wiimote with an attached
9	Guitar Hero guitar extension**, speaking Bluetooth straight to a real Wii console.
10	It is a **parallel proof-of-concept** alternative to the existing actuation path:
11	today the [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) MCU physically presses buttons on a
12	*real* Wii guitar controller via open-drain GPIO. fauxmote instead *becomes* the
13	controller — eventually driven by [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md)'s high-level
14	fret/strum commands, removing the physical actuator + real controller from the loop.
15	
16	The fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative until fauxmote is proven; nothing
17	in marvin/fretboard/edge-ai changes as part of this subproject.
18	
19	## 2. Hardware
20	
21	| Component | Detail |
22	|---|---|
23	| Board | **Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2** (product 5400) — *original* dual-core ESP32 (Tensilica LX6), 8 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM, USB-C. |
24	| Radio | ESP32 has a **Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR)** radio — required, because the Wiimote link is Classic HID. (ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and would *not* work.) |
25	| Wii console | Real retail Wii; pairing via the sync button or the controller's 1+2 button. |
26	
27	## 3. The link fauxmote emulates (verified protocol facts)
28	
29	- **Transport:** Bluetooth Classic **HID** over L2CAP — PSM `0x11` (control),
30	  PSM `0x13` (data). Input reports (device→host) prefixed `0xa1`; output reports
31	  (host→device) prefixed `0xa2`.
32	- **Identity the Wii expects (SDP):** device name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`,
33	  VID `0x057e`, PID `0x0306`, matching Class-of-Device, and the Wiimote HID report
34	  descriptor.
35	- **Pairing PIN (legacy):** the PIN is a BD_ADDR in **reverse byte order** (raw 6
36	  bytes). The 1+2 temporary-pair flow uses the *Wiimote's own* address — which
37	  fauxmote knows — so fauxmote can answer the GAP PIN request itself.
38	- **Guitar extension:** identity bytes `00 00 A4 20 01 03` at register offset `0xfa`
39	  of the `0xa4` extension space. The 6-byte report (frets G/R/Y/B/O, strum up/down,
40	  whammy in byte 3, touch bar, analog stick, +/− buttons; **byte 0/1 bits 7-6 = 1**
41	  to identify a GH3 Les Paul) rides inside any extension-bearing data report — GH3
42	  streams mode `0x37`.
43	- **Guitar extension encryption (required for GH3):** GH3 writes `0x55`→`0xf0` and
44	  reads the ID in the clear (to tell GH3 vs GHWT), then `0xAA`→`0xf0` plus a 16-byte
45	  key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. After that the streamed report bytes *and* the `0x20`
46	  calibration must be encrypted with the standard Wii extension cipher; plaintext
47	  reads as garbage in-game.
48	
49	References: wiibrew [`Wiimote`](https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote) and
50	[`Guitar Hero (Wii) Guitars`](https://wiibrew.org/wiki/Wiimote/Extension_Controllers/Guitar_Hero_(Wii)_Guitars).
51	
52	## 4. Interfaces
53	
54	- **Downstream (fauxmote → Wii):** Bluetooth Classic HID, as above.
55	- **Upstream (commands → fauxmote):** the **marvin command link** — a layered
56	  message protocol, **UART first** (T1S later), specified in
57	  [`docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`](../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md). marvin sends a
58	  tiny fixed `GUITAR` hot message (fret/strum mask + whammy + aux), a `WIIMOTE` nav
59	  message (core buttons/D-pad/stick), and `LINK_CMD` (Bluetooth link management:
60	  pair/stop/reconnect/unlink/ext); fauxmote returns `STATUS`. Absolute/latest-wins;
61	  a link timeout releases all inputs. The link is a second front-end over the same
62	  module APIs the CLI uses. Early bring-up still uses the local CLI (§ below).
63	- **Debug:** USB-C CDC serial for flashing + logs (`idf.py monitor`).
64	
65	## 5. Software
66	
67	- **Framework:** ESP-IDF (v6.x; developed against v6.0.1), Bluedroid stack in **Bluetooth-Classic-only** mode
68	  (BLE disabled).
69	- **BT architecture (settled in Phase 1):** `esp_hidd` is *not* usable — the Wii
70	  rejects its SDP record and its hardcoded HID attributes/descriptor limits don't
71	  fit a Wiimote. Instead fauxmote serves a **byte-exact Wiimote SDP record** built
72	  via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` database API (`wiimote_sdp.c`; needs
73	  `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN`/`ATTR_LEN` raised) and handles HID over **raw L2CAP**
74	  (`esp_bt_l2cap`) on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). Legacy PIN pairing
75	  (SSP off; PIN = host BD_ADDR reversed). Detail + the record bytes in
76	  [`docs/wiimote-sdp.md`](docs/wiimote-sdp.md) and the journal.
77	- **Extension architecture:** extensions register with the base Wiimote through a
78	  small interface (`wiimote_ext.h`: register bank + report/button/reset hooks); the
79	  guitar lives in `guitar.c`, leaving `wiimote.c` extension-agnostic. The Wii
80	  extension cipher (`ext_crypto.c`) lives in the base — it captures the host's key
81	  handshake and encrypts outgoing extension data (streamed bytes + register reads),
82	  which Guitar Hero 3 requires.
83	- **Allocation:** application code follows the project's **static-allocation**
84	  preference (no `malloc` in our code). Bluedroid's internal allocation is
85	  framework-owned and out of scope.
86	
87	## 6. Milestones / success criteria
88	
89	| Phase | Goal | Done when |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| **0** ✅ | Toolchain + radio bring-up | Builds + flashes to the Feather V2; the board is discoverable by name in a PC/phone Bluetooth scan. |
92	| **1** ✅ | Bluetooth identity / pairing (highest risk) | A real Wii authenticates and opens the HID channels (PSM 0x11 control + 0x13 interrupt) without immediately dropping. *Done via custom SDP + raw L2CAP (§5).* |
93	| **2** ✅ | Core Wiimote emulation | Wii shows one stable connected Wiimote; emulated buttons drive the Home-menu cursor; connection survives minutes. Includes device-initiated reconnect after idle + keep-awake (see journal). |
94	| **3** ✅ | Guitar extension emulation | A real Guitar Hero / Rock Band Wii title detects the guitar and registers scripted fret+strum notes. *Done: GH3 detects the guitar and frets/strum/whammy register in-game, through the extension cipher (§3). Known open: GH3 game-launch handoff drops the link — workaround is to restart fauxmote after the game starts (see journal).* |
95	| **4** | Command source | Local test driver (serial console + canned patterns) exercises the emulator independently; a clean seam is left for the marvin link. *Protocol spec done ([`docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`](../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md)); `marvin_link.c` implementation pending.* |
96	
97	## 7. Out of scope
98	
99	- Retiring or modifying the fretboard GPIO-press path.
100	- The exact link wiring (marvin FLEXCOM instance + fauxmote UART GPIO pins) — set at integration.
101	- Any edge-ai retargeting toward fauxmote.
102
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# fauxmote
2	
3	ESP32 firmware that emulates a Nintendo Wiimote (with a Guitar Hero guitar
4	extension) to a real Wii console, on an **Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2** (product 5400).
5	
6	See [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) for what this is and [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md)
7	for the running plan, decisions, and open questions.

9	## Build & flash (ESP-IDF v6.x — developed against v6.0.1)
10	
11	```sh
12	. $IDF_PATH/export.sh          # activate the ESP-IDF environment
13	idf.py set-target esp32        # original ESP32 (Feather V2) — has Bluetooth Classic
14	idf.py build flash monitor     # build, flash over USB-C, open the serial log
15	```
16	
17	The board comes up as `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01` and, on a Wii red-SYNC press, pairs and
18	opens both HID channels (custom SDP record + raw L2CAP; see [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) §5
19	and the journal). Responding to the Wii's reports so it stays an assigned, live
20	Wiimote is Phase 2.
21
```
