1	# Wiimote SDP record + HID report descriptor (reference)
2	
3	Exact bytes a real Wiimote (`RVL-CNT-01`) exposes, needed to satisfy the Wii's
4	SDP validation. Sourced from wiibrew + the SDP dump in `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator`
5	(`sdp.c`). This is what fauxmote must serve once it moves off `esp_hidd` to a
6	custom SDP record (see journal decision 2026-06-12).
7	
8	## HID attribute values the Wii checks (HID profile SDP attributes)
9	
10	| Attr ID | Name | Value |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| 0x0200 | HIDDeviceReleaseNumber | `0x0100` |
13	| 0x0201 | HIDParserVersion | `0x0111` |
14	| 0x0202 | HIDDeviceSubclass | `0x04` |
15	| 0x0203 | HIDCountryCode | `0x33` |
16	| 0x0204 | HIDVirtualCable | `false` |
17	| 0x0205 | HIDReconnectInitiate | `true` |
18	| 0x0206 | HIDDescriptorList | (217-byte descriptor below) |
19	| 0x0207 | HIDLANGIDBaseList | LANGID 0x0409 / base 0x0100 |
20	| 0x0208 | HIDSDPDisable | `false` |
21	| 0x0209 | HIDBatteryPower | `true` |
22	| 0x020A | HIDRemoteWake | `true` |
23	| 0x020B | HIDProfileVersion | `0x0100` |
24	| 0x020C | HIDSupervisionTimeout | `0x0C80` |
25	| 0x020D | HIDNormallyConnectable | `false` |
26	| 0x020E | HIDBootDevice | `false` |
27	
28	Plus the standard service-class (`0x1124` HID), protocol descriptor list
29	(L2CAP PSM `0x0011` + HIDP), language base, additional-protocol list
30	(L2CAP PSM `0x0013` + HIDP), service name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`, provider
31	`Nintendo`. VID `0x057e` / PID `0x0306`.
32	
33	## HID report descriptor (217 bytes, attr 0x0206 value)
34	
35	Generic Desktop / Game Pad collection. Output reports `0x10`–`0x1a`, input
36	reports `0x20`–`0x3f`; each non-global item is `report-id, count, vendor-usage,
37	in/out`. This is the array currently in `main/bt_hid_device.c`.
38	
39	```
40	05 01 09 05 A1 01

```text
102	        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
103	        .frame_count     = frame_count,
104	        .width           = s_src_w,
105	        .height          = s_src_h,
106	        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
107	    };
108	
109	    uint32_t subscriber_mask = 0u;
110	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
111	    {
112	        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
113	        if (q != NULL)
114	        {
115	            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
116	            subscriber_mask |= (1u << i);
117	        }
118	    }
119	    PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH, frame_count,
120	                             subscriber_mask, &higher_priority_task_woken);
121	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
122	}
123	
124	/* ─── Active-area detection (video-task ctx) ───────────────────────────── */
125	
126	static uint8_t luma3(const uint8_t *p)
127	{
128	    uint8_t m = p[0];
129	    if (p[1] > m) { m = p[1]; }
130	    if (p[2] > m) { m = p[2]; }
131	    return m;
132	}
133	
134	/* Find the bright-content bounds of one frame by scanning inward from each edge
135	 * until a sampled pixel clears the threshold. Each scan is bounded to the deepest
136	 * border the min-size gate allows (a border thicker than that can't yield an
137	 * accepted rect anyway) — so the common case stops after a few lines and the
138	 * worst case (a fully dark frame) is still cheap and bounded. Returns false when
139	 * any edge isn't found within its bound (blank/dark/too-bordered frame → skipped,
140	 * not counted). */
141	static bool frame_edges(const uint8_t *buf, uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
142	                        uint16_t *top, uint16_t *bot, uint16_t *left, uint16_t *right)
143	{
144	    const uint32_t stride = (uint32_t)w * VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
145	    const uint16_t step   = VIDEO_ACTIVE_SAMPLE_STEP;
146	    const uint16_t ybord  = (h > VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_H) ? (uint16_t)(h - VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_H) : 0u;
147	    const uint16_t xbord  = (w > VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_W) ? (uint16_t)(w - VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_W) : 0u;
148	    bool ft = false, fb = false, fl = false, fr = false;
149	
150	    for (uint16_t y = 0u; y <= ybord && !ft; y++)
151	    {
152	        const uint8_t *row = buf + (uint32_t)y * stride;
153	        for (uint16_t x = 0u; x < w; x += step)
154	            if (luma3(row + (uint32_t)x * VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) > VIDEO_ACTIVE_LUMA_THR)
155	                { *top = y; ft = true; break; }
156	    }
157	    if (!ft) { return false; }
158	
159	    for (uint16_t y = 0u; y <= ybord && !fb; y++)
160	    {
161	        uint16_t yy = (uint16_t)(h - 1u - y);
162	        const uint8_t *row = buf + (uint32_t)yy * stride;
163	        for (uint16_t x = 0u; x < w; x += step)
164	            if (luma3(row + (uint32_t)x * VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) > VIDEO_ACTIVE_LUMA_THR)
165	                { *bot = yy; fb = true; break; }
166	    }
167	    if (!fb) { return false; }
168	
169	    for (uint16_t x = 0u; x <= xbord && !fl; x++)
170	        for (uint16_t y = 0u; y < h; y += step)
171	            if (luma3(buf + (uint32_t)y * stride + (uint32_t)x * VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) > VIDEO_ACTIVE_LUMA_THR)
172	                { *left = x; fl = true; break; }
173	    if (!fl) { return false; }
174	
175	    for (uint16_t x = 0u; x <= xbord && !fr; x++)
176	    {
177	        uint16_t xx = (uint16_t)(w - 1u - x);
178	        for (uint16_t y = 0u; y < h; y += step)
179	            if (luma3(buf + (uint32_t)y * stride + (uint32_t)xx * VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) > VIDEO_ACTIVE_LUMA_THR)
180	                { *right = xx; fr = true; break; }
181	    }
182	
183	    return ft && fb && fl && fr;
184	}
185	
186	static void active_reset(void)
187	{
188	    s_active_valid = false;
189	    s_acc_count    = 0u;
190	}
191	
192	/* One detection step per tick until locked: union this frame's bright bounds
193	 * into the accumulator; after enough bright frames, lock the union if it clears
194	 * the minimum plausible size, else reset and keep trying (fallback stays
195	 * full-frame meanwhile). Reads the latest complete ring slot (non-cached DDR,
196	 * so coherent; a 4-slot ring means it isn't overwritten mid-scan). */
197	static void detect_active(void)
198	{
199	    if (s_active_valid) { return; }
200	
201	    const uint8_t *buf = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)s_latest_buffer;
202	    uint16_t w = s_src_w, h = s_src_h;
203	    if (buf == NULL || w == 0u || h == 0u) { return; }
204	
205	    uint16_t t, b, l, r;
206	    if (!frame_edges(buf, w, h, &t, &b, &l, &r)) { return; }   /* dark frame — skip */
207	
208	    if (s_acc_count == 0u)
209	    {
210	        s_acc_top = t; s_acc_bot = b; s_acc_left = l; s_acc_right = r;
211	    }
212	    else
213	    {
214	        if (t < s_acc_top)   { s_acc_top   = t; }
215	        if (b > s_acc_bot)   { s_acc_bot   = b; }
216	        if (l < s_acc_left)  { s_acc_left  = l; }
217	        if (r > s_acc_right) { s_acc_right = r; }
218	    }
219	    if (++s_acc_count < VIDEO_ACTIVE_ACCUM_FRAMES) { return; }
220	
221	    uint16_t aw = s_acc_right - s_acc_left + 1u;
222	    uint16_t ah = s_acc_bot   - s_acc_top  + 1u;
223	    if (aw >= VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_W && ah >= VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_H)
224	    {
225	        s_active_x = s_acc_left; s_active_y = s_acc_top;
226	        s_active_w = aw;         s_active_h = ah;
227	        s_active_valid = true;
228	        LOG_INFO("VIDEO: active area %ux%u @(%u,%u) in %ux%u frame\r\n",
229	                 (unsigned)aw, (unsigned)ah, (unsigned)s_acc_left, (unsigned)s_acc_top,
230	                 (unsigned)w, (unsigned)h);
231	    }
232	    else
233	    {
234	        static uint8_t warn_budget = 4u;
235	        if (warn_budget > 0u)
236	        {
237	            LOG_WARN("VIDEO: active-area detect %ux%u below min %ux%u; retrying\r\n",
238	                     (unsigned)aw, (unsigned)ah,
239	                     (unsigned)VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_W, (unsigned)VIDEO_ACTIVE_MIN_H);
240	            warn_budget--;
241	        }
242	        s_acc_count = 0u;   /* discard and re-accumulate */
243	    }
244	}
245	
246	/* ─── Capture state machine ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
247	
248	static bool capture_arm(void)
249	{
250	    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
251	    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }
252	
253	    if (!ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)) { return false; }
254	    s_src_w = w;
255	    s_src_h = h;
256	    active_reset();   /* fresh source — re-detect the active area */
257	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(true);
258	    if (!ISC_Capture_Start())
259	    {
260	        (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
261	        return false;
262	    }
263	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture ARMED %ux%u\r\n", w, h);
264	    return true;
265	}
266	
267	static void capture_disarm(void)
268	{
269	    ISC_Capture_Stop();
270	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
271	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture IDLE\r\n");
272	}
273	
274	/* Each tick: align capture-chain state to intent + source lock, then hand the
275	 * current source validity/size to the compositor's display-reconcile hook (if
276	 * any) so it can (re)bind/unbind HEO in this task's context. The source size is
277	 * captured at arm time and persists across capture teardown, so the compositor
278	 * can keep HEO bound on a stale frame if it wants. */
279	static void reconcile(void)
280	{
281	    bool locked = TC358743_IsLocked();
282	
283	    /* Capture: armed iff intent + lock. */
284	    bool want_capture = s_capture_enabled && locked;
285	    if (want_capture && !s_capture_armed)
286	    {
287	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
288	    }
289	    else if (!want_capture && s_capture_armed)
290	    {
291	        capture_disarm();
292	        s_capture_armed = false;
293	    }
294	
295	    /* Detect the active picture rect once frames are flowing, before handing the
296	     * source to the compositor so it can pick up the crop the same tick. */
297	    if (s_capture_armed) { detect_active(); }
298	
299	    if (s_reconcile_cb != NULL)
300	    {
301	        s_reconcile_cb((s_src_w != 0u) && (s_src_h != 0u), s_src_w, s_src_h);
302	    }
303	}
304	
305	/* The CSI-2 D-PHY RX can be knocked out of HS lock by a heavy GFX burst (e.g. a
306	 * UI transition) while the TC358743 still reports the source locked, so the ISC
307	 * frame counter stops advancing but reconcile() never re-arms. Detect that stall
308	 * — armed + source locked but no new frame for VIDEO_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS — and cycle
309	 * the capture chain, which re-inits the D-PHY and re-locks cleanly once the bus
310	 * is quiet. The frame-count reference is reset after each re-arm (ISC_Capture_-
311	 * Configure zeroes the counter), so a stuck source retries at most once per
312	 * window rather than every tick. */
313	static void capture_watchdog(void)
314	{
315	    static uint32_t  last_count;
316	    static TickType_t last_advance_tick;
317	
318	    /* Not actively capturing: hold the reference fresh so a subsequent arm gets
319	     * a full timeout window before it can look stalled. */
320	    if (!s_capture_armed || !s_capture_enabled || !TC358743_IsLocked())
321	    {
322	        last_count        = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
323	        last_advance_tick = xTaskGetTickCount();
324	        return;
325	    }
326	
327	    uint32_t  count = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
328	    TickType_t now  = xTaskGetTickCount();
329	
330	    if (count != last_count)
331	    {
332	        last_count        = count;
333	        last_advance_tick = now;
334	        return;
335	    }
336	
337	    if ((now - last_advance_tick) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS))
338	    {
339	        LOG_WARN("VIDEO: capture stalled at frame %lu (source locked) — re-arming\r\n",
340	                 (unsigned long)count);
341	        /* Dump the pipeline register state for the first few collapses so the
342	         * error class is visible without flooding the UART on every re-arm. */
343	        static uint8_t diag_budget = 8u;
344	        if (diag_budget > 0u) { ISC_Capture_DumpDiag("stall"); diag_budget--; }
345	        capture_disarm();
346	        s_capture_armed = false;
347	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
348	
349	        last_count        = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
350	        last_advance_tick = xTaskGetTickCount();
351	    }
352	}
353	
354	/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
355	
356	static void video_task(void *param)
357	{
358	    (void)param;
359	
360	    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
361	     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge, and
362	     * parks the panel in UI-only mode. The backlight is NOT enabled here — the
363	     * UI boot task lights it once the splash is on screen, so the panel never
364	     * shows a pre-splash/garbage frame. */
365	    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
366	    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
367	    TC358743_Initialize();
368	
369	    for (;;)
370	    {
371	        TC358743_Tasks();
372	        reconcile();
373	        capture_watchdog();
374	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
375	    }
376	}
377	
378	/* ─── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
379	
380	static StackType_t  s_task_stack[VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
381	static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
382	
383	void Video_Initialize(void)
384	{
385	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(video_task,
386	                                       "VideoTask",
387	                                       VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
388	                                       NULL,
389	                                       VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY,
390	                                       s_task_stack,
391	                                       &s_task_tcb);
392	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_VIDEO, h);
393	}
394	
395	void Video_CaptureEnable(void)  { s_capture_enabled = true;  }
396	void Video_CaptureDisable(void) { s_capture_enabled = false; }
397	
398	void Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(void (*cb)(uint32_t buffer_addr))
399	{
400	    s_frame_latch_cb = cb;
401	}
402	
403	void Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(void (*cb)(bool source_valid,
404	                                                  uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h))
405	{
406	    s_reconcile_cb = cb;
407	}
408	
409	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
410	{
411	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
412	
413	    bool ok = false;
414	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
415	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
416	    {
417	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q) { ok = true; break; }     /* already in */
418	        if (s_subscribers[i] == NULL)
419	        {
420	            s_subscribers[i] = q;
421	            ok = true;
422	            break;
423	        }
424	    }
425	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
426	
427	    if (!ok) { LOG_ERROR("VIDEO: subscriber table full (max %u)\r\n",
428	                         (unsigned)VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS); }
429	    return ok;
430	}
431	
432	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
433	{
434	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
435	
436	    bool ok = false;
437	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
438	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
439	    {
440	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q)
441	        {
442	            s_subscribers[i] = NULL;
443	            ok = true;
444	            break;
445	        }
446	    }
447	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
448	    return ok;
449	}
450	
451	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info)
452	{
453	    if (info == NULL) { return; }
454	    info->buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)s_latest_buffer;
455	    info->frame_count     = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
456	    info->width           = s_src_w;
457	    info->height          = s_src_h;
458	    info->bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
459	}
460	
461	bool Video_GetActiveRect(uint16_t *x, uint16_t *y, uint16_t *w, uint16_t *h)
462	{
463	    bool valid = s_active_valid;
464	    if (valid)
465	    {
466	        if (x != NULL) { *x = s_active_x; }
467	        if (y != NULL) { *y = s_active_y; }
468	        if (w != NULL) { *w = s_active_w; }
469	        if (h != NULL) { *h = s_active_h; }
470	    }
471	    else
472	    {
473	        if (x != NULL) { *x = 0u; }
474	        if (y != NULL) { *y = 0u; }
475	        if (w != NULL) { *w = s_src_w; }
476	        if (h != NULL) { *h = s_src_h; }
477	    }
478	    return valid;
479	}
```

```text
42	## Decision log
43	
44	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
45	|------|----------|-----------|
46	| 2026-06-17 | **Deployment timing: keep the command on the fretboard's 240 Hz tick cadence; manage the new T1S transport delay via SPI speed / label lead-comp, not by changing the tick.** The fretboard now drives the guitar **over T1S** (not local GPIO): the per-sample bitmask is gated to the 240 Hz grid and sent, adding ~1.5–2 ms transport (host-SPI chunk each end @ 1 MHz dominates; planned 12 MHz removes ~1 ms). Do NOT decouple the command from the tick to shave latency. | Mirrors the training-side timing pin (300/40, below): the model *is* the photo→fret+strum timing function, so deployment must stay consistent with what it was characterised under, and the 240 Hz grid is part of that. The **T1S move is a real timing change** vs. the old local-GPIO standalone (actuation now later by the transport delay); if play drifts, fix via faster SPI or `--label-lead` (NEXT item 6c) and **re-validate gameplay on the T1S rig**. Worst-case command latency ≈ 6–7 ms (≈4.2 ms tick + transport). See fretboard journal 2026-06-17 + `../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`. |
47	| 2026-06-04 | **Deploy model = 16 channels (not the 8ch training default), trained on the full 5-song corpus (`--no-holdout`), `--strum-weight 5`, 50 epochs; quantised at strum thresh 0.80 / refractory 8.** | 8ch is capacity-limited on the sparse strum class (proven: 8ch overfit strum recall ~.86 vs 64ch ~.99; on hardware the 8ch full-corpus model overstrummed and no threshold fixed it — 0.85 missed real strums *and* still overstrummed, i.e. the precision/recall curve itself was the wall). 16ch lifts the curve (mono .856/.969 → .942/.981) so a threshold lands both. Affordable because inference now runs in the main loop, not the ISR — ~12.5k MACs / ~2–3 ms, 240 Hz sampling unaffected, RAM ~4 KB of 8 KB. `--strum-weight 5` (< the ~8–10 auto) trims the recall bias at the source. Threshold stays a header-only knob (0.80↔0.85 the live range). |
48	| 2026-06-04 | **Corpus + firmware timing pinned at `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS=300` / `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS=40` (marvin `8e5d18`, tuned for hard).** The 5-song hard corpus was captured at these values; the model is only valid for the timing it was distilled from — do **not** mix captures from other timing regimes (e.g. the old 220/25) into one corpus. If timing changes again, re-capture the whole corpus. | The deployed model *is* the timing function (photo→fret+strum), so the strum onset it learns is set by `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` and the pulse width by `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS`. Mixing regimes would teach two different photo→strum lags for identical inputs — the same ill-posed averaging as mixing difficulties. No model/architecture change needed for the 220→300/25→40 bump: the RF85 overfit A/B was *itself* run on this 300/40 corpus and fit it (frets 0.99, strum recall 0.97, p95 16.7 ms), which empirically proves RF85 covers this timing's lag; the monostable also normalises the output pulse to `--strum-hold`, so the wider 40 ms label pulse doesn't force a knob change. |
49	| 2026-06-04 | **Default model RF widened to `(1,4,16)` (RF 85) from `(1,4)` (RF 21).** Added a `--dilations` CLI flag; saved in the checkpoint and read back at eval (fallback `(1,4)` for pre-flag checkpoints). | Overfit A/B on clean line-263 `actuator-fb` data (slowride-hard, train==eval): RF21 caps at frets ~0.86 / loss plateau 0.31 — it can't see back to the photo cue ~48 samples before the strike line, so it can't hold the fret. RF85 (50k MACs, under the ~100k budget) recovers to frets 0.97–0.99 / strum recall 0.97 / p95 16.7 ms. Exactly the masked-by-detfb limitation model.md predicted would bite `actuator-fb`. Frets are the headline; widening RF costs ~19k MACs and is well affordable. |
50	| 2026-06-03 | **Primary path is programmatic (PyTorch), not MPLAB ML / SensiML.** MPLAB ML is demoted to an eventual *parallel demonstration* track, not the critical path. Inverts [`training.md` §5.1](training.md), which had the auto-pipeline first. | The hard part of this task is *temporal strum timing* — learning the photo-dip→strum delay over a causal window. SensiML's AutoML is feature-extraction + tree/ensemble over windowed stats: strong at "classify this window," weak at sequence/event-timing, which is exactly the part we care about (and review.md already named a causal 1D-CNN as the fallback). PyTorch gives full control over the window-length sweep (the #1 hyperparameter, [review.md Q3](review.md)), the sparse-strum class weighting, and the custom Phase-2 eval metrics (per-bit accuracy + strum-event timing distribution + visual side-by-side) the gate is judged on. Cost accepted: we own int8 quantisation + the on-device inference C in Phase 3 — tractable for a ≲1 k-MAC, 2-conv model, and the bit-exact control actually helps Phase 3's "matches host inference" gate. MPLAB ML stays valuable later as the Microchip-tooling demonstration once a known-good shape exists. |
51	| 2026-06-03 | **v1 trains on a single difficulty — Expert.** Corpus = many songs at Expert, one held out. NOT mixed-difficulty (which reverses the old [`review.md`](review.md) "train on Easy+Med+Expert" prescription). | If the game's highway scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms` — the first term is inversely proportional to scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, identical inputs map to different correct delays across difficulties: an ill-posed regression the model can only resolve by averaging (wrong on all). This is an *observability* gap, not a coverage gap, so more mixed data can't fix it. Single-difficulty is low-regret: if scroll speed turns out constant we lose nothing and can merge later; if it varies we've dodged the ill-posed case. Expert chosen for densest strum signal (helps the ~5.8 % rare class) and shortest delay (smallest window). Eventual structure if speed varies: one model per difficulty, difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller. |
52	| 2026-06-03 | Phase 1 exporter implemented as a `--labels={detector,actuator}` switch on the existing `export-ml` command rather than a new subcommand. Default stays `detector` (back-compat); `actuator` emits the `fret_*,strum` schema. | The two modes share the whole capture-read / timestamp / forward-fill loop; only the label-source record (`Detector` vs `Actuator`) and the output columns differ. A flag keeps one code path and one set of edge-case handling (missing SESSION, pre-label rows, strict mode). The detector path's CSV bytes are unchanged, so the existing corpus/tooling keeps working. |
53	| 2026-06-03 | `n_strum_events` stat counts **rising edges** (0→1 transitions) of the collapsed strum bit, not strum-active rows. | "Events" = distinct strums, which is the quantity to sanity-check against a song's note count. Per-row density ("a few %") is still eyeballable from the CSV; the rising-edge count is the more information-dense single number and doesn't conflate hold-duration with strum count. |
54	| 2026-06-03 | Collapsed strum bit computed from `Actuator.intended_mask` bits 5\|6 (the doc formula), not from the separate `strum_dir` field. | `intended_mask` is the actual 7-bit wire byte marvin sent (`FretboardLink_Send` value at [fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)); distilling against the byte-on-the-wire is the whole point. `strum_dir` is a redundant convenience enum. Using the mask keeps the label = exactly what fretboard saw. |
55	| 2026-06-03 | ACTUATOR producer wiring confirmed present in marvin firmware before building the exporter. | `PerfLog_EmitActuator` is called unconditionally inside `FretboardLink_Send` ([fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)), which both `timing_pipeline` and `manual_control` drive. So any self-play capture with the `ACTUATOR` (0x0A) mask bit set carries `intended_mask` + `strum_dir` per Send — no firmware work needed for Phase 1. |
56	| 2026-06-03 | Phase 2 windowing slices by **row index** (60 consecutive rows = one 250 ms window), **not** by the CSV `timestamp` column. Proceed assuming a uniform 240 Hz cadence. | The first real capture revealed `FretboardRaw` timestamps are bursty (stamped at marvin's RX/emit time, not at fretboard sample time) — see the open-questions entry. Each row is still exactly one true fretboard sample at the fixed 240 Hz rate, so counting rows gives correct, jitter-free windows; slicing by wall-clock timestamp would not. The `timestamp` column stays useful for plotting/duration only. |

62	## Open questions
63	
64	> Phase-1-blocking items first; the design forks for phase 2+ live in [`review.md`](review.md).
65	
66	- **[Future hardware — user wants to pursue] 2 photosensors per fret channel (like the CV detector).** Add a second sensor per fret so each channel sees two points along the note's travel (à la marvin's CV detector). Implications: input grows 5→10 channels (`MODEL_N_IN`, the input ring, the input affine — all parameterised already, but the trained model + `model_weights.h` change); two sensors per fret give the model an explicit *velocity/approach* signal (a note dimming sensor A then B encodes speed + direction), which should sharpen onset timing and could reduce the photo→strum lag ambiguity — possibly even let one model span difficulties (relates to the deferred scroll-speed-sensor idea below). Needs: fretboard HW revision (10 ADC inputs / channel mux), a fret_scan update, a wire-format/`FretboardRaw` bump for 10 channels, re-capture the corpus on the new HW, retrain. Big change; the current 5-sensor model is the baseline it must beat. **Discuss scope before building.**
67	
68	- **[Open follow-up] Red fret is the lone laggard (held-out .890 vs ≥.96 for the others).** Consistent across epochs and was joint-weakest in overfit too, so it's real, not noise. *Not* a corpus-coverage gap — slowride red density (26 %) is mid-pack vs the training songs (24–30 %). Hypotheses to test: (a) single-holdout variance — **rotate the holdout** across all five songs and see if the weak fret tracks the song (variance) or stays red (systemic); (b) neighbour confusion — red sits between green/yellow, so check red's false-positives/negatives against green/yellow activity; (c) `ph_red` channel quality (saturation/standardisation stats). Cheapest first move: rotate-holdout cross-val. Carried as a known caveat into Phase 3; confirm whether it actually costs notes against game score before treating it as blocking.
69	
70	- **Need a real self-play capture to close the Phase-1 gate.** The exporter is verified against synthetic records, but the rollout's Phase-1 "done when" requires inspecting one real captured-gameplay CSV. Required record types in the capture's `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`: `SESSION` + `ACTUATOR` + `FRETBOARD_RAW` (the exporter strictly needs only these three); `DETECTOR` recommended for cross-checking `pressed_mask` vs `intended_mask`. The existing files in [`tools/marvin-perf/captures/`](../../marvin-perf/captures/) are *already-exported detector CSVs*, not raw `.bin` captures, so they can't be re-exported through the actuator path — a fresh raw capture is needed.
71	- **Corpus for Phase 2.** Many songs **at Expert** (single difficulty — see decision log), one held-out song reserved and reused across iterations so per-iteration metrics are comparable.
72	
73	- **[Deferred — not fixing now] Label↔feature pairing crosses two USB directions.** Distinct from the timestamp-burstiness issue above. The label (`PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`) is timestamped when marvin *sends* the command to fretboard; the feature (`FRETBOARD_RAW`) is timestamped when marvin *receives* the sample. The exporter forward-fills one onto the other as if they share a clock, but the two streams travel opposite directions over USB CDC with independent latency + jitter, so the reconstructed "which command was active when this ADC sample was taken" pairing has an unknown, independently-varying skew. (Overlaps the [`review.md`](review.md) "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk, but is sharper: it's a *cross-stream* pairing error, not just emit-time jitter.)
74	  - **Candidate fix (deferred, pairs with the timestamp fix):** have the fretboard frame carry the **actuator bitmask it currently has applied** alongside the ADC scan (and its local sample timestamp). Then (sensor, label) is captured atomically on-device in one 240 Hz tick — no cross-stream join, zero skew. This is also the *most faithful* supervision: it's exactly the function the deployed model replaces (fretboard sees ADC → must emit the bitmask to apply now). marvin stays the teacher; we'd read its command off the wire at the point of truth instead of re-timing it on marvin. Training would then prefer fretboard-reported actuator state over `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`.
75	  - **Cost:** fretboard wire-format growth + `FretboardRaw` schema add on marvin + a new exporter label source. See fretboard journal open-question #4. **For now we proceed with the marvin-side join** — the skew is bounded (small ms) and was present at runtime too; revisit if Phase 2 shows label noise is the accuracy ceiling (ties to [`review.md` Q4](review.md)).
76	
77	- **[CONFIRMED] Legato fret-hold was the fret-accuracy ceiling.** marvin's timing pipeline suppresses a fret release whenever a queued upcoming note needs that fret ([timing_pipeline.c:263](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L263)) — so across consecutive same-fret notes it holds the fret continuously, and in the gap the photosensor reads bright while the label stays `1` (driven by marvin's note-queue lookahead, not observable from the photo). **Proven by the `--labels=detector-fb` probe** (detector `pressed_mask` frets = clean per-note structure, no legato): on slowride-hard overfit, frets went **0.94→0.99 across the board** and the green→orange gradient flattened (loss 0.13→0.063); strum unchanged (same source). Sustains are safe under a line-263 change because a sustain holds via continuous detector `pressed` (no release edge), never reaching the suppression.
78	  - **But detector-fb is a probe, not the deployable label:** detector `pressed` (y=311) leads the photo dip by ~20 ms and releases ~220 ms *before* the strum, so a model trained on it would release the fret before strumming. Correct *structure*, wrong *timing*.
79	  - **Deployable fix (implemented 2026-06-03):** gated line-263 change in marvin's `timing_pipeline.c` — release a fret between separate notes, hold only when re-needed at/before its scheduled release (back-to-back); sustains untouched. Reflash **marvin only**, re-capture hard, export `actuator-fb` → expect ~0.99 deployable frets at correct strike-line timing. (No fretboard/wire change; `applied_mask` still == the command because there's no lazy actuator yet.)
80	
81	- **[Decided] Final actuation architecture: released commands + lazy fretboard + log the command.** For good play at higher difficulties we want (1) marvin/model to command *released-style* per-note play (clean labels — done via line-263), and (2) a fretboard **lazy actuator** that physically holds a fret across same-fret gaps (releases only on a different non-empty fret command or a no-activity timeout) so fast Expert runs don't thrash release/repress and sustains aren't dropped (a dropped sustain makes the on-screen bar disappear → corrupts the feedback loop). Because the lazy layer makes physical state ≠ command, the training label must then be the **commanded** byte: when lazy lands, add a `commanded_mask` field to the fretboard frame/record (the reserved byte absorbs it; frame 17→18 B, schema v5) and the exporter sources `actuator-fb` labels from it. **Sequencing:** line-263 now (hard mode, `applied_mask` already == command); lazy actuator + `commanded_mask` together as the Expert follow-on. Strum mechanisms (monostable + threshold + weight) already validated — onset p95 ~16.7 ms, clean uniform pulses, glitches→0; recall/precision knee to be set on the consistent line-263 dataset (bias toward recall).
82	
83	- **[Future] 3-state fret actuator (user idea).** Give each fret three states instead of two: *pressed-and-note-active*, *pressed-but-between-notes* (legato hold), and *released*. Would let the label distinguish "this fret is down because a note is here now" from "down only because it's reused soon" — directly encoding the legato hold rather than hiding it. Could be a cleaner supervision target than collapsing to a binary press. Parked until the detector-fb probe tells us whether the binary clean-structure label is enough.
84	
85	- **[Future] Dedicated fret-line (scroll-speed) sensor.** The game highway's bar/measure lines scroll past a fixed point at a frequency that *is* the scroll speed — a direct observable of the one variable (difficulty/scroll-speed) that single-row note sensors can't see. A 6th ADC channel aimed at a column where only the horizontal fret lines pass (not the colored notes) would give the model an explicit scroll-speed signal, potentially letting **one** model generalise across difficulties instead of needing per-difficulty models. Open question whether a tiny model can actually exploit it to adjust strum timing. Pairs with [`review.md` Q1/Q5](review.md) (sensor count/placement). Flag for later; v1 stays Expert-only with the existing 5 channels.
86	
87	- **Measure the photo→strum lag before fixing the window length.** With difficulty fixed, the lag is a constant we can measure (cross-correlate photo dips vs strum events in the real capture) rather than guess. Sizes the causal window precisely and turns [`review.md` Q3](review.md) from a blind sweep into a measurement + a narrow sweep around it. Lag-measurement utility is part of the Phase-2 package.
88	
89	- **[Deferred — not fixing now] Fretboard ADC samples carry no true sample timestamp.** The first real self-play capture ([`tools/marvin-perf/captures/web-20260603-104406.csv`](../../marvin-perf/captures/web-20260603-104406.csv), 251.5 s, 59 958 rows) shows the per-row `timestamp` is **bursty, not uniform 240 Hz**: ~2.9 samples cluster within <0.05 ms, then a >10 ms gap (≈12 ms burst period), with *no* rows near the expected 4.17 ms spacing. Cause: `FretboardRaw.hdr.ts_counter` is stamped at marvin's USB-CDC RX/emit time, not at the fretboard's physical sample instant; the host receives the stream in bursts and the RX task drains buffered frames back-to-back.
90	  - **Consequences:** (1) row-index windowing is mandatory (see decision log); (2) forward-filled command labels can skew by up to one burst (~12 ms / ~3 samples) near command transitions — same effect as the "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk in [`review.md`](review.md); measure its magnitude in Phase 2.
91	  - **Candidate fix (deferred):** have the fretboard MCU stamp each 12-byte data frame with its own sample-time counter and carry it on the wire, so marvin records the *absolute sample-time truth* instead of RX time. That's a fretboard wire-format + firmware change (and a `FretboardRaw` schema add on marvin) — out of scope for now. **For the moment we proceed assuming regular 240 Hz intervals and window by row count.** Revisit if Phase 2 shows the label skew hurts strum-timing accuracy.
```

```text
70	    uint8_t         node_id;      /* PLCA id, also the MAC low byte */
71	    uint8_t         detector_id;  /* detector_state_t.detector_id (T1S_NO_DETECTOR for actuators) */
72	    t1s_node_type_t type;
73	} t1s_node_t;
74	
75	static const t1s_node_t s_nodes[] = {
76	    { 1u, (uint8_t)DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD, T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD },  /* detector (RX) */
77	    { 2u, T1S_NO_DETECTOR,                 T1S_NODE_GUITAR },     /* actuator (TX target) */
78	};
79	
80	#define T1S_NODE_TABLE_LEN  (sizeof(s_nodes) / sizeof(s_nodes[0]))
81	
82	/* Per-node runtime presence (parallel to s_nodes), updated on heartbeat RX. */
83	static struct {
84	    uint32_t last_seen_tick;
85	    uint32_t last_seq;
86	    bool     seen;
87	} s_node_rt[T1S_NODE_TABLE_LEN];
88	
89	static const char *node_type_name(t1s_node_type_t t)
90	{
91	    switch (t) {
92	        case T1S_NODE_FRETBOARD:     return "detector";
93	        case T1S_NODE_PHOTODETECTOR: return "detector";
94	        case T1S_NODE_GUITAR:        return "guitar";
95	        default:                     return "?";
96	    }
97	}
98	
99	/* Fill a follower MAC for a node id: 02:00:00:00:00:<id>. */
100	static void node_mac(uint8_t out[T1S_MAC_LEN], uint8_t node_id)
101	{
102	    out[0] = 0x02u;
103	    out[1] = 0x00u;
104	    out[2] = 0x00u;
105	    out[3] = 0x00u;
106	    out[4] = 0x00u;
107	    out[5] = node_id;
108	}
109	
110	/* Look up a node by type (NULL if none of that type is configured). */
111	static const t1s_node_t *node_for_type(t1s_node_type_t type)
112	{
113	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < (sizeof(s_nodes) / sizeof(s_nodes[0])); i++) {
114	        if (s_nodes[i].type == type) {
115	            return &s_nodes[i];
116	        }
117	    }
118	    return NULL;
119	}
120	
121	/* Look up a node by its source MAC (NULL if unknown). */
122	static const t1s_node_t *node_for_mac(const uint8_t mac[T1S_MAC_LEN])
123	{
124	    if ((mac[0] != 0x02u) || (mac[1] | mac[2] | mac[3] | mac[4])) {
125	        return NULL;
126	    }
127	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < (sizeof(s_nodes) / sizeof(s_nodes[0])); i++) {
128	        if (s_nodes[i].node_id == mac[5]) {
129	            return &s_nodes[i];
130	        }
131	    }
132	    return NULL;
133	}
134	
135	/* TX frame staging: TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket keeps a pointer to the buffer
136	 * until its TX callback fires, so the buffer must stay valid meanwhile. One
137	 * in-flight frame at a time (guarded by s_tx_busy) suffices for the link's
138	 * rates. */
139	static uint8_t       s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + 64u];
140	static volatile bool s_tx_busy;
141	
142	/* Latest-wins outbound command to the guitar, flushed by the service task. */
143	static volatile uint8_t s_cmd;
144	static volatile bool    s_cmd_dirty;
145	
146	static T1SLink_FrameHandler s_frame_handler;
147	
148	/* Traffic counters (read by the console t1s/nodes commands). */
149	static volatile uint32_t s_tx_count;   /* command frames sent */
150	static volatile uint32_t s_rx_count;   /* frames received from a known node */
151	static volatile uint32_t s_service_overruns; /* service_pump hit its iter cap (stuck MAC-PHY) */
152	
153	static TC6_t            *s_tc6;
154	static volatile bool     s_need_service;
155	static volatile bool     s_link_up;
156	
157	static SemaphoreHandle_t s_svc_sem;
158	static StaticSemaphore_t s_svc_sem_buf;
159	
160	static StackType_t       s_task_stack[T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
161	static StaticTask_t      s_task_tcb;
162	
163	/* RX reassembly: TC6 delivers an Ethernet frame as slices; collect them here
164	 * and process on the OnRxEthernetPacket completion callback. */
165	static uint8_t           s_rx_buf[1518];
166	
167	/* FLEXCOM4 SPI completion ISR callback: the chunk transfer is done, hand the
168	 * buffer back to the TC6 driver and wake the service task. */
169	static void spi_done_cb(uintptr_t context)
170	{
171	    (void)context;
172	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
173	    TC6_SpiBufferDone(T1S_INSTANCE, true);
174	    (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_svc_sem, &hpw);
175	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
176	}
177	
178	/* T1S_IRQ_N falling-edge PIO ISR callback: the MAC-PHY needs servicing. */
179	static void irq_cb(PIO_PIN pin, uintptr_t context)
180	{
181	    (void)pin;
182	    (void)context;
183	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
184	    s_need_service = true;
185	    (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_svc_sem, &hpw);
186	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
187	}
188	
189	/* TX completion: the staged frame buffer is free for reuse. */
190	static void tx_done_cb(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pTx, uint16_t len,
191	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
192	{
193	    (void)pInst;
194	    (void)pTx;
195	    (void)len;
196	    (void)pTag;
197	    (void)pGlobalTag;
198	    s_tx_busy = false;
199	}
200	
201	/* Frame a payload to a node (dst = 02:00:00:00:00:<node_id>) and queue it.
202	 * Returns false if a TX is already in flight or the driver rejected it. */
203	static bool send_to_node(uint8_t node_id, const uint8_t *payload, uint16_t payload_len)
204	{
205	    if (s_tx_busy || !s_link_up) {
206	        return false;
207	    }
208	    if (payload_len > (sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
209	        return false;
210	    }
211	    node_mac(&s_tx_frame[0], node_id);          /* dest MAC */
212	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[6], s_mac, T1S_MAC_LEN);  /* src MAC  */
213	    s_tx_frame[12] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE >> 8);
214	    s_tx_frame[13] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE & 0xFFu);
215	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN], payload, payload_len);
216	
217	    s_tx_busy = true;
218	    bool ok = TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_tx_frame,
219	                                        (uint16_t)(T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + payload_len),
220	                                        0u, tx_done_cb, NULL);
221	    if (!ok) {
222	        s_tx_busy = false;
223	    }
224	    return ok;
225	}
226	
227	/* Run the protocol stack until it has no immediately pending work. IRQ_N is
228	 * active-low; TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
229	/* Returns true if it bailed with work still pending (hit the iteration cap) —
230	 * the caller must then yield so a stuck MAC-PHY can't starve other tasks. */
231	static bool service_pump(void)
232	{
233	    unsigned iters = 0u;
234	    do {
235	        s_need_service = false;
236	        bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);
237	        (void)TC6_Service(s_tc6, no_int);
238	    } while (s_need_service && (++iters < T1S_SERVICE_MAX_ITERS));
239	
240	    TC6Regs_CheckTimers();
241	
242	    /* Persistent need-service = the MAC-PHY isn't quiescing (stuck IRQ / no
243	     * peer). Don't spin on it; count it and tell the caller to yield. */
244	    if (s_need_service) { s_service_overruns++; return true; }
245	    return false;
246	}
247	
248	/* One MAC-PHY bring-up attempt: reset pulse, push the register + PLCA config,
249	 * and drive the async writes to completion within a deadline. Returns true only
250	 * if the chip acked init done. False = absent/unresponsive → the caller backs
251	 * off and retries (so an unpopulated LAN8651 never turns into a dead-bus spin).
252	 * Re-pulsing reset each attempt also resets a chip attached after boot. */
253	static bool t1s_try_bringup(void)
254	{
255	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST is active-low, idle high). */
256	    T1S_RST_Clear();
257	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
258	    T1S_RST_Set();
259	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
260	
261	    /* Configure the LAN8651 registers + PLCA (coordinator, id 0). promiscuous
262	     * during bring-up so RX isn't filtered before the node table exists.
263	     * TC6Regs_Init only queues the writes — bounded accept retry. */
264	    TickType_t accept_dl = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(T1S_BRINGUP_ACCEPT_MS);
265	    while (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, T1S_PLCA_ENABLE, T1S_NODE_ID,
266	                         T1S_NODE_COUNT, 0u, 0u, true, false, false)) {
267	        if ((int32_t)(accept_dl - xTaskGetTickCount()) <= 0) { return false; }
268	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(50));
269	    }
270	
271	    /* Drive the async register writes to completion (bounded). */
272	    TickType_t done_dl = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(T1S_BRINGUP_INITDONE_MS);
273	    while (!TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6) &&
274	           ((int32_t)(done_dl - xTaskGetTickCount()) > 0)) {
275	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(2));
276	        (void)service_pump();
277	    }
278	    return TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6);
279	}
280	
281	static void t1s_task(void *param)
282	{
283	    (void)param;
284	
285	    /* SPI: Mode 0 (CPOL=0 idle low, CPHA=0 leading edge), 8-bit, 15 MHz.
286	     * Source clock 0 => PLib uses the FLEXCOM4 peripheral clock. One-time. */
287	    FLEXCOM_SPI_TRANSFER_SETUP setup = {
288	        .clockFrequency = T1S_SPI_HZ,
289	        .clockPhase     = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_PHASE_LEADING_EDGE,
290	        .clockPolarity  = FLEXCOM_SPI_CLOCK_POLARITY_IDLE_LOW,
291	        .dataBits       = FLEXCOM_SPI_DATA_BITS_8,
292	    };
293	    (void)FLEXCOM4_SPI_TransferSetup(&setup, 0u);
294	    FLEXCOM4_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);
295	
296	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
297	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
298	        LOG_ERROR("T1S: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
299	        vTaskDelete(NULL);
300	        return;
301	    }
302	
303	    (void)PIO_PinInterruptCallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN, irq_cb, 0u);
304	    PIO_PinInterruptEnable(T1S_IRQ_N_PIN);
305	
306	    bool warned_absent = false;
307	
308	    for (;;) {
309	        /* Bring up (or re-bring-up) the MAC-PHY. Absent/unresponsive → warn once
310	         * and retry with backoff instead of servicing a dead bus. */
311	        if (!s_link_up) {
312	            if (!t1s_try_bringup()) {
313	                if (!warned_absent) {
314	                    LOG_WARN("T1S: MAC-PHY not responding (LAN8651 populated? wiring?); "
315	                             "retry every %ums\r\n", (unsigned)T1S_ABSENT_RETRY_MS);
316	                    warned_absent = true;
317	                }
318	                vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(T1S_ABSENT_RETRY_MS));
319	                continue;
320	            }
321	            s_link_up      = true;
322	            warned_absent  = false;
323	            TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
324	            LOG_INFO("T1S: LAN8651 up — chipRev=%u, MAC=%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X, "
325	                     "PLCA coord id=%u/%u\r\n",
326	                     (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
327	                     s_mac[0], s_mac[1], s_mac[2], s_mac[3], s_mac[4], s_mac[5],
328	                     (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
329	        }
330	
331	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_svc_sem, pdMS_TO_TICKS(1));
332	        /* If the pump bailed with work still pending, force a yield so this
333	         * prio-5 task can never monopolize the CPU on a stuck MAC-PHY. */
334	        if (service_pump()) { vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1)); }
335	
336	        /* Flush the latest pending command to the active guitar (actuator)
337	         * node. All TC6 access stays in this task; producers only stash via
338	         * the API. (Single guitar today; an active-guitar selector goes here
339	         * when multiple guitar nodes share the bus.) */
340	        if (s_cmd_dirty && !s_tx_busy) {
341	            const t1s_node_t *guitar = node_for_type(T1S_NODE_GUITAR);
342	            if (guitar != NULL) {
343	                /* Clear before reading so a concurrent update re-arms dirty
344	                 * rather than being dropped (latest-wins). */
345	                s_cmd_dirty = false;
346	                uint8_t mask = s_cmd;
347	                if (send_to_node(guitar->node_id, &mask, 1u)) {
348	                    s_tx_count++;
349	                }
350	            }
351	        }
352	    }
353	}

355	void T1SLink_Initialize(void)
356	{
357	    s_svc_sem = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_svc_sem_buf);
358	    configASSERT(s_svc_sem != NULL);
359	
360	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(t1s_task, "T1SLink", T1S_TASK_STACK_WORDS, NULL,
361	                            T1S_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
362	}

390	bool T1SLink_GetNodeInfo(uint8_t idx, T1SLink_NodeInfo *out)
391	{
392	    if ((idx >= T1S_NODE_TABLE_LEN) || (out == NULL)) {
393	        return false;
394	    }
395	    out->node_id = s_nodes[idx].node_id;
396	    out->type    = node_type_name(s_nodes[idx].type);
397	    if (s_node_rt[idx].seen) {
398	        uint32_t age = xTaskGetTickCount() - s_node_rt[idx].last_seen_tick;
399	        out->age_ms  = (uint32_t)(age * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
400	        out->present = (age < pdMS_TO_TICKS(T1S_PRESENCE_TIMEOUT_MS));
401	    } else {
402	        out->age_ms  = 0u;
403	        out->present = false;
404	    }
405	    return true;
406	}

424	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6 driver callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
425	
426	bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
427	                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
428	{
429	    (void)tc6instance;
430	    (void)pGlobalTag;
431	    /* Non-blocking full-duplex transfer; spi_done_cb calls TC6_SpiBufferDone.
432	     * Returns false if the PLib is busy — the driver retries. */
433	    return FLEXCOM4_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len);
434	}
435	
436	void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
437	{
438	    (void)pInst;
439	    (void)pGlobalTag;
440	    /* May be called from task or ISR context; just flag. ISR sources also give
441	     * the semaphore, so the service task always wakes. */
442	    s_need_service = true;
443	}
444	
445	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset,
446	                              uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
447	{
448	    (void)pInst;
449	    (void)pGlobalTag;
450	    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
451	        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
452	    }
453	}
454	
455	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
456	                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
457	{
458	    (void)pInst;
459	    (void)rxTimestamp;
460	    (void)pGlobalTag;
461	
462	    if (!success || (len < T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
463	        return;
464	    }
465	
466	    uint16_t ethertype = (uint16_t)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]);
467	    if ((ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE) && (ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB)) {
468	        return;  /* not ours (promiscuous RX during bring-up) */
469	    }
470	
471	    const uint8_t *src = &s_rx_buf[6];
472	    const t1s_node_t *node = node_for_mac(src);
473	    if (node == NULL) {
474	        LOG_DEBUG("T1S: rx from unknown node %02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X\r\n",
475	                  src[0], src[1], src[2], src[3], src[4], src[5]);
476	        return;
477	    }
478	    uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)(node - s_nodes);
479	
480	    const uint8_t *payload = &s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN];
481	    uint16_t       payload_len = (uint16_t)(len - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN);
482	
483	    if (ethertype == T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB) {
484	        /* Presence heartbeat: stamp last-seen; capture the seq if present. */
485	        s_node_rt[idx].last_seen_tick = xTaskGetTickCount();
486	        s_node_rt[idx].seen = true;
487	        if (payload_len >= T1S_HB_LEN) {
488	            s_node_rt[idx].last_seq = (uint32_t)payload[4]
489	                                    | ((uint32_t)payload[5] << 8)
490	                                    | ((uint32_t)payload[6] << 16)
491	                                    | ((uint32_t)payload[7] << 24);
492	        }
493	        return;
494	    }
495	
496	    s_rx_count++;
497	    if (s_frame_handler != NULL) {
498	        s_frame_handler(node->detector_id, payload, payload_len);
499	    }
500	}
501	
502	void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
503	{
504	    (void)pGlobalTag;
505	    LOG_WARN("T1S: error: %s\r\n", TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
506	    switch (err) {
507	        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
508	        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
509	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
510	        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
511	        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
512	        case TC6Error_SpiError:
513	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
514	            break;
515	        default:
516	            break;
517	    }
518	}
519

521	
522	uint32_t TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs(void)
523	{
524	    /* configTICK_RATE_HZ is 1000, so one tick is one millisecond. */
525	    return (uint32_t)xTaskGetTickCount();
526	}

541	}
```

```text
31	/* --- apply a received input message by driving the existing control APIs -------- */
32	
33	static void apply_guitar(uint8_t mask, uint8_t whammy, uint8_t aux)
34	{
35	    Wiimote_SetButton("green",     mask & MF_G_GREEN);
36	    Wiimote_SetButton("red",       mask & MF_G_RED);
37	    Wiimote_SetButton("yellow",    mask & MF_G_YELLOW);
38	    Wiimote_SetButton("blue",      mask & MF_G_BLUE);
39	    Wiimote_SetButton("orange",    mask & MF_G_ORANGE);
40	    Wiimote_SetButton("strumdown", mask & MF_G_STRUM_DOWN);
41	    Wiimote_SetButton("strumup",   mask & MF_G_STRUM_UP);
42	    Guitar_SetWhammy(whammy & MF_WHAMMY_MASK);
43	    Wiimote_SetButton("gplus",  aux & MF_AUX_PLUS);
44	    Wiimote_SetButton("gminus", aux & MF_AUX_MINUS);
45	    Wiimote_SetButton("pedal",  aux & MF_AUX_PEDAL);
46	    /* MF_AUX_STARPOWER: no-op until the ACCEL/tilt slice is live. */
47	}
48	
49	static void apply_wiimote(uint8_t core, uint8_t dpad, uint8_t sx, uint8_t sy)
50	{
51	    Wiimote_SetButton("a",     core & MF_W_A);
52	    Wiimote_SetButton("b",     core & MF_W_B);
53	    Wiimote_SetButton("one",   core & MF_W_ONE);
54	    Wiimote_SetButton("two",   core & MF_W_TWO);
55	    Wiimote_SetButton("plus",  core & MF_W_PLUS);
56	    Wiimote_SetButton("minus", core & MF_W_MINUS);
57	    Wiimote_SetButton("home",  core & MF_W_HOME);
58	    Wiimote_SetButton("up",    dpad & MF_W_UP);
59	    Wiimote_SetButton("down",  dpad & MF_W_DOWN);
60	    Wiimote_SetButton("left",  dpad & MF_W_LEFT);
61	    Wiimote_SetButton("right", dpad & MF_W_RIGHT);
62	    Guitar_SetStick(sx, sy);
63	}
64	
65	static void apply_pointer(uint8_t x, uint8_t y, uint8_t flags)
66	{
67	    if (flags & 0x01) {
68	        Wiimote_SetPointer((float)x / 255.0f, (float)y / 255.0f);
69	    } else {
70	        Wiimote_ClearPointer();
71	    }
72	}
73	
74	/* Release everything to safe defaults (link watchdog fired). */
75	static void neutralize(void)
76	{
77	    apply_guitar(0, MF_WHAMMY_REST, 0);
78	    apply_wiimote(0, 0, MF_STICK_CENTER, MF_STICK_CENTER);
79	    Wiimote_ClearPointer();
80	}
81	
82	static void handle_link_cmd(uint8_t op)
83	{
84	    s_last_result = 0;
85	    switch (op) {
86	    case MF_CMD_PAIR:       Fauxmote_EnterPairing();     break;
87	    case MF_CMD_STOP:       Fauxmote_StopPairing();      break;
88	    case MF_CMD_RECONNECT:  Fauxmote_Reconnect();        break;
89	    case MF_CMD_UNLINK:     Fauxmote_Unlink();           break;
90	    case MF_CMD_EXT_ATTACH: Wiimote_SetExtension(true);  break;
91	    case MF_CMD_EXT_DETACH: Wiimote_SetExtension(false); break;
92	    case MF_CMD_STATUS_REQ: /* handled by the caller (forces a STATUS send) */ break;
93	    default:                s_last_result = 1;           break;   /* unknown opcode */
94	    }
95	}
96	
97	/* --- STATUS uplink ------------------------------------------------------------- */
98	
99	static void mf_send(uint8_t type, const uint8_t *payload, uint8_t len)
100	{
101	    uint8_t frame[3 + MF_MAX_PAYLOAD + 1];
102	    uint8_t hdr[2 + MF_MAX_PAYLOAD];
103	    frame[0] = MF_SOF;
104	    frame[1] = type;
105	    frame[2] = len;
106	    hdr[0] = type;
107	    hdr[1] = len;
108	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < len; i++) {
109	        frame[3 + i] = payload[i];
110	        hdr[2 + i]   = payload[i];
111	    }
112	    frame[3 + len] = mf_crc8(hdr, (size_t)(2 + len));
113	    uart_write_bytes(MF_UART_PORT, frame, (size_t)(4 + len));
114	}
115	
116	static void build_status(uint8_t out[MF_LEN_STATUS])
117	{
118	    uint8_t flags = 0;
119	    if (Fauxmote_IsDiscoverable()) flags |= MF_ST_DISCOVERABLE | MF_ST_PAIRING;
120	    if (Wiimote_IsConnected())     flags |= MF_ST_CONNECTED;
121	    if (Wiimote_IsAssigned())      flags |= MF_ST_ASSIGNED;
122	    if (Wiimote_ExtAttached())     flags |= MF_ST_EXT_ATTACHED;
123	    if (Fauxmote_WiiAddr())        flags |= MF_ST_BONDED;
124	    out[0] = flags;
125	    out[1] = (uint8_t)Wiimote_PlayerSlot();
126	    out[2] = Wiimote_ReportMode();
127	    out[3] = s_last_result;
128	}
129	
130	/* --- frame parser -------------------------------------------------------------- */
131	
132	typedef enum { P_SOF, P_TYPE, P_LEN, P_PAYLOAD, P_CRC } parse_state_t;
133	
134	typedef struct {
135	    parse_state_t state;
136	    uint8_t       type;
137	    uint8_t       len;
138	    uint8_t       idx;
139	    uint8_t       payload[MF_MAX_PAYLOAD];
140	} parser_t;
141	
142	/* Returns true if a valid input message updated the controller state (resets the
143	 * watchdog); STATUS_REQ sets *status_req. */
144	static bool parse_byte(parser_t *p, uint8_t b, bool *status_req)
145	{
146	    switch (p->state) {
147	    case P_SOF:
148	        if (b == MF_SOF) p->state = P_TYPE;
149	        break;
150	    case P_TYPE:
151	        if (b == 0x00) { p->state = P_SOF; break; }   /* 0x00 never valid */
152	        p->type  = b;
153	        p->state = P_LEN;
154	        break;
155	    case P_LEN:
156	        if (b > MF_MAX_PAYLOAD) { p->state = P_SOF; break; }  /* corrupt -> rescan */
157	        p->len = b;
158	        p->idx = 0;
159	        p->state = (b == 0) ? P_CRC : P_PAYLOAD;
160	        break;
161	    case P_PAYLOAD:
162	        p->payload[p->idx++] = b;
163	        if (p->idx >= p->len) p->state = P_CRC;
164	        break;
165	    case P_CRC: {
166	        uint8_t hdr[2 + MF_MAX_PAYLOAD];
167	        hdr[0] = p->type;
168	        hdr[1] = p->len;
169	        memcpy(&hdr[2], p->payload, p->len);
170	        p->state = P_SOF;
171	        if (mf_crc8(hdr, (size_t)(2 + p->len)) != b) break;   /* bad CRC -> drop */
172	
173	        switch (p->type) {
174	        case MF_MSG_GUITAR:
175	            if (p->len != MF_LEN_GUITAR) break;
176	            apply_guitar(p->payload[0], p->payload[1], p->payload[2]);
177	            return true;
178	        case MF_MSG_WIIMOTE:
179	            if (p->len != MF_LEN_WIIMOTE) break;
180	            apply_wiimote(p->payload[0], p->payload[1], p->payload[2], p->payload[3]);
181	            return true;
182	        case MF_MSG_POINTER:
183	            if (p->len != MF_LEN_POINTER) break;
184	            apply_pointer(p->payload[0], p->payload[1], p->payload[2]);
185	            return true;
186	        case MF_MSG_ACCEL:
187	            if (p->len != MF_LEN_ACCEL) break;
188	            /* planned: drive the Wiimote accel field; no-op for now */
189	            return true;
190	        case MF_MSG_LINK_CMD:
191	            if (p->len != MF_LEN_LINK_CMD) break;
192	            if (p->payload[0] == MF_CMD_STATUS_REQ) *status_req = true;
193	            else handle_link_cmd(p->payload[0]);
194	            break;
195	        default:
196	            break;   /* unknown type: ignore */
197	        }
198	        break;
199	    }
200	    }
201	    return false;
202	}
203	
204	/* --- task ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */
205	
206	static void marvin_link_task(void *arg)
207	{
208	    (void)arg;
209	    parser_t parser = { .state = P_SOF };
210	    uint8_t  rx[64];
211	
212	    TickType_t last_input  = xTaskGetTickCount();
213	    TickType_t last_status = 0;
214	    bool       safed       = true;   /* start neutralized until marvin talks */
215	    uint8_t    prev_status[MF_LEN_STATUS] = { 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF };
216	
217	    for (;;) {
218	        int n = uart_read_bytes(MF_UART_PORT, rx, sizeof(rx), pdMS_TO_TICKS(20));
219	        bool status_req = false;
220	        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
221	            if (parse_byte(&parser, rx[i], &status_req)) {
222	                last_input = xTaskGetTickCount();
223	                safed = false;
224	            }
225	        }
226	
227	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
228	
229	        /* Watchdog: if no input slice arrived within the timeout, release all. */
230	        if (!safed && (now - last_input) > pdMS_TO_TICKS(MF_INPUT_TIMEOUT_MS)) {
231	            neutralize();
232	            safed = true;
233	        }
234	
235	        /* STATUS: on change, on request, or as a heartbeat. */
236	        uint8_t status[MF_LEN_STATUS];
237	        build_status(status);
238	        bool changed = memcmp(status, prev_status, MF_LEN_STATUS) != 0;
239	        if (status_req || changed ||
240	            (now - last_status) > pdMS_TO_TICKS(MF_STATUS_PERIOD_MS)) {
241	            mf_send(MF_MSG_STATUS, status, MF_LEN_STATUS);
242	            memcpy(prev_status, status, MF_LEN_STATUS);
243	            last_status = now;
244	        }
245	    }
246	}
247	
248	void MarvinLink_Start(void)
249	{
250	    const uart_config_t cfg = {
251	        .baud_rate = MF_UART_BAUD,
252	        .data_bits = UART_DATA_8_BITS,
253	        .parity    = UART_PARITY_DISABLE,
254	        .stop_bits = UART_STOP_BITS_1,
255	        .flow_ctrl = UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_DISABLE,
256	        .source_clk = UART_SCLK_DEFAULT,
257	    };
258	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(uart_driver_install(MF_UART_PORT, 512, 512, 0, NULL, 0));
259	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(uart_param_config(MF_UART_PORT, &cfg));
260	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(uart_set_pin(MF_UART_PORT, MF_UART_TX_PIN, MF_UART_RX_PIN,
261	                                 UART_PIN_NO_CHANGE, UART_PIN_NO_CHANGE));
262	
263	    xTaskCreateStatic(marvin_link_task, "mflink", sizeof(s_task_stack) / sizeof(StackType_t),
264	                      NULL, 5, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
265	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "marvin link up on UART%d (TX=%d RX=%d, %lu baud)",
266	             MF_UART_PORT, MF_UART_TX_PIN, MF_UART_RX_PIN, (unsigned long)MF_UART_BAUD);
267	}
268
```

```text
21	    MF_MSG_GUITAR   = 0x01,   /* m->f, 3B: hot gameplay input */
22	    MF_MSG_WIIMOTE  = 0x02,   /* m->f, 4B: menu-nav input */

30	#define MF_LEN_WIIMOTE   4u
31	#define MF_LEN_LINK_CMD  1u
32	#define MF_LEN_ACCEL     3u
33	#define MF_LEN_POINTER   3u
34	#define MF_LEN_STATUS    4u
35	#define MF_MAX_PAYLOAD   8u   /* largest LEN across all types */

84	#define MF_ST_ASSIGNED     (1u << 2)

89	/* CRC-8/CCITT, poly 0x07, init 0x00, no reflection. Over TYPE, LEN, payload. */
90	static inline uint8_t mf_crc8(const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
91	{
92	    uint8_t crc = 0x00;
93	    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++) {
94	        crc ^= data[i];
95	        for (int b = 0; b < 8; b++) {
96	            crc = (crc & 0x80) ? (uint8_t)((crc << 1) ^ 0x07) : (uint8_t)(crc << 1);
97	        }
98	    }
99	    return crc;
100	}
```

```text
1	"""Baseline causal 1D-CNN: 5 ADC channels over a window → 6 logits.
2	
3	Dilated causal conv layers (one per dilation factor), then a linear head on the
4	last timestep. Output is 6 logits (5 frets + collapsed strum) for independent
5	weighted-BCE. int8 quantisation is a Phase-3 concern; this trains in float32.
6	
7	The receptive field must cover the ~48-sample photo->strum lag, or the head
8	can't hold a fret to the strike line: dilations (1, 4, 16) kernel 5 give RF 85
9	(~354 ms) and overfit frets to ~0.99, whereas (1, 4) [RF 21] caps at ~0.86 on
10	actuator-fb labels. See docs/model.md §4. Imports torch — only loaded when
11	training/eval run.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import torch
17	import torch.nn as nn
18	
19	from . import FRET_COUNT, N_LABELS
20	
21	
22	class CausalConv1d(nn.Module):
23	    """Conv1d with left padding only, so output[t] depends on inputs ≤ t."""
24	
25	    def __init__(self, in_ch: int, out_ch: int, kernel: int, dilation: int):
26	        super().__init__()
27	        self.pad = (kernel - 1) * dilation
28	        self.conv = nn.Conv1d(in_ch, out_ch, kernel, dilation=dilation)
29	
30	    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
31	        x = nn.functional.pad(x, (self.pad, 0))
32	        return self.conv(x)
33	
34	
35	class StrumNet(nn.Module):
36	    def __init__(
37	        self,
38	        *,
39	        channels: int = 8,
40	        kernel: int = 5,
41	        dilations: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 4, 16),
42	        n_in: int = FRET_COUNT,
43	        n_out: int = N_LABELS,
44	    ):
45	        super().__init__()
46	        layers: list[nn.Module] = []
47	        prev = n_in
48	        for d in dilations:
49	            layers.append(CausalConv1d(prev, channels, kernel, d))
50	            layers.append(nn.ReLU())
51	            prev = channels
52	        self.features = nn.Sequential(*layers)
53	        self.head = nn.Linear(channels, n_out)
54	
55	    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
56	        # x: (B, n_in, window) -> features (B, channels, window) -> last step
57	        h = self.features(x)
58	        last = h[:, :, -1]
59	        return self.head(last)
60	
61	    @torch.no_grad()
62	    def predict_bits(self, x: torch.Tensor, thresh: float = 0.5) -> torch.Tensor:
63	        return (torch.sigmoid(self.forward(x)) >= thresh).int()
64	
65	
66	def count_macs(model: StrumNet, window: int) -> int:
67	    """Rough MAC count for one inference, to check against the on-device budget."""
68	    macs = 0
69	    for m in model.modules():
70	        if isinstance(m, nn.Conv1d):
71	            k = m.kernel_size[0]
72	            macs += m.in_channels * m.out_channels * k * window
73	        elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
74	            macs += m.in_features * m.out_features
75	    return macs
76
```

```text
1	"""Load actuator-fb SensiML CSVs and build causal training windows.
2	
3	The CSV is produced by `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator-fb`:
4	
5	    timestamp, fb_seq,
6	    ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,
7	    fret_green,fret_red,fret_yellow,fret_blue,fret_orange,
8	    strum
9	
10	Each row is one true 240 Hz fretboard sample with its label (the actuator
11	bitmask the fretboard was driving during the scan) paired atomically at the
12	source — no cross-stream join, so timing is clean. `fb_seq` is the fretboard's
13	monotonic sample counter; gaps mean frames dropped in transit. Windows are
14	sliced **by row index** and never span a `fb_seq` gap (see `contiguous_runs`),
15	so a dropped frame can't silently stitch two non-adjacent samples together.
16	
17	CSV parsing, the window-index logic, and label/feature extraction are
18	stdlib-only. `build_arrays` materialises numpy tensors and imports numpy
19	lazily so the rest of the module loads without it.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import csv
25	from dataclasses import dataclass
26	from pathlib import Path
27	
28	from . import FRET_COUNT, N_LABELS
29	
30	EXPECTED_HEADER = [
31	    "timestamp", "fb_seq",
32	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
33	    "fret_green", "fret_red", "fret_yellow", "fret_blue", "fret_orange",
34	    "strum",
35	]
36	
37	_ADC_COL0 = 2   # first ph_ column index
38	_LABEL_COL0 = 7  # first fret_ column index
39	
40	
41	class DataError(Exception):
42	    """Raised on a malformed or wrong-schema CSV."""
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class Capture:
47	    """One loaded capture. `adc[i]` is a 5-tuple, `labels[i]` a 6-tuple,
48	    `fb_seq[i]` the fretboard sample counter for row i."""
49	
50	    name: str
51	    timestamps: list[float]
52	    fb_seq: list[int]
53	    adc: list[tuple[int, ...]]
54	    labels: list[tuple[int, ...]]
55	
56	    def __len__(self) -> int:
57	        return len(self.adc)
58	
59	    @property
60	    def n_seq_gaps(self) -> int:
61	        return sum(
62	            1 for i in range(1, len(self.fb_seq))
63	            if self.fb_seq[i] != self.fb_seq[i - 1] + 1
64	        )
65	
66	    @property
67	    def strum_fraction(self) -> float:
68	        if not self.labels:
69	            return 0.0
70	        return sum(row[5] for row in self.labels) / len(self.labels)
71	
72	    @property
73	    def n_strum_events(self) -> int:
74	        prev = 0
75	        n = 0
76	        for row in self.labels:
77	            if row[5] and not prev:
78	                n += 1
79	            prev = row[5]
80	        return n
81	
82	
83	def load_capture(path: str | Path) -> Capture:
84	    """Read one actuator-fb CSV into a Capture (stdlib only)."""
85	    path = Path(path)
86	    with path.open(newline="") as fh:
87	        reader = csv.reader(fh)
88	        try:
89	            header = next(reader)
90	        except StopIteration:
91	            raise DataError(f"{path}: empty file")
92	        if header != EXPECTED_HEADER:
93	            raise DataError(
94	                f"{path}: header is not the actuator-fb schema.\n"
95	                f"  expected: {EXPECTED_HEADER}\n"
96	                f"  got:      {header}\n"
97	                "Export with `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator-fb`."
98	            )
99	        timestamps: list[float] = []
100	        fb_seq: list[int] = []
101	        adc: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
102	        labels: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
103	        for lineno, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
104	            if len(row) != len(EXPECTED_HEADER):
105	                raise DataError(
106	                    f"{path}:{lineno}: expected {len(EXPECTED_HEADER)} fields, "
107	                    f"got {len(row)}"
108	                )
109	            timestamps.append(float(row[0]))
110	            fb_seq.append(int(row[1]))
111	            adc.append(tuple(int(row[_ADC_COL0 + c]) for c in range(FRET_COUNT)))
112	            labels.append(tuple(int(row[_LABEL_COL0 + b]) for b in range(N_LABELS)))
113	    return Capture(
114	        name=path.stem, timestamps=timestamps, fb_seq=fb_seq, adc=adc, labels=labels
115	    )
116	
117	
118	def contiguous_runs(fb_seq: list[int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
119	    """Index ranges `[start, end)` over which `fb_seq` increments by exactly 1.
120	
121	    A break (dropped frame → seq jump) starts a new run, so windowing within a
122	    run never stitches two non-adjacent samples across a gap.
123	    """
124	    if not fb_seq:
125	        return []
126	    runs = []
127	    start = 0
128	    for i in range(1, len(fb_seq)):
129	        if fb_seq[i] != fb_seq[i - 1] + 1:
130	            runs.append((start, i))
131	            start = i
132	    runs.append((start, len(fb_seq)))
133	    return runs
134	
135	
136	def causal_window_indices(n_rows: int, window: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]:
137	    """Causal "now-cast" windows over a single capture's rows.
138	
139	    Returns `(start, end, label_row)` triples where rows `[start, end)` are the
140	    `window` feature samples (end is exclusive) and the label is taken at
141	    `label_row = end - 1` — i.e. the window ends *at* the row being predicted,
142	    so only past+present samples feed the prediction. Rows before the first
143	    full window have insufficient history and are skipped.
144	    """
145	    if window < 1:
146	        raise ValueError("window must be >= 1")
147	    return [(i - window + 1, i + 1, i) for i in range(window - 1, n_rows)]
148	
149	
150	def compute_norm_stats(captures: list[Capture]):
151	    """Per-channel (mean, std) over all rows, for input standardisation.
152	
153	    Standardising the narrow ADC band (idle ≈ 3900, dips ≈ 1000) is what makes
154	    the net trainable; raw /4095 leaves inputs clustered near 0.95 and starves
155	    gradients. The affine folds into the int8 input quantisation at deploy, so
156	    this stays deploy-compatible. Returns numpy arrays (mean[5], std[5]).
157	    """
158	    import numpy as np
159	
160	    rows = np.concatenate(
161	        [np.asarray(c.adc, dtype=np.float32) for c in captures if len(c) > 0], axis=0
162	    )
163	    mean = rows.mean(axis=0)
164	    std = rows.std(axis=0)
165	    std[std < 1e-6] = 1.0
166	    return mean, std
167	
168	
169	def _dilate_strum(strum, k: int):
170	    """Widen each strum positive by ±k samples (training labels only)."""
171	    import numpy as np
172	
173	    out = strum.copy()
174	    for off in range(1, k + 1):
175	        out[off:] = np.maximum(out[off:], strum[:-off])
176	        out[:-off] = np.maximum(out[:-off], strum[off:])
177	    return out
178	
179	
180	def build_arrays(
181	    captures: list[Capture],
182	    window: int,
183	    *,
184	    stats=None,
185	    strum_dilate: int = 0,
186	    label_lead: int = 0,
187	):
188	    """Materialise (X, Y, stats) for all captures, windowed per capture.
189	
190	    X: float32 (n_windows, FRET_COUNT, window) — channels-first for Conv1d,
191	       per-channel standardised by `stats` (computed from `captures` if None).
192	    Y: float32 (n_windows, N_LABELS) — the 6 label bits at each window's
193	       label_row. With `strum_dilate>0` the strum label (bit 5) is widened by
194	       ±k samples so a near-miss isn't fully penalised — use for *training*
195	       only, never for eval.
196	
197	    Windows never cross capture boundaries, and never span a `fb_seq` gap
198	    within a capture (each contiguous run is windowed independently).
199	    """
200	    import numpy as np
201	
202	    if stats is None:
203	        stats = compute_norm_stats(captures)
204	    mean, std = stats
205	
206	    xs = []
207	    ys = []
208	    for cap in captures:
209	        adc = (np.asarray(cap.adc, dtype=np.float32) - mean) / std  # (rows, 5)
210	        lab = np.asarray(cap.labels, dtype=np.float32)              # (rows, 6)
211	        if strum_dilate > 0:
212	            lab = lab.copy()
213	            lab[:, 5] = _dilate_strum(lab[:, 5], strum_dilate)
214	        for run_start, run_end in contiguous_runs(cap.fb_seq):
215	            run_len = run_end - run_start
216	            if run_len < window:
217	                continue
218	            for start, end, label_row in causal_window_indices(run_len, window):
219	                lr = label_row + label_lead   # >0 = predict the command N samples ahead
220	                if lr >= run_len:
221	                    continue                  # no future label that far ahead in this run
222	                xs.append(adc[run_start + start:run_start + end].T)   # (5, window)
223	                ys.append(lab[run_start + lr])                        # (6,)
224	    if not xs:
225	        raise DataError(
226	            f"no windows produced — every capture shorter than window={window}?"
227	        )
228	    return np.stack(xs).astype(np.float32), np.stack(ys).astype(np.float32), stats
229	
230	
231	def strum_pos_weight(captures: list[Capture]) -> float:
232	    """Inverse-frequency positive weight for the sparse strum bit: (neg/pos)."""
233	    pos = sum(row[5] for cap in captures for row in cap.labels)
234	    total = sum(len(cap) for cap in captures)
235	    neg = total - pos
236	    return (neg / pos) if pos else 1.0
237
```

```text
/* ---- transport ---------------------------------------------------------- */

static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;
    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;

    switch (event)
    {
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
            break;
        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
            (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ErrorGet();
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }

    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
}

static void console_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    LOG_INFO("CON: console started (FLEXCOM2)\r\n");

    for (;;)
    {
        if (FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
        {
            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(CON_RX_WAIT_MS));
        }

        uint8_t c;
        while (FLEXCOM2_USART_Read(&c, 1u) == 1u)
        {
            embeddedCliReceiveChar(s_cli, (char)c);
        }

        embeddedCliProcess(s_cli);
    }
}

void Console_Initialize(void)
{
    EmbeddedCliConfig *cfg = embeddedCliDefaultConfig();
    cfg->invitation        = "marvin> ";
    cfg->rxBufferSize      = 64u;
    cfg->cmdBufferSize     = 64u;
    cfg->historyBufferSize = 128u;
    cfg->maxBindingCount   = 24u;
    cfg->enableAutoComplete = true;
    cfg->cliBuffer         = s_cli_buf;
    cfg->cliBufferSize     = sizeof(s_cli_buf);

    configASSERT(embeddedCliRequiredSize(cfg) <= sizeof(s_cli_buf));

    s_cli = embeddedCliNew(cfg);
    configASSERT(s_cli != NULL);
    s_cli->writeChar = console_write_char;

    register_commands();

    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);

    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM2 ISR; a persistent
     * 1-byte threshold notification wakes console_task on each inbound byte. */
    FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
    FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadThresholdSet(CON_RX_THRESHOLD);
    (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);

    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(console_task,
                            "Console",
                            CON_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL,
                            CON_TASK_PRIORITY,
                            s_task_stack,
                            &s_task_tcb);
}
```
