```text
1	# gameplay — GH3 game-state engine (offline prototype)
2	
3	Host-side prototype for marvin's game-state observer/controller (spec §4.8, milestone
4	M9/M10). Algorithms are proven here against the real-screen corpus, then the proven,
5	simple logic ports to a firmware `gameplay_engine` module. See
6	[`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`.
7	
8	So far:
9	- **Screen classifier** — which GH3 screen is this (`main_menu`, `song_select`, `in_song`,
10	  …) or `UNKNOWN`.
11	- **Static-list selection reader** — within a recognized static-list screen, which menu
12	  item is highlighted.
13	- **song_select reader** — which song is in the highlight slot (and which setlist).
14	- **Navigator (M10)** — plan a high-level verb (practice-run a song on a difficulty) and
15	  execute it closed-loop along the menu graph, verified against a simulated menu and the real
16	  observer.
17	
18	## Screen classifier
19	
20	Coarse **fixed-region colour fingerprint** + **nearest-centroid** classifier with an
21	**UNKNOWN reject** rule (Q10: fixed-region matching, not general CV). A frame is split
22	into a `cols×rows` grid; each region collapses to its mean BGR; the concatenated vector
23	is compared by integer L1 distance to one centroid per screen class. The design is shaped
24	to port to cheap integer C and is **memory-bound, not compute-bound** on the SAM9X75.
25	
26	Two knobs (chosen empirically by `gameplay eval`, defaults baked into `FingerprintConfig`):
27	
28	- **sample density** — dense (every pixel; ~7–20 ms on-device) vs a sparse N×N lattice per
29	  region (sub-millisecond). Default: 5×5 lattice.
30	- **normalization** — per-frame value standardization, which cancels the **gain/offset
31	  value-slop** of the Wii's analog-component → HDMI path. Default: on (it is what lifts
32	  slop-robustness to ~99.8%).
33	
34	Default config (12×8, 5×5 samples, normalized): 96% leave-one-out accuracy (= 100% of all
35	multi-sample classes; the 4 single-sample classes can't be LOO-matched), ~99.8% robustness
36	across the synthetic analog-slop envelope, ~0.1–0.4 ms estimated per classification.
37	
38	## Static-list selection reader
39	
40	For the 8 fixed-count static-list screens, per-screen menu metadata (ordered items +
41	menu-band geometry, in `metadata.py`) divides the band into one cell per item. The selected
42	cell is the one that deviates most from its **unselected baseline** (learned per screen from
43	the corpus) — GH3 marks selection by *changing* a row (colour/bar), not by making it
44	brightest, so "what changed" is the robust signal. Cell colours are normalized per frame to
45	cancel gain/offset slop. Result: 100% clean / ~99.4% slop on the 33 labelled frames.
46	
47	## song_select reader
48	
49	The selected song sits in a fixed highlight slot (except each setlist's first song, which
50	sits one row lower). We identify it by matching the slot's low-res grayscale bitmap against
51	the 64 per-song templates — across **both** setlists, so main/bonus falls out of the match.
52	A small read-time offset search re-aligns the slot, which makes the fine grid tolerant of
53	positional slop. Result: 64/64 clean, ~99.1% under slop. The active setlist is also read
54	independently from the page background colour (main = yellow, bonus = white; warmth R−B):
55	100% clean and under slop.
56	
57	Char-level OCR is deliberately out of scope: menu items and song titles are a closed set we
58	already have reference bitmaps for (match, don't decode); digit OCR comes only with score
59	reading. `section_select` (variable list) and reading the scrolling neighbour list are deferred.
60	
61	## Navigator (M10)
62	
63	`navgraph.py` encodes the menu graph (`firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`) as data;
64	`navigator.py` plans a verb (`plan_practice_run`, `plan_goto`) and runs it closed-loop through
65	an `Observer`/`Actuator` seam. The controller is observation-driven — each step runs against
66	the screen actually observed — which yields normal progress, the `part_select` skip, and RED
67	recovery from one rule. Offline it's driven by `simgame.py` (the test oracle); on the device
68	the same seam takes the CV observer + fretboard link. Selections strum the signed delta from
69	the observed cursor (sticky-safe); FULL SONG/FULL SPEED strum up until the selection stops
70	moving (no blind count).
71	
72	## Usage
73	
74	```sh
75	uv sync --group dev
76	
77	uv run gameplay eval                 # classifier + selection reader: accuracy, robustness, thresholds, HW time
78	uv run gameplay eval --no-sweep      # skip the parameter sweep
79	uv run gameplay classify path/to/frame.png   # screen id (+ selection / song)
80	uv run gameplay rows path/to/frame.png       # debug per-cell selection scores
81	uv run gameplay navigate --song 19 --difficulty hard   # plan + run a practice run vs the sim
82	uv run gameplay export-c --out gameplay_metadata.h     # freeze recognizer metadata to a C header
83	
84	uv run pytest
85	```
86	
87	## Firmware port (marvin `gameplay_engine`, spec §4.8)
88	
89	The proven algorithms are being ported to marvin firmware in phases (see `docs/journal.md`).
90	Phase 0 (done) is `gameplay export-c`: it emits all recognizer data — classifier
91	centroids/thresholds, static-list menu geometry + baselines, song templates/ROIs — as a single
92	generated C header (`gameplay_metadata.h`, plain PODs + flat arrays) that the firmware compiles
93	in. Floats are only the per-frame-normalized baselines/song vectors (soft-float on the ARM926).
94	The generated header is verified to compile under `cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra`.
95	
96	The corpus is read from `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (override with
97	`$GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR`). Labels come from each filename's prefix.
98
```
</details></tool-use>

1	"""Train and evaluate the baseline StrumNet on actuator-labelled captures.
2	
3	Imports torch/numpy — invoked via the `train` / `eval` CLI subcommands, which
4	require the `train` dependency group installed.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	from . import N_LABELS
13	from .data import Capture, build_arrays, compute_norm_stats, load_capture, strum_pos_weight
14	from .metrics import (
15	    PulseStats,
16	    StrumTiming,
17	    monostable,
18	    per_bit_accuracy,
19	    per_bit_f1,
20	    strum_event_timing,
21	    strum_pulse_stats,

23	
24	
25	@dataclass
26	class EvalReport:
27	    per_bit_acc: list[float]
28	    per_bit_f1: list[float]
29	    strum: StrumTiming           # raw predicted strum, event timing
30	    pulse: PulseStats            # raw predicted strum, pulse shape
31	    strum_post: StrumTiming | None = None   # after the monostable post-processor
32	    pulse_post: PulseStats | None = None
33	
34	
35	def _predict_capture(model, cap: Capture, window: int, stats, strum_thresh: float = 0.5):
36	    """Return (pred_bits, true_bits, pred_strum_seq, true_strum_seq) for one capture.
37	
38	    Eval never dilates the strum label — `strum_dilate=0` — so timing is scored
39	    against the true single-tick events. `strum_thresh` is the decision
40	    threshold for the strum bit only (frets stay at 0.5); raise it to trade
41	    strum recall for precision.
42	    """
43	    import numpy as np
44	    import torch
45	
46	    X, Y, _ = build_arrays([cap], window, stats=stats, strum_dilate=0)
47	    model.eval()
48	    with torch.no_grad():
49	        probs = torch.sigmoid(model(torch.from_numpy(X))).cpu().numpy()
50	    bits = (probs >= 0.5).astype(int)
51	    bits[:, 5] = (probs[:, 5] >= strum_thresh).astype(int)
52	    pred_bits = bits.tolist()
53	    true_bits = Y.astype(int).tolist()
54	    pred_strum = [int(r[5]) for r in pred_bits]
55	    true_strum = [int(r[5]) for r in true_bits]
56	    return pred_bits, true_bits, pred_strum, true_strum
57	
58	
59	def _agg_timing(errs, nt, npred, m) -> StrumTiming:
60	    return StrumTiming(
61	        n_true=nt, n_pred=npred, matched=m,
62	        precision=(m / npred) if npred else 0.0,
63	        recall=(m / nt) if nt else 0.0,
64	        errors_ms=errs,
65	    )
66	
67	
68	def evaluate(
69	    model, captures: list[Capture], window: int, stats,
70	    *, tol_samples: int = 5, hold: int = 0, refractory: int = 0,
71	    strum_thresh: float = 0.5,
72	) -> EvalReport:
73	    all_pred: list[list[int]] = []
74	    all_true: list[list[int]] = []
75	    raw = {"err": [], "nt": 0, "np": 0, "m": 0, "pulses": 0, "glitch": 0, "short": 0, "dur": []}
76	    post = {"err": [], "nt": 0, "np": 0, "m": 0, "pulses": 0, "glitch": 0, "short": 0, "dur": []}
77	    do_post = hold > 0
78	
79	    def _accum(acc, st, ps):
80	        acc["err"].extend(st.errors_ms); acc["nt"] += st.n_true
81	        acc["np"] += st.n_pred; acc["m"] += st.matched
82	        acc["pulses"] += ps.n_pulses; acc["glitch"] += ps.n_glitches
83	        acc["short"] += ps.n_too_short; acc["dur"].extend(ps.durations_ticks)
84	
85	    for cap in captures:
86	        if len(cap) < window:
87	            continue
88	        pred_bits, true_bits, pred_strum, true_strum = _predict_capture(
89	            model, cap, window, stats, strum_thresh)
90	        all_pred.extend(pred_bits)
91	        all_true.extend(true_bits)
92	        _accum(raw,
93	               strum_event_timing(pred_strum, true_strum, tol_samples=tol_samples),
94	               strum_pulse_stats(pred_strum))
95	        if do_post:
96	            clean = monostable(pred_strum, hold=hold, refractory=refractory)
97	            _accum(post,
98	                   strum_event_timing(clean, true_strum, tol_samples=tol_samples),
99	                   strum_pulse_stats(clean))
100	
101	    def _pulse(acc):
102	        return PulseStats(acc["pulses"], acc["glitch"], acc["short"], acc["dur"])
103	
104	    return EvalReport(
105	        per_bit_acc=per_bit_accuracy(all_pred, all_true),
106	        per_bit_f1=per_bit_f1(all_pred, all_true),
107	        strum=_agg_timing(raw["err"], raw["nt"], raw["np"], raw["m"]),
108	        pulse=_pulse(raw),
109	        strum_post=_agg_timing(post["err"], post["nt"], post["np"], post["m"]) if do_post else None,
110	        pulse_post=_pulse(post) if do_post else None,
111	    )
112	
113	
114	def train(args) -> None:
115	    import numpy as np
116	    import torch
117	    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
118	
119	    from .model import StrumNet, count_macs
120	    from .metrics import LABEL_NAMES
121	
122	    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
123	
124	    if args.overfit:
125	        # Diagnostic: train and evaluate on the same single capture. If frets
126	        # can't reach ~98% here, the problem is model/optimisation/formulation,
127	        # not data variety.
128	        cap = load_capture(args.overfit)
129	        train_caps = [cap]
130	        eval_caps = [cap]
131	        print(f"OVERFIT mode: train==eval on {cap.name} "
132	              f"({len(cap)} rows, strum {cap.strum_fraction*100:.1f}%)")
133	    elif getattr(args, "no_holdout", False):
134	        train_caps = [load_capture(p) for p in args.data]
135	        eval_caps = train_caps   # deploy model: use everything; eval = train (optimistic)
136	        print(f"DEPLOY mode: train on all {len(train_caps)} captures, no holdout "
137	              f"(eval = training set)")
138	        for c in train_caps:
139	            print(f"  {c.name}: {len(c)} rows, strum {c.strum_fraction*100:.1f}%, "
140	                  f"{c.n_strum_events} events")
141	    else:
142	        holdout_path = Path(args.holdout)
143	        train_caps = [load_capture(p) for p in args.data if Path(p) != holdout_path]
144	        eval_caps = [load_capture(holdout_path)]
145	        print(f"train: {len(train_caps)} captures, holdout: {eval_caps[0].name}")
146	        for c in train_caps:
147	            print(f"  {c.name}: {len(c)} rows, strum {c.strum_fraction*100:.1f}%, "
148	                  f"{c.n_strum_events} events")
149	
150	    lead = getattr(args, "label_lead", 0)
151	    stats = compute_norm_stats(train_caps)
152	    X, Y, _ = build_arrays(train_caps, args.window, stats=stats,
153	                           strum_dilate=args.strum_dilate, label_lead=lead)
154	    pos_w = args.strum_weight if args.strum_weight else strum_pos_weight(train_caps)
155	    print(f"windows: {X.shape[0]}, input {X.shape[1:]} | strum pos_weight={pos_w:.1f}"
156	          f"{' | strum_dilate=' + str(args.strum_dilate) if args.strum_dilate else ''}"
157	          f"{' | label_lead=' + str(lead) if lead else ''}")
158	
159	    model = StrumNet(channels=args.channels, kernel=args.kernel, dilations=args.dilations)
160	    print(f"dilations={args.dilations} | ~{count_macs(model, args.window)} MACs/inference "
161	          f"(budget ≈100k @ 24MHz)")
162	
163	    pos_weight = torch.tensor([1.0] * (N_LABELS - 1) + [pos_w], dtype=torch.float32)
164	    loss_fn = torch.nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(pos_weight=pos_weight)
165	    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=args.lr)
166	
167	    ds = TensorDataset(torch.from_numpy(X), torch.from_numpy(Y))
168	    dl = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=True)
169	
170	    for epoch in range(1, args.epochs + 1):
171	        model.train()
172	        total = 0.0
173	        for xb, yb in dl:
174	            opt.zero_grad()
175	            loss = loss_fn(model(xb), yb)
176	            loss.backward()
177	            opt.step()
178	            total += loss.item() * xb.shape[0]
179	        rep = evaluate(model, eval_caps, args.window, stats, tol_samples=args.tol,
180	                       hold=args.strum_hold, refractory=args.strum_refractory,
181	                       strum_thresh=args.strum_thresh)
182	        acc_str = " ".join(f"{n}={a:.3f}" for n, a in zip(LABEL_NAMES, rep.per_bit_acc))
183	        print(f"epoch {epoch:3d} | loss {total/len(ds):.4f} | acc {acc_str}")
184	        print(f"            | raw  {rep.strum.summary()} | {rep.pulse.summary()}")
185	        if rep.strum_post is not None:
186	            print(f"            | mono {rep.strum_post.summary()} | {rep.pulse_post.summary()}")
187	
188	    if args.out:
189	        torch.save({"state_dict": model.state_dict(),
190	                    "window": args.window,
191	                    "channels": args.channels,
192	                    "kernel": args.kernel,
193	                    "dilations": list(args.dilations),
194	                    "label_lead": lead,
195	                    "norm_mean": stats[0].tolist(),
196	                    "norm_std": stats[1].tolist()}, args.out)
197	        print(f"saved {args.out}")

```text
1	# Fret-Tuner Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Web-based Python tool for developing and refining fret-press detection algorithms. Consumes the same raw ADC data the firmware sees -- either live from the board over UART or replayed from a captured CSV -- runs detection logic in Python, and visualizes everything in an interactive browser UI. Optionally sends actuation commands back to the microcontroller, moving the entire detection and strum-timing pipeline to the PC for rapid iteration.
6	
7	## Video reference (always-on)
8	
9	A first-class always-on subsystem. The UI exposes a video viewport at all times; behavior is independent of which detector is active.
10	
11	**Primary role**: time-aligned visual reference and recording against the ADC sample timeline and any derived signals (waveforms, detector state, fret/strum events). The question it answers: does what was on screen at time *t* match what the ADC and algorithms reported at *t*?
12	
13	**Secondary roles**: debugging alignment between capture and charts, reviewing a session after the fact, documenting false positives/negatives.
14	
15	### Requirements
16	
17	- **Primacy**: video reference is a first-class always-on subsystem, not gated on detector choice.
18	- **Source ownership**: the fret-tuner **backend** owns the camera. Exactly one source feeds the reference ring buffer at a time. The source is selectable in the UI from cameras enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option, plus any video file supplied for replay.
19	- **Buffer**: server-side ring buffer with **≥30 s wall-clock coverage** at a **target 30 Hz** capture rate. The buffer accepts whatever rate the camera delivers, sized to retain ≥30 s even when the source runs as fast as 60 Hz.
20	- **Synchronization**: every buffered frame carries a sample-clock timestamp anchored to the ADC stream so that any time *t* in the chart timeline maps to the closest buffered frame.
21	- **Live behavior**: while playing, the browser shows the most recent server frame with overlays composed for that frame's *t*.
22	- **Paused / scrubbing**: when paused, or while panning/zooming the charts, the video display follows the chart cursor / center time, picking the closest buffered frame.
23	- **Overlays**: per-frame composition (live and paused) at the display path's natural rate. Required minimum set:
24	    - 5 fret **pressed-state** indicators (per ADC channel)
25	    - **strum state** indicators (down + up, sourced from the actuator pipeline)
26	    - **scrub-time** text cursor
27	  Detectors may register additional overlay layers via the extension hook (see [Detection Algorithm Contract → Overlay extension](#overlay-extension)).
28	- **Detector consumption**: detectors that need pixel data (e.g. `detect_video`) **read from the reference buffer**; they do not own a separate camera grab.
29	
30	## Actuation (always-on)
31	
32	A first-class always-on subsystem that owns the GPIO command serial link to the actuator microcontroller. Behavior is independent of which detector is active and of where the ADC data comes from (live serial, CSV replay, or none).
33	
34	**Primary role**: consume detector state each tick, run the strum timing pipeline (chord window, FIFO scheduling, fret early/late, strum pulse), and emit a 1-byte GPIO bitmask to the actuator board over UART.
35	
36	### Requirements
37	
38	- **Primacy**: actuation is a first-class always-on subsystem, not a side effect of opening a data port. It can be enabled with any detector and any data source (including CSV-only replay against a live actuator board).
39	- **Source ownership**: the actuator owns its own `serial.Serial` handle. The port is selectable in the UI from ports enumerated by the backend, plus a "none" option.
40	- **Port sharing**: the actuator port may name the same `/dev/cu.*` device as an ADC data port (single-board case). In that case the backend opens the device once and shares the handle between the data reader and the actuator writer; the writer never blocks on the reader and vice versa.
41	- **Reconnect**: when the actuator port is lost (unplug, USB sleep, etc.) the writer goes silent without raising; on reconnect, output resumes. Auto-reconnect runs at the same cadence as the data-port reconnect.
42	- **Enable gate**: a UI toggle gates output at the *bitmask* level. When disabled, the timing pipeline still runs (and reports `output_mask = 0`), but no bytes are written. Manual GPIO override (`manual_output`) still works when actuation is disabled, so individual buttons can be poked from the browser without engaging the full pipeline.
43	- **Always-on lifecycle**: created at server startup, persists across detector switches, never owned by a detector.
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	The backend is organized around two **always-on subsystems** (video reference, actuation) and one swappable **detector subsystem**. Always-on subsystems own their I/O and run regardless of which detector is active. The detector consumes whatever inputs it needs (ADC stream, video frames, etc.), produces detection state, and feeds it to the actuator.
48	
49	```
50	Browser (localhost:8080)
51	  ├── Video viewport (live or scrubbed frame + composited overlays)
52	  ├── uPlot charts (zoom, pan, pause)
53	  ├── Controls (camera source, actuator port, detector, params, recording)
54	  └── WebSocket  (sample data, detector state, sources, actuator status)
55	        ↕
56	FastAPI backend (Python)
57	  ├── camera.py          (OpenCV capture → shared ring buffer, ≥30 s @ ≥30 Hz)   [always-on]
58	  ├── actuator.py        (strum timing pipeline + GPIO serial TX)                 [always-on]
59	  ├── stream.py          (serial/CSV ADC source for ADC-based detectors)
60	  ├── detect_*.py        (consume samples and/or video frames; emit overlay layers)
61	  └── server.py          (WebSocket + HTTP video transport, subsystem wiring)
62	        ↕
63	Microcontrollers (PIC32CM)
64	  ├── Data board   →  fret_scan + data_stream     (17-byte ADC frames over UART)
65	  └── Actuator board → cmd_receive                (1-byte bitmask → GPIO assert/release)
66	                       The data board and actuator board may be the same physical
67	                       device sharing one UART, or two different devices.
68	```
69	
70	Browser and backend are deployed as a split / resizable layout: video viewport and ADC charts are co-equal, neither dominant by default. The shared video ring buffer lives in the backend; detector pixel consumers and the browser display both read from it.
71	
72	## File Layout
73	
74	```
75	tools/fret-tuner/
76	    fret-tuner.py          # CLI entry point (launches server, opens browser)
77	    server.py              # FastAPI app, WebSocket, data pipeline wiring
78	    camera.py              # OpenCV capture + shared video ring buffer
79	    index.html             # Browser UI (uPlot charts + video viewport, no build step)
80	    stream.py              # Serial + CSV data sources
81	    actuator.py            # Strum timing pipeline (port of fret_button.c)
82	    detect_threshold.py    # Detection: fixed per-channel hysteresis
83	    detect_trough.py       # Detection: baseline + trough FSM
84	    detect_slope.py        # Detection: EMA + slope FSM with re-press handling
85	    detect_video.py        # Detection: pixel sampling against the reference buffer
86	    video_calibrate.py     # Standalone helper for marking detect_video sensor coords
87	    requirements.txt       # Python dependencies
88	    SPEC.md                # This file
89	    .gitignore
90	
91	firmware/fretboard/
92	    cmd_receive.c          # UART RX command handler
93	    cmd_receive.h          # Header
94	```
95	
96	## Data Source
97	
98	### UART Binary Frame (micro → PC)
99	
100	The fretboard firmware streams 17-byte packed frames at **240 Hz** over SERCOM1 USART at **500000 baud** (8N1):
101	
102	```
103	Offset  Size   Field
104	------  -----  -----
105	0       1      Start byte (0x03)
106	1       2      Green   (uint16 LE, 12-bit ADC)
107	3       2      Red     (uint16 LE)
108	5       2      Yellow  (uint16 LE)
109	7       2      Blue    (uint16 LE)
110	9       2      Orange  (uint16 LE)
111	11      4      sample_seq (uint32 LE) — monotonic counter, one per tick; gaps indicate dropped frames
112	15      1      applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven during this scan (edge-ai training sync)
113	16      1      End byte (0xFC)
114	```
115	
116	### Command Byte (PC → micro)
117	
118	Single byte bitmask sent over the same serial connection (full-duplex). Each bit directly controls one GPIO output:
119	
120	```
121	Bit   Output
122	---   ------
123	0     Green fret
124	1     Red fret
125	2     Yellow fret
126	3     Blue fret
127	4     Orange fret
128	5     Strum down
129	6     Strum up
130	```
131	
132	Bit = 1 → assert (drive low). Bit = 0 → release (tri-state). The firmware applies the latest received byte each tick. When no bytes are received, outputs remain unchanged.
133	
134	### Serial Auto-Reconnect
135	
136	When the USB serial connection is lost (board unplugged, USB sleep, etc.), the feed loop catches the error, closes the stale serial handle, and retries opening the port every 2 seconds until the device reappears. On disconnect and reconnect, the server pushes `serial_status` messages over WebSocket so the browser UI can display the current state (amber "Serial disconnected -- reconnecting..." while down, green "Connected" on recovery). CSV replay sources are not affected.
137	
138	### CSV Replay Format
139	
140	CSV files captured from Microchip Data Visualizer. Expected columns:
141	
142	```
143	timestamp,BLUE RAW,BLUE,GREEN RAW,GREEN,ORANGE RAW,ORANGE,RED RAW,RED,YELLOW RAW,YELLOW
144	```
145	
146	Only the `timestamp` and `* RAW` columns are consumed.
147	
148	## Detection Algorithm Contract
149	
150	Each detector lives in its own `detect_*.py` file and exports a `Detector` class:
151	
152	```python
153	class Detector:
154	    @classmethod
155	    def default_params(cls) -> dict:
156	        """Return default parameter values."""
157	
158	    def __init__(self, **params):
159	        """Accept tunable parameters as keyword args."""
160	
161	    def update(self, sample: Sample) -> dict:
162	        """Process one sample. Return per-channel state dict:
163	        {
164	            "green":  {"pressed": bool, "baseline": int, ...},
165	            ...
166	        }
167	        """
168	```
169	
170	The `update()` return dict must include `"pressed"` (bool) and `"baseline"` (int) per channel. Additional keys are detector-specific and available for charting.
171	
172	The server auto-injects `"raw"` (the raw ADC reading for that channel) into each per-channel state dict before charting, so detectors do not need to copy it themselves.
173	
174	### Chart schema
175	
176	Detectors describe what their five chart slots should display via:
177	
178	```python
179	class Detector:
180	    def chart_schema(self) -> list[dict]:
181	        """Return 5 slot specs:
182	        {
183	            "id":      str,             # state-dict key (e.g. "green")
184	            "label":   str,             # axis label
185	            "color":   "#rrggbb",
186	            "y_range": [min, max],
187	            "series":  [
188	                {"key": str, "label": str, "color": "#rrggbb",
189	                 "width": float, "dash": [int, int] | None},
190	                ...
191	            ],
192	        }
193	        """
194	```
195	
196	Each `series.key` names a field inside that channel's state dict. `stream.adc_chart_schema(extra_series=[...])` builds the conventional `raw + <extras>` layout for ADC detectors. Detectors with no use for raw ADC (e.g. `detect_video`) simply omit the `"raw"` series.
197	
198	The browser rebuilds its chart slots whenever a new schema arrives, so switching detectors swaps the chart contents (labels, colors, y-range, plotted series) along with the algorithm.
199	
200	### Overlay extension
201	
202	Detectors may optionally contribute named overlay layers to the video viewport:
203	
204	```python
205	class Detector:
206	    def overlays(self) -> list[OverlayLayer]:
207	        """Optional. Return list of overlay layers to draw on the video.
208	        Each layer = {name: str, draw(ctx, frame_meta, sample_state) -> None}.
209	        Returning [] (or omitting the method) means no detector-specific overlays.
210	        """
211	        return []
212	```
213	
214	Layers compose on top of the always-on minimum set (fret pressed-state, strum state, scrub time). Transport for overlay drawcalls is implementation-defined: the server may bake them into delivered frames, or stream drawcall metadata (see [WebSocket Protocol](#websocket-protocol) `video_meta`) for client-side compositing.
215	
216	`detect_video`, for example, registers a layer that draws its sensor sample points and per-button signal levels.
217	
218	### Adding a new detector
219	
220	1. Create `tools/fret-tuner/detect_myalgo.py`
221	2. Implement a `Detector` class following the contract above
222	3. Select it from the dropdown in the browser UI (or `--detector detect_myalgo` on the CLI)
223	
224	The server hot-reloads detector modules on switch, so you can edit the file and switch to it without restarting.
225	
226	## Bundled Detector: detect_threshold
227	
228	Fixed per-channel hysteresis. Matches the current firmware `fret_detect.c`.
229	
230	| Parameter | Default | Description |
231	|-----------|---------|-------------|
232	| `GREEN_PRESS` | 2500 | Green press threshold |
233	| `GREEN_RELEASE` | 2800 | Green release threshold |
234	| `RED_PRESS` | 2500 | Red press threshold |
235	| `RED_RELEASE` | 2800 | Red release threshold |
236	| `YELLOW_PRESS` | 1500 | Yellow press threshold |
237	| `YELLOW_RELEASE` | 1700 | Yellow release threshold |
238	| `BLUE_PRESS` | 1500 | Blue press threshold |
239	| `BLUE_RELEASE` | 1700 | Blue release threshold |
240	| `ORANGE_PRESS` | 2000 | Orange press threshold |
241	| `ORANGE_RELEASE` | 2200 | Orange release threshold |
242	
243	## Bundled Detector: detect_trough
244	
245	Baseline + trough FSM. Three states: IDLE → DESCENDING → PRESSED.
246	
247	| Parameter | Default | Description |
248	|-----------|---------|-------------|
249	| `MIN_DROP` | 200 | ADC counts below baseline to begin descent tracking |
250	| `RISE_CONFIRM` | 50 | ADC counts above running minimum to confirm press |
251	| `RELEASE_MARGIN` | 300 | Counts within baseline to trigger release |
252	| `BASELINE_DECAY_RATE` | 250 | Samples between 1-count baseline decrements |
253	
254	## Actuator (actuator.py)
255	
256	Python port of `firmware/fretboard/fret_button.c`. Translates detector press/release edges into a timed sequence of fret assertions and strum pulses.
257	
258	### Timing Pipeline
259	
260	1. **Chord window** -- new presses within `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` are accumulated
261	2. **Chord commit** -- schedules note assert at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS - FRET_EARLY_MS` and strum at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`
262	3. **Note FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending fret assertions, processed in order
263	4. **Strum FIFO** (cap 8) -- pending strum triggers, alternating up/down
264	5. **Strum pulse** -- held for `STRUM_PULSE_MS`, then released
265	6. **Delayed releases** -- each released fret is scheduled for release at `t + STRUM_DELAY_MS`, skipped if still needed by pending notes/strums
266	
267	### Timing Parameters
268	
269	| Parameter | Default | Description |
270	|-----------|---------|-------------|
271	| `STRUM_DELAY_MS` | 220 | Delay from chord commit to strum |
272	| `FRET_EARLY_MS` | 50 | How early frets assert before strum |
273	| `STRUM_PULSE_MS` | 50 | How long the strum output is held |
274	| `CHORD_WINDOW_MS` | 20 | Window for accumulating chord presses |
275	
276	All timing is driven by sample timestamps, not wall clock, so the pipeline behaves identically in live and CSV replay modes.
277	
278	### Output
279	
280	Computes a 7-bit bitmask each tick and writes it to the serial port. Actuation is disabled by default and toggled from the browser UI.
281	
282	## Firmware: cmd_receive
283	
284	Minimal command receiver added to the fretboard firmware. Replaces `fret_detect` and `fret_button` in `main.c` -- the microcontroller becomes a scan/stream/actuate relay.
285	
286	### Main loop (modified)
287	
288	```c
289	fret_scan_all();
290	data_stream_send();
291	cmd_receive_update();
292	```
293	
294	### cmd_receive_update()
295	
296	1. Checks `SERCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet()` for available bytes
297	2. Reads all available bytes, keeps the last one
298	3. Applies the bitmask: for each bit, asserts (drive low + output enable) or releases (input enable) the corresponding GPIO
299	
300	## Browser UI
301	
302	Single-file HTML served by the backend at `http://localhost:8080`. Loads uPlot from CDN (no build step).
303	
304	### Charts
305	
306	- 5 stacked uPlot time-series charts, one per fret slot (green, red, yellow, blue, orange)
307	- The active detector's `chart_schema()` defines the series, labels, colors, and y-range for each slot. ADC detectors plot raw ADC + their baseline / threshold lines; `detect_video` plots its hold + edge signals (no raw ADC). Switching detectors swaps the chart contents.
308	- Shaded press bands and (where the detector emits `press_count`) re-press tick marks are overlaid in the slot color
309	- Native mouse-drag zoom, scroll-wheel zoom, double-click to reset
310	
311	### Controls (sidebar)
312	
313	- **Pause / Resume** -- freezes chart updates; data continues to buffer server-side
314	- **Window width** -- slider controlling visible time range (0.5--30 seconds)
315	- **Detector dropdown** -- switch between available `detect_*.py` modules live
316	- **Parameter sliders** -- dynamically generated from the active detector's `default_params()`, changes take effect immediately
317	- **Camera source dropdown** -- enumerated cameras + "none"; controls the always-on video reference
318	- **Actuator port dropdown** -- enumerated `/dev/cu.*` (or platform equivalent) serial ports + "none"; controls the always-on actuator. Selecting the same device as a live ADC data port shares the handle.
319	- **Actuation toggle** -- enable/disable writing command bytes (the timing pipeline runs either way)
320	- **Timing sliders** -- strum delay, fret early, strum pulse, chord window
321	- **Connection status** indicators -- separate badges for the data port and the actuator port
322	
323	### Layout
324	
325	Split / resizable two-pane layout. The **video viewport** and the **ADC charts** are co-equal first-class panes; neither is dominant by default and the user can resize the split. Sidebar controls remain to one side.
326	
327	### Video viewport
328	
329	Backed by the always-on subsystem in [Video reference (always-on)](#video-reference-always-on). UI surface:
330	
331	- **Source selector** -- lists cameras enumerated by the backend, plus "none" and any `--video FILE` replay file. Selection persisted by the backend, applied immediately.
332	- **Recording controls** -- start / stop / save buffer (writes paired video + ADC log; see [Recording & paired CSV replay](#recording--paired-csv-replay)). Default off.
333	- **Pause / scrub** -- synchronized with the charts' pause; chart center time drives the displayed frame.
334	- **Overlays** -- always-on minimum (5 fret pressed-state indicators, strum state, scrub time) plus any layers the active detector registers via [Overlay extension](#overlay-extension).
335	
336	### Recording & paired CSV replay
337	
338	- A live session can be **recorded**: the backend drains the reference ring buffer to a video file alongside the ADC sample log (CSV), with a shared time anchor written into the recording so the two replay in sync.
339	- `python fret-tuner.py --csv FILE [--video FILE]` replays both. If `--video` is omitted, the video viewport shows "no recorded video for this CSV" and disables source selection for the duration of the replay.
340	- Recording is started/stopped explicitly from the sidebar; default off.
341	
342	### WebSocket Protocol
343	
344	Sample data, detector state, and overlay metadata flow over the WebSocket; raw video frames are delivered over a parallel HTTP video transport (implementation choice; the existing tool uses MJPEG). Both share the same sample-clock timestamps so chart and video scrubbing target the same *t*.
345	
346	#### Master clock: the displayed video frame
347	
348	The currently displayed video frame is the single source of truth for *now*. Each captured frame has a `seq` (monotonic id) and a `t` (sample-clock timestamp), and every UI element (chart cursor, viewport scroll, overlay text) aligns to the *currently displayed* frame's `t` -- not to the latest ADC sample, the wall clock, or the network arrival time.
349	
350	- **Live mode**: the server emits a `frame_tick` message on every buffer write (~30 Hz). The browser updates `currentFrame = {seq, t}` and re-clips the chart's leading edge to that `t`. ADC samples that arrived *after* the latest displayed frame are buffered but not yet visible; they are revealed on the next tick. Chart movement is therefore quantized at the camera frame rate, which is the trade-off we accept to keep video, charts, and overlays exactly aligned.
351	- **Pause / scrub**: `frame_tick` is ignored. The user moves `currentFrame` via the timeline, frame-step buttons, or slow-mo playback. Each scrub action returns from the server with a `{seq, t}` pair, which the browser writes back into `currentFrame`.
352	- **CSV / no-camera fallback**: when no camera is attached, no `frame_tick` is emitted. The browser falls back to the latest ingested ADC sample timestamp as `currentFrame.t`, with `seq=null`.
353	
354	Server → client:
355	
356	```json
357	{"type": "data", "samples": [...], "state": [...], "actuator_mask": 0}
358	{"type": "frame_tick", "seq": 1234, "t": 12.345}          // ~30 Hz, camera only
359	{"type": "detector", "name": "...", "params": {...}, "available": [...],
360	 "timing": {...}, "actuate_enabled": false}
361	{"type": "serial_status", "connected": true}              // data port
362	{"type": "actuator_status", "connected": true,
363	 "available": [...], "active": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}   // actuator port
364	{"type": "video_meta", "t": 12.345, "layers": [...]}
365	{"type": "sources", "available": [...], "active": "..."}  // camera sources
366	{"type": "recording", "active": false, "path": null}
367	```
368	
369	Client → server:
370	
371	```json
372	{"type": "pause"}
373	{"type": "resume"}
374	{"type": "set_params", "params": {"KEY": value}}
375	{"type": "set_detector", "name": "detect_trough"}
376	{"type": "set_timing", "params": {"STRUM_DELAY_MS": 200}}
377	{"type": "set_actuate", "enabled": true}
378	{"type": "set_source", "name": "..."}            // camera source
379	{"type": "set_actuator_port", "name": "/dev/cu.usbmodem21202"}  // or "none"
380	{"type": "manual_output", "mask": 0}
381	{"type": "record_start"}
382	{"type": "record_stop"}
383	```
384	
385	The backend also exposes:
386	
387	- `GET /api/sources` -- camera sources (mirror of the WS `sources` message)
388	- `GET /api/serial-ports` -- enumerated serial ports for the actuator dropdown
389	- `GET /video` -- live MJPEG of the working-resolution buffer (server-rendered overlays applied)
390	- `GET /video/snap?t=<sec>` -- single JPEG of the buffered frame closest to *t*. Response carries `X-Frame-Seq` and `X-Frame-Time` headers (and a matching `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`) so the browser can sync `currentFrame` to the snapped frame even when the snapped *t* differs from the requested *t*.
391	- `GET /video/step?dir=next|prev&n=N&{seq=S | t=T}` -- walk the ring buffer to the n-th next/prev frame. Address by `seq` for exact stepping (preferred when the browser holds a known frame); fall back to `t` for the first scrub when seq is unknown. Returns `{"seq": int, "t": float, "buffered": int}`.
392	
393	## CLI Reference
394	
395	```
396	usage: fret-tuner.py [-h] (--port PORT | --csv FILE) [--video FILE]
397	                     [--actuator-port PORT] [--camera ID]
398	                     [--detector MODULE] [--param KEY=VALUE] [--fast]
399	                     [--host HOST] [--web-port PORT]
400	```
401	
402	`--port` selects the **data** serial port (ADC frame source). `--actuator-port` selects the **actuator** serial port; if omitted, the actuator starts idle and a port can be chosen at runtime from the sidebar dropdown. If `--actuator-port` names the same device as `--port`, the backend opens it once and shares the handle for read and write.
403	
404	### Examples
405	
406	```bash
407	# Single board: ADC stream + actuator on the same port (handle is shared)
408	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
409	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202
410	
411	# Two boards: ADC stream on one device, actuator on another
412	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 \
413	    --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
414	
415	# CSV replay against a live actuator board
416	python fret-tuner.py --csv session.csv --actuator-port /dev/cu.usbmodem31301
417	
418	# CSV replay, no actuator (UI dropdown can attach one later)
419	python fret-tuner.py --csv ../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard-sample-raw.csv
420	
421	# Start with trough detector and custom parameters
422	python fret-tuner.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodem21202 --detector detect_trough \
423	    --param MIN_DROP=150 --param RISE_CONFIRM=30
424	
425	# Fast CSV replay (no real-time pacing)
426	python fret-tuner.py --csv capture.csv --fast
427	```
428	
429	## Dependencies
430	
431	Managed with `uv` (inline script metadata in `ds_monitor.py`; `pyproject.toml` for the main tool). Required packages:
432	
433	- `pyserial >= 3.5`
434	- `numpy >= 1.24`
435	- `fastapi >= 0.115`
436	- `uvicorn[standard] >= 0.30`
437	- `websockets >= 12.0`
438	- `opencv-python` (server-side video capture and `detect_video`)
439	
440	## Bundled Detector: detect_video
441	
442	Pixel-sampling detector that **consumes the shared reference video buffer**. It does not own a camera and does not serve its own video stream; sensor sample points and per-button signal levels are exposed as an [overlay layer](#overlay-extension) for the viewport.
443	
444	Two sensor points per button, both above the strike line:
445	
446	- **Sensor 1 (hold)** -- brightness detect (color OR white). Sets `pressed=True` whenever max channel brightness exceeds `THRESHOLD`.
447	- **Sensor 2 (edge)** -- color-filtered leading-edge detect. Increments `press_count` on each new note arrival for strum timing.
448	
449	Detection thresholds are applied directly to raw pixel values (dark background is implicit zero, no settle/calibration phase).
450	
451	### Observed Game Colors (camera-captured BGR)
452	
453	Colors are highly saturated with negligible off-channel values:
454	
455	| Color  | B    | G    | R    | Notes |
456	|--------|------|------|------|-------|
457	| Red    | <10  | <10  | >100 | Almost completely red |
458	| Green  | <10  | >100 | <10  | Completely green |
459	| Blue   | >100 | ~67  | <10  | B dominant, G about 2/3 of B, low R |
460	| Yellow | <10  | ~100 | ~100 | Even mix of G and R, very low B |
461	| Orange | <10  | ~50  | >100 | R dominant, G about half of R, low B |
462	| White (fret bar) | ~160 | ~160 | ~160 | Equal channels at brightest, sat near 0 |
463	
464	The edge detector uses a color filter with saturation scaling `(max-min)/max` to reject white/gray fret bars regardless of camera white balance.
465	
466	### Parameters
467	
468	| Parameter | Default | Description |
469	|-----------|---------|-------------|
470	| `THRESHOLD` | 50 | Detection threshold (brightness for hold, color signal for edge) |
471	| `RELEASE_FRAC` | 60 | Release threshold as % of press threshold (hysteresis) |
472	| `PATCH_RADIUS` | 2 | Pixel averaging radius around sample point |
473	| `{COLOR}_X/Y` | varies | Hold sensor pixel coordinates per button |
474	| `{COLOR}_EX/EY` | varies | Edge sensor pixel coordinates per button |
475	
476	Camera selection lives in the always-on video subsystem, not the detector; there is no `DEVICE_ID` parameter here. Sensor markers are drawn through the `overlays()` hook, replacing the previous `SHOW_PREVIEW`/`/video` path.
477	
478	### Calibration
479	
480	Use `video_calibrate.py` to interactively mark sensor positions:
481	
482	```bash
483	# Full calibration (10 points: 5 hold + 5 edge)
484	python video_calibrate.py --device 0
485	
486	# Color sampling mode (inspect BGR values without calibrating)
487	python video_calibrate.py --sample
488	```
489	
490	## Future Work
491	
492	- **Detector-owned data sources**: lift the ADC stream out of the top-level CLI into the detector itself, so each detector declares what inputs it needs (ADC serial / CSV / camera frames / nothing). The runtime UI would then expose a per-detector source picker. (Chart schemas already follow this model: each detector returns a `chart_schema()` and the browser rebuilds the 5 chart slots from it.) The current scope keeps `--port` / `--csv` as a top-level concern.
493	- Multi-detector overlay (compare two algorithms side-by-side on the same chart)
494	- Per-channel enable/disable toggles for actuation
495	- Latency measurement display (round-trip time from ADC sample to GPIO assertion)
496	- Multi-camera reference (more than one source recorded and replayable in sync)
497

```text
1	"""Post-training int8 quantisation of StrumNet for the fretboard MCU.
2	
3	Produces an integer-only inference path (no FPU) that is bit-exact between this
4	host reference (`int8_sim_*`) and the on-device C in `firmware/fretboard/
5	model_infer.c`. The same arrays are emitted as `model_weights.h`.
6	
7	Scheme (per-tensor symmetric int8 weights, int32 accumulators, int64
8	fixed-point requant):
9	
10	  input affine   q_in_c = clamp_i8( (adc_c*M_in[c] - B_in[c] + 2^(S_in-1)) >> S_in )
11	                 folds per-channel standardisation (adc-mean)/std AND the input
12	                 quant scale into integer (M_in, B_in) + a shared shift S_in.
13	  conv layer l   acc_i32 = qbias[l][o] + Σ_i Σ_k qW[l][o,i,k] * q_in[i, p+k*d]
14	                 (causal, left zero-pad (K-1)*d — replicates the 60-sample
15	                 training window with zeros beyond it)
16	                 relu:    acc = max(acc, 0)
17	                 requant: q = clamp_i8_pos( (acc*MULT[l] + 2^(S[l]-1)) >> S[l] )
18	  head           acc_i32[o] = qbias_h[o] + Σ_i qW_h[o,i] * act_last[i]
19	                 bit o = (acc_i32[o] >= TQ[o])      (no sigmoid: sigmoid(x)>=t
20	                 ⇔ x>=logit(t) ⇔ acc>=TQ; frets TQ=0, strum TQ=logit(thresh)/scale)
21	
22	All right shifts are arithmetic (round-half-up via the +2^(S-1) bias before the
23	shift). The requant multiply uses int64 to avoid overflow.
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import math
29	from dataclasses import dataclass
30	
31	from . import FRET_COUNT, N_LABELS
32	from .data import Capture, causal_window_indices, contiguous_runs
33	
34	# Fixed shifts. Chosen generously: int8 quant error dominates, the fixed-point
35	# rounding is far below it. The requant multiply is int64 so MULT magnitude is
36	# unconstrained; S_IN is bounded so adc*M_in stays well inside int32.
37	S_IN = 15
38	S_REQUANT = 15
39	_QMAX = 127  # symmetric int8 range [-127, 127]
40	
41	
42	@dataclass
43	class QuantParams:
44	    # architecture
45	    channels: int
46	    kernel: int
47	    dilations: tuple[int, ...]
48	    window: int
49	    # input affine (per channel), shared shift S_IN
50	    m_in: list[int]      # int32
51	    b_in: list[int]      # int32
52	    s_in_shift: int
53	    # conv layers: weights int8 [Cout][Cin][K], bias int32 [Cout], requant
54	    conv_w: list[list[list[list[int]]]]
55	    conv_b: list[list[int]]
56	    conv_mult: list[int]   # int32 per layer
57	    conv_shift: list[int]  # per layer
58	    # head: weights int8 [N_LABELS][channels], bias int32, integer thresholds
59	    head_w: list[list[int]]
60	    head_b: list[int]
61	    head_tq: list[int]     # int32 per output
62	    # strum monostable post-processor (deploy-time)
63	    strum_hold: int
64	    strum_refractory: int
65	    # bookkeeping (not emitted to C)
66	    strum_thresh: float
67	    scales: dict
68	
69	
70	def _round_half_up_shift(x: int, shift: int) -> int:
71	    """(x + 2^(shift-1)) >> shift with arithmetic (floor) shift — matches C."""
72	    return (x + (1 << (shift - 1))) >> shift
73	
74	
75	def _quantize_weight_tensor(w):
76	    """Per-tensor symmetric int8. Returns (q_int_list, scale)."""
77	    import numpy as np
78	
79	    amax = float(np.max(np.abs(w))) if w.size else 0.0
80	    scale = amax / _QMAX if amax > 0 else 1.0
81	    q = np.clip(np.round(w / scale), -_QMAX, _QMAX).astype(np.int64)
82	    return q, scale
83	
84	
85	def _conv_float(x, w, b, d):
86	    """Causal float conv. x:(N,Cin,L) w:(Cout,Cin,K) b:(Cout,) -> (N,Cout,L)."""
87	    import numpy as np
88	
89	    n, cin, length = x.shape
90	    cout, _, k = w.shape
91	    pad = (k - 1) * d
92	    xp = np.concatenate([np.zeros((n, cin, pad), x.dtype), x], axis=2)
93	    out = np.zeros((n, cout, length), dtype=np.float64)
94	    for j in range(k):
95	        out += np.einsum("oi,nil->nol", w[:, :, j], xp[:, :, j * d : j * d + length])
96	    return out + b[None, :, None]
97	
98	
99	def _raw_windows(cap: Capture, window: int):
100	    """Raw int ADC windows (N,5,window) + the true label rows (N,6), in the same
101	    run/window order build_arrays uses, so int8 metrics line up with float eval."""
102	    import numpy as np
103	
104	    adc = np.asarray(cap.adc, dtype=np.int64)      # (rows, 5)
105	    lab = np.asarray(cap.labels, dtype=np.int64)   # (rows, 6)
106	    xs, ys = [], []
107	    for run_start, run_end in contiguous_runs(cap.fb_seq):
108	        run_len = run_end - run_start
109	        if run_len < window:
110	            continue
111	        for start, end, label_row in causal_window_indices(run_len, window):
112	            xs.append(adc[run_start + start : run_start + end].T)  # (5, window)
113	            ys.append(lab[run_start + label_row])
114	    if not xs:
115	        return np.zeros((0, FRET_COUNT, window), np.int64), np.zeros((0, N_LABELS), np.int64)
116	    return np.stack(xs), np.stack(ys)
117	
118	
119	def quantize(ckpt_path: str, calib_caps: list[Capture], *, strum_thresh: float = 0.5,
120	             strum_hold: int = 0, strum_refractory: int = 4) -> QuantParams:
121	    """Calibrate activation ranges on `calib_caps` and produce int8 params."""
122	    import numpy as np
123	    import torch
124	
125	    ck = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location="cpu")
126	    sd = ck["state_dict"]
127	    channels, kernel = ck["channels"], ck["kernel"]
128	    dilations = tuple(ck.get("dilations", (1, 4)))
129	    window = ck["window"]
130	    mean = np.asarray(ck["norm_mean"], dtype=np.float64)
131	    std = np.asarray(ck["norm_std"], dtype=np.float64)
132	
133	    conv_keys = [k for k in sd if k.startswith("features.") and k.endswith(".conv.weight")]
134	    conv_keys.sort(key=lambda s: int(s.split(".")[1]))
135	    w_convs = [sd[k].numpy().astype(np.float64) for k in conv_keys]
136	    b_convs = [sd[k.replace("weight", "bias")].numpy().astype(np.float64) for k in conv_keys]
137	    w_head = sd["head.weight"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
138	    b_head = sd["head.bias"].numpy().astype(np.float64)
139	
140	    # --- calibration: float forward over all calib windows, record activation maxes
141	    Xall = []
142	    for cap in calib_caps:
143	        xw, _ = _raw_windows(cap, window)
144	        if xw.shape[0]:
145	            Xall.append(xw)
146	    if not Xall:
147	        raise ValueError("no calibration windows produced")
148	    raw = np.concatenate(Xall, axis=0).astype(np.float64)          # (N,5,window)
149	    xstd = (raw - mean[None, :, None]) / std[None, :, None]        # standardised
150	    in_amax = float(np.max(np.abs(xstd)))
151	    s_in = in_amax / _QMAX
152	
153	    act = xstd
154	    act_scales = []
155	    for w, b, d in zip(w_convs, b_convs, dilations):
156	        act = np.maximum(_conv_float(act, w, b, d), 0.0)           # post-ReLU
157	        amax = float(np.max(act)) if act.size else 1.0
158	        act_scales.append(amax / _QMAX if amax > 0 else 1.0)
159	    s_act_last = act_scales[-1]
160	
161	    # --- input affine: q = round((adc-mean)/(std*s_in)) folded to integer
162	    m_in, b_in = [], []
163	    for c in range(FRET_COUNT):
164	        kc = 1.0 / (std[c] * s_in)
165	        m_in.append(int(round(kc * (1 << S_IN))))
166	        b_in.append(int(round(mean[c] * kc * (1 << S_IN))))
167	
168	    # --- conv weights, biases, requant
169	    conv_w, conv_b, conv_mult, conv_shift, w_scales = [], [], [], [], []
170	    s_in_l = s_in
171	    for li, (w, b, d) in enumerate(zip(w_convs, b_convs, dilations)):
172	        qw, sw = _quantize_weight_tensor(w)
173	        w_scales.append(sw)
174	        acc_scale = sw * s_in_l
175	        qb = [int(round(v / acc_scale)) for v in b]
176	        mreq = acc_scale / act_scales[li]                         # accum -> next int8
177	        conv_mult.append(int(round(mreq * (1 << S_REQUANT))))
178	        conv_shift.append(S_REQUANT)
179	        conv_w.append(qw.tolist())
180	        conv_b.append(qb)
181	        s_in_l = act_scales[li]
182	
183	    # --- head: int thresholds in accumulator units
184	    qhw, shw = _quantize_weight_tensor(w_head)
185	    head_acc_scale = shw * s_act_last
186	    qhb = [int(round(v / head_acc_scale)) for v in b_head]
187	    tq = [0] * N_LABELS                                           # frets: logit>=0
188	    logit_t = math.log(strum_thresh / (1.0 - strum_thresh))       # strum threshold
189	    tq[5] = int(round(logit_t / head_acc_scale))
190	
191	    return QuantParams(
192	        channels=channels, kernel=kernel, dilations=dilations, window=window,
193	        m_in=m_in, b_in=b_in, s_in_shift=S_IN,
194	        conv_w=conv_w, conv_b=conv_b, conv_mult=conv_mult, conv_shift=conv_shift,
195	        head_w=qhw.tolist(), head_b=qhb, head_tq=tq,
196	        strum_hold=strum_hold, strum_refractory=strum_refractory,
197	        strum_thresh=strum_thresh,
198	        scales={"s_in": s_in, "w": w_scales, "act": act_scales, "head_w": shw},
199	    )
200	
201	
202	def _conv_int(xq, qw, qb, d, mult, shift):
203	    """Causal int8 conv + ReLU + requant. xq:(N,Cin,L) int -> (N,Cout,L) int8."""
204	    import numpy as np
205	
206	    n, cin, length = xq.shape
207	    qw = np.asarray(qw, dtype=np.int64)        # (Cout,Cin,K)
208	    cout, _, k = qw.shape
209	    pad = (k - 1) * d
210	    xp = np.concatenate([np.zeros((n, cin, pad), np.int64), xq.astype(np.int64)], axis=2)
211	    acc = np.zeros((n, cout, length), dtype=np.int64)
212	    for j in range(k):
213	        acc += np.einsum("oi,nil->nol", qw[:, :, j], xp[:, :, j * d : j * d + length])
214	    acc += np.asarray(qb, dtype=np.int64)[None, :, None]
215	    acc = np.maximum(acc, 0)
216	    q = (acc * int(mult) + (1 << (shift - 1))) >> shift
217	    return np.minimum(q, _QMAX).astype(np.int64)
218	
219	
220	def int8_sim_windows(qp: QuantParams, raw_windows):
221	    """Run integer inference over raw ADC windows (N,5,window) -> bits (N,6)."""
222	    import numpy as np
223	
224	    if raw_windows.shape[0] == 0:
225	        return np.zeros((0, N_LABELS), np.int64)
226	    raw = raw_windows.astype(np.int64)
227	    m = np.asarray(qp.m_in, np.int64)[None, :, None]
228	    b = np.asarray(qp.b_in, np.int64)[None, :, None]
229	    qin = (raw * m - b + (1 << (qp.s_in_shift - 1))) >> qp.s_in_shift
230	    act = np.clip(qin, -_QMAX, _QMAX)
231	    for w, qb, d, mult, shift in zip(qp.conv_w, qp.conv_b, qp.dilations, qp.conv_mult, qp.conv_shift):
232	        act = _conv_int(act, w, qb, d, mult, shift)
233	    last = act[:, :, -1]                                    # (N, channels)
234	    hw = np.asarray(qp.head_w, np.int64)                    # (6, channels)
235	    hb = np.asarray(qp.head_b, np.int64)
236	    acc = last @ hw.T + hb[None, :]                         # (N, 6) int
237	    tq = np.asarray(qp.head_tq, np.int64)[None, :]
238	    return (acc >= tq).astype(np.int64)
239	
240	
241	def int8_sim_capture(qp: QuantParams, cap: Capture):
242	    """(pred_bits, true_bits) lists for one capture, matching float-eval order."""
243	    raw, true = _raw_windows(cap, qp.window)
244	    bits = int8_sim_windows(qp, raw)
245	    return bits.tolist(), true.tolist()
246	
247	
248	def evaluate_int8(qp: QuantParams, captures: list[Capture], *, tol_samples=5,
249	                  hold=0, refractory=0):
250	    """int8 counterpart of train.evaluate — same EvalReport, so float vs int8
251	    print identically."""
252	    from .metrics import (per_bit_accuracy, per_bit_f1, strum_event_timing,
253	                          strum_pulse_stats, monostable, PulseStats)
254	    from .train import EvalReport, _agg_timing
255	
256	    all_pred, all_true = [], []
257	    raw = {"err": [], "nt": 0, "np": 0, "m": 0, "pulses": 0, "glitch": 0, "short": 0, "dur": []}
258	    post = {k: ([] if isinstance(v, list) else 0) for k, v in raw.items()}
259	    do_post = hold > 0
260	
261	    def _accum(acc, st, ps):
262	        acc["err"].extend(st.errors_ms); acc["nt"] += st.n_true
263	        acc["np"] += st.n_pred; acc["m"] += st.matched
264	        acc["pulses"] += ps.n_pulses; acc["glitch"] += ps.n_glitches
265	        acc["short"] += ps.n_too_short; acc["dur"].extend(ps.durations_ticks)
266	
267	    for cap in captures:
268	        if len(cap) < qp.window:
269	            continue
270	        pred_bits, true_bits = int8_sim_capture(qp, cap)
271	        all_pred.extend(pred_bits); all_true.extend(true_bits)
272	        pred_strum = [r[5] for r in pred_bits]
273	        true_strum = [r[5] for r in true_bits]
274	        _accum(raw, strum_event_timing(pred_strum, true_strum, tol_samples=tol_samples),
275	               strum_pulse_stats(pred_strum))
276	        if do_post:
277	            clean = monostable(pred_strum, hold=hold, refractory=refractory)
278	            _accum(post, strum_event_timing(clean, true_strum, tol_samples=tol_samples),
279	                   strum_pulse_stats(clean))
280	
281	    def _pulse(acc):
282	        return PulseStats(acc["pulses"], acc["glitch"], acc["short"], acc["dur"])
283	
284	    return EvalReport(
285	        per_bit_acc=per_bit_accuracy(all_pred, all_true),
286	        per_bit_f1=per_bit_f1(all_pred, all_true),
287	        strum=_agg_timing(raw["err"], raw["nt"], raw["np"], raw["m"]),
288	        pulse=_pulse(raw),
289	        strum_post=_agg_timing(post["err"], post["nt"], post["np"], post["m"]) if do_post else None,
290	        pulse_post=_pulse(post) if do_post else None,
291	    )
292	
293	
294	def _fmt_arr(vals, per_line=12):
295	    """Comma-joined ints with line wrapping for readable C initialisers."""
296	    out, line = [], []
297	    for v in vals:
298	        line.append(str(int(v)))
299	        if len(line) >= per_line:
300	            out.append(", ".join(line)); line = []
301	    if line:
302	        out.append(", ".join(line))
303	    return ",\n    ".join(out)
304	
305	
306	def _sanitize_name(name: str) -> str:
307	    s = "".join(ch if (ch.isalnum() or ch == "_") else "_" for ch in name).strip("_")
308	    if not s or s[0].isdigit():
309	        s = "m_" + s
310	    return s.lower()
311	
312	
313	def emit_c_header(qp: QuantParams, name: str = "model") -> str:
314	    """Render a model_weights.h defining one named `model_def_t model_<name>`.
315	
316	    Per-model arrays are prefixed so several models (e.g. one per difficulty)
317	    can be linked together and chosen at runtime via model_infer_set_model().
318	    The architecture dims are shared #defines (first included model defines
319	    them); a _Static_assert makes a mismatched-architecture model fail the build.
320	    `MODEL_DEFAULT` points at the first model included.
321	    """
322	    nm = _sanitize_name(name)
323	    P = f"M_{nm.upper()}_"          # array symbol prefix
324	    K = qp.kernel
325	    C = qp.channels
326	    n_layers = len(qp.dilations)
327	
328	    L = [f"#ifndef MODEL_WEIGHTS_{nm.upper()}_H",
329	         f"#define MODEL_WEIGHTS_{nm.upper()}_H", "",
330	         "/* Generated by edge_ai.quantize — do not edit by hand. */",
331	         "#include <stdint.h>", '#include "model_infer.h"', "",
332	         "/* Shared architecture dims — first model included sets them; all "
333	         "linked models must match. */",
334	         "#ifndef MODEL_ARCH_DIMS",
335	         "#define MODEL_ARCH_DIMS",
336	         f"#define MODEL_CHANNELS {C}",
337	         f"#define MODEL_KERNEL   {K}",
338	         f"#define MODEL_WINDOW   {qp.window}",
339	         f"#define MODEL_N_IN     {FRET_COUNT}",
340	         f"#define MODEL_N_OUT    {N_LABELS}",
341	         f"#define MODEL_N_LAYERS {n_layers}",
342	         "#endif",
343	         f"_Static_assert(MODEL_CHANNELS == {C} && MODEL_KERNEL == {K} && "
344	         f"MODEL_WINDOW == {qp.window} && MODEL_N_IN == {FRET_COUNT} && "
345	         f"MODEL_N_OUT == {N_LABELS} && MODEL_N_LAYERS == {n_layers},",
346	         f'               "model {nm}: architecture must match the other linked models");', ""]
347	
348	    L += [f"static const int32_t {P}M_IN[{FRET_COUNT}] = {{ {_fmt_arr(qp.m_in)} }};",
349	          f"static const int32_t {P}B_IN[{FRET_COUNT}] = {{ {_fmt_arr(qp.b_in)} }};",
350	          f"static const uint8_t {P}DILATION[{n_layers}] = "
351	          f"{{ {', '.join(str(d) for d in qp.dilations)} }};",
352	          f"static const int32_t {P}REQ_MULT[{n_layers}] = "
353	          f"{{ {', '.join(str(m) for m in qp.conv_mult)} }};",
354	          f"static const uint8_t {P}REQ_SHIFT[{n_layers}] = "
355	          f"{{ {', '.join(str(s) for s in qp.conv_shift)} }};", ""]
356	    for li, (w, b) in enumerate(zip(qp.conv_w, qp.conv_b)):
357	        cout = len(w); cin = len(w[0])
358	        flat = [w[o][i][k] for o in range(cout) for i in range(cin) for k in range(K)]
359	        L += [f"/* layer {li}: Conv1d({cin}->{cout}, k={K}, d={qp.dilations[li]}) */",
360	              f"static const int8_t {P}W{li}[{cout * cin * K}] = {{\n    {_fmt_arr(flat)}\n}};",
361	              f"static const int32_t {P}B{li}[{cout}] = {{ {_fmt_arr(b)} }};", ""]
362	    L += [f"static const int8_t *const {P}W[{n_layers}] = "
363	          f"{{ {', '.join('%sW%d' % (P, i) for i in range(n_layers))} }};",
364	          f"static const int32_t *const {P}B[{n_layers}] = "
365	          f"{{ {', '.join('%sB%d' % (P, i) for i in range(n_layers))} }};",
366	          f"static const uint8_t {P}CIN[{n_layers}] = "
367	          f"{{ {', '.join(str(len(w[0])) for w in qp.conv_w)} }};", ""]
368	    hw_flat = [qp.head_w[o][i] for o in range(N_LABELS) for i in range(C)]
369	    L += [f"static const int8_t {P}HEAD_W[{N_LABELS * C}] = {{\n    {_fmt_arr(hw_flat)}\n}};",
370	          f"static const int32_t {P}HEAD_B[{N_LABELS}] = {{ {_fmt_arr(qp.head_b)} }};",
371	          f"static const int32_t {P}HEAD_TQ[{N_LABELS}] = {{ {_fmt_arr(qp.head_tq)} }};", ""]
372	
373	    L += [f"static const model_def_t model_{nm} = {{",
374	          f"    .m_in = {P}M_IN, .b_in = {P}B_IN, .s_in_shift = {qp.s_in_shift},",
375	          f"    .w = {P}W, .b = {P}B, .cin = {P}CIN, .dilation = {P}DILATION,",
376	          f"    .req_mult = {P}REQ_MULT, .req_shift = {P}REQ_SHIFT,",
377	          f"    .head_w = {P}HEAD_W, .head_b = {P}HEAD_B, .head_tq = {P}HEAD_TQ,",
378	          f"    .strum_hold = {qp.strum_hold}, .strum_refractory = {qp.strum_refractory},",
379	          "};", "",
380	          "#ifndef MODEL_DEFAULT",
381	          f"#define MODEL_DEFAULT (&model_{nm})",
382	          "#endif", "",
383	          f"#endif /* MODEL_WEIGHTS_{nm.upper()}_H */", ""]
384	    return "\n".join(L)
385

1	"""Evaluation metrics (stdlib only).
2	
3	Two families:
4	- Per-bit accuracy / F1 over the 6 output bits (5 frets + strum).
5	- Strum-event timing: match predicted strum rising edges to true ones within a
6	  tolerance and report the timing-error distribution + precision/recall. This
7	  is the Phase-2 gate metric (p95 ≤ 20 ms ≈ 5 samples).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	
14	from . import N_LABELS, SAMPLE_RATE_HZ
15	
16	LABEL_NAMES = ["green", "red", "yellow", "blue", "orange", "strum"]
17	
18	
19	def per_bit_accuracy(pred: list[list[int]], true: list[list[int]]) -> list[float]:
20	    n = len(true)
21	    if n == 0:
22	        return [0.0] * N_LABELS
23	    acc = []
24	    for b in range(N_LABELS):
25	        correct = sum(1 for i in range(n) if pred[i][b] == true[i][b])
26	        acc.append(correct / n)
27	    return acc
28	
29	
30	def per_bit_f1(pred: list[list[int]], true: list[list[int]]) -> list[float]:
31	    out = []
32	    for b in range(N_LABELS):
33	        tp = sum(1 for i in range(len(true)) if pred[i][b] == 1 and true[i][b] == 1)
34	        fp = sum(1 for i in range(len(true)) if pred[i][b] == 1 and true[i][b] == 0)
35	        fn = sum(1 for i in range(len(true)) if pred[i][b] == 0 and true[i][b] == 1)
36	        denom = 2 * tp + fp + fn
37	        out.append((2 * tp / denom) if denom else 1.0)
38	    return out
39	
40	
41	def _rising_edges(seq: list[int]) -> list[int]:
42	    edges = []
43	    prev = 0
44	    for i, s in enumerate(seq):
45	        if s and not prev:
46	            edges.append(i)
47	        prev = s
48	    return edges
49	
50	
51	@dataclass(frozen=True)
52	class StrumTiming:
53	    n_true: int
54	    n_pred: int
55	    matched: int
56	    precision: float
57	    recall: float
58	    errors_ms: list[float]  # signed: pred - true, for matched events
59	
60	    def percentile_abs_ms(self, p: float) -> float:
61	        if not self.errors_ms:
62	            return float("nan")
63	        vals = sorted(abs(e) for e in self.errors_ms)
64	        k = max(0, min(len(vals) - 1, int(round(p / 100.0 * (len(vals) - 1)))))
65	        return vals[k]
66	
67	    def summary(self) -> str:
68	        return (
69	            f"strum events: true={self.n_true} pred={self.n_pred} "
70	            f"matched={self.matched} | precision={self.precision:.3f} "
71	            f"recall={self.recall:.3f} | |err| p50={self.percentile_abs_ms(50):.1f}ms "
72	            f"p95={self.percentile_abs_ms(95):.1f}ms"
73	        )
74	
75	
76	def strum_event_timing(
77	    pred_strum: list[int],
78	    true_strum: list[int],
79	    *,
80	    tol_samples: int = 5,
81	) -> StrumTiming:
82	    """Greedy nearest-match of predicted strum edges to true edges.
83	
84	    Each true edge matches the nearest unused predicted edge within
85	    `tol_samples`. Default tol 5 ≈ 20.8 ms (one ADC sample over the Phase-2
86	    p95 gate). Timing error is signed (pred - true) in ms.
87	    """
88	    true_e = _rising_edges(true_strum)
89	    pred_e = _rising_edges(pred_strum)
90	    used = [False] * len(pred_e)
91	    errors_ms = []
92	    matched = 0
93	    for t in true_e:
94	        best_k = -1
95	        best_d = tol_samples + 1
96	        for k, p in enumerate(pred_e):
97	            if used[k]:
98	                continue
99	            d = abs(p - t)
100	            if d <= tol_samples and d < best_d:
101	                best_d = d
102	                best_k = k
103	        if best_k >= 0:
104	            used[best_k] = True
105	            matched += 1
106	            errors_ms.append((pred_e[best_k] - t) / SAMPLE_RATE_HZ * 1000.0)
107	    precision = matched / len(pred_e) if pred_e else 0.0
108	    recall = matched / len(true_e) if true_e else 0.0
109	    return StrumTiming(
110	        n_true=len(true_e),
111	        n_pred=len(pred_e),
112	        matched=matched,
113	        precision=precision,
114	        recall=recall,
115	        errors_ms=errors_ms,
116	    )
117	
118	
119	def _runs_of_ones(seq: list[int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
120	    """Maximal [start, end) runs where seq == 1."""
121	    runs = []
122	    i, n = 0, len(seq)
123	    while i < n:
124	        if seq[i]:
125	            j = i
126	            while j < n and seq[j]:
127	                j += 1
128	            runs.append((i, j))
129	            i = j
130	        else:
131	            i += 1
132	    return runs
133	
134	
135	@dataclass(frozen=True)
136	class PulseStats:
137	    """Shape of a predicted strum stream — what matters for in-game registration.
138	
139	    The rising edge is what the game catches; duration matters only insofar as
140	    the pulse is long enough to register and free of mid-pulse dropouts. So we
141	    report pulse count, how many are too short to register, and how many brief
142	    0-gaps sit between pulses (glitches that would register as a double-strum).
143	    """
144	
145	    n_pulses: int
146	    n_glitches: int
147	    n_too_short: int
148	    durations_ticks: list[int]
149	
150	    def median_ms(self) -> float:
151	        if not self.durations_ticks:
152	            return 0.0
153	        d = sorted(self.durations_ticks)
154	        return d[len(d) // 2] / SAMPLE_RATE_HZ * 1000.0
155	
156	    def summary(self) -> str:
157	        return (
158	            f"pulses={self.n_pulses} median={self.median_ms():.1f}ms "
159	            f"glitches={self.n_glitches} too_short={self.n_too_short}"
160	        )
161	
162	
163	def strum_pulse_stats(
164	    seq: list[int],
165	    *,
166	    min_ticks: int = 6,
167	    glitch_max_ticks: int = 2,
168	) -> PulseStats:
169	    """Describe the pulse shape of a binary strum stream.
170	
171	    `min_ticks`: a pulse shorter than this may not register in-game (marvin
172	    asserts ~6 ticks / 25 ms). `glitch_max_ticks`: a 0-gap this short between
173	    two pulses is treated as a mid-strum dropout (one strum split in two).
174	    """
175	    runs = _runs_of_ones(seq)
176	    durations = [e - s for s, e in runs]
177	    n_too_short = sum(1 for d in durations if d < min_ticks)
178	    n_glitches = sum(
179	        1 for k in range(1, len(runs))
180	        if (runs[k][0] - runs[k - 1][1]) <= glitch_max_ticks
181	    )
182	    return PulseStats(
183	        n_pulses=len(runs),
184	        n_glitches=n_glitches,
185	        n_too_short=n_too_short,
186	        durations_ticks=durations,
187	    )
188	
189	
190	def monostable(seq: list[int], *, hold: int, refractory: int) -> list[int]:
191	    """Deploy-time strum post-processor: rising-edge-triggered one-shot.
192	
193	    Triggers only on a 0→1 transition (one strum = one rising edge; you can't
194	    strum twice without releasing). On a trigger, force the output high for
195	    `hold` ticks, then block new triggers for `refractory` more ticks. So a
196	    single sustained input assertion yields exactly one pulse (no retriggering
197	    inside it), mid-pulse glitches are absorbed, and two real strums must be
198	    ≥ hold+refractory apart. Cheap enough for the MCU runtime (a small counter).
199	    """
200	    out = [0] * len(seq)
201	    hold_until = 0     # output forced high while i < hold_until
202	    block_until = 0    # no new trigger while i < block_until
203	    prev = 0
204	    for i, v in enumerate(seq):
205	        if v == 1 and prev == 0 and i >= block_until:
206	            hold_until = i + hold
207	            block_until = i + hold + refractory
208	        if i < hold_until:
209	            out[i] = 1
210	        prev = v
211	    return out
212

```text
1	# marvin-perf
2	
3	Host-side decoder and analyzer for the marvin firmware **perf-log** wire format.
4	
5	The firmware emits framed binary records (schema version 1) over its USB-device
6	CDC ACM port. This tool consumes that stream live, records it to disk, replays
7	captures offline, and produces summary analyses (latency attribution, drop
8	accounting, stack high-water trends).
9	
10	Wire format source-of-truth lives in the firmware tree at
11	[`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`](../../firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h).
12	The Python schema mirror in [`marvin_perf/records.py`](marvin_perf/records.py)
13	must match it byte-for-byte; bump `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` on both sides
14	together.
15	
16	## Setup
17	
18	All Python work runs through [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). First-time
19	bootstrap:
20	
21	    cd tools/marvin-perf
22	    uv sync --group viewer   # include viewer deps for the serve command
23	
24	`uv sync` creates `.venv/` and writes `uv.lock`. Subsequent invocations use the
25	existing venv automatically. Omit `--group viewer` if you only need the CLI
26	decode/record commands.
27	
28	## Usage
29	
30	    # Launch the visual review server (default when no subcommand is given)
31	    uv run marvin-perf
32	    uv run marvin-perf serve
33	    uv run marvin-perf serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765
34	    uv run marvin-perf serve --capture session.bin   # pre-load a capture on startup
35	
36	    # Capture raw bytes from the marvin USB-device CDC port (no decode)
37	    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out session.bin
38	
39	    # Push a type-mask to a running device without attaching for capture
40	    uv run marvin-perf set-mask --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --types ALL
41	
42	## Tests
43	
44	    uv run pytest
45	
46	Fixtures under [`tests/fixtures/`](tests/fixtures/) are hand-built byte streams
47	covering one frame per record type plus framing edge cases (FCS mismatch,
48	truncated payload, mid-stream join needing SOF resync).
49
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# GH3 Cover Art Tools
2	
3	Tools for fetching and processing Guitar Hero III cover art for the marvin game UI.
4	
5	## Structure
6	
7	- `fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` — Fetch cover art from MusicBrainz Cover Art Archive
8	- `process_gh3_cover_art.py` — Resize + install covers straight into the marvin art tree
9	- `data/` — Original JPG files (fetched by `fetch_gh3_cover_art.py`, tracked in git as the
10	  stable re-process inputs; the fuzzy MusicBrainz fetch isn't reproducible)
11	
12	## Setup
13	
14	```bash
15	cd tools/gh3-cover-art
16	uv sync
17	```
18	
19	## Usage
20	
21	### Fetch Original Cover Art
22	
23	Requires MusicBrainz API contact info (your email or project URL).
24	
25	```bash
26	uv run fetch_gh3_cover_art.py --contact your@email.com
27	```
28	
29	Optional: Generate the song catalog CSV alongside with year/genre metadata:
30	
31	```bash
32	uv run fetch_gh3_cover_art.py --contact your@email.com \
33	    --catalog ../../firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv
34	```
35	
36	### Process + install covers (one step)
37	
38	After fetching, generate both tiers straight into the marvin art tree:
39	
40	```bash
41	uv run process_gh3_cover_art.py
42	```
43	
44	This writes (clearing any stale cover files first), keyed by the recognizer's
45	`<setlist>-<NN>` and pulling each song's difficulty from `songs.csv`:
46	- `../../firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/art/large/<setlist>-<NN>.png` (508×208)
47	- `../../firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/art/small/<setlist>-<NN>.jpg` (144×144)
48	
49	Point `--out` elsewhere to stage into a different tree.
50	
51	## Asset Format
52	
53	- **large (`art/large/<setlist>-<NN>.png`)** — 508×208 song-select detail strip: the
54	  cover scaled to 508 wide, center-cropped to the middle 208 px band, with a top/bottom
55	  **difficulty-colored fade** baked in (main tiers `"1".."8"` → green→red, `"bonus"`/unknown
56	  → gray, read from `songs.csv`). PNG so the gradient stays lossless. Fade depth/brightness
57	  are the `FADE_PX` / `FADE_VALUE` tunables at the top of the script.
58	- **small (`art/small/<setlist>-<NN>.jpg`)** — 144×144 now-playing thumbnail: scaled to fit
59	  with black pillarbox/letterbox, no fade. JPEG quality 92.
60	
61	Both are offline-processed once; marvin decodes them into static RGB888 caches at boot
62	(`firmware/marvin/default/src/game/art.c`) and loads with no runtime scaling.
63
```

1	# marvin SD-card data (seed)
2	
3	Files here mirror the FAT32 layout marvin expects on the SD card. Copy the tree
4	to the card root. Paths are relative to the mount point (spec §4.6.2, §4.8).
5	
6	```
7	games/gh3-wii/
8	  songs.csv          song catalog — labels keyed by (setlist, index); spec §4.8.3
9	  art/               album art, keyed by the same (setlist, index); spec §4.8.7
10	    small/  <setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}     e.g. main-04.jpg   (one DDR cache tier)
11	    large/  <setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}     e.g. bonus-12.png  (one DDR cache tier)
12	players/
13	  results.csv        per-player high scores (written by marvin); spec §4.8.6
14	```
15	
16	`songs.csv` columns: `setlist,index,title,artist,album,bpm,length_s,year,genre,difficulty`.
17	`setlist` is `main`/`bonus`; `title`/`artist`/`album`/`genre`/`difficulty` are
18	CSV-quoted (and may be empty); `bpm`/`length_s`/`year` are integers, `0` when
19	unknown. Rows may be sparse or out of order — only `(setlist, index)` is the key.
20	
21	`title`/`artist`/`album` are sourced from the `SONGS` table in
22	[`tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py`](../../../../tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py); that
23	script's `--catalog` mode also fills `year` and `genre` from MusicBrainz. `bpm`,
24	`length_s`, and `difficulty` are reserved-but-blank for now (GH3 exposes no
25	per-song difficulty rating).
26	
27	The catalog is **labels only**: recognition is compile-time in flash, so a
28	missing or partial `songs.csv` just shows "Unknown song" and never affects play.
29	Album art is derived directly from `(setlist, index)` and is **not** referenced
30	from `songs.csv` — the two are independent.
31	
32	> **The checked-in `songs.csv` is a placeholder seed** generated from the
33	> recognizer's song slugs (titles auto-humanized; `artist`/`bpm`/`length_s`
34	> blank). Replace the values with real metadata before relying on the display.
35	
36	## Boot splash (`ui/splash.raw`)
37	
38	The boot splash is **not** read from the SD card — it lives in QSPI NOR and is
39	provisioned over JTAG. `ui/splash.jpg` is the editable source; `ui/splash.raw` is
40	the pre-decoded framebuffer the firmware actually loads.
41	
42	Regenerate the raw from the source with [`ui/make-splash.sh`](ui/make-splash.sh):
43	
44	```
45	ui/make-splash.sh [input] [output]   # defaults: ui/splash.jpg -> ui/splash.raw
46	```
47	
48	It produces headerless raw RGBA8888, 1280×800, in the XLCDC layer's native byte
49	order (pixel word `0xRRGGBBAA`, memory bytes `[A,B,G,R]`) — exactly 4,096,000
50	bytes, the only size `splash.c` accepts. Uses `uv` + Pillow (no ImageMagick/ffmpeg).
51	
52	Then flash it: `../../openocd/program-qspi.sh splash` (writes `ui/splash.raw` to
53	QSPI `0x000000`).
54
```
