171	    memcpy(&s_hb_frame[6], s_mac, 6u);         /* src = this node   */
172	    s_hb_frame[12] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB >> 8);
173	    s_hb_frame[13] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB & 0xFFu);
174	    s_hb_frame[14] = T1S_HB_VERSION;
175	    s_hb_frame[15] = T1S_HB_TYPE_GUITAR;
176	    s_hb_frame[16] = (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID;
177	    s_hb_frame[17] = synced ? 0x01u : 0x00u;   /* flags: bit0 = synced */
178	    s_hb_seq++;
179	    s_hb_frame[18] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq);
180	    s_hb_frame[19] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 8);
181	    s_hb_frame[20] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 16);
182	    s_hb_frame[21] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 24);
183	
184	    s_hb_busy = true;
185	    if (!TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_hb_frame, T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + T1S_HB_LEN,
186	                                   0u, hb_tx_done, NULL)) {
187	        s_hb_busy = false;
188	    }
189	}
190	
191	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  Public API  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
192	
193	void T1SFollower_Initialize(void)
194	{
195	    SYSTICK_TimerStart();    /* MCC inits the timer; the app enables it */
196	
197	    log_str("guitar: boot - t1s follower + cli\r\n");  /* one-time banner */
198	
199	    buttons_release_all();   /* pins boot Out/Low (asserted) — release first */
200	
201	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST active-low, idle high). */
202	    T1S_CS_Set();
203	    T1S_RST_Clear();
204	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
205	    T1S_RST_Set();
206	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
207	
208	    SERCOM0_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);  /* Mode 0 set by MCC init */
209	
210	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
211	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
212	        log_str("guitar: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
213	        return;
214	    }
215	
216	    EIC_CallbackRegister(EIC_PIN_13, irq_cb, 0u);   /* EXTINT13 enabled in EIC_Initialize */
217	
218	    /* Configure the LAN8651 + PLCA as follower id 2. Not promiscuous — the
219	     * MAC-PHY filters to this node's MAC + broadcast. Non-blocking: the
220	     * register sequence finishes in the background via T1SFollower_Tasks, so
221	     * the CLI is never gated behind the link coming up. */
222	    if (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, true, T1S_NODE_ID, T1S_NODE_COUNT,
223	                      0u, 0u, false, false, false)) {
224	        log_str("guitar: TC6Regs_Init rejected\r\n");
225	    }
226	}
227	
228	void T1SFollower_Tasks(void)
229	{
230	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
231	        return;
232	    }
233	    service_pump();
234	    if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
235	        s_link_up = true;
236	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
237	        char buf[80];
238	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
239	                       "guitar: LAN8651 up - chipRev=%u, MAC=02:00:00:00:00:%02X, "
240	                       "PLCA follower id=%u/%u\r\n",
241	                       (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
242	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID,
243	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
244	        log_str(buf);
245	    }
246	
247	    /* Periodic presence heartbeat to the coordinator. */
248	    if (s_link_up) {
249	        uint32_t now = SYSTICK_GetTickCounter();
250	        if ((now - s_hb_last_ms) >= T1S_HB_INTERVAL_MS) {
251	            s_hb_last_ms = now;
252	            send_heartbeat();
253	        }
254	    }
255	}

292	/* Diagnostic: log the raw value of a control register (async — the result
293	 * prints from the service loop a moment later). */
294	static void on_id_read(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint32_t addr, uint32_t value,
295	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
296	{
297	    (void)pInst;
298	    (void)pTag;
299	    (void)pGlobalTag;
300	    char buf[88];
301	    if (addr == 0x00000001u) {
302	        /* PHY id register — oui/model are meaningful here (lib wants 0x1F0/0x1B). */
303	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
304	                       "guitar: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d, oui=0x%03lX model=0x%02lX)\r\n",
305	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success,
306	                       (unsigned long)(value >> 10), (unsigned long)((value >> 4) & 0x3FFu));
307	    } else {
308	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "guitar: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d)\r\n",
309	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success);
310	    }
311	    log_str(buf);
312	}
313	
314	void T1SFollower_ReadId(void)
315	{
316	    /* 0x00 = OA IDVER, 0x01 = PHY id (lib expects oui 0x1F0 / model 0x1B),
317	     * 0x000A0094 = chip rev. */
318	    static const uint32_t addrs[3] = { 0x00000000u, 0x00000001u, 0x000A0094u };
319	
320	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
321	        log_str("guitar: t1s not initialized\r\n");
322	        return;
323	    }
324	    /* Just enqueue; the main service loop completes the reads and on_id_read
325	     * logs each result a moment later. Don't hammer TC6_Service here — doing so
326	     * while the link is live can trip a transient Loss_of_Framing. */
327	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 3u; i++) {
328	        (void)TC6_ReadRegister(s_tc6, addrs[i], false, on_id_read, NULL);
329	    }
330	}

376	bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
377	                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
378	{
379	    (void)tc6instance;
380	    (void)pGlobalTag;
381	    if (s_spi_busy) {
382	        return false;
383	    }
384	    s_spi_busy = true;
385	    T1S_CS_Clear();          /* CS low — start of transaction (held across the chunk) */
386	    if (!SERCOM0_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len)) {
387	        T1S_CS_Set();
388	        s_spi_busy = false;
389	        return false;
390	    }
391	    return true;
392	}

394	void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
395	{

397	    (void)pGlobalTag;
398	    s_need_service = true;
399	}

401	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset,
402	                              uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
403	{
404	    (void)pInst;
405	    (void)pGlobalTag;
406	    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
407	        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
408	    }
409	}
410	
411	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
412	                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
413	{
414	    (void)pInst;
415	    (void)rxTimestamp;
416	    (void)pGlobalTag;
417	
418	    if (!success || (len < (T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + 1u))) {
419	        return;
420	    }
421	    uint16_t ethertype = (uint16_t)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]);
422	    if (ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE) {
423	        return;
424	    }
425	    /* Command byte is the first payload octet; trailing min-frame padding is
426	     * ignored. Apply directly (latest-wins). */
427	    uint8_t mask = (uint8_t)(s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN] & T1S_CMD_BIT_MASK);
428	    s_last_cmd = mask;
429	    s_rx_count++;
430	    buttons_apply_mask(mask);
431	}
432	
433	void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
434	{
435	    (void)pGlobalTag;
436	    s_err_count++;
437	    diag_log("guitar: t1s error: ", TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
438	    switch (err) {
439	        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
440	        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
441	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
442	        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
443	        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
444	        case TC6Error_SpiError:
445	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
446	            break;
447	        default:
448	            break;
449	    }
450	}

463	    switch (event) {
464	        case TC6Regs_Event_Loss_of_Framing_Error:
465	        case TC6Regs_Event_RX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
466	        case TC6Regs_Event_TX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
467	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
468	            break;
469	        default:
470	            break;

472	}

167	static void flush_data_frame(void)

169	    if (!s_frame_ready || s_tx_busy) {
170	        return;
171	    }
172	    /* Snapshot the ISR-staged payload (the scan tick may overwrite s_pending). */
173	    __disable_irq();
174	    uint16_t len = s_pending_len;
175	    if (len > (uint16_t)(sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
176	        len = (uint16_t)(sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN);
177	    }
178	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN], (const void *)s_pending, len);
179	    s_frame_ready = false;
180	    __enable_irq();
181	
182	    s_tx_busy = true;
183	    if (TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_tx_frame, (uint16_t)(T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + len),
184	                                  0u, tx_done, NULL)) {
185	        s_tx_count++;
186	    } else {

205	        s_cmd_count++;
206	    } else {
207	        s_cmd_busy = false;   /* retry next pass */
208	    }
209	}
210	
211	/* Announce presence to the coordinator (ethertype 0x88B6). */
212	static void send_heartbeat(void)
213	{
214	    if (s_hb_busy || !s_link_up) {
215	        return;
216	    }
217	    bool synced = false;
218	    TC6_GetState(s_tc6, NULL, NULL, &synced);
219	
220	    s_hb_frame[14] = T1S_HB_VERSION;
221	    s_hb_frame[15] = T1S_HB_TYPE_DETECTOR;
222	    s_hb_frame[16] = (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID;
223	    s_hb_frame[17] = synced ? 0x01u : 0x00u;   /* flags: bit0 = synced */
224	    s_hb_seq++;
225	    s_hb_frame[18] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq);
226	    s_hb_frame[19] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 8);
227	    s_hb_frame[20] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 16);
228	    s_hb_frame[21] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 24);
229	
230	    s_hb_busy = true;
231	    if (!TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_hb_frame, T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + T1S_HB_LEN,
232	                                   0u, hb_tx_done, NULL)) {
233	        s_hb_busy = false;
234	    }
235	}

238	
239	void T1SDetector_Initialize(void)
240	{
241	    SYSTICK_TimerStart();    /* MCC inits the timer; the app enables it */
242	
243	    log_str("fretboard: boot - t1s detector + actuator\r\n");  /* one-time banner */
244	
245	    /* Prebuild the constant Ethernet headers (payload filled per send). */
246	    fill_eth_header(s_tx_frame,  s_coord_mac,  T1S_ETHERTYPE);
247	    fill_eth_header(s_cmd_frame, s_guitar_mac, T1S_ETHERTYPE);
248	    fill_eth_header(s_hb_frame,  s_coord_mac,  T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB);
249	
250	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST active-low, idle high). */
251	    T1S_CS_Set();
252	    T1S_RST_Clear();
253	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
254	    T1S_RST_Set();
255	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
256	
257	    SERCOM0_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);  /* Mode 0 set by MCC init */
258	
259	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
260	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
261	        log_str("fretboard: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
262	        return;
263	    }
264	
265	    EIC_CallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_EIC_PIN, irq_cb, 0u);  /* enabled in EIC_Initialize */
266	
267	    /* Configure the LAN8651 + PLCA as follower id 1. Not promiscuous — the
268	     * MAC-PHY filters to this node's MAC + broadcast. Non-blocking: the
269	     * register sequence finishes in the background via T1SDetector_Tasks. */
270	    if (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, true, T1S_NODE_ID, T1S_NODE_COUNT,
271	                      0u, 0u, false, false, false)) {
272	        log_str("fretboard: TC6Regs_Init rejected\r\n");
273	    }
274	}
275	
276	void T1SDetector_Tasks(void)
277	{
278	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
279	        return;
280	    }
281	    service_pump();
282	    if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
283	        s_link_up = true;
284	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
285	        char buf[80];
286	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
287	                       "fretboard: LAN8651 up - chipRev=%u, MAC=02:00:00:00:00:%02X, "
288	                       "PLCA follower id=%u/%u\r\n",
289	                       (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
290	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID,
291	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
292	        log_str(buf);
293	    }
294	
295	    if (s_link_up) {
296	        flush_data_frame();
297	
298	        /* Periodic command refresh so a dropped command frame self-heals. */
299	        uint32_t now = SYSTICK_GetTickCounter();
300	        if ((now - s_cmd_refresh_ms) >= T1S_CMD_REFRESH_MS) {
301	            s_cmd_refresh_ms = now;
302	            s_cmd_dirty = true;
303	        }
304	        flush_command();
305	
306	        if ((now - s_hb_last_ms) >= T1S_HB_INTERVAL_MS) {
307	            s_hb_last_ms = now;
308	            send_heartbeat();
309	        }
310	    }
311	}

318	bool T1SDetector_SendFrame(const uint8_t *payload, uint16_t len)
319	{
320	    if (!s_link_up) {
321	        return false;
322	    }
323	    if (len > sizeof(s_pending)) {
324	        len = sizeof(s_pending);
325	    }
326	    /* Single ISR writer; the main loop snapshots under __disable_irq. Latest-
327	     * wins: overwrite any frame not yet flushed (shows as a sample_seq gap). */
328	    memcpy((void *)s_pending, payload, len);
329	    s_pending_len = len;
330	    s_frame_ready = true;
331	    return true;

364	/* Diagnostic: log the raw value of a control register (async — the result
365	 * prints from the service loop a moment later). */
366	static void on_id_read(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint32_t addr, uint32_t value,
367	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
368	{
369	    (void)pInst; (void)pTag; (void)pGlobalTag;
370	    char buf[88];
371	    if (addr == 0x00000001u) {
372	        /* PHY id register — oui/model are meaningful here (lib wants 0x1F0/0x1B). */
373	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
374	                       "fretboard: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d, oui=0x%03lX model=0x%02lX)\r\n",
375	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success,
376	                       (unsigned long)(value >> 10), (unsigned long)((value >> 4) & 0x3FFu));
377	    } else {
378	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "fretboard: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d)\r\n",
379	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success);
380	    }
381	    log_str(buf);
382	}
383	
384	void T1SDetector_ReadId(void)
385	{
386	    /* 0x00 = OA IDVER, 0x01 = PHY id (lib expects oui 0x1F0 / model 0x1B),
387	     * 0x000A0094 = chip rev. */
388	    static const uint32_t addrs[3] = { 0x00000000u, 0x00000001u, 0x000A0094u };
389	
390	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
391	        log_str("fretboard: t1s not initialized\r\n");
392	        return;
393	    }
394	    /* Enqueue only; the main service loop completes the reads and on_id_read
395	     * logs each result. Don't hammer TC6_Service here — doing so while the link
396	     * is live can trip a transient Loss_of_Framing. */
397	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 3u; i++) {
398	        (void)TC6_ReadRegister(s_tc6, addrs[i], false, on_id_read, NULL);
399	    }
400	}

62	static void send_frame(uint8_t type, const uint8_t *payload, uint8_t len)
63	{
64	    uint8_t f[3u + MF_MAX_PAYLOAD + 1u];
65	    f[0] = MF_SOF;
66	    f[1] = type;
67	    f[2] = len;
68	    if (len != 0u) { memcpy(&f[3], payload, len); }
69	    f[3u + len] = mf_crc8(&f[1], (size_t)(2u + len));   /* CRC over TYPE,LEN,payload */
70	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_Write(f, (size_t)(4u + len));
71	}
72	
73	static void fx_tx_task(void *param)
74	{
75	    (void)param;
76	    LOG_INFO("FX: fauxmote link started (FLEXCOM1, %lu baud)\r\n",
77	             (unsigned long)MF_UART_BAUD);
78	
79	    for (;;)
80	    {
81	        /* Wake on a producer change (low latency) or the floor refresh timeout. */
82	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_tx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FX_REFRESH_MS));
83	
84	        uint8_t g[MF_LEN_GUITAR];
85	        uint8_t nav[MF_LEN_WIIMOTE];
86	        bool    nav_dirty;
87	
88	        taskENTER_CRITICAL();
89	        g[0] = s_g_mask;
90	        g[1] = s_g_whammy;
91	        g[2] = s_g_aux;
92	        nav[0] = s_nav_core;
93	        nav[1] = s_nav_dpad;
94	        nav[2] = s_nav_sx;
95	        nav[3] = s_nav_sy;
96	        nav_dirty = s_nav_dirty;
97	        s_nav_dirty = false;
98	        taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
99	
100	        send_frame(MF_MSG_GUITAR, g, MF_LEN_GUITAR);   /* every wake: change + floor refresh */
101	        if (nav_dirty) { send_frame(MF_MSG_WIIMOTE, nav, MF_LEN_WIIMOTE); }
102	
103	        uint8_t op;
104	        while (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &op, 0) == pdTRUE)
105	        {
106	            send_frame(MF_MSG_LINK_CMD, &op, MF_LEN_LINK_CMD);
107	        }
108	    }
109	}

111	/* ---- RX (STATUS uplink parser) ------------------------------------------ */
112	
113	typedef enum { P_SOF, P_TYPE, P_LEN, P_PAYLOAD, P_CRC } parse_state_t;
114	
115	static void parse_byte(uint8_t b)
116	{
117	    static parse_state_t state = P_SOF;
118	    static uint8_t type, len, idx;
119	    static uint8_t payload[MF_MAX_PAYLOAD];
120	
121	    switch (state)
122	    {
123	        case P_SOF:
124	            if (b == MF_SOF) { state = P_TYPE; }
125	            break;
126	        case P_TYPE:
127	            if (b == 0x00u) { state = P_SOF; break; }
128	            type = b;
129	            state = P_LEN;
130	            break;
131	        case P_LEN:
132	            if (b > MF_MAX_PAYLOAD) { state = P_SOF; break; }
133	            len = b;
134	            idx = 0u;
135	            state = (b == 0u) ? P_CRC : P_PAYLOAD;
136	            break;
137	        case P_PAYLOAD:
138	            payload[idx++] = b;
139	            if (idx >= len) { state = P_CRC; }
140	            break;
141	        case P_CRC:
142	        {
143	            uint8_t hdr[2u + MF_MAX_PAYLOAD];
144	            hdr[0] = type;
145	            hdr[1] = len;
146	            memcpy(&hdr[2], payload, len);
147	            state = P_SOF;
148	            if (mf_crc8(hdr, (size_t)(2u + len)) != b) { break; }   /* bad CRC */
149	
150	            if (type == MF_MSG_STATUS && len == MF_LEN_STATUS)
151	            {
152	                bool changed = !s_status_valid ||
153	                               memcmp(s_status, payload, MF_LEN_STATUS) != 0;
154	                taskENTER_CRITICAL();
155	                memcpy(s_status, payload, MF_LEN_STATUS);
156	                s_status_valid = true;
157	                s_status_tick  = xTaskGetTickCount();
158	                taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
159	                if (changed)
160	                {
161	                    LOG_INFO("FX: status flags=0x%02x slot=%u mode=0x%02x res=%u\r\n",
162	                             payload[0], payload[1], payload[2], payload[3]);
163	                }
164	            }
165	            break;
166	        }
167	        default:
168	            state = P_SOF;
169	            break;
170	    }
171	}

178	    switch (event)

180	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
181	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:

196	{
197	    (void)param;
198	
199	    for (;;)
200	    {
201	        if (FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
202	        {

243	    (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_tx_notify);
244	}
245	
246	void Fauxmote_SendCmd(uint8_t op)
247	{
248	    if (!s_ready) { return; }
249	    (void)xQueueSend(s_cmd_queue, &op, 0);
250	    (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_tx_notify);
251	}
252	
253	bool Fauxmote_GetStatus(uint8_t *flags, uint8_t *player_slot,
254	                        uint8_t *report_mode, uint8_t *last_result, uint32_t *age_ms)
255	{
256	    uint8_t    snap[MF_LEN_STATUS];
257	    bool       valid;
258	    TickType_t tick;
259	
260	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
261	    valid = s_status_valid;
262	    memcpy(snap, s_status, MF_LEN_STATUS);
263	    tick = s_status_tick;
264	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
265	
266	    if (!valid) { return false; }
267	
268	    if (flags)       { *flags       = snap[0]; }
269	    if (player_slot) { *player_slot = snap[1]; }
270	    if (report_mode) { *report_mode = snap[2]; }
271	    if (last_result) { *last_result = snap[3]; }
272	    if (age_ms)      { *age_ms = (uint32_t)(xTaskGetTickCount() - tick) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS; }
273	    return true;
274	}
275	
276	void Fauxmote_Initialize(void)
277	{
278	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FX_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH, sizeof(uint8_t),
279	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage, &s_cmd_queue_buf);
280	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
281	    s_tx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_tx_notify_buf);
282	    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
283	    configASSERT(s_tx_notify != NULL && s_rx_notify != NULL);
284	
285	    /* Reconfigure FLEXCOM1 (MCC default 500000, unused while the guitar is on T1S)
286	     * to the link baud, 8-N-1. */
287	    FLEXCOM_USART_SERIAL_SETUP setup = {
288	        .baudRate = MF_UART_BAUD,
289	        .dataWidth = FLEXCOM_USART_DATA_8_BIT,
290	        .parity    = FLEXCOM_USART_PARITY_NONE,
291	        .stopBits  = FLEXCOM_USART_STOP_1_BIT,
292	    };
293	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_SerialSetup(&setup, FLEXCOM1_USART_FrequencyGet());
294	
295	    /* Arm continuous RX for the STATUS uplink: wake the parser on each byte. */
296	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
297	    FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadThresholdSet(1u);
298	    (void)FLEXCOM1_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);
299	
300	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(fx_tx_task, "FxTx", FX_TX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
301	                            NULL, FX_TASK_PRIORITY, s_tx_stack, &s_tx_tcb);
302	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(fx_rx_task, "FxRx", FX_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
303	                            NULL, FX_TASK_PRIORITY, s_rx_stack, &s_rx_tcb);
304	
305	    s_ready = true;
306	}
307

1	# edge-ai
2	
3	Distill marvin's emitted gameplay commands into a small causal model over the
4	fretboard's 5-channel ADC stream. **Design + plan live in [`docs/`](docs/)** —
5	start with [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) and [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md).
6	
7	This package is the host-side pipeline (PyTorch): train a causal CNN, then int8
8	post-training quantise it into the `model_weights.h` the fretboard firmware runs.
9	Input is the actuator-labelled CSV from `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator-fb`.
10	
11	## Layout
12	
13	- `edge_ai/data.py` — CSV loader + causal row-index windowing (stdlib).
14	- `edge_ai/lag.py` — photo-dip → strum lag measurement (stdlib).
15	- `edge_ai/metrics.py` — per-bit accuracy/F1 + strum-event timing (stdlib).
16	- `edge_ai/model.py` — causal 1D-CNN (`StrumNet`, torch).
17	- `edge_ai/train.py` — training loop + holdout evaluation (torch).
18	- `edge_ai/quantize.py` — int8 post-training quantiser + `model_weights.h` emitter (numpy/torch).
19	- `edge_ai/viz.py` — torchinfo summary, torchview graph, receptive-field cone plot (`viz` group).
20	- `edge_ai/cli.py` — `edge-ai {lag,train,eval,quantize,viz}`.
21	
22	The stdlib pieces (`data`, `lag`, `metrics`) run without numpy/torch; only
23	`model`/`train`/`eval` need the `train` dependency group.
24	
25	## Use
26	
27	```sh
28	export UV_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/uv-cache"   # only needed inside a restricted sandbox
29	
30	# size the causal window from real data (no torch needed)
31	uv run edge-ai lag path/to/song-expert.csv --curve
32	
33	# install the heavy deps and train
34	uv sync --group train --group dev
35	uv run edge-ai train --holdout heldout.csv song1.csv song2.csv song3.csv \
36	    --window 60 --out model.pt
37	uv run edge-ai eval --model model.pt heldout.csv
38	
39	# int8 quantise -> firmware header (deploy model: --no-holdout --channels 16 --window 85)
40	uv run edge-ai quantize --model model.pt --name hard \
41	    --strum-thresh 0.80 --out ../../firmware/fretboard/model_weights.h song1.csv song2.csv
42	
43	# visualise the model (summary + RF cone always; graph needs the graphviz binary)
44	uv sync --group train --group viz   # adds torchinfo, torchview, matplotlib
45	uv run edge-ai viz --model model.pt --rf-cone rf_cone.png --graph graph.svg
46	
47	# tests (stdlib-only; needs the dev group for pytest)
48	uv run --group dev pytest
49	```
50	
51	For block diagrams beyond these, export the float model to ONNX and open it in
52	[Netron](https://netron.app), or redraw in PlotNeuralNet / NN-SVG.
53	
54	Corpus is Expert-only, one song held out — see [`docs/training.md`](docs/training.md) §4.
55
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# edge-ai — Design Specification
2	
3	> **Status:** running on hardware (2026-06-04). A 16-channel int8 StrumNet, distilled from marvin's hard-mode play across 5 songs, runs standalone on the fretboard PIC32CM — reads its own photosensors, drives the controller, plays hard reasonably well on the bench with marvin disconnected. Offline phases (data pipeline, training, int8 quantisation) and the on-device port are done; remaining work is play-quality polish and difficulty/timing coverage. See [rollout.md](rollout.md) for phase status, the [journal](journal.md) for current focus, and [review.md](review.md) for open questions, risks, and rejected alternatives.
4	
5	## 1. Purpose & scope
6	
7	A development effort to build a small ML model that takes the fretboard's 5-channel phototransistor ADC stream and emits the same 1-byte fret + strum bitmask that marvin's timing pipeline produces today. Once trained, validated, and deployed, it removes marvin from the runtime gameplay loop.
8	
9	This is intentionally an **offline-first development effort**. Almost all of the work — capture, label, train, validate, debug — happens on a dev PC against recorded marvin self-play data. The on-device deployment is the *last* phase, after the model has been proven offline.
10	
11	**In scope:**
12	
13	- Training-data plumbing: a new export mode in [tools/marvin-perf](../../marvin-perf/) that turns marvin self-play perf-log captures into labelled CSV.
14	- Host-side training, validation, and model artifacts.
15	- On-device runtime integration (**built**). The deployment target is the fretboard MCU (PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz) — see [runtime.md](runtime.md); the offline phases were MCU-agnostic and the target could have been revisited if the model size/shape demanded it, but the int8 model fits with large margin.
16	
17	**Out of scope:**
18	
19	- Replacing marvin as the *reference* detector. Marvin remains the source of truth for training and diagnostics.
20	- Game-state / menu navigation. The edge AI plays gameplay only; whole-session control still belongs to marvin (system [SPEC.md §4.8 of marvin spec](../../../firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md)).
21	- The fretboard-takeover fallback ([fretboard journal](../../../firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md), 2026-06-02 entry). That mode runs `fret_button.c` standalone; the edge AI is a separate operating mode if/when it deploys to fretboard.
22	
23	## 2. Why now
24	
25	Two concrete pressures came out of the recent training-data work:
26	
27	### 2.1 Spatial mismatch between current label and ADC
28	
29	The current SensiML CSV exporter ([tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py)) labels each fretboard ADC sample with `cv_marvin_v1`'s `pressed_mask`, broadcast forward by `frame_epoch`. But the two sensors look at different points on the screen:
30	
31	- `cv_marvin_v1` samples at `y = 311` ([detector/cv_marvin_v1.c](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c)), above the strike line.
32	- The five phototransistors physically sit "above the TV strike line" ([fretboard SPEC.md](../../../firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md)), at a different (unverified) row than `y = 311`.
33	
34	Same falling note, different sensors, different times. Aligning them on `frame_epoch` bakes in a fixed offset that is only correct at one scroll speed. Fixing this in hardware is finicky and locks the system to a single mechanical layout.
35	
36	### 2.2 Strum timing missing from the AI's job
37	
38	Today's training pipeline emits per-fret pressed labels only. The chord window + +220 ms strum scheduler ([actuator/timing_pipeline.c:21,198,199](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) is real, non-trivial work that the AI is not being asked to learn. Whatever the AI replaces, the timing pipeline still has to live somewhere.
39	
40	The simplifying observation is that the model only needs to learn *when* to strum — not *which direction* — because alternating up/down is a human ergonomics constraint the controller doesn't enforce. That collapses 2 strum bits into 1 and halves the rare-class label density problem.
41	
42	## 3. Decisions locked
43	
44	| Decision | Why (one line) |
45	|---|---|
46	| **Output:** 6 bits — 5 fret bits + 1 collapsed strum bit. At the wire it's emitted as strum-down (bit 5) only; bit 6 is always 0. | Pulls strum timing into the AI; alternating up/down is a human ergonomic constraint the controller doesn't enforce. The collapse happens *at export time*, not in the recording — `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` keeps both strum bits as captured so a future human-trainer corpus can preserve direction information for other uses. |
47	| **Supervision:** distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` from marvin self-play. | Sidesteps spatial mismatch — labels are marvin's chosen byte, not a CV intermediate. |
48	| **Intended deployment target:** fretboard PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz. | Removes marvin from the gameplay loop; truly "edge". Offline phases are MCU-agnostic, so this can be revisited if the model demands more compute. |
49	| **Inputs at inference (v1):** the existing 5 ADC channels only. | Cheapest start; per-fret HW expansion deferred (see [review.md](review.md) Q1). |
50	| **Training corpus:** marvin self-play recordings only. | Simplest closure. AI inherits marvin's behavior — good and bad — see [review.md §risks](review.md#risks). |
51	
52	The key insight that makes this work: **distilling against marvin's commands dissolves the spatial-mismatch problem.** The label is the byte marvin chose with the +220 ms strum delay already baked in. The model just needs a wide enough causal window of ADC to learn whatever delay maps photo dip → strum, regardless of where the photoxistors physically sit. Mechanical alignment becomes a non-requirement.
53	
54	## 4. Document map
55	
56	| Doc | What's in it |
57	|---|---|
58	| [architecture.md](architecture.md) | Training-time and inference-time data flow; cadence; sanity-check that the shape addresses §2 |
59	| [training.md](training.md) | Exporter changes, CSV schema, capture protocol, model architecture |
60	| [model.md](model.md) | The actual network (StrumNet) layer by layer — design rationale, receptive field, params, int8 deploy path, limitations |
61	| [runtime.md](runtime.md) | On-device deployment (as built) — the two int8 inference modules (streaming / recompute), callback wiring, mode toggle, memory budget |
62	| [rollout.md](rollout.md) | Phased plan with explicit offline/hardware split, plus per-phase verification (offline + on-device port done) |
63	| [review.md](review.md) | Risks, open questions surfaced for reviewer pushback, and alternatives considered |
64
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# model — StrumNet (the actual network)
2	
3	What the model *is*, layer by layer, and *why* it's shaped that way. Code: [`edge_ai/model.py`](../edge_ai/model.py). For the data it consumes see [`training.md`](training.md); for the on-device int8 path see [`runtime.md`](runtime.md); for the historical decision trail (why a CNN over MPLAB ML, how the RF was sized) see the [journal](journal.md) decision log.
4	
5	> **TL;DR.** A tiny causal 1D-CNN: 5 ADC channels → **3 dilated causal conv layers** `(d=1,4,16)` → a linear head on the **last timestep** → 6 sigmoids (5 frets + 1 strum). Three facts shape every choice:
6	> 1. It is a **predict-now** model — the head reads only the newest timestep, so the architecture is built around that timestep's **receptive field**.
7	> 2. The receptive field **must cover the photo→strum lag** (~48 samples / 200 ms on hard). That is why there are three dilated layers, not two: `(1,4,16)` gives **RF 85 (~354 ms)**; the old two-layer `(1,4)` was RF 21 and couldn't reach back to the cue, capping frets at ~0.86.
8	> 3. The model is the **timing function** marvin used to play. It learns whatever photo-dip→command delay was baked into the corpus, so it is only valid for the difficulty + timing constants it was distilled from (see [journal](journal.md) decision log).
9	
10	The shipped model: `StrumNet(channels=16, kernel=5, dilations=(1,4,16))`, trained at `window=85`, int8-quantised, running standalone on the fretboard PIC32CM. The training *default* is `channels=8`; deploy passes `--channels 16` (§8).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. Input
15	
16	- **Shape:** `(batch, 5, window)` — 5 phototransistor ADC channels (G/R/Y/B/O), `window` consecutive 240 Hz samples, channels-first for `Conv1d`.
17	- **Normalisation:** per-channel standardise (zero-mean / unit-variance) using stats computed on the training set and saved in the checkpoint ([`data.compute_norm_stats`](../edge_ai/data.py)). **Why it's load-bearing:** the raw ADC band is narrow (idle ≈ 3900, dips ≈ 1000); naive `/4095` leaves every input clustered near 0.95 and starves gradients — the first baseline underfit until standardisation was added. At deploy this affine folds losslessly into the int8 input quantisation, so it costs nothing on device.
18	- **Windowing:** sliced **by row index** within a contiguous `fb_seq` run, never by the bursty `timestamp` column. Each CSV row is one true 240 Hz sample paired atomically with its label on-device; a dropped frame breaks the run so a window never stitches two non-adjacent samples (see [`data.contiguous_runs`](../edge_ai/data.py), and the [journal](journal.md) timestamp-burstiness entry).
19	- **At deploy:** one inference per 240 Hz tick. The window is the most recent `window` ADC samples (recompute path) or — in the streaming path — a continuous causal convolution that needs no explicit window buffer at all (§7).
20	
21	## 2. Output
22	
23	- **6 logits → sigmoids**, thresholded to bits: `[green, red, yellow, blue, orange, strum]`.
24	- **Independent per-bit** (no chord-shape coupling). Strum is the **collapsed** down|up bit; at the wire it maps to bit 5 (strum-down), bit 6 stays 0. The collapse halves the rare-class problem and reflects that alternating up/down is a human-ergonomics constraint the controller doesn't enforce ([SPEC.md §3](SPEC.md)).
25	- Frets thresholded at 0.5; **strum has its own threshold** (`--strum-thresh`, default 0.5) because its precision/recall curve has headroom we deliberately trade. After thresholding, the strum bit passes through the **monostable** post-processor — not part of the network, lives at deploy time (§7).
26	
27	## 3. Architecture, layer by layer
28	
29	```
30	  5 ADC channels × W samples              input  (5, W)
31	  (G R Y B O), per-channel standardised
32	            │
33	            ▼
34	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
35	  │ CausalConv1d  5→C  k=5  d=1   + ReLU │  left-pad 4    → (C, W)
36	  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
37	            │
38	            ▼
39	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
40	  │ CausalConv1d  C→C  k=5  d=4   + ReLU │  left-pad 16   → (C, W)
41	  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
42	            │
43	            ▼
44	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
45	  │ CausalConv1d  C→C  k=5  d=16  + ReLU │  left-pad 64   → (C, W)
46	  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
47	            │
48	            ▼   last timestep only:  h[:, :, -1]          → (C,)
49	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
50	  │ Linear  C→6                          │               → 6 logits
51	  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
52	            │
53	            ▼   sigmoid → threshold (frets 0.5, strum tunable)
54	     [ G  R  Y  B  O │ strum ]
55	                         │
56	                         ▼   deploy only (not in the net): monostable one-shot
57	                      clean strum pulse → wire byte bit 5
58	```
59	
60	The same structure traced from the shipped 16-channel checkpoint (`edge-ai viz`), with tensor shapes at `window=85`. Note the growing left-pad (89 → 101 → 149 from `d=1,4,16`) and the `__getitem__` last-timestep pluck `(1,16,85) → (1,16)` feeding the linear head:
61	
62	![StrumNet layer graph: input (1,5,85) through three CausalConv1d+ReLU blocks, last-timestep slice, then Linear to 6 logits](img/strumnet-graph.png)
63	
64	Parameter counts at the training default `StrumNet(channels=8, kernel=5, dilations=(1,4,16))`:
65	
66	| Layer | Op | Out shape | Params |
67	|---|---|---|---|
68	| input | — | (5, W) | — |
69	| `CausalConv1d` 0 | Conv1d(5→8, k=5, **d=1**) + left-pad 4 | (8, W) | 5·8·5 + 8 = **208** |
70	| ReLU | — | (8, W) | — |
71	| `CausalConv1d` 1 | Conv1d(8→8, k=5, **d=4**) + left-pad 16 | (8, W) | 8·8·5 + 8 = **328** |
72	| ReLU | — | (8, W) | — |
73	| `CausalConv1d` 2 | Conv1d(8→8, k=5, **d=16**) + left-pad 64 | (8, W) | 8·8·5 + 8 = **328** |
74	| ReLU | — | (8, W) | — |
75	| take last timestep | `h[:, :, -1]` | (8,) | — |
76	| `head` | Linear(8→6) | (6,) | 8·6 + 6 = **54** |
77	| | | **total** | **918** |
78	
79	The shipped 16-channel model is **3 110** params (§8). Only width changes with `--channels`; depth (3 layers) and the dilation schedule are fixed.
80	
81	### Why these layers, in this order
82	
83	- **1D convolution, not a dense window or an RNN.** The signal is a 5-channel time series whose informative event (a phototransistor dimming, then recovering) is *local in time but shift-equivariant* — it can occur at any offset within the window. Convolution shares weights across time, so it learns the dip→command mapping once rather than per-position; that is exactly what a dense layer over the flattened window cannot do efficiently, and it has no recurrent state to unroll on an MCU.
84	- **Causal padding (left-pad only).** [`CausalConv1d`](../edge_ai/model.py) left-pads by `(kernel-1)·dilation` and uses a plain `Conv1d`, so `output[t]` depends only on inputs `≤ t` — no future leakage. This is what lets us train densely on whole windows yet deploy as a streaming "predict-now" model: the training-time and deploy-time computations of `output[t]` are identical.
85	- **Dilation `(1, 4, 16)`, three layers.** Stacking dilated convs grows the receptive field *geometrically* for a *linear* parameter cost. Three layers at kernel 5 reach RF 85 (§4) — enough to cover the lag — for 918 params; reaching the same RF with un-dilated kernel-5 layers would need ~21 layers. The schedule `1→4→16` keeps coverage gap-free (each layer's stride is ≤ the previous layer's reach) while quadrupling reach per layer.
86	- **8 channels (training default).** Width sets capacity. 5→8 in layer 0 is a mild expansion; 8 is the smallest width that fit the frets well in early experiments. The strum class is sparse enough that capacity *there* is the binding constraint, which is why deploy uses 16 (§8).
87	- **ReLU.** Cheap, int8-friendly (a clamp at 0 in the requant), no FPU needed.
88	- **Linear head on the last timestep only.** The job is "what command applies *now*", so only `h[:, :, -1]` feeds the head. A temporal-pooling head would use the whole window but blur *when* an event happened — fatal for strum onset. The right way to use more of the window is to widen the RF (done), not to pool.
89	
90	## 4. Receptive field — the thing the architecture is built around
91	
92	Only the **last timestep** feeds the head (`h[:, :, -1]`). Its receptive field — how many of the newest input samples can influence the prediction — is:
93	
94	```
95	RF = 1 + Σ (kernel-1)·dilation = 1 + (5-1)·(1 + 4 + 16) = 85 samples ≈ 354 ms
96	```
97	
98	**What "dilation" is.** A kernel-5 conv always has 5 weights; dilation `d` sets how far apart in time those 5 taps reach — it inserts `d-1` skipped samples between them:
99	
100	```
101	 d=1  (normal):  t  t-1  t-2  t-3  t-4              5 adjacent samples,  spans  5
102	 d=4          :  t  t-4  t-8  t-12 t-16             5 taps, gap 3,       spans 17
103	 d=16         :  t  t-16 t-32 t-48 t-64             5 taps, gap 15,      spans 65
104	```
105	
106	A dilated layer leaves holes, but the layer below has already summarised them: each `conv2` output condenses a `d=4` neighbourhood, each `conv1` output condenses 5 adjacent inputs, so when `conv3` (d=16) samples 5 coarse points each one already carries its surroundings — **no input sample is ignored** even though the top layer touches only 1 in 16 directly. That is what buys the *geometric* RF growth for a *linear* parameter cost (the §3 "why these layers" point): `1→4→16` reaches RF 85 in **3 layers**, where plain `d=1` kernel-5 layers would need ~21.
107	
108	The cone below (`edge-ai viz --rf-cone`) is that sum drawn out — the head reads one `conv3` output (top), whose `d=16` taps fan back to 5 `conv2` positions, each fanning through `d=4` then `d=1` until the taps tile a **contiguous 85-sample input span**, gap-free by construction:
109	
110	![Receptive-field cone: output[t] fans back through conv3 (d=16), conv2 (d=4), conv1 (d=1) to a contiguous 85-sample input span](img/receptive-field-cone.png)
111	
112	Reading it top→bottom, the dot counts go **1 → 5 → 21 → 85** as each fan-out multiplies the spread:
113	
114	| Row (label = that layer's own dilation) | Dots | Why |
115	|---|---|---|
116	| `conv3 out (d=16)` | 1 | the single `output[t]` the head reads |
117	| `conv2 out (d=4)` | 5 | conv3's d=16 taps → 5 points spaced **16** apart |
118	| `conv1 out (d=1)` | 21 | each fans to 5 points spaced **4** apart; they tile to 21 |
119	| `input (5 ch)` | 85 | each fans to 5 **adjacent** points; they tile to the full 85 |
120	
121	(The `(d=X)` in a row label is *that layer's own* dilation — the spacing it uses to read the row below. The spacing of the dots you *see* in a row comes from the layer above sampling it, so the `conv2 out (d=4)` row shows dots 16 apart, set by conv3.)
122	
123	This single number governs the architecture, because of three consequences:
124	
125	1. **The window cannot help past the RF.** Inputs older than 85 samples are convolved internally but never reach the head. This is why early `--window 96 / 128` sweeps gave nothing over `60` *when the RF was 21* — anything past the RF is discarded. The window only needs to be **≥ RF**; we train the deploy model at `window=85` (= RF) so the streaming deploy path is bit-exact (§7).
126	
127	2. **The RF must cover the photo→strum lag.** The photo dip that *causes* a strum sits ~48 samples (~200 ms on hard) before the strike-line command. If the RF is shorter than that lag, the head literally cannot see the cue:
128	
129	   ```
130	     prediction at "now" depends ONLY on the last RF samples:
131	
132	       … now-48 ───────────────────────────────────── now
133	          │                                             │
134	          ▼            │<──────── RF = 85 ─────────────>│
135	     photo dip that    │   covers the cue ✓             │
136	     CAUSES this strum  └────────────────────────────────┘
137	     (~48 samples back, now INSIDE the receptive field)
138	   ```
139	
140	   With the old RF-21 default the dip was *outside* the RF; the model only worked at all because slow hard-mode scrolling widened each note's occlusion enough that its tail leaked into the last 21 samples. Faster difficulties → narrower occlusion → less of it inside the RF → harder. RF 85 removes that fragility.
141	
142	### Why RF 85, decided by an overfit A/B
143	
144	The fret-accuracy ceiling was first diagnosed on a detector-labelled probe (labels coincident with the photo dip, so *inside* even a tiny RF — frets hit 0.99 trivially) and then predicted to bite the deployable `actuator-fb` labels (strike-line timing, ~48 samples after the dip). An overfit A/B on the line-263 `actuator-fb` data (slowride-hard, train == eval) confirmed the prediction and the fix in one shot:
145	
146	| | RF 21 `(1,4)` | RF 85 `(1,4,16)` |
147	|---|---|---|
148	| frets (G/R/Y/B/O) | 0.86 / 0.84 / 0.89 / 0.91 / 0.94 | **0.97 / 0.97 / 0.98 / 0.98 / 0.99** |
149	| loss (plateau) | 0.309 | **0.080** |
150	| strum recall / precision | 0.84 / 0.53 | **0.97 / 0.82** |
151	| strum p95 | 20.8 ms | 16.7 ms |
152	
153	RF 21 can't reach back to the cue → caps at ~0.86; RF 85 recovers to ~0.99 at ~50 k dense MACs (well under budget — §5). `(1,4,16)` is the default in [`model.py`](../edge_ai/model.py) / [`cli.py`](../edge_ai/cli.py); the dilation list is a `--dilations` flag and is stored in the checkpoint (older checkpoints fall back to `(1,4)`).
154	
155	## 5. Compute cost — `count_macs` is a loose upper bound
156	
157	[`count_macs`](../edge_ai/model.py) multiplies each conv's cost by the **full window** — it assumes every output position is computed, as in dense training:
158	
159	| config | `count_macs` (dense, ×window) |
160	|---|---|
161	| 8 ch, window 60 | ~50 k |
162	| 8 ch, window 85 | ~71 k |
163	| 16 ch, window 85 | ~252 k |
164	
165	But at deploy you only need the **last timestep**. Two on-device paths exploit that (both in firmware, both bit-exact with the host int8 sim — §7):
166	
167	| path | what it computes per tick | 16 ch, window 85 |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| **recompute** ([`model_infer.c`](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer.c)) | only the conv positions the last timestep transitively needs (back-propagated `s_need`: 21 / 5 / 1 positions per layer) | **~16 k MACs** (~12.5 k at window 60) |
170	| **streaming** ([`model_infer_stream.c`](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer_stream.c)) | exactly **one new conv column per layer**, caching prior columns in small rings | **~3.1 k MACs** (888 at 8 ch) |
171	
172	So against the ~100 k MAC/tick budget at 24 MHz, **even the 16-channel model fits comfortably**, and the streaming path clears 240 Hz with large margin. The "13× over budget" figure we once quoted was a `count_macs` artifact of the dense formula — real deploy cost is 1–2 orders of magnitude lower. We are **not** as capacity-constrained as the dense printout implies, which is what made widening to 16 channels affordable.
173	
174	## 6. Training
175	
176	- **Loss:** [`BCEWithLogitsLoss`](../edge_ai/train.py) with a `pos_weight` vector — 1.0 on each fret, `pos_weight` on strum (auto = inverse strum frequency, ~10–17; override with `--strum-weight`). Strum sparsity (~7–13 % on hard) otherwise collapses it to "always 0". The deploy model uses `--strum-weight 5` (below the auto value) to trim the recall bias at the source (§8).
177	- **Optimiser:** Adam, lr 1e-3, batch 256, 30 epochs (deploy: 50).
178	- **Strum label dilation** (`--strum-dilate`): optionally widen the strum positive by ±k samples in the *training* labels so a near-miss isn't fully penalised. Eval is **never** dilated.
179	- **Lead compensation** (`--label-lead`): shift training labels earlier by N samples to pre-empt on-device lag; eval uses the true labels. Unused in the shipped model (kept for residual-lag tuning — see [journal](journal.md) next-steps).
180	- **Checkpoint** stores `state_dict`, `window`, `channels`, `kernel`, `dilations`, `label_lead`, and the norm `mean`/`std` — everything needed to reconstruct the model and the input affine at eval and quantise time.
181	
182	## 7. Inference & deployment (int8, on hardware)
183	
184	This is **built and running standalone on the fretboard PIC32CM** (the int8 path is no longer a future "Phase 3" — it is the deployed path; see [`runtime.md`](runtime.md) and the [journal](journal.md)).
185	
186	- **Quantisation — post-training, int8, essentially lossless.** [`quantize.py`](../edge_ai/quantize.py) does per-tensor symmetric int8 weights, int32 accumulators, and int64 fixed-point requant back to int8 activations (the target M0+ has no FPU, so float inference is out). Standardisation folds into an integer **input affine** `(M_in, B_in, S_in)`; output thresholding folds into an integer **compare on the head accumulator** (no on-device sigmoid: `sigmoid(x) ≥ t ⇔ x ≥ logit(t)`, so frets compare against 0 and strum against `logit(thresh)`). Measured PTQ error on slowride-hard: frets within ±0.001 of float, strum recall unchanged — so **no QAT is needed**.
187	- **Bit-exactness gate.** The host int8 reference (`quantize.int8_sim_*`) is asserted bit-for-bit against the actual firmware C — both the recompute path ([`tests/test_bitexact.py`](../tests/test_bitexact.py)) and the streaming path ([`tests/test_stream_bitexact.py`](../tests/test_stream_bitexact.py)), over a full capture, 0 mismatches.
188	- **Threshold** the 6 head accumulators (frets at 0, strum at the folded `--strum-thresh`).
189	- **Monostable** on the strum bit: a rising-edge-triggered one-shot (`hold` ticks high, then `refractory` ticks blocking new triggers — [`metrics.monostable`](../edge_ai/metrics.py)). It guarantees clean uniform pulses, absorbs mid-pulse glitches, and emits exactly one pulse per rising edge. A few counters; runs on the MCU. The same logic lives in both firmware paths.
190	- **Streaming vs recompute (why two paths).** The streaming path is bit-exact with a continuous causal conv, which only matches a model **trained at `window ≥ RF` (= 85)** — at a shorter window the moving zero-pad boundary differs. So the shipped model is trained at window 85 and deployed streaming (locks to 240 Hz, ~3 k MACs/tick). The recompute path works at any trained window but re-runs the needed positions each tick (~93 Hz at 16 ch) and is kept as the general-window fallback. Selected at build time by `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING` in [`fretboard_config.h`](../../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard_config.h).
191	- **Runtime weight swap.** The active model is a `model_def_t` pointer; the quantiser emits one named `model_<name>` per `--name`, several link together (shared arch dims guarded by a `_Static_assert`), and `model_infer_set_model()` swaps at runtime — the mechanism for per-difficulty models.
192	
193	## 8. Capacity, limitations & open design questions
194	
195	- **Deploy width = 16 channels (not the 8 ch training default).** 8 ch is capacity-limited on the sparse strum class: it overstrummed on hardware and **no threshold fixed it** — 0.85 missed real strums *and* still overstrummed, i.e. the precision/recall *curve itself* was the wall (the same signature as the early 8 ch-vs-64 ch overfit diagnostic, strum recall .86 vs .99). 16 ch lifts the whole curve (mono precision/recall .856/.969 → .942/.981) so a single threshold lands both. It's affordable because inference runs cheaply on device (§5: ~3 k MACs streaming, RAM ~4 KB of 8 KB). 32 ch would be RAM-bound, not compute-bound. The training *default* stays 8 ch; deploy passes `--channels 16`.
196	- **~~Receptive field too small for the lag~~ (resolved §4).** Was the headline issue; `(1,4,16)` RF-85 covers the lag (overfit frets ~0.99, held-out ≥0.96 except red). The remaining open item is generalisation polish, not the RF.
197	- **Red fret is the lone laggard** (held-out ~0.89 vs ≥0.96 for the others), consistent across epochs and not a corpus-coverage gap. Hypotheses (holdout variance / green-yellow neighbour confusion / `ph_red` channel quality) are listed in the [journal](journal.md) open questions; cheapest test is rotate-holdout cross-val. Carried as a known caveat — confirm it costs game score before treating it as blocking.
198	- **Last-timestep head** — correct for a predict-*now* model; fine as-is now the RF covers the lag. Temporal pooling would use more of the window but blur onset timing — not the right fix.
199	- **Per-bit independence** — chords occupy a tiny subset of 2⁶; a chord-shape head or the two-head event detector ([review.md](review.md)) is the fallback if independence caps accuracy. Not hit yet.
200	- **Single-difficulty validity.** The model *is* the timing function it was distilled from; mixing difficulties (or timing-constant regimes) teaches two photo→strum lags for identical inputs — ill-posed. v1 is one model per regime; multi-difficulty routes (per-difficulty models, or a scroll-speed sensor) are in [review.md](review.md) / the [journal](journal.md).
201	</content>
202	</invoke>
203
```

1	# architecture
2	
3	How the edge AI fits at training time and at inference time. For decisions and the document map, see [SPEC.md](SPEC.md).
4	
5	## 1. Training-time data flow (offline)
6	
7	```
8	Wii ──► marvin (cv_marvin_v1 + timing_pipeline)
9	          │   │
10	          │   ├── PERF_REC_ACTUATOR (intended_mask, strum_dir)   ──┐
11	          │   └── (commands over USB CDC to fretboard)              │
12	          │                                                          ▼
13	          │                                                  marvin-perf
14	          │                                                   (offline)
15	          │   ▲                                                      │
16	          │   │ PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (5×ADC @ 240 Hz)              │
17	          │   │                                                      │
18	          │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
19	          │                                                          │
20	          │                                                          ▼
21	          │                                                   SensiML CSV
22	          │                                            (per-row: 5 ADC + 6 labels)
23	                                                                     │
24	                                                                     ▼
25	                                                        host training (PyTorch)
26	                                                                     │
27	                                                                     ▼
28	                                                          int8 quantised model
29	                                                            (model_weights.h)
30	```
31	
32	Both record streams already flow through perf-log keyed by `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`. The exporter joins them offline. See [training.md](training.md) for the exporter change and CSV schema.
33	
34	## 2. Inference-time data flow (on-device, as built)
35	
36	```
37	fretboard TC0 ISR @ 240 Hz (short & bounded):
38	    fret_scan_all()                  ──► model_infer_stream_step(scan) ──► cmd
39	                                            │  (streaming: ~1 conv col/layer/tick,
40	                                            │   no full-window buffer)
41	                                            ▼
42	    cmd_receive_apply_mask(enabled ? cmd : 0)  (open-drain fret GPIOs + strum)
43	    data_stream_send()                          (applied_mask telemetry)
44	```
45	
46	The marvin command stream (`cmd_receive`) is bypassed when fretboard is in `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode; the model owns the wire. The deployed path is **streaming** inference (locks to 240 Hz, runs inline); a **recompute** fallback runs in the main loop for non-RF-width models. SW0 toggles model control at runtime. See [runtime.md](runtime.md) for the full integration shape and the two inference modules.
47	
48	## 3. Inference cadence
49	
50	One inference per 240 Hz tick (every 4.17 ms). Budget at 24 MHz with no FPU is ≈100 k cycles. The deployed 16-channel model costs ~3 k MACs/tick streaming (~16 k recompute) — comfortably inside budget; the dense `count_macs` figure (~252 k) is a loose upper bound (see [model.md §5](model.md)).
51	
52	## 4. Why this shape addresses both concerns
53	
54	- **Spatial mismatch dissolved.** No CV-row → photo-row alignment needed at training time. The causal window (RF 85 ≈ 354 ms) captures whatever upstream photoxistor signal preceded the strum, regardless of physical sensor placement on the screen.
55	- **Strum timing learned.** The strum bit is part of the output. Weighted BCE (the strum bit is sparse — see [review.md §risks](review.md#risks)) lets the model learn the photo→strum delay implicitly from the data — provided the receptive field reaches back far enough to see the cue ([model.md §4](model.md)).
56	- **Edge AI is end-to-end standalone.** Once deployed, fretboard runs the model on its own ADC stream; marvin can be off and gameplay still works. Marvin's role becomes "training-data source + reference detector for diagnostics + game-state controller".
57

```text
1	# runtime
2	
3	On-device deployment shape. **As built and running standalone on the fretboard MCU (2026-06-04).** The int8 model reads its own photosensors and drives the controller with marvin disconnected.
4	
5	## 1. Intended target
6	
7	PIC32CM6408PL10048, Cortex-M0+ @ 24 MHz, no FPU, **64 KB Flash / 8 KB SRAM** (datasheet DS40002667). The current fretboard MCU. See [SPEC.md §3](SPEC.md#3-decisions-locked) on why this is a soft target rather than a locked one — the offline phases are MCU-agnostic. The deployed 16-channel int8 model fits with large margin (§5, §6).
8	
9	## 2. Two inference modules (as built)
10	
11	There are **two** int8 inference implementations of the same model; one is selected at build time by `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING` in [`fretboard_config.h`](../../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard_config.h). Both are integer-only (no FPU), bit-exact with the host reference `edge_ai.quantize.int8_sim`, share the `model_def_t` weight struct from the generated `model_weights.h`, and apply the same strum monostable.
12	
13	**Streaming — [`model_infer_stream.c`](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer_stream.c) (default, `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING=1`).** Computes a *continuous* causal convolution: one new conv column per layer per tick, caching prior columns in small per-layer rings (depths 5 / 17 / 65, sized to each layer's deepest tap). ~3 k MACs/tick at 16 ch — locks comfortably to 240 Hz. The catch: a continuous conv is only bit-exact with a model **trained at `window ≥ receptive field` (= 85 for `(1,4,16)`)** — at a shorter window the windowed model's moving zero-pad boundary wouldn't match. A `_Static_assert(MODEL_WINDOW >= 85)` guards this. The cascade is hard-coded for the 3-layer / kernel-5 / 5-in / 6-out arch (an `#error` guards a mismatched regeneration). `model_infer_stream_step(adc[5])` is called once per scan, in order.
14	
15	**Recompute — [`model_infer.c`](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer.c) (`MODEL_INFER_STREAMING=0`).** Owns a `MODEL_WINDOW × 5` input ring; each tick re-runs only the conv positions the last timestep transitively needs (a back-propagated `s_need` table — 21 / 5 / 1 positions per layer at window 85), skipping the dense per-position conv. Works at **any** trained window, so it's the general-window fallback, but it re-runs the receptive field each tick (~16 k MACs at 16 ch / window 85, measured ~93 Hz) so it **must run in the main loop, not the ISR** (§3). `model_infer_push(adc[5])` from the ISR, `model_infer_run()` from the main loop.
16	
17	Both modules guard their entire body on `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING`, so the inactive translation unit is empty and allocates no static buffers — both can stay in the MPLAB project; flip the mode in `fretboard_config.h` (or with `-D`) with no add/remove of source files. `model_infer_set_model(const model_def_t *m)` (each module) does the runtime weight swap (per-difficulty).
18	
19	## 3. The recompute path must run OUTSIDE the TC0 ISR — proven on hardware (2026-06-04)
20	
21	> Applies to the **recompute** path (`model_infer.c`). The streaming path is cheap enough (~3 k MACs/tick) to run inline; this section is why the recompute path can't.
22	
23	
24	The first bring-up ran `model_infer_run()` *inside* the 240 Hz TC0 callback. That fails two ways at once: the long ISR delays the next tick (sampling drops to ~150–190 Hz, so the model's window is no longer 250 ms and its learned photo→strum lag is wrong → late/missed notes), **and** it starves the interrupt-driven SERCOM TX, collapsing the data stream (recv ~22 fps with heavy drops). Measured with [`tools/marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py`](../../marvin-perf/fretboard_rate.py), which reads `sample_seq` to report the true tick rate.
25	
26	**Final shape — decouple sampling from inference:**
27	
28	```c
29	TC0 ISR (240 Hz, short & bounded)
30	    fret_scan_all();
31	    model_infer_push(scan);                 // sample the window at a clean 240 Hz
32	    enabled = poll_sw0_debounced();         // SW0 toggles model control; LED0 shows it
33	    cmd_receive_apply_mask(enabled ? s_latest_cmd : 0u);
34	    data_stream_send();                     // applied_mask carries the model's command
35	
36	main loop (best-effort)
37	    s_latest_cmd = model_infer_run();       // heavy inference, preempted by the ISR
38	```
39	
40	`s_latest_cmd` is a single `volatile uint8_t` (atomic on the M0+). `model_infer_run()` snapshots the ring cursor on entry so a concurrent `push()` can't shift the window mid-inference. Result: ISR stays short → 240 Hz sampling + serial both clean (measured 240/240, ~0 drops); command latency ≈ one inference period (~5 ms) + ≤1 tick. Build at **`-O2`/`-O3`** — `-O0` alone overruns the tick (the int8 conv + requant is heavy without optimisation).
41	
42	The command byte goes through `cmd_receive_apply_mask()` ([cmd_receive.c](../../../firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.c)) — bits 0..4 fret GPIOs, bit 5 strum-down, bit 6 left 0.
43	
44	> Caveat: the strum monostable lives inside `run()`, so its ticks are inference iterations, not 240 Hz ticks — pulse *width* ≈ `hold × inference_period`. Onset (what the game catches) is unaffected. Move it to the ISR if exact width ever matters.
45	
46	## 4. Operating mode + enable switch
47	
48	Build-time `FRETBOARD_MODE` (`MODEL_DRIVEN` default, `MARVIN_DRIVEN` to restore the marvin-driven path) in [main.c](../../../firmware/fretboard/main.c). **SW0 (PB03, active-low momentary)** toggles model control at runtime; **LED0 (PB02)** lit while enabled; boots disabled (outputs released). When disabled the ISR applies mask 0 (all released) but keeps sampling, so re-enable is seamless. Eventual plan: marvin commands the difficulty/enable over serial (§ runtime weight swap).
49	
50	## 5. Inference budget
51	
52	24 MHz × 4.17 ms ≈ 100 k cycles per tick. The deployed 16-channel model costs ~3 k MACs/tick streaming (the recompute path ~16 k at window 85) — both well inside budget; the dense `count_macs` figure (~252 k) is a loose upper bound that assumes every window position is computed (see [model.md §5](model.md)). Measured rates: streaming locks to 240 Hz; recompute ~93 Hz at 16 ch.
53	
54	## 6. Memory budget (8 KB SRAM)
55	
56	**Streaming (deployed: `(1,4,16)`, channels 16, window 85)** — `model_infer_stream.c` static scratch:
57	
58	- `s_qin` ring: 5 × 5 = 25 B.
59	- L0 ring: 17 × 16 = 272 B.
60	- L1 ring: 65 × 16 = 1040 B.
61	- ≈ **1.4 KB total** (rings + monostable state). No full-window buffer — the streaming cascade keeps only each layer's deepest-tap history.
62	
63	**Recompute (`model_infer.c`, channels 16, window 85)** static scratch, for contrast:
64	
65	- Input ring: 85 × 5 × 2 B = 850 B.
66	- Standardised int8 input `s_qin`: 85 × 5 = 425 B.
67	- Per-layer int8 activations `s_act`: 3 × 85 × 16 ≈ 4.1 KB.
68	- Needed-position table `s_need`: 3 × 85 = 255 B.
69	- ≈ **5.6 KB total** (the `s_act` window×channels term dominates — this is what makes 32 ch RAM-bound).
70	
71	Weights are flash-`const` (0 RAM) in both. A **RAM-resident programmable weight set** (loading weights over serial without reflashing) would add ≈ **1.1 KB** (int8 conv weights + biases + head + scales); confirm against the linker `.map`. One override slot fits; multiple RAM-resident models would not.
72	
73	## 7. Runtime weight swap (built) + programmable weights (future)
74	
75	The active model is a `model_def_t` pointer ([model_infer.h](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer.h)) — a struct of pointers to the int8 weights/scales/thresholds. `model_infer_set_model()` swaps it at runtime. The quantiser emits one named `model_<name>` per `--name`; several link together (an aggregator `model_weights.h` that `#include`s the per-difficulty headers), arch dims are shared `#define`s guarded by a `_Static_assert`, and `MODEL_DEFAULT` = the first one. **Per-difficulty models**: train one per difficulty, generate a header each, switch with `set_model()` — selection signal (serial command from marvin / button / scroll-speed sensor) is the open piece.
76	
77	**Programmable weights over serial (future, fits RAM):** because the active model is just a pointer, a RAM-resident `model_def_t` whose arrays point into a received buffer is a drop-in. Needs: a binary blob emitter in the quantiser (`--out-bin`), a framed/checksummed serial receive on the fretboard that validates magic/version/arch and copies into a RAM store, then `set_model(&ram_model)`. Flash `MODEL_DEFAULT` stays the fallback. Lets training iterations be loaded without reflashing.
78
```

 `./tools/edge-ai/docs/training.md`

```text
1	# training
2	
3	The offline pipeline: how marvin self-play recordings become training data, and the model that consumes them.
4	
5	## 1. Data flow
6	
7	Recap (full diagram in [architecture.md](architecture.md)):
8	
9	```
10	perf-log capture (.bin, schema v4: fretboard frame carries sample_seq + applied_mask)
11	    │
12	    ▼
13	marvin-perf  export-ml --labels=actuator-fb capture.bin out.csv
14	    │   (labels from the in-frame applied_mask — paired with the ADC scan
15	    │    atomically on-device, no cross-stream join)
16	    ▼
17	CSV (per-row: timestamp, fb_seq, 5 ADC, 6 labels)
18	    │
19	    ▼
20	host training (PyTorch)
21	```
22	
23	## 2. New label source in the SensiML exporter
24	
25	[tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) has a `--labels=` switch (the original `pressed_mask` path stays as `--labels=detector` for back-compat). Two modes matter:
26	
27	- **`actuator` (original, cross-stream).** Forward-fills `Actuator.intended_mask` onto each `FretboardRaw` row, emitting frets at bits 0..4 verbatim and a **collapsed strum bit** = `((intended_mask >> 5) | (intended_mask >> 6)) & 1` (logical OR of strum-down and strum-up). The label (send path) and feature (receive path) cross two USB-CDC directions, so the join has an unknown skew (see [review.md](review.md) / journal).
28	- **`actuator-fb` (deployed, atomic — schema v4).** The fretboard frame itself carries `sample_seq` + the `applied_mask` it was driving during the scan, paired with the ADC sample on-device in one 240 Hz tick. The exporter sources labels from `applied_mask` — **no cross-stream join, zero skew** — and emits an `fb_seq` column. This is the corpus the shipped model trains on; it is also the most faithful supervision (exactly the function the deployed model replaces). `detector-fb` is the analogous atomic detector probe.
29	
30	The strum collapse is a property of *these* exporter modes, not the raw capture. `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` records both strum bits as marvin emitted them; a future human-trainer corpus (where alternating up/down is meaningful) keeps both bits intact on disk for a future direction-aware exporter.
31	
32	## 3. CSV schema (`actuator-fb`)
33	
34	```
35	timestamp, fb_seq,
36	ph_green, ph_red, ph_yellow, ph_blue, ph_orange,
37	fret_green, fret_red, fret_yellow, fret_blue, fret_orange,
38	strum
39	```
40	
41	One row per `FretboardRaw` ≈ 240 Hz. `fb_seq` is the fretboard's monotonic sample counter; the loader windows **within contiguous `fb_seq` runs** so a dropped frame can't stitch two non-adjacent samples ([`data.contiguous_runs`](../edge_ai/data.py)). (The original `actuator` mode omits `fb_seq`.)
42	
43	## 4. Capture protocol
44	
45	A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures **at a single difficulty** across song variety. **v1 targets `hard`** (the shipped corpus is 5 hard songs — hitme/rockroll/slowride/story/talkdirty); Expert is the eventual follow-on (see the journal — hard was picked first for slower scroll + all 5 frets). The corpus is also pinned to a single **timing regime** — `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS=300 / TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS=40` for the current corpus — because the model *is* the photo→command timing function; mixing timing regimes is the same ill-posed averaging as mixing difficulties (see journal decision log). Each capture is exported `--labels=actuator-fb` (in-frame `applied_mask`, no cross-stream join). For deploy, all songs train with `--no-holdout`; for generalisation checks one song is held out and reused across iterations so metrics are comparable.
46	
47	> **Why single-difficulty.** If the game highway's scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay is `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + delay` — inversely dependent on scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one screen row and no difficulty input, mixing difficulties makes identical inputs map to different correct delays: an *ill-posed* regression, not merely an under-sampled one. So v1 fixes a single difficulty. If scroll speed turns out constant across difficulties, difficulties can be merged later at no cost. Eventual multi-difficulty support is one-model-per-difficulty (difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller), or a dedicated fret-line scroll-speed sensor — see journal open questions.
48	
49	## 5. Model
50	
51	For the network itself — layer-by-layer shape, receptive field, and the design rationale — see [model.md](model.md). This section records the training-pipeline choices.
52	
53	### 5.1 The model (as built)
54	
55	- **Input:** 5 ADC channels × `window` causal samples @ 240 Hz, windowed **by row index** (each CSV row is one true 240 Hz sample; the `timestamp` column is bursty — see journal), per-channel standardised then int8 at deploy. The deploy model uses `window=85` (= the receptive field, required by the streaming inference path — see [runtime.md](runtime.md)).
56	- **Output:** 6 sigmoids during training (independent BCE per bit) — 5 frets + 1 collapsed strum; thresholded to binary at deploy. The runtime stage maps the strum bit into the wire byte's bit 5 (strum-down); bit 6 stays 0.
57	- **Architecture (primary):** tiny causal 1D-CNN — **three** dilated causal conv layers, kernel 5, dilations **`(1, 4, 16)`** (receptive field 85, to cover the photo→strum lag — see [model.md §4](model.md)), → linear head on the last timestep → 6 sigmoids. Training default 8 channels; deploy uses **16** (capacity for the sparse strum class — [model.md §8](model.md)). Quantise to int8. This is the primary path (see journal decision log): the strum-timing problem is a sequence/event problem the auto-pipeline's windowed-feature + tree/ensemble shape handles poorly.
58	- **MPLAB ML / SensiML (later demonstration track):** windowed feature extractor (MAV, std, slope, peak, simple FIR taps) feeding a gradient-boosted ensemble or tiny dense head. SensiML targets exactly this MCU class, so once a known-good model shape exists it's a strong "here's the Microchip-tooling path" comparison — but it is **not** the v1 critical path.
59	
60	### 5.2 Sizing the window: receptive field, then the lag
61	
62	The window must be **≥ the receptive field** (85 samples for `(1,4,16)`), and the receptive field must **cover the photo→strum lag** — that's the binding constraint, established by the overfit A/B in [model.md §4](model.md), not by a blind window sweep. The lag itself is a constant at fixed difficulty + timing, measurable with the `edge-ai lag` utility (cross-correlating photo dips against strum events); `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` is only the *fixed* part (the rest is scroll-time from the photo row to marvin's CV row). The deploy window is pinned at 85 (= RF) so the streaming deploy path is bit-exact — see [review.md Q3](review.md#q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast).
63	
64	### 5.3 Quantisation (built — int8, post-training)
65	
66	Per-tensor symmetric **int8 weights, int32 accumulators, int8 activations** (int64 fixed-point requant between layers); int8 output via an integer threshold compare on the head accumulator (no on-device sigmoid). The target M0+ has no FPU, so float inference is a non-starter. PTQ is essentially lossless (frets ±0.001 vs float, strum recall unchanged), so QAT is not needed. Standardisation folds into an integer input affine. Implemented in [`quantize.py`](../edge_ai/quantize.py); host↔device bit-exactness is gated by tests. Full scheme in [model.md §7](model.md) / [runtime.md](runtime.md).
67	
68	## 6. Loss
69	
70	Independent BCE per output bit, weighted to compensate for class imbalance:
71	
72	- Fret bits are dense (often 1 for many ticks per chord); near-1:1 weighting works.
73	- The strum bit is sparse — **~7–13 %** of samples across the hard corpus; weight positively (`--strum-weight`, auto = inverse class frequency ≈ 10–17×) to avoid the trivial "always 0" minimum. The deploy model uses `--strum-weight 5` (below auto) to trim the recall bias at the source, then sets the precision/recall operating point with the strum threshold + monostable at quantise time (header-only, no retrain). Focal loss is a sane alternative if simple weighting plateaus.
74	
75	If per-bit independence produces poor strum timing, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [review.md §alternatives](review.md#12-alternatives-considered).
76
```
</details></tool-use>

73	    for i, (item, (x0, y0, x1, y1)) in enumerate(zip(layout.items, _cell_bounds(layout))):
74	        mark = " <== selected" if i == sel.index else ""
75	        star = " (TRUE)" if truth == item else ""
76	        print(f"  [{i}] {item:<16} dev={sel.scores[i]:>5.2f}  cell=({x0},{y0},{x1},{y1}){mark}{star}")
77	    if truth is not None:
78	        print(f"predicted={sel.item}  true={truth}  {'OK' if sel.item == truth else 'WRONG'}")
79	    return 0

103	def cmd_navigate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
104	    """Plan a practice run and execute it closed-loop against the simulated menu."""
105	    plan = plan_practice_run(args.song, args.difficulty, part=args.part)
106	    print(f"plan: practice-run song #{args.song}, {args.difficulty}, {args.part}")
107	    for i, step in enumerate(plan.steps):
108	        print(f"  {i}. [{step.expected_from}] {step.desc} -> {step.expected_to}")
109	
110	    cfg = SimConfig(part_present=not args.skip_part, sticky=({"difficulty_select": 2} if args.sticky else {}))
111	    game = SimGame("main_menu", cfg)
112	    controller = NavController(SimObserver(game), SimActuator(game))
113	    end = controller.run(plan)
114	    print("\nsim trace:")
115	    for line in controller.trace:
116	        print(f"  {line}")
117	    print(f"\nend: {end.screen}  chosen={game.state.chosen}")
118	    return 0 if end.screen == plan.goal else 1

121	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
122	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
123	        prog="gameplay",
124	        description="GH3 game-state engine prototype: screen classifier.",
125	    )
126	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command")
127	
128	    def add_fp_args(sp: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
129	        d = FingerprintConfig()  # chosen defaults
130	        sp.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=d.cols, help=f"grid columns (default {d.cols})")
131	        sp.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=d.rows, help=f"grid rows (default {d.rows})")
132	        sp.add_argument(
133	            "--samples", type=int, default=d.samples_per_region,
134	            help=f"N x N samples per region (default {d.samples_per_region}); ignored with --dense",
135	        )
136	        sp.add_argument("--dense", action="store_true", help="dense per-region mean (every pixel)")
137	        sp.add_argument(
138	            "--normalize", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=d.normalize,
139	            help="per-frame value normalization (on by default; --no-normalize to disable)",
140	        )
141	
142	    p_classify = sub.add_parser("classify", help="Classify one image against the corpus templates.")
143	    p_classify.add_argument("image", help="path to a PNG/BGR frame")
144	    add_fp_args(p_classify)
145	    p_classify.set_defaults(func=cmd_classify)
146	
147	    p_eval = sub.add_parser("eval", help="Evaluate the classifier against the corpus.")
148	    add_fp_args(p_eval)
149	    p_eval.add_argument("--no-sweep", action="store_true", help="skip the parameter sweep")
150	    p_eval.set_defaults(func=cmd_eval)
151	
152	    p_rows = sub.add_parser("rows", help="Debug the static-list selection reader on one image.")
153	    p_rows.add_argument("image", help="path to a PNG/BGR frame")
154	    p_rows.add_argument("--screen", help="screen id (default: inferred from filename)")
155	    p_rows.set_defaults(func=cmd_rows)
156	
157	    p_export = sub.add_parser("export-c", help="Emit recognizer metadata as a C header for the firmware.")
158	    p_export.add_argument("--out", help="output .h path (default: stdout)")
159	    p_export.set_defaults(func=cmd_export_c)
160	
161	    p_nav = sub.add_parser("navigate", help="Plan + run a practice run against the simulated menu.")
162	    p_nav.add_argument("--song", type=int, default=0, help="song index (default 0)")
163	    p_nav.add_argument("--difficulty", default="hard", help="easy|medium|hard|expert (default hard)")
164	    p_nav.add_argument("--part", default="lead", help="lead|rhythm (default lead)")
165	    p_nav.add_argument("--skip-part", action="store_true", help="simulate a song with no part_select")
166	    p_nav.add_argument("--sticky", action="store_true", help="simulate a sticky (non-zero) difficulty default")
167	    p_nav.set_defaults(func=cmd_navigate)
168	
169	    return p
170	
171	
172	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
173	    parser = build_parser()
174	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
175	    if args.command is None:
176	        args = parser.parse_args(["eval"])
177	    return args.func(args)
178	
179	
180	if __name__ == "__main__":
181	    sys.exit(main())

42	
43	def parse_types_arg(spec: str | None) -> int | None:
44	    """Resolve a `--types` spec to a u32 mask. Returns None if `spec` is None.
45	
46	    Accepts a comma-separated list of RecordType names plus the special tokens
47	    `ALL` (0xFFFFFFFF) and `MIN` (SESSION|DROP). Case-insensitive.
48	    """
49	    if spec is None:
50	        return None
51	    mask = 0
52	    for raw in spec.split(","):
53	        token = raw.strip().upper()
54	        if not token:
55	            continue
56	        if token == "ALL":
57	            return TYPE_MASK_ALL
58	        if token == "MIN":
59	            mask |= TYPE_MASK_MIN
60	            continue
61	        if token not in RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME:
62	            valid = ", ".join(sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME))
63	            raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
64	                f"unknown record type {token!r}; valid: {valid}, ALL, MIN"
65	            )
66	        mask |= 1 << RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME[token]
67	    return mask

72	        f"{name}={int(rt)}" for name, rt in sorted(RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME.items())

76	        f"Names: {bit_lines}. Special: ALL (default), MIN (SESSION+DROP). "
77	        "SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask. Old firmware ignores the command."

90	def cmd_record(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
91	    """Pure pass-through to disk; no decode.

93	    Two modes: `--out FILE.bin` writes a raw legacy file; `--out-dir DIR`
94	    writes a capture directory (DIR/perf.bin + manifest.json finalized on
95	    close).
96	    """
97	    if (args.out is None) == (args.out_dir is None):
98	        print("record: exactly one of --out or --out-dir is required", file=sys.stderr)
99	        return 2
100	
101	    if args.out_dir is not None:
102	        cap_dir = init_capture_dir(args.out_dir, exist_ok=False)
103	        bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME

110	    mask = parse_types_arg(args.types)

113	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser, bin_path.open("wb") as fh:
114	        if mask is not None:

116	        try:
117	            for chunk in ser:
