```text
120	                bytes_written += len(chunk)
121	                now = time.monotonic()
122	                if (now - last_status) >= 1.0:
123	                    print(f"{label}: {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
124	                    last_status = now
125	        except KeyboardInterrupt:
126	            print(f"\nstopped after {bytes_written} B", file=sys.stderr)
127	
128	    if cap_dir is not None:

160	def _idle_chunks(ser: SerialSource, idle_timeout_s: float):
161	    """Yield serial chunks until `idle_timeout_s` elapses with no new bytes.
162	
163	    Lets `iter_frames` terminate once the snapshot burst stops (or stalls),
164	    instead of blocking forever on the infinite SerialSource iterator.
165	    """
166	    deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
167	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
168	        chunk = ser.read_chunk()
169	        if chunk:
170	            deadline = time.monotonic() + idle_timeout_s
171	            yield chunk
172	
173	
174	def _resolve_snapshot_out(out: str | None) -> Path:
175	    """Resolve the `--out` argument to a concrete .png path.
176	
177	    A value ending in `.png` is taken literally. Anything else (including the
178	    default when `--out` is omitted) is treated as a directory, and the next
179	    free `snapshot-NNNN.png` in it is chosen so rapid captures never clobber.
180	    """
181	    p = Path(out) if out else Path("snapshots")
182	    if p.suffix.lower() == ".png":
183	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
184	        return p
185	
186	    p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
187	    nums = [
188	        int(m.group(1))
189	        for f in p.glob("snapshot-*.png")
190	        if (m := re.fullmatch(r"snapshot-(\d+)", f.stem))
191	    ]
192	    nxt = (max(nums) + 1) if nums else 1
193	    return p / f"snapshot-{nxt:04d}.png"

196	def cmd_snapshot(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
197	    """Trigger a full-frame snapshot and save it as a lossless PNG.
198	
199	    Sends PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT, reassembles the returned SNAPSHOT band strips into
200	    one frame, and writes a PNG. With `--out` omitted (or pointed at a
201	    directory) the filename auto-increments as `snapshot-NNNN.png` for quick
202	    repeated captures.
203	    """
204	    out_path = _resolve_snapshot_out(args.out)
205	
206	    assembler = SnapshotAssembler()
207	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
208	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_snapshot_payload()))
209	        print("[snapshot] requested; waiting for bands…", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
210	        snap = None
211	        for fb in iter_frames(_idle_chunks(ser, args.timeout)):
212	            rec = decode_record(fb.payload)
213	            if not isinstance(rec, Strip):
214	                continue
215	            snap = assembler.add(rec)
216	            if snap is not None:
217	                break
218	
219	    if snap is None:
220	        print(
221	            f"snapshot: no complete frame within {args.timeout:.1f}s idle timeout. "
222	            "Is marvin connected, HDMI locked, and the firmware schema current?",
223	            file=sys.stderr,
224	        )
225	        return 1
226	
227	    written = save_snapshot(snap, out_path)
228	    print(
229	        f"snapshot: {snap.width}×{snap.height} (frame_epoch {snap.frame_epoch}) → "
230	        + ", ".join(str(p) for p in written),
231	        file=sys.stderr,
232	    )
233	    return 0
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Program a QSPI NOR region (splash / assets) from the host over JTAG — no SD card.
3	# Stages an init-and-stop at91bootstrap (brings up DDR) + a u-boot SF flasher + the
4	# blob into DDR over JTAG, starts u-boot, then erases + writes + verifies the QSPI
5	# from the DBGU console. macOS/OpenOCD only. See program-qspi.md. Mirrors
6	# program-nand.sh.
7	#
8	# Offsets come from default/src/flash/qspi_layout.h:
9	#   splash -> 0x000000 (4 MiB)   assets -> 0x400000 (~3.98 MiB)   settings 0x7FC000 (off-limits)
10	#
11	# PREREQUISITES (see program-qspi.md):
12	#   * JP4 (QSPI-CS) IN  — the part must be connected for `sf` to reach it. QSPI holds
13	#     no boot image, so RomBOOT skips it (won't boot).
14	#   * JP3 (NAND-CS) OUT and no bootable microSD — so nothing boots marvin and the
15	#     core is caught cold (DDR off). program-qspi.cfg refuses if the core is in DDR.
16	#   * Nothing else holding the FT4232H or the DBGU console node.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   ./program-qspi.sh shell                    # stage u-boot only -> console (test `sf probe 0`)
20	#   ./program-qspi.sh splash [file]            # -> QSPI 0x000000  (default $root/data/ui/splash.raw)
21	#   ./program-qspi.sh assets <file> [offset]   # -> QSPI 0x400000 + offset
22	#   ./program-qspi.sh raw <qspi_off> <file>    # -> QSPI <qspi_off> (escape hatch)
23	#
24	# Env overrides:
25	#   BOOTSTRAP_ELF  init-and-stop at91bootstrap ELF (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf)
26	#   UBOOT_BIN      u-boot raw binary with SF support, links/enters at 0x23f00000.
27	#                  Default is the NAND flasher — its build includes `sf` (confirmed
28	#                  `sf probe` detects the SST26), so it doubles as the QSPI flasher;
29	#                  no separate qspiflash build is needed.
30	#   FTDI_SERIAL    target a specific board by its FT4232H serial
31	#   CONSOLE        DBGU console node (FT4232H channel C); auto-detected if unset
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
35	root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"
36	
37	# QSPI region bases (keep in sync with default/src/flash/qspi_layout.h).
38	QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET=0x000000
39	QSPI_ASSETS_OFFSET=0x400000
40	QSPI_SETTINGS_OFFSET=0x7FC000     # off-limits to this tool
41	QSPI_FLASH_SIZE=0x800000
42	
43	[ $# -ge 1 ] || { sed -n '2,30p' "$0"; exit 1; }
44	region="$1"; shift
45	
46	case "$region" in
47	    shell)  ;;   # stage u-boot only, then drop to the interactive console (sf probe etc.)
48	    splash) QOFF=$QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET; BLOB="${1:-$root/data/ui/splash.raw}" ;;
49	    assets) [ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: ./program-qspi.sh assets <file> [offset]" >&2; exit 1; }
50	            BLOB="$1"; QOFF=$(printf '0x%x' $(( QSPI_ASSETS_OFFSET + ${2:-0} ))) ;;
51	    raw)    [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: ./program-qspi.sh raw <qspi_off> <file>" >&2; exit 1; }
52	            QOFF="$1"; BLOB="$2" ;;
53	    *)      echo "unknown region '$region' (splash|assets|raw)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
54	esac
55	
56	BOOTSTRAP_ELF="${BOOTSTRAP_ELF:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf}"
57	UBOOT_BIN="${UBOOT_BIN:-$root/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin}"
58	FTDI_SERIAL="${FTDI_SERIAL:-}"
59	CONSOLE="${CONSOLE:-$(ls /dev/cu.usbserial-* 2>/dev/null | sort | sed -n '3p')}"
60	
61	STAGE_ADDR=0x21100000             # blob staging in low DDR (matches qspi_console RB headroom)
62	
63	# Shared by all modes: bootstrap + u-boot present, console known, bootstrap entry.
64	for f in "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" "$UBOOT_BIN"; do
65	    [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "missing: $f" >&2; exit 1; }
66	done
67	[ -n "$CONSOLE" ] || { echo "no DBGU console found; set CONSOLE=/dev/cu.usbserial-... (channel C)" >&2; exit 1; }
68	
69	xc32bin="$(ls -d /Applications/microchip/xc32/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
70	READELF="${READELF:-${xc32bin:+$xc32bin/}xc32-readelf}"
71	boot_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"
72	
73	common=(-f "$here/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg" -f "$here/program-qspi.cfg")
74	[ -n "$FTDI_SERIAL" ] && common=(-c "set FTDI_SERIAL $FTDI_SERIAL" "${common[@]}")
75	
76	# `shell`: stage u-boot only (no blob, no programming), then hand over the console
77	# — e.g. to check this u-boot has SF support with `sf probe 0` before committing.
78	if [ "$region" = "shell" ]; then
79	    echo "u-boot (SF flasher)  : $UBOOT_BIN -> 0x23f00000"
80	    echo "console              : $CONSOLE"
81	    openocd "${common[@]}" -c "init" \
82	        -c "stage_uboot_only $BOOTSTRAP_ELF $boot_entry $UBOOT_BIN" \
83	        -c "shutdown"
84	    echo
85	    echo ">>> u-boot is running (JTAG released). Open the console and try 'sf probe 0':"
86	    echo ">>>   screen $CONSOLE 115200        (exit screen: Ctrl-A then k)"
87	    echo ">>> 'SF: Detected sst26...' => this u-boot can program QSPI; use ./program-qspi.sh splash|assets."
88	    echo ">>> no such command / error   => build the qspiflash u-boot (see program-qspi.md)."
89	    exit 0
90	fi
91	
92	[ -f "$BLOB" ] || { echo "missing: $BLOB" >&2; exit 1; }
93	LEN=$(stat -f%z "$BLOB")
94	LEN_HEX=$(printf '0x%x' "$LEN")   # u-boot parses command args as HEX — pass lengths in hex
95	# u-boot's SF driver erases this SST26 in 64 KiB blocks, so the erase length must
96	# be 64 KiB-aligned (4 KiB-aligned gives `sf erase ... ERROR -22`).
97	roundup64k() { printf '0x%x' $(( ( ($1 + 0xffff) / 0x10000 ) * 0x10000 )); }
98	ESZ=$(roundup64k "$LEN")
99	
100	# Bounds + settings-region guard (all arithmetic in (( )), which parses 0x...).
101	# Any write whose end passes the settings base reaches into it (settings runs to
102	# the top of the device), so a single `end > settings` test covers both a write
103	# that spills in and one that starts inside.
104	qoff_d=$(( QOFF )); end_d=$(( qoff_d + ESZ ))
105	if (( end_d > QSPI_FLASH_SIZE )); then
106	    echo "refusing: $(printf '0x%x' $qoff_d) + $ESZ exceeds device size $QSPI_FLASH_SIZE" >&2; exit 1
107	fi
108	if (( end_d > QSPI_SETTINGS_OFFSET )); then
109	    echo "refusing: write [$(printf '0x%x' $qoff_d)..$(printf '0x%x' $end_d)) overlaps the settings region ($QSPI_SETTINGS_OFFSET)." >&2; exit 1
110	fi
111	
112	echo "bootstrap (DDR init) : $BOOTSTRAP_ELF (entry $boot_entry)"
113	echo "u-boot (SF flasher)  : $UBOOT_BIN -> 0x23f00000"
114	echo "blob                 : $BLOB ($LEN bytes) -> DDR $STAGE_ADDR -> QSPI $QOFF (erase $ESZ)"
115	echo "console              : $CONSOLE"
116	
117	# Pre-flight: confirm the DBGU console is free before touching the board.
118	uv run --with pyserial python "$here/qspi_console.py" "$CONSOLE" probe
119	
120	# 1) Stage blob + u-boot into DDR over JTAG and start u-boot (JTAG released).
121	openocd "${common[@]}" -c "init" \
122	    -c "stage_for_qspi $BOOTSTRAP_ELF $boot_entry $UBOOT_BIN $BLOB $STAGE_ADDR" \
123	    -c "shutdown"
124	
125	# 2) Drive sf erase + write + verify from the console (lengths in hex for u-boot).
126	uv run --with pyserial python "$here/qspi_console.py" "$CONSOLE" program \
127	    "$STAGE_ADDR" "$QOFF" "$LEN_HEX" "$ESZ"
128	
129	echo
130	echo ">>> Done. QSPI $region region written + verified."
131
```

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./firmware/marvin/openocd/program-qspi.cfg`

```text
1	# Stage a QSPI blob + u-boot into DDR over JTAG, then start u-boot as an SF
2	# flasher. macOS/OpenOCD only. See program-qspi.md. Mirrors program-nand.cfg.
3	#
4	# QSPI NOR needs no ECC/boot header (unlike NAND/PMECC), so programming is just
5	# `sf probe` -> `sf erase` -> `sf write` -> verify, driven from the u-boot console
6	# after this one JTAG pass. Memory map:
7	#
8	#   <stage_addr>  blob (splash.raw / assets) -> QSPI <offset> via `sf write`
9	#   0x23f00000    u-boot itself (entry) — the flasher; its SF stack drives the
10	#                 SST26 over the QSPI controller
11	#
12	# The blob stages in low DDR (0x211xxxxx), below u-boot's autoboot read window
13	# (0x22000000+) and the relocated u-boot up top, so a brief autoboot can't clobber
14	# it. Mechanism mirrors load-ram.cfg: the init-and-stop at91bootstrap brings up the
15	# 266 MHz clocks + in-package DDR3L, then we load the blob + u-boot and jump.
16	
17	# Bring up clocks + DDR via the init-and-stop at91bootstrap and switch to the fast
18	# transfer clock. Shared by stage_for_qspi and stage_uboot_only.
19	proc qspi_ddr_init {bootstrap_elf boot_entry} {
20	    # reset init resets the SoC from any state and disables the watchdog
21	    # (sam9x75-chybrid.cfg). Adaptive clocking (RTCK) is mandatory while
22	    # at91bootstrap switches the master clock.
23	    reset init
24	
25	    # Guard: this flow stages into low DDR and runs the init-and-stop bootstrap, which
26	    # must be the *only* DDR3L init — both require a cold, non-booting board. Two ways
27	    # the board can already be booting: marvin (caught in DDR, MMU on — the PC tells
28	    # us), or a valid boot-region at91bootstrap looping on a corrupt app (caught in
29	    # SRAM, MMU off, but DDR already up — a PC test can't tell it from the cold ROM
30	    # monitor, so probe DDR). Either way, proceeding would stage into a live DMA region
31	    # and re-init an already-trained MPDDRC (mistrains it → reads shift a halfword →
32	    # u-boot never runs). Bail — pull JP3 (NAND) + remove any SD so the core is caught
33	    # cold (QSPI holds no boot image, so JP4/QSPI may stay IN, which `sf` requires).
34	    set _pc_out [capture {reg pc}]
35	    regexp {0x[0-9a-fA-F]+} $_pc_out _pc
36	    set _booting 0
37	    if {$_pc >= 0x20000000 && $_pc < 0x30000000} {
38	        set _booting 1
39	    } else {
40	        catch {
41	            write_memory 0x23f00000 32 {0xdeadbeef 0x12345678}
42	            set _rb [read_memory 0x23f00000 32 2]
43	            if {[lindex $_rb 0] == 0xdeadbeef && [lindex $_rb 1] == 0x12345678} { set _booting 1 }
44	        }
45	    }
46	    if {$_booting} {
47	        error "program-qspi: board is already booting from a medium (marvin or a looping partial bootstrap). Pull JP3 (NAND) + remove any SD so the core is caught cold (DDR off), then re-run."
48	    }
49	
50	    adapter speed 0
51	    reg cpsr 0x000000d3
52	
53	    # Run the bootstrap to completion (crt0 BKPT_NOTIFY_DONE) — clocks + DDR up.
54	    load_image $bootstrap_elf
55	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
56	    resume $boot_entry
57	    wait_halt 6000
58	    echo ">>> at91bootstrap init complete: clocks + DDR3L up, MMU/caches off"
59	
60	    # Clocks stable -> fast fixed TCK + DCC for the bulk transfer.
61	    adapter speed 6000
62	    arm7_9 dcc_downloads enable
63	}
64	
65	# Full flow: stage the blob + u-boot, then start u-boot to program QSPI.
66	proc stage_for_qspi {bootstrap_elf boot_entry uboot_bin blob_bin stage_addr} {
67	    qspi_ddr_init $bootstrap_elf $boot_entry
68	
69	    echo ">>> staging blob       -> DDR $stage_addr"
70	    load_image $blob_bin $stage_addr bin
71	    echo ">>> loading u-boot     -> DDR 0x23f00000"
72	    load_image $uboot_bin 0x23f00000 bin
73	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
74	
75	    echo ">>> starting u-boot — JTAG done; program QSPI from the console"
76	    resume 0x23f00000
77	}
78	
79	# u-boot only (no blob): bring up DDR, load + start u-boot, release JTAG. Use the
80	# DBGU console interactively afterwards — e.g. `sf probe 0` to check this u-boot
81	# has SF support before committing to the full flow.
82	proc stage_uboot_only {bootstrap_elf boot_entry uboot_bin} {
83	    qspi_ddr_init $bootstrap_elf $boot_entry
84	
85	    echo ">>> loading u-boot     -> DDR 0x23f00000"
86	    load_image $uboot_bin 0x23f00000 bin
87	    arm mcr 15 0 7 5 0 0
88	
89	    echo ">>> starting u-boot — JTAG done; open the DBGU console and use it (sf probe 0)"
90	    resume 0x23f00000
91	}
92
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Drive the marvin u-boot console over the DBGU serial port for QSPI (SF) ops.
3	
4	Used by program-qspi.sh. Run via uv so pyserial is present:
5	    uv run --with pyserial python qspi_console.py <port> <op> [args...]
6	
7	Ops:
8	    probe                          open the port exclusively and exit (pre-flight)
9	    program <sa> <off> <len> <esz> sf-probe, erase <off>..<esz> (4 KiB-rounded),
10	                                   write <len> bytes from DDR <sa> to QSPI <off>,
11	                                   then verify by reading back to scratch DDR and
12	                                   cmp.b against the staged copy
13	
14	Mirrors nand_console.py: every op first waits for a STABLE U-Boot prompt (so the
15	"Hit any key to stop autoboot" countdown can't eat commands), and each sf command
16	is retried once if its expected keyword is missing. Exit status is 0 only on
17	confirmed success.
18	"""
19	import sys, time
20	
21	try:
22	    import serial
23	except ImportError:
24	    sys.exit("qspi_console: pyserial missing — run via: uv run --with pyserial python ...")
25	
26	BAUD = 115200
27	# Read-back scratch in low DDR, clear of the staged blob (0x21100000 + <=4 MiB)
28	# and below u-boot's autoboot window (0x22000000+).
29	RB = "0x21600000"
30	
31	
32	def open_port(port):
33	    try:
34	        return serial.Serial(port, BAUD, timeout=0.3, exclusive=True)
35	    except Exception as e:
36	        sys.exit(f"qspi_console: cannot open console {port}: {e}\n"
37	                 f"  In use elsewhere (screen/minicom)? Close it, or set CONSOLE=<node>.")
38	
39	
40	def wait_prompt(ser, timeout=12):
41	    end = time.time() + timeout
42	    while time.time() < end:
43	        ser.write(b"\r\n"); time.sleep(0.4)
44	        buf = ser.read(8192)
45	        if buf.rstrip().endswith(b"U-Boot>"):
46	            time.sleep(0.3)
47	            if not ser.read(8192):          # quiet -> prompt settled (autoboot stopped)
48	                return True
49	    return False
50	
51	
52	def cmd(ser, c, t=300):
53	    # u-boot's sf erase/write emit nothing until they finish (seconds to tens of
54	    # seconds for a multi-MB write), so print a heartbeat dot every ~2 s of silence
55	    # — otherwise a long op looks hung.
56	    ser.reset_input_buffer(); ser.write(c.encode() + b"\r\n")
57	    print(f"\n=== $ {c} ===", flush=True)
58	    end = time.time() + t; buf = b""; beat = time.time(); dotted = False
59	    while time.time() < end:
60	        d = ser.read(4096)
61	        if d:
62	            buf += d
63	            if buf.rstrip().endswith(b"U-Boot>"): break
64	        elif time.time() - beat >= 2.0:
65	            sys.stdout.write("."); sys.stdout.flush(); beat = time.time(); dotted = True
66	    txt = buf.decode("utf-8", "replace")
67	    print(("\n" if dotted else "") + txt)
68	    return txt
69	
70	
71	def run(ser, c, expect, t=300):
72	    out = cmd(ser, c, t)
73	    if expect not in out:                   # raced the prompt — resync and retry once
74	        print(f">>> '{c}' missing '{expect}'; resyncing prompt and retrying")
75	        wait_prompt(ser); out = cmd(ser, c, t)
76	    return out
77	
78	
79	def main():
80	    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
81	        sys.exit("usage: qspi_console.py <port> <probe|program> [args...]")
82	    port, op = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
83	    ser = open_port(port)
84	
85	    if op == "probe":
86	        ser.close(); print(f"qspi_console: {port} available"); return 0
87	
88	    print(">>> connecting to u-boot console (booting + stopping autoboot)...", flush=True)
89	    if not wait_prompt(ser):
90	        sys.exit(f"qspi_console: no stable U-Boot prompt on {port} (is u-boot running?)")
91	
92	    if op == "program":
93	        # Lengths/offsets are passed in hex — u-boot parses command args as hex.
94	        sa, off, length, esz = sys.argv[3:7]
95	
96	        # `sf probe` must succeed or nothing else will; bail clearly if the SF
97	        # stack isn't in this u-boot build (then build the qspiflash defconfig).
98	        if "Detected" not in run(ser, "sf probe 0", "Detected"):
99	            ser.close()
100	            sys.exit("qspi_console: `sf probe` failed — no SF support / no flash detected.")
101	
102	        # Match the ': OK' suffix — `Erased`/`Written` also appear in the error
103	        # lines ('Erased: ERROR -22'), so the bare verb is not enough.
104	        if "Erased: OK" not in run(ser, f"sf erase {off} {esz}", "Erased: OK"):
105	            ser.close()
106	            sys.exit(f"qspi_console: sf erase {off} {esz} FAILED "
107	                     f"(erase length must be 64 KiB-aligned for this part). See output.")
108	        if "Written: OK" not in run(ser, f"sf write {sa} {off} {length}", "Written: OK"):
109	            ser.close()
110	            sys.exit(f"qspi_console: sf write {off} {length} FAILED. See output.")
111	
112	        cmd(ser, f"sf read {RB} {off} {length}")
113	        v = cmd(ser, f"cmp.b {sa} {RB} {length}")
114	        ser.close()
115	        # cmp.b prints 'Total of 0 byte(s) were the same' AND a 'byte at X != Y'
116	        # line on mismatch, so require the match phrase and the absence of '!='.
117	        ok = ("were the same" in v) and ("!=" not in v)
118	        print("\n>>> QSPI programmed and verified." if ok
119	              else "\n>>> WARNING: verify FAILED — check output above.")
120	        return 0 if ok else 1
121	
122	    ser.close()
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Prepare a bootable microSD for marvin on macOS (SAM9X75 ROM SD-card boot).
3	#
4	# With the board's boot jumpers set for SD, the SAM9X75 BootROM looks for
5	# "boot.bin" in the FAT root and loads it (at91bootstrap, the SD bootstrap), which
6	# in turn loads its configured second stage. Our SD bootstrap is built with
7	# CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME="harmony.bin" (the Harmony MPU convention), so it loads marvin
8	# from "harmony.bin". This formats the card FAT and writes both files. The result
9	# boots standalone — no JTAG.
10	#
11	# macOS only. THIS ERASES THE TARGET DISK.
12	#
13	# Usage:   ./make-sdcard.sh /dev/diskN        (find it with: diskutil list)
14	# Env overrides:
15	#   BOOT_BIN   SD bootstrap (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin)
16	#   APP_BIN    marvin app image (default: ../out/harmony.bin)
17	#   APP_NAME   second-stage filename on the card (default: harmony.bin)
18	#   VOL_NAME   FAT volume label (default: MARVIN)
19	set -euo pipefail
20	
21	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
22	root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"
23	
24	BOOT_BIN="${BOOT_BIN:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin}"
25	APP_BIN="${APP_BIN:-$root/out/harmony.bin}"
26	APP_NAME="${APP_NAME:-harmony.bin}"
27	VOL_NAME="${VOL_NAME:-MARVIN}"
28	
29	disk="${1:-}"
30	[ -n "$disk" ] || { echo "usage: $0 /dev/diskN   (see 'diskutil list')" >&2; exit 1; }
31	[ -f "$BOOT_BIN" ] || { echo "missing SD bootstrap: $BOOT_BIN" >&2; exit 1; }
32	[ -f "$APP_BIN" ]  || { echo "missing app image: $APP_BIN (build marvin first)" >&2; exit 1; }
33	
34	disk="/dev/$(basename "$disk")"   # normalize "disk4" -> "/dev/disk4"
35	
36	info="$(diskutil info "$disk" 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "not a disk: $disk" >&2; exit 1; }
37	
38	# Safety net: refuse a fixed internal disk (the system drive). A built-in SD
39	# slot reports Internal:Yes but Removable Media:Removable — that is allowed.
40	if grep -qE 'Internal:[[:space:]]+Yes' <<<"$info" \
41	   && ! grep -qE 'Removable Media:[[:space:]]+Removable' <<<"$info"; then
42	  echo "REFUSING: $disk looks like a fixed internal disk." >&2
43	  exit 1
44	fi
45	
46	echo "Target: $disk"
47	grep -E 'Device / Media Name|Disk Size|Removable Media|Internal:' <<<"$info" || true
48	echo
49	echo "This will ERASE ALL DATA on $disk and write:"
50	echo "  boot.bin    <- $BOOT_BIN"
51	echo "  $APP_NAME   <- $APP_BIN"
52	echo
53	read -r -p "Type the disk identifier ($(basename "$disk")) to confirm: " ans
54	[ "$ans" = "$(basename "$disk")" ] || { echo "aborted." >&2; exit 1; }
55	
56	echo ">>> formatting $disk as FAT (MBR), label $VOL_NAME ..."
57	diskutil eraseDisk MS-DOS "$VOL_NAME" MBRFormat "$disk"
58	
59	mnt="/Volumes/$VOL_NAME"
60	[ -d "$mnt" ] || { echo "expected mount at $mnt not found" >&2; exit 1; }
61	
62	echo ">>> copying boot.bin + $APP_NAME to $mnt ..."
63	cp "$BOOT_BIN" "$mnt/boot.bin"
64	cp "$APP_BIN"  "$mnt/$APP_NAME"
65	sync
66	
67	echo ">>> ejecting ..."
68	diskutil eject "$disk"
69	echo "done. Set the board boot jumpers for SD, insert the card, and power-cycle."
70
```

```text
1	# review
2	
3	This is the document to push back on. Three categories: things we know can fail (risks), forks we haven't decided (open questions), and shapes we explicitly rejected (alternatives).
4	
5	> Several phase-2 risks below are now **resolved** by the as-built model — marked inline. The remaining live risks are inherited-teacher bugs and the cross-stream label skew (the latter mostly closed by the atomic `actuator-fb` schema).
6	
7	## Risks
8	
9	- **Strum class imbalance (managed).** The collapsed strum bit is sparse (~7–13% on hard). Weighted BCE (`--strum-weight`) + a strum threshold + the monostable post-processor keep it off the "always 0" minimum; the *binding* constraint turned out to be model **capacity** on this class, fixed by deploying 16 channels (see [model.md §8](model.md)).
10	- **~~Window-too-short failure mode~~ (resolved → receptive field).** Reframed: the limiter wasn't the *window* but the *receptive field*. RF 21 `(1,4)` couldn't reach the ~48-sample lag (frets capped ~0.86); RF 85 `(1,4,16)` covers it (frets ~0.99). Window only needs to be ≥ RF. See [model.md §4](model.md).
11	- **Per-bit independence vs. chord structure (not hit).** Treating bits as independent sigmoids ignores that real chords occupy a tiny subset of the 2⁶ space. Hasn't capped accuracy so far; if it does, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [§alternatives](#12-alternatives-considered).
12	- **Multi-difficulty is ill-posed, not just out-of-distribution (resolved → single-difficulty v1).** Original guidance here was "train on Easy + Medium + Expert." That is wrong if scroll speed varies with difficulty: the photo→strum lag = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms`, so the same photo-dip pattern maps to *different* correct delays across difficulties. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, the model can't disambiguate — mixing difficulties is an ill-posed regression more data can't fix. **Resolution:** v1 trains on a single difficulty (**hard** for v1; see journal decision log + [training.md §4](training.md)). Per-difficulty models, or a fret-line scroll-speed sensor ([Q5](#q5-photoxistor-placement)), are the multi-difficulty routes for later.
13	- **Inheriting marvin's bugs.** Distillation can't beat the teacher. Mistimed strums in marvin become mistimed strums in the AI. Acceptable for v1; future work could layer human-play recordings on top (see [Q4](#q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source)).
14	- **CDC + RTOS jitter in labels, and a cross-stream pairing skew.** `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` timestamps the moment marvin *emits* the command, not the moment fretboard asserts the GPIO. Sharper still: the label is stamped on the **send** path and the feature (`FRETBOARD_RAW`) on the **receive** path — opposite USB-CDC directions with independent latency/jitter — so the exporter's forward-fill pairs them with an unknown, varying skew. Probably fine for v1 (fretboard saw that same jitter at runtime), but it's a candidate accuracy ceiling. The clean fix is to pair sensor + applied-actuator-state atomically on the fretboard and carry both on the wire (fretboard journal open-questions #3/#4; edge-ai journal). Measure the impact in phase 2 before committing to the firmware change.
15	
16	## Open questions
17	
18	> Reviewers: each of these is a real fork. Speak up *before* phase 1 lands.
19	
20	<a id="q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret"></a>
21	### Q1: Hold vs. edge channel per fret — add HW now, or wait?
22	
23	The current 5-channel ADC at 240 Hz may alias on fast transients. Two ways to add information:
24	
25	- **(a)** Two photoxistors per fret at *different* screen rows — gives the model an intrinsic "note approaching" + "note here" pair, doubling temporal resolution at hardware cost.
26	- **(b)** One extra photoxistor per fret with a colour filter, mimicking `cv_marvin_v1`'s colour-edge channel — separates "any brightness here" from "specifically a green note here".
27	
28	Either doubles the ADC scan time. Bias is to start with the existing 5 channels and only add HW if phase 2 shows the model is starved for input.
29	
30	<a id="q2-ar-feedback"></a>
31	### Q2: AR feedback — let the model see its own past output?
32	
33	Most fret-bit predictions at time `T` are highly correlated with the prediction at `T-1` (held notes). An AR model could be much smaller / more accurate. Cost: a feedback loop at runtime (bugs amplify), and harder training (teacher forcing vs. scheduled sampling). Defer until non-AR baseline is known.
34	
35	<a id="q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast"></a>
36	### Q3: Window length — measure first, then sweep narrowly
37	
38	Window length is the most important hyperparameter, but with difficulty fixed it need not be a blind sweep. The photo→strum lag is a constant we can **measure** by cross-correlating photo dips against strum events on real data (the `edge-ai lag` utility); size the causal window to span the measured lag + margin, then sweep ±1–2 samples around it. (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220` is only the fixed part — the full lag includes scroll-time from the photo row to marvin's CV row.)
39	
40	**Look-ahead vs. now-cast.** Currently formulated as "predict the command at *now*". Could instead predict at `T + K_ms` to cover model+actuator latency. Irrelevant while actuators are GPIOs (latency ≈ 0); revisit when mechanical actuators land (system [SPEC.md §5](../../../SPEC.md), [hardware/actuators/](../../../hardware/actuators/)).
41	
42	<a id="q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source"></a>
43	### Q4: Strike-line CV detector as alternative label source?
44	
45	If phase 2 reveals that distillation hits a noise ceiling (CDC jitter + chord-window quantisation), an alternative is to add a `cv_strike_v1` detector on marvin that samples the *strike row* directly at 60 Hz. Cleaner labels for fret state, but loses strum-event timing — would need to re-add a rule-based "strum when strike row goes active". Flag for now, don't build.
46	
47	<a id="q5-photoxistor-placement"></a>
48	### Q5: Phototransistor placement / count — what's optimal?
49	
50	Today's PCB ([hardware/Sensor-LCD5/](../../../hardware/Sensor-LCD5/)) has 5 sensors above the strike line. Optimum-for-this-AI is unknown:
51	
52	- *Higher* on the screen → longer lookahead but more time for the note appearance to change.
53	- *At the strike line* → simplest label (the photo dip *is* the answer) but no anticipation, breaking strum scheduling.
54	- *Two rows* → see [Q1](#q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret).
55	- *A dedicated fret-line / scroll-speed channel* → a 6th sensor aimed at a column where only the highway's horizontal bar/measure lines pass (not the colored notes). The frequency at which lines cross it **is** the scroll speed — the exact variable single-row note sensors can't observe (see the multi-difficulty risk above). Could let one model span difficulties instead of one-per-difficulty. Open whether a tiny int8 model can actually use it to modulate strum timing. v1 stays 5-channel single-difficulty; flagged for future work.
56	
57	Open until phase 2 data tells us which placement makes the model's job easiest.
58	
59	## 12. Alternatives considered
60	
61	Three other shapes were on the table before the current distillation choice landed:
62	
63	- **Shape A — frame classifier with co-located CV.** Model predicts `pressed_mask` from a single ADC sample; labels come from a *new* CV detector at the photoxistor row. Pros: small model, easy to label. Rejected because it still leaves the strum decision outside the AI, and forces mechanical alignment between CV and photoxistors — exactly the problem we're trying to dissolve.
64	- **Shape B — sequence-to-strike-line oracle.** Model takes a causal ADC window, outputs what's at the strike row right now. Labels come from a new strike-row CV detector. Pros: clean physical meaning ("predict the moment of truth"). Rejected because, like A, it doesn't include strum timing — a downstream rule still has to schedule strums. We'd be solving the easier half of the problem twice.
65	- **Shape D — two-head (continuous fret + sparse strum events).** One head for held-note state, one head for `[time-to-strum, mask, dir]` events. Closer to the underlying physics. Rejected as v1 because it's significantly more complex to architect, train, and validate. **Worth revisiting if the per-bit-independence loss in the current shape produces poor strum timing in phase 2** — D's sparse-event head is a natural cure.
66
```

```text
1	"""Measure the photo-dip → strum lag from real data (stdlib only).
2	
3	With difficulty fixed, the delay from a note dipping a phototransistor to
4	marvin issuing the strum is a constant. We recover it by cross-correlating a
5	"photo darkness" signal against the strum rising-edge impulses: for each
6	candidate lag L, score how strongly a dip L samples *before* a strum predicts
7	that strum. The peak L is the dominant lag; it sizes the causal window.
8	
9	This is a diagnostic, not training — kept dependency-free so it runs anywhere.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	from dataclasses import dataclass
15	
16	from . import SAMPLE_RATE_HZ
17	from .data import Capture
18	
19	
20	@dataclass(frozen=True)
21	class LagResult:
22	    best_lag_samples: int
23	    best_lag_ms: float
24	    centroid_ms: float
25	    n_strum_events: int
26	    curve: list[tuple[int, float]]  # (lag_samples, normalised_score)
27	
28	    def summary(self) -> str:
29	        return (
30	            f"peak lag {self.best_lag_samples} samples "
31	            f"({self.best_lag_ms:.1f} ms), centroid {self.centroid_ms:.1f} ms, "
32	            f"over {self.n_strum_events} strum events"
33	        )
34	
35	
36	def _darkness(cap: Capture) -> list[float]:
37	    """Per-row aggregate dip magnitude: sum over channels of (bright - adc).
38	
39	    `bright` is a per-channel high baseline (max over the capture, i.e. the
40	    idle/unlit level since lower ADC = brighter sensor = note present). Clipped
41	    at 0 so only dips contribute. Zero-mean so the cross-correlation isn't
42	    dominated by a DC term.
43	    """
44	    n = len(cap)
45	    if n == 0:
46	        return []
47	    n_ch = len(cap.adc[0])
48	    bright = [max(cap.adc[i][c] for i in range(n)) for c in range(n_ch)]
49	    d = [0.0] * n
50	    for i in range(n):
51	        acc = 0.0
52	        row = cap.adc[i]
53	        for c in range(n_ch):
54	            v = bright[c] - row[c]
55	            if v > 0:
56	                acc += v
57	        d[i] = acc
58	    mean = sum(d) / n
59	    return [v - mean for v in d]
60	
61	
62	def _strum_rising_edges(cap: Capture) -> list[int]:
63	    edges = []
64	    prev = 0
65	    for i, row in enumerate(cap.labels):
66	        s = row[5]
67	        if s and not prev:
68	            edges.append(i)
69	        prev = s
70	    return edges
71	
72	
73	def measure_lag(cap: Capture, *, max_lag_ms: float = 600.0) -> LagResult:
74	    """Cross-correlate dip signal vs strum rising edges over lags [0, max]."""
75	    d = _darkness(cap)
76	    edges = _strum_rising_edges(cap)
77	    max_lag = int(round(max_lag_ms / 1000.0 * SAMPLE_RATE_HZ))
78	    if not edges or max_lag < 1:
79	        return LagResult(0, 0.0, 0.0, len(edges), [])
80	
81	    curve: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
82	    for L in range(0, max_lag + 1):
83	        acc = 0.0
84	        cnt = 0
85	        for e in edges:
86	            j = e - L
87	            if j >= 0:
88	                acc += d[j]
89	                cnt += 1
90	        curve.append((L, acc / cnt if cnt else 0.0))
91	
92	    scores = [s for _, s in curve]
93	    lo = min(scores)
94	    shifted = [s - lo for s in scores]  # >= 0 for centroid weighting
95	    best_idx = max(range(len(curve)), key=lambda k: curve[k][1])
96	    best_lag = curve[best_idx][0]
97	
98	    wsum = sum(shifted)
99	    centroid_samples = (
100	        sum(L * w for (L, _), w in zip(curve, shifted)) / wsum if wsum else 0.0
101	    )
102	
103	    return LagResult(
104	        best_lag_samples=best_lag,
105	        best_lag_ms=best_lag / SAMPLE_RATE_HZ * 1000.0,
106	        centroid_ms=centroid_samples / SAMPLE_RATE_HZ * 1000.0,
107	        n_strum_events=len(edges),
108	        curve=curve,
109	    )
110
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Prepend the SAM9X7 ROM-code NAND boot header to an at91bootstrap binary, so the
3	# boot region can be written by a plain `nand write` (the u-boot/JTAG path in
4	# ../openocd/program-nand.md) instead of SAM-BA's `writeboot` (which synthesizes
5	# the header itself).
6	#
7	# The ROM reads page 0 without ECC, expecting 52 copies of a 32-bit word encoding
8	# the NAND/PMECC params, with the bootstrap code at offset 0xD0 (SAM9X7 Data Sheet
9	# DS60001813D, "NAND Flash Specific Header Detection"). The word MUST match the
10	# actual chip (u-boot `nand info`), NOT at91bootstrap addpmecchead.py's SAM9X7
11	# defaults (2048/64/4) — this board's NAND is 4096/256/8-bit/512 -> 0xc2605007.
12	#
13	# The header word + offset math is inlined here (mirrors at91bootstrap
14	# scripts/pmecc_head.py) so this is self-contained — no external tree needed.
15	#
16	# Usage: ./make-pmecchead.sh [in.bin] [out.bin] [page oob eccbits sector]
17	set -euo pipefail
18	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
19	IN="${1:-$here/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin}"
20	OUT="${2:-$here/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin}"
21	PAGE="${3:-4096}"; OOB="${4:-256}"; ECC="${5:-8}"; SECTOR="${6:-512}"
22	
23	python3 - "$IN" "$OUT" "$PAGE" "$OOB" "$ECC" "$SECTOR" <<'PY'
24	import sys, struct
25	inp, out, page, oob, ecc, sector = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], *map(int, sys.argv[3:7])
26	
27	# ecc bytes per sector for BCH: m = 12 + sector/512 (Galois field degree)
28	ecc_bytes = ((12 + sector // 512) * ecc + 7) // 8
29	nb_sectors = page // sector
30	ecc_offset = oob - nb_sectors * ecc_bytes
31	
32	# bitfield codes (pmecc_head.json): index into the "meaning" maps
33	sectors_code = {1: 0, 2: 1, 4: 2, 8: 3}[nb_sectors]
34	ecc_code     = {2: 0, 4: 1, 8: 2, 12: 3, 24: 4}[ecc]
35	sector_code  = {512: 0, 1024: 1}[sector]
36	
37	word = (
38	    (1            << 0)   |  # usePmecc
39	    (sectors_code << 1)   |  # nbSectorPerPage  (bits 1-3)
40	    (oob          << 4)   |  # spareSize        (bits 4-12)
41	    (ecc_code     << 13)  |  # eccBitReq        (bits 13-15)
42	    (sector_code  << 16)  |  # sectorSize       (bits 16-17)
43	    (ecc_offset   << 18)  |  # eccOffset        (bits 18-26)
44	    (0xc          << 28)     # key = valid      (bits 28-31)
45	)
46	
47	hdr = struct.pack("<I", word) * 52   # 208 bytes (0xd0); code follows at 0xd0
48	data = open(inp, "rb").read()
49	open(out, "wb").write(hdr + data)
50	print("PMECC header word 0x%08x (page=%d oob=%d ecc=%d sector=%d, eccOffset=%d); "
51	      "code at 0x%x; wrote %s (%d bytes)"
52	      % (word, page, oob, ecc, sector, ecc_offset, len(hdr), out, len(hdr) + len(data)))
```

```text
1	# FT4232H EEPROM image for the SAM9X75 cHybrid REV1 (U8 FT4232H + U9 93LC46B).
2	#
3	# Channel A is hardwired to the onboard JTAG (MPSSE) bus, so it is set D2XX-only
4	# (cha_vcp=false): it should NOT enumerate as a serial port, leaving it cleanly
5	# available to OpenOCD/libusb. Channel C is the DBGU console (populated via
6	# R149/R151, sch sheet 14) and stays VCP. Channels B and D are unconnected on
7	# this design (B's resistors are DNP), so they are also D2XX to suppress their
8	# phantom serial ports. Net result: a single /dev/cu node, the DBGU on channel C.
9	
10	vendor_id=0x0403
11	product_id=0x6011
12	
13	manufacturer="Microchip"
14	product="SAM9X75 cHybrid"
15	use_serial=true
16	serial="W16-2026-359"
17	
18	self_powered=false
19	max_power=500
20	
21	# Driver per channel: false = D2XX (no /dev/cu node), true = VCP (serial port).
22	cha_vcp=false
23	chb_vcp=false
24	chc_vcp=true
25	chd_vcp=false
26	
27	# A/B are MPSSE-capable; keep plain UART signaling. MPSSE/JTAG is engaged by the
28	# host at runtime regardless of this field.
29	cha_type=UART
30	chb_type=UART
31	
32	filename="ft4232h-chybrid-rev1.bin"
33
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Flash the FT4232H EEPROM on the connected SAM9X75 cHybrid with a per-board serial.
3	# Run with the target board (and only that board, to be safe) connected via USB.
4	#
5	#   ./flash-eeprom.sh W16-2026-360
6	#
7	# Uses ft4232h-chybrid.conf as the base image and overrides only the serial.
8	# Must run outside the Claude command sandbox (it blocks USB).
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	serial="${1:?usage: flash-eeprom.sh <SERIAL>}"
12	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
13	base="$here/ft4232h-chybrid.conf"
14	
15	tmp="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ft4232h.XXXXXX")"
16	conf="$tmp.conf"
17	bin="$tmp.bin"
18	trap 'rm -f "$tmp" "$conf" "$bin"' EXIT
19	
20	sed -e "s/^serial=.*/serial=\"$serial\"/" \
21	    -e "s|^filename=.*|filename=\"$bin\"|" "$base" > "$conf"
22	
23	ftdi_eeprom --device i:0x0403:0x6011 --flash-eeprom "$conf"
24	echo "Flashed serial: $serial — unplug/replug the board to re-enumerate."
25
```

```text
352	
353	    `adc` is a 5-tuple of 12-bit unsigned ADC samples (0–4095, lower means
354	    a brighter sensor) ordered by `fret_t`: green, red, yellow, blue, orange.
355	
356	    `fb_sample_seq` and `applied_mask` are stamped by the fretboard itself
357	    and carried on the wire (schema v4+): the sequence counter (one per
358	    fretboard tick, monotonic) reconstructs true sample order and exposes
359	    frames dropped in transit, and `applied_mask` is the 7-bit actuator
360	    bitmask the fretboard was driving during this scan — sensor and actuator
361	    paired atomically at the source, not joined across marvin's TX/RX clocks.
362	
363	    At ~240 Hz fretboard rate against 60 Hz video, the same `frame_epoch`
364	    tags ~4 consecutive records — `fb_sample_seq` (or `hdr.ts_counter`)
365	    gives sub-frame ordering.
366	    """
367	
368	    hdr: Header
369	    adc: tuple[int, ...]   # length FRET_COUNT, indexed by fret_t
370	    fb_sample_seq: int
371	    applied_mask: int
372	
373	    # 5×u16 adc + u32 seq + u8 applied_mask + u8 reserved
374	    _BODY: ClassVar[struct.Struct] = struct.Struct("<5H I B B")
375	    SIZE: ClassVar[int] = HDR_SIZE + _BODY.size  # 16 + 16 = 32
376	
377	
378	@dataclass(frozen=True)
379	class UnknownRecord:
380	    hdr: Header
381	    raw: bytes
382	
383	
384	# Largest record bytes — used by framing.py to bound LEN sanity check.
385	MAX_RECORD_BYTES = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + STRIP_MAX_BYTES  # 65028
386	
387	
388	# ─── Host→device commands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
389	
390	# Bit n of the type-mask is RecordType value n. Bit 0 is unused.
391	RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME: dict[str, int] = {rt.name: int(rt) for rt in RecordType}
392	
393	# Common preset masks used by the CLI.
394	TYPE_MASK_ALL = 0xFFFFFFFF
395	TYPE_MASK_MIN = (1 << RecordType.SESSION) | (1 << RecordType.DROP)
396	
397	
398	_CMD_SET_MASK_FMT = struct.Struct("<HBBI")  # magic, cmd_id, reserved, mask
399	
400	
401	def encode_set_mask_payload(mask: int) -> bytes:
402	    """Pack a SET_TYPE_MASK command payload (no SOF/LEN/FCS framing)."""
403	    return _CMD_SET_MASK_FMT.pack(
404	        PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC, PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK, 0, mask & 0xFFFFFFFF
405	    )
406	
407	
408	_CMD_HDR_FMT = struct.Struct("<HBB")  # magic, cmd_id, reserved
409	
410	
411	def encode_snapshot_payload() -> bytes:
412	    """Pack a SNAPSHOT command payload (header-only; no SOF/LEN/FCS framing)."""
413	    return _CMD_HDR_FMT.pack(PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC, PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT, 0)
414	
415	
416	_CMD_SET_OVERLAY_FMT = struct.Struct("<HBBI")  # magic, cmd_id, reserved, flags
417	
418	
419	def encode_set_overlay_payload(flags: int) -> bytes:
420	    """Pack a SET_OVERLAY command payload (no SOF/LEN/FCS framing)."""
421	    return _CMD_SET_OVERLAY_FMT.pack(
422	        PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC, PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY, 0, flags & 0xFFFFFFFF
423	    )
424
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Process GH3 cover art directly into marvin's game-data tree.
3	
4	Reads original JPG covers from ./data/ (named <setlist>_<idx>_<slug>.jpg) and
5	writes the two firmware asset tiers straight into the marvin art folder, named
6	by the recognizer key the firmware expects (<setlist>-<NN>):
7	
8	- large: 508x208 middle strip for the song-select detail screen, with a baked
9	  overlay matching the on-screen album-art card: the difficulty tier's dark tint
10	  (Tailwind <hue>-900 at 40%) washes the zinc-900 card behind the cover, the
11	  cover is dimmed to 60%, and a black gradient darkens the bottom edge so the
12	  title/artist text sits on a legible backdrop. Saved as PNG so the overlay is
13	  lossless. The tint is looked up per song from songs.csv: main tiers "1".."8"
14	  map to an 8-tier Tailwind palette (see TIER_PALETTE), bonus (or unknown) maps
15	  to a neutral gray.
16	  -> <out>/large/<setlist>-<NN>.png
17	- small: 144x144 dashboard now-playing thumbnail (pillarboxed, clean, no fade).
18	  Saved as PNG: on-device the covers are decoded offscreen into a static DDR
19	  cache, and Legato's JPEG decoder gates its block writes on the (stale, at boot)
20	  renderer clip rect — so a runtime JPEG decode lands as noise. The PNG decoder
21	  does a plain color-converting buffer copy with no clip dependency, so both tiers
22	  use PNG on the card.
23	  -> <out>/small/<setlist>-<NN>.png
24	
25	This is a one-step process+install: <out> defaults to the marvin art tree, so
26	there is no separate install step. Existing cover files in each tier are cleared
27	first, so a re-run leaves no stale files (e.g. old .jpg larges).
28	
29	Usage:
30	    cd tools/gh3-cover-art
31	    uv run process_gh3_cover_art.py
32	    uv run process_gh3_cover_art.py --source ./data --out /path/to/art

47	LARGE_W = 508
48	LARGE_H = 208
49	SMALL_SIZE = 144

91	        return table
92	    with p.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:

96	            except (KeyError, ValueError):
97	                continue
98	            table[key] = (row.get("difficulty") or "").strip()
99	    return table

102	def tier_tint(diff_str):
103	    """Map a difficulty string to its baked art tint: "1".."8" -> TIER_PALETTE
104	    tint, anything else (e.g. "bonus", empty) -> neutral gray."""
105	    try:
106	        tier = int(diff_str)
107	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
108	        tier = None
109	    entry = TIER_PALETTE.get(tier)
110	    return entry[1] if entry else BONUS_TINT

112	
113	def _blend_rgb(a, b, t):
114	    """Linear blend of two RGB tuples: (1-t)*a + t*b."""
115	    return tuple(int(round(a[i] * (1.0 - t) + b[i] * t)) for i in range(3))
116	
117	
118	def _bottom_gradient_alpha(w, h):
119	    """L-mode alpha mask for the bottom black gradient: 0 at the top, GRAD_BOTTOM
120	    at the bottom edge (shaped by GRAD_GAMMA). Matches the CSS overlay
121	    `bg-gradient-to-t from-black/80 to-transparent`."""
122	    col = Image.new("L", (1, h))
123	    cp = col.load()
124	    for y in range(h):
125	        t = y / (h - 1) if h > 1 else 0.0
126	        a = GRAD_BOTTOM * (t ** GRAD_GAMMA)
127	        cp[0, y] = max(0, min(255, int(round(a * 255))))
128	    return col.resize((w, h))

131	def make_large(img, tint):
132	    """Scale to 508 wide, center-crop the middle 508x208 band, then bake the
133	    album-art overlay: the tier `tint` washes the zinc-900 card behind the cover,
134	    the cover is dimmed to IMAGE_OPACITY, and a black gradient darkens the bottom
135	    edge. Returns an RGB image."""
136	    ratio = LARGE_W / img.width
137	    scaled = img.resize((LARGE_W, max(LARGE_H, int(round(img.height * ratio)))),
138	                        Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
139	    top = (scaled.height - LARGE_H) // 2
140	    strip = scaled.crop((0, top, LARGE_W, top + LARGE_H)).convert("RGB")
141	
142	    card = _blend_rgb(ZINC_900, tint, TINT_ALPHA)            # tier tint over the card
143	    backdrop = Image.new("RGB", (LARGE_W, LARGE_H), card)
144	    dimmed = Image.blend(backdrop, strip, IMAGE_OPACITY)     # cover at opacity-60
145	    black = Image.new("RGB", (LARGE_W, LARGE_H), (0, 0, 0))
146	    alpha = _bottom_gradient_alpha(LARGE_W, LARGE_H)
147	    return Image.composite(black, dimmed, alpha)             # bottom black gradient
148

150	def make_small(img):
151	    """Scale to fit a 144x144 box, pillarbox/letterbox on black. Returns RGB."""
152	    scale = min(SMALL_SIZE / img.width, SMALL_SIZE / img.height)
153	    new_w = int(img.width * scale)
154	    new_h = int(img.height * scale)
155	    scaled = img.resize((new_w, new_h), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
156	    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (SMALL_SIZE, SMALL_SIZE), (0, 0, 0))
157	    canvas.paste(scaled, ((SMALL_SIZE - new_w) // 2, (SMALL_SIZE - new_h) // 2))
158	    return canvas

162	    """Remove existing cover files (any image extension) from a tier dir, so a

164	    for f in d.iterdir():

166	            f.unlink()

169	def process_cover_art(src_dir, out_base, catalog_path):
170	    """Process all JPGs in src_dir into the marvin art tree."""
171	    src_path = Path(src_dir)
172	
173	    out_large = Path(out_base) / "large"
174	    out_small = Path(out_base) / "small"
175	    out_large.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
176	    out_small.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
177	    clear_covers(out_large)
178	    clear_covers(out_small)
179	
180	    difficulty = load_difficulty(catalog_path)
181	
182	    jpg_files = sorted(f for f in src_path.iterdir()
183	                       if f.is_file() and f.suffix.lower() in (".jpg", ".jpeg"))
184	    if not jpg_files:
185	        print(f"No JPG files found in {src_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
186	        return 1
187	
188	    print(f"Processing {len(jpg_files)} cover images -> {out_base}\n")
189	
190	    processed = 0
191	    failed = []
192	
193	    for jpg_path in jpg_files:
194	        try:
195	            m = KEY_RE.match(jpg_path.name)
196	            if not m:
197	                print(f"  WARNING: {jpg_path.name} has no <setlist>_<idx>_ prefix; skipped")
198	                continue
199	            setlist, index = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
200	            key = (setlist, index)
201	            stem = f"{setlist}-{index:02d}"            # firmware naming
202	            tint = tier_tint(difficulty.get(key))
203	
204	            img = Image.open(jpg_path)

207	                rgb.paste(img, mask=img.split()[-1] if img.mode == "RGBA" else None)
208	                img = rgb

210	                img = img.convert("RGB")

212	            # large: PNG strip with baked album-art overlay (tier tint + gradient)
213	            make_large(img, tint).save(out_large / (stem + ".png"), "PNG")
214	            # small: clean 144x144 PNG (PNG decoder is clip-independent offscreen;
215	            # the JPEG decoder is not — see the module docstring)
216	            make_small(img).save(out_small / (stem + ".png"), "PNG")
217	
218	            print(f"  {jpg_path.name}: tier {difficulty.get(key) or '-'} "
219	                  f"tint {tint} -> large/{stem}.png, small/{stem}.png")
220	            processed += 1

222	        except Exception as e:

227	    if failed:

233	    print(f"\nInstalled to:")

235	    print(f"  {out_small}  (dashboard, PNG)")
236	    return 0
```

```text
10	 *   4: bit6 strum-down, bit4 minus, bit2 plus (others 1)
11	 *   5: bit7 orange, bit6 red, bit5 blue, bit4 green, bit3 yellow, bit2 pedal,
12	 *      bit0 strum-up (bit1 = 1)
13	 * The GH3 ident bits matter: with them clear, GH3 treats us as a GHWT guitar and
14	 * ignores the strum bar. See firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md. */
15	
16	static uint8_t s_regs[256];                    /* register bank (ID at 0xfa) */
17	static uint8_t s_sx = 0x20, s_sy = 0x20;       /* analog stick, centered */
18	static uint8_t s_tb;                           /* touch bar (GH3 unused) */
19	static uint8_t s_whammy = 0x10;                /* whammy bar (rest) */
20	static uint8_t s_btn4 = 0xFF, s_btn5 = 0xFF;   /* button bytes, active-low (rest 0xFF) */
21	
22	static const struct { const char *name; uint8_t byte; uint8_t mask; } k_btn[] = {
23	    { "green",   5, 0x10 }, { "red",    5, 0x40 }, { "yellow", 5, 0x08 },
24	    { "blue",    5, 0x20 }, { "orange", 5, 0x80 }, { "pedal",  5, 0x04 },
25	    { "strumup", 5, 0x01 }, { "strumdown", 4, 0x40 },
26	    { "gplus",   4, 0x04 }, { "gminus", 4, 0x10 },
27	};
28	
29	static void guitar_build_report(uint8_t *d)
30	{
31	    d[0] = 0xC0 | (s_sx & 0x3F);   /* bits7-6 = 1: identify as a GH3 Les Paul guitar */
32	    d[1] = 0xC0 | (s_sy & 0x3F);
33	    d[2] = s_tb;
34	    d[3] = s_whammy;
35	    d[4] = s_btn4;
36	    d[5] = s_btn5;
37	}
38	
39	static bool guitar_set_button(const char *name, bool pressed)
40	{
41	    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(k_btn) / sizeof(k_btn[0]); i++) {
42	        if (strcmp(name, k_btn[i].name) == 0) {
43	            uint8_t *b = (k_btn[i].byte == 4) ? &s_btn4 : &s_btn5;
44	            if (pressed) *b &= (uint8_t)~k_btn[i].mask;   /* active-low: pressed = clear */
45	            else *b |= k_btn[i].mask;
46	            return true;
47	        }
48	    }
49	    return false;
50	}
51	
52	static void guitar_reset(void)
53	{
54	    s_btn4 = s_btn5 = 0xFF;
55	    s_whammy = 0x10;
56	}
57	
58	void Guitar_SetWhammy(uint8_t value)
59	{
60	    s_whammy = value & 0x1F;
61	}
62	
63	void Guitar_SetStick(uint8_t x, uint8_t y)
64	{
65	    s_sx = x & 0x3F;
66	    s_sy = y & 0x3F;
67	}
68	
69	static const wiimote_extension_t s_guitar = {
70	    .name        = "guitar",
71	    .regs        = s_regs,
72	    .report_len  = 6,
73	    .build_report = guitar_build_report,
74	    .set_button  = guitar_set_button,
75	    .reset       = guitar_reset,
76	};
77	
78	void Guitar_Init(void)
79	{
80	    memset(s_regs, 0, sizeof(s_regs));
81	    static const uint8_t k_id[6] = { 0x00, 0x00, 0xA4, 0x20, 0x01, 0x03 };  /* GH guitar */
82	    memcpy(&s_regs[0xFA], k_id, sizeof(k_id));
83	    Wiimote_RegisterExtension(&s_guitar);
84	}
85
```

```text
69	    add_proto.list_elem[1].protocol_uuid = UUID_PROTOCOL_HIDP;  add_proto.list_elem[1].num_params = 0;
```

```text
34	 * canvas is hidden, so layer binds always precede gfxcShowCanvas.

38	 *      own framebuffer and drives SPLASH_HW_LAYER directly (ScreenSplash_Show; no canvas,

42	 *      which places each layer-screen onto its own Legato layer/canvas (dashboard

44	 *      active canvases are bound to display layers and paint behind the splash.

84	static void bind_canvas(uint32_t canvas, uint32_t hw, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE mode, bool show)
```
