121	/* Byte offset from a ring-slot base to the active picture's top-left, applied to
122	 * every HEO frame address. Set by heo_bind (video task), added by heo_frame_latch
123	 * (ISC IRQ) — single-writer/single-reader of one aligned word. */
124	static volatile uint32_t s_heo_crop_off;
125	
126	/* HEO scaler factor is 12.20 fixed-point: factor = (src / dst) << 20; 1.0 = 1:1. */
127	static uint32_t scaler_factor(uint32_t src, uint32_t dst)
128	{
129	    if (dst == 0u) { return 0x100000u; }
130	    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)src << 20) / dst);
131	}
132	
133	/* ── HEO video levels expansion (per-component gamma CLUT) ─────────────────────
134	 * The captured source is mildly range-compressed (~5 black pedestal, ~233 white
135	 * ceiling) against the panel's full 0..255. The HEO CBHS limited-range block is
136	 * YCbCr-only, but the per-component gamma CLUT operates on true RGB, so we load it
137	 * with a linear levels-expansion curve (BLACK→0, WHITE→255) and enable GAM. This is
138	 * display-only — the capture in DDR is untouched, so the detector/gameplay see raw
139	 * pixels — and free at runtime (applied by the LCDC at scanout).
140	 *
141	 * The CLUT must be written while CLUTEN and GAM are clear (true at init, after MCC's
142	 * XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer); XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode rewrites HEOCFG1 with GAM(0) on
143	 * every bind, so heo_bind re-asserts GAM after it. Fixed curve — retune VIDEO_LEVELS_*
144	 * for a different source. */
145	#define VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK    5u    /* input level mapped to 0   */
146	#define VIDEO_LEVELS_WHITE  233u    /* input level mapped to 255 */
147	
148	static volatile bool s_video_levels = true;   /* GAM (levels CLUT) on; `gamma` cmd toggles */
149	
150	static void heo_gamma_load(void)
151	{
152	    const int32_t den = (int32_t)(VIDEO_LEVELS_WHITE - VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK);
153	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < 256u; i++)
154	    {
155	        uint32_t c;
156	        if (i <= VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK)
157	        {
158	            c = 0u;
159	        }
160	        else
161	        {
162	            int32_t v = ((int32_t)(i - VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK) * 255 + den / 2) / den;
163	            c = (v > 255) ? 255u : (uint32_t)v;
164	        }
165	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCLUT[i] = LCDC_HEOCLUT_ACLUT(0xFFu) |
166	                                      LCDC_HEOCLUT_RCLUT(c) |
167	                                      LCDC_HEOCLUT_GCLUT(c) |
168	                                      LCDC_HEOCLUT_BCLUT(c);
169	    }
170	}
171	
172	/* Bind HEO to the capture buffer at the window, engaging the bicubic scaler only
173	 * when dst != the active source size. The scaler reads only the detected active
174	 * picture rect (Video_GetActiveRect) — cropping the source's dead black bars — by
175	 * offsetting the frame base to the active top-left, sizing HEOCFG4 to the active
176	 * w/h, and skipping the cropped columns each line via XSTRIDE. Full-frame until
177	 * detection locks (safe fallback). The matching BASE DMA-discard behind the opaque
178	 * video is set by base_discard_reconcile (single DISCEN owner). Seeds HEO with the
179	 * latest frame (0 until the first frame, which heo_frame_latch then fixes within a
180	 * frame-time). Video-task ctx. */
181	static void heo_bind(uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h,
182	                     uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
183	{
184	    if (x + dst_w > BASE_W || y + dst_h > BASE_H)
185	    {
186	        LOG_WARN("UI: video window %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) exceeds panel; skip bind\r\n",
187	                 (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
188	                 (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y);
189	        return;
190	    }
191	
192	    Video_FrameInfo fi;
193	    Video_GetFrameInfo(&fi);
194	
195	    /* Active picture crop within the full frame (full-frame fallback pre-lock). */
196	    uint16_t ax, ay, aw, ah;
197	    (void)Video_GetActiveRect(&ax, &ay, &aw, &ah);
198	    uint32_t bpp        = fi.bytes_per_pixel;
199	    uint32_t stride     = (uint32_t)src_w * bpp;                 /* full line bytes */
200	    uint32_t crop_off   = (uint32_t)ay * stride + (uint32_t)ax * bpp;
201	    uint32_t addr       = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)fi.buffer + crop_off;
202	
203	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
204	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, false);
205	    /* Re-apply the levels CLUT enable (RGBColorMode clears GAM); off = raw pass-through. */
206	    if (s_video_levels) { XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG1 |=  LCDC_HEOCFG1_GAM_Msk; }
207	    else                { XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG1 &= ~LCDC_HEOCFG1_GAM_Msk; }
208	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, addr, false);
209	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, (uint32_t)(src_w - aw) * bpp, false);
210	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, false);
211	
212	    /* Display rect (HEOCFG3, dst) vs source-memory rect (HEOCFG4, active crop):
213	     * equal for 1:1, differ when scaling. Written directly — XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize
214	     * sets both equal. */
215	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG3 = LCDC_HEOCFG3_XSIZE(dst_w - 1u) | LCDC_HEOCFG3_YSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
216	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG4 = LCDC_HEOCFG4_XMEMSIZE(aw - 1u) | LCDC_HEOCFG4_YMEMSIZE(ah - 1u);
217	
218	    bool scaling = (dst_w != aw) || (dst_h != ah);
219	    if (scaling)
220	    {
221	        uint32_t hf = scaler_factor(aw, dst_w);
222	        uint32_t vf = scaler_factor(ah, dst_h);
223	
224	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(1)
225	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(1);
226	        /* Bicubic luma + chroma, both planes (mirrors MCC's surface-set path). */
227	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG30 = LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYBICU(1)
228	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCBICU(1);
229	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG31 = LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYBICU(1)
230	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCCFG(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCBICU(1);
231	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG24 = LCDC_HEOCFG24_VXSYFACT(vf);
232	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG25 = LCDC_HEOCFG25_VXSCFACT(vf);
233	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG26 = LCDC_HEOCFG26_HXSYFACT(hf);
234	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG27 = LCDC_HEOCFG27_HXSCFACT(hf);
235	    }
236	    else
237	    {
238	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(0) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(0)
239	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(0) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(0);
240	    }
241	
242	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, true, true);
243	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
244	
245	    s_heo_crop_off = crop_off;
246	    s_bound_src_w = src_w; s_bound_src_h = src_h;
247	    s_bound_ax = ax; s_bound_ay = ay; s_bound_aw = aw; s_bound_ah = ah;
248	    LOG_INFO("UI: HEO bound src %ux%u active %ux%u@(%u,%u) -> dst %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) %s\r\n",
249	             (unsigned)src_w, (unsigned)src_h, (unsigned)aw, (unsigned)ah, (unsigned)ax, (unsigned)ay,
250	             (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
251	             (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y, scaling ? "scaled" : "1:1");
252	}
253	
254	/* Disable HEO output. The BASE discard is dropped (or handed to the dialog rect)
255	 * by base_discard_reconcile, which owns DISCEN. */
256	static void heo_unbind(void)
257	{
258	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
259	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
260	}
261	
262	/* ── BASE DMA-discard (single DISCEN owner, video-task ctx) ───────────────────
263	 * The LCDC has one BASE discard window (§44.6.4.7): BASE skips its DDR read where
264	 * an opaque layer fully covers it, freeing read bandwidth. base_discard_reconcile
265	 * picks the region each tick — the video rect while HEO is bound, else the dialog
266	 * rect while the song-select modal is open, else none — and applies only on change
267	 * so it isn't re-committing BASE every tick. Keeping every DISCEN write here (never
268	 * in heo_bind/heo_unbind or the UI task) keeps BASE single-writer. */
269	static struct { bool on; uint32_t x, y, w, h; } s_base_disc;
270	
271	static void base_discard_apply(bool on, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)
272	{
273	    if (on == s_base_disc.on && x == s_base_disc.x && y == s_base_disc.y &&
274	        w == s_base_disc.w && h == s_base_disc.h) { return; }
275	
276	    if (on)
277	    {
278	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG5 = LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCXPOS(x) | LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCYPOS(y);
279	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG6 = LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCXSIZE(w - 1u) | LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCYSIZE(h - 1u);
280	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 |= LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
281	    }
282	    else
283	    {
284	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 &= ~LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
285	    }
286	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);   /* commit the CFG change */
287	
288	    s_base_disc.on = on;
289	    s_base_disc.x = x; s_base_disc.y = y; s_base_disc.w = w; s_base_disc.h = h;
290	}
291	
292	static void base_discard_reconcile(void)
293	{
294	    if (s_video_bound)
295	    {
296	        rect_t r = s_video_win;
297	        base_discard_apply(true, r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h);
298	    }
299	    else if (s_dialog_discard)
300	    {
301	        base_discard_apply(true, DIALOG_X, DIALOG_Y, DIALOG_W, DIALOG_H);
302	    }
303	    else
304	    {
305	        base_discard_apply(false, 0u, 0u, 0u, 0u);
306	    }
307	}
308	
309	/* video-task tick: converge HEO to intent + source. Bind on first show, window
310	 * change (rebind flag), source-size change, or active-crop change (detection
311	 * locking flips the source from full-frame to the active rect); unbind when
312	 * hidden. */
313	static void heo_reconcile(bool source_valid, uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h)
314	{
315	    rect_t w = s_video_win;
316	    bool   win_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
317	    bool   want = s_video_shown && source_valid && win_valid;
318	
319	    uint16_t ax, ay, aw, ah;
320	    (void)Video_GetActiveRect(&ax, &ay, &aw, &ah);
321	    bool geom_changed = src_w != s_bound_src_w || src_h != s_bound_src_h ||
322	                        aw != s_bound_aw || ah != s_bound_ah ||
323	                        ax != s_bound_ax || ay != s_bound_ay;
324	
325	    if (want && (!s_video_bound || s_video_rebind || geom_changed))
326	    {
327	        heo_bind(src_w, src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
328	        s_video_bound  = true;
329	        s_video_rebind = false;
330	    }
331	    else if (!want && s_video_bound)
332	    {
333	        heo_unbind();
334	        s_video_bound = false;
335	    }
336	
337	    /* Own the single BASE discard window (video rect / dialog rect / none). Runs
338	     * after the HEO decision above so it sees the current s_video_bound. */
339	    base_discard_reconcile();
340	}
341	
342	/* ISC IRQ: point HEO at the just-completed ring slot every frame so it always scans
343	 * the freshest complete frame (not a slot the capture engine is mid-write on). This
344	 * is unconditional: writing the layer address while HEO is disabled (video hidden)
345	 * is harmless, and keeping the write out of any task/IRQ-shared flag guarantees the
346	 * scanout base advances regardless of task timing. Latches at the next vsync. */
347	static void heo_frame_latch(uint32_t buffer_addr)
348	{
349	    /* Non-blocking base update: write the HEO frame address and *request* the layer
350	     * attribute update, but do NOT wait for the sync. XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(...,true)
351	     * → XLCDC_UpdateLayerAttributes busy-waits on LCDC_ATTRE/ATTRS_SIP until the update
352	     * latches (a vsync away while HEO scans) — too costly for this per-frame ISC IRQ.
353	     * The address register is double-buffered, so the hardware latches the new base at
354	     * the next vsync on its own; the following frame writes the newer address. OR into
355	     * ATTRE so a pending BASE/OVR update isn't cleared. The crop offset (0 until
356	     * the active area is detected) points HEO at the active top-left of the slot. */
357	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEO[0].LCDC_HEOYFBA = buffer_addr + s_heo_crop_off;
358	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_ATTRE |= LCDC_ATTRE_HEO_Msk;
359	}
360	
361	void UiManager_VideoShow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)
362	{
363	    rect_t r = { x, y, w, h };
364	    s_video_win    = r;
365	    s_video_rebind = true;
366	    s_video_shown  = true;
367	}
368	
369	void UiManager_VideoHide(void)
370	{
371	    s_video_shown = false;
372	}
373	
374	/* ── video frame overlay (OVR1, above HEO) ────────────────────────────────────
375	 * A caller-owned ARGB_4444 surface composited on OVR1 over the video for the
376	 * rounded anti-aliased frame. Driven directly via the PLIB (not the canvas
377	 * framework, which has no 4444 mode) — same pattern as the splash/HEO. OVR1 is
378	 * time-shared with the song-select dialog canvas; the frame is hidden whenever
379	 * video is (fullscreen / dialog open), so they never contend. */
380	void UiManager_VideoOverlayShow(const void *buf, uint32_t x, uint32_t y,
381	                                uint32_t w, uint32_t h)
382	{
383	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, false, true);
384	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_ARGB_4444, false);
385	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)buf, false);
386	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, 0u, false);   /* buffer == window, no gap */
387	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, x, y, false);
388	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, w, h, false);
389	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, true, true);
390	}
391	
392	void UiManager_VideoOverlayHide(void)
393	{
394	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, false, true);
395	}
396	
397	void UiManager_SetVideoLevels(bool on)
398	{
399	    s_video_levels = on;
400	    s_video_rebind = true;   /* reconcile re-binds HEO next tick, applying the new GAM state */
401	}
402	
403	bool UiManager_GetVideoLevels(void)
404	{
405	    return s_video_levels;
406	}
407	
408	/* ── navigation drawer layer (OVR2) ───────────────────────────────────────────
409	 * The drawer canvas rides OVR2 (above the video frame on OVR1, so an open drawer
410	 * covers the frame's left edge). bind_canvas sets OVR2 to the drawer's RGB565 mode
411	 * each show — needed because album-art leaves OVR2 in RGBA8888. The drawer module
412	 * drives the slide FX after showing. */
413	void UiManager_ShowNavLayer(void)
414	{
415	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAVIGATION, HW_OVR2, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
416	}
417	
418	void UiManager_HideNavLayer(void)
419	{
420	    gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_NAVIGATION);
421	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_NAVIGATION);
422	}
423	
424	/* ── song-select modal (OVR1 dialog + OVR2 cover strip) ───────────────────────
425	 * The dialog and its full-color cover are a coupled pair shown/hidden together.
426	 * Both canvases paint continuously into their surfaces; open binds them onto
427	 * OVR1/OVR2 and shows them, close hides them (freeing OVR1 for the nav drawer).
428	 * bind_canvas needs the canvas hidden for gfxcSetLayer — true while closed. */
429	static bool s_songsel_open = false;
430	
431	/* Route input for the song-select modal via the layer-screens' background panels.
432	 * Legato treats every layer-screen as stacked and pickable regardless of canvas
433	 * visibility, so a hidden overlay still captures touches meant for the dashboard
434	 * beneath it unless its background panel is disabled (the MGS layer-screen
435	 * "background panel" pattern). PANEL_SONG_SELECT (layer 2) and
436	 * PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART (layer 3) are the first pickable widgets on their
437	 * IGNOREPICK roots, i.e. the layers' background panels. `on` = dialog shown:
438	 * enable the dialog panels and *disable the dashboard* (PANEL_DASHBOARD, layer 0) so
439	 * it's a true modal — nothing behind the dialog (header tap, hamburger) reacts.
440	 * Inverted while closed: dashboard live, overlays pass input through. */
441	/* Gate a panel's whole subtree from picking without repainting it. leWidget's
442	 * setEnabled toggles LE_WIDGET_ENABLED but also invalidates, which would repaint
443	 * an unchanged surface and stall touch (Legato defers input while drawing). We
444	 * only want the pick effect — leUtils_PickFromWidget descends only into ENABLED
445	 * children, and the renderer never reads ENABLED — so toggle the flag directly.
446	 * IGNOREPICK would not do: it stops the panel being the pick result but still lets
447	 * its children be picked, so the subtree wouldn't be gated. */
448	static void panel_set_pickable(leWidget *w, leBool on)
449	{
450	    if (on) { w->flags |=  LE_WIDGET_ENABLED; }
451	    else    { w->flags &= ~LE_WIDGET_ENABLED; }
452	}
453	
454	static void songsel_set_input(leBool on)
455	{
456	    panel_set_pickable(Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD, on ? LE_FALSE : LE_TRUE);
457	    panel_set_pickable(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT, on);
458	    panel_set_pickable(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART, on);
459	}
460	
461	void UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(bool on)
462	{
463	    panel_set_pickable(Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD, on ? LE_TRUE : LE_FALSE);
464	}
465	
466	void UiManager_OpenSongSelect(void)
467	{
468	    if (s_songsel_open) { return; }
469	    songsel_set_input(LE_TRUE);
470	
471	    /* The dialog takes OVR1 from the video frame overlay; drop the frame first
472	     * (video is hidden below, so there's nothing to frame). */
473	    UiManager_VideoOverlayHide();
474	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_SONGSEL,   HW_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565,   true);
475	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART, HW_OVR2, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, true);
476	
477	    /* The opaque dialog fully covers the video window, so free the DDR read
478	     * bandwidth its display was costing: hide HEO (capture keeps running for the
479	     * detector/gameplay) and discard BASE DMA behind the 1100x660 dialog. This is
480	     * the contention that knocked the CSI-2 D-PHY out of lock on every song switch
481	     * (album-art decode/blit + repaint). Both are intent only — the video-task
482	     * reconcile applies them, so HEO/BASE stay single-writer. */
483	    UiManager_VideoHide();
484	    s_dialog_discard = true;
485	
486	    s_songsel_open = true;
487	}
488	
489	void UiManager_CloseSongSelect(void)
490	{
491	    if (!s_songsel_open) { return; }
492	    gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_SONGSEL);   gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SONGSEL);
493	    gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART); gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART);
494	    songsel_set_input(LE_FALSE);
495	
496	    /* Dashboard is back: drop the modal's BASE discard and bring the live video
497	     * back up (reconcile re-binds HEO once the source is locked). */
498	    s_dialog_discard = false;
499	    ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed();
500	
501	    s_songsel_open = false;
502	}
503	
504	static uint32_t s_backlight_pct;
505	
506	/* Set the backlight brightness (0–100%, clamped). The backlight is PWM-dimmed on
507	 * PC18 (PWM channel 0, configured by MCC), period read at runtime so this tracks
508	 * whatever MCC sets. The channel is CPOL_LOW — it idles low (dark) when stopped,
509	 * so the panel stays off until the splash — which means CDTY is the LOW-level
510	 * time and brightness is the high fraction: CDTY = period·(100−pct)/100, so
511	 * pct=100 → CDTY 0 → full bright, pct=0 → CDTY period → off. PWM_ChannelDutySet
512	 * writes CDTY directly while stopped and the update register once running, so
513	 * this is valid both before the channel starts and at runtime. */
514	void UiManager_SetBacklight(uint32_t pct)
515	{
516	    if (pct > 100u) { pct = 100u; }
517	    s_backlight_pct = pct;
518	    uint32_t period = PWM_ChannelPeriodGet(PWM_CHANNEL_0);
519	    PWM_ChannelDutySet(PWM_CHANNEL_0, (period * (100u - pct)) / 100u);
520	}
521	
522	uint32_t UiManager_GetBacklight(void)
523	{
524	    return s_backlight_pct;
525	}
526	
527	/* Light the backlight at the persisted brightness (Settings_Get loads the QSPI
528	 * ring on first use, or the compiled default if no record). The PWM channel is
529	 * stopped (no output) until started here, so the panel stays dark until the
530	 * splash is up — no pre-splash frame. PWM_Initialize ran at startup; this sets
531	 * the duty (while stopped, so the channel starts straight at the target) and
532	 * starts it. */
533	static void enable_backlight(void)
534	{
535	    UiManager_SetBacklight(Settings_Get()->backlight_pct);
536	    PWM_ChannelsStart(PWM_CHANNEL_0_MASK);
537	}
538	
539	/* ── Legato render serialization ──────────────────────────────────────────────
540	 * leAddRootWidget/leRemoveRootWidget mutate Legato's per-layer root lists with no
541	 * locking, and LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks (both run from scheduler start)
542	 * traverse those lists. The boot task edits the scene graph post-scheduler, so it
543	 * suspends those two readers around the edits. Safe to suspend here: at guard
544	 * time no app roots are attached (the splash is pure LCDC scanout), so the
545	 * renderer is idle; resuming hands rendering back. GFX_CANVAS_Tasks is left
546	 * running (it commits canvases; not a root-list reader). */
547	static TaskHandle_t s_legato_task;
548	static TaskHandle_t s_input_task;
549	
550	static void scene_edit_begin(void)
551	{
552	    s_legato_task = xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks");
553	    s_input_task  = xTaskGetHandle("SYS_INPUT_Tasks");
554	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_legato_task); }
555	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_input_task);  }
556	    if (s_legato_task == NULL || s_input_task == NULL)
557	    {
558	        LOG_WARN("UI: render task handle not found; scene edit unguarded\r\n");
559	    }
560	}
561	
562	static void scene_edit_end(void)
563	{
564	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_input_task);  }
565	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_legato_task); }
566	}
567	
568	/* Build the Marvin master screen and run per-panel setup. screenInit_Marvin builds
569	 * all layer-screens and places each on its own Legato layer/canvas (dashboard 0,
570	 * navigation 1, song-select 2) — no re-hosting. Each panel module's *_Setup() then sets
571	 * its canvas window and wires its content/events. */
572	static void init_screens(void)
573	{
574	    /* screenInit_Marvin only flips the one-time "initialized" flag; the widget
575	     * tree (all three layers) is constructed in screenShow_Marvin, which also
576	     * attaches each layer's root to its Legato layer (leAddRootWidget rootN, N). */
577	    (void)screenInit_Marvin();
578	    (void)screenShow_Marvin();
579	
580	    /* The album-art layer (3) must be RGBA8888: the 2D engine has no RGB888 support
581	     * (gfx2dFormats[RGB_888] = -1), so a 24bpp canvas can't be GFX2D-blitted and
582	     * renders garbage. MGS currently emits LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888 for this layer;
583	     * override it here to match the RGBA8888 canvas surface + OVR2 scanout. (Set the
584	     * layer-screen to RGBA8888 in MGS to make this override redundant.) */
585	    leSetLayerColorMode(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888);
586	
587	    ScreenDashboard_Setup();
588	    ScreenVideo_Setup();
589	    ScreenNavigation_Setup();
590	    ScreenSongSelect_Setup();
591	    ScreenAlbumArt_Setup();
592	
593	    /* Song-select starts closed: disable its layer-screens' background panels so
594	     * those (hidden) overlays don't capture touches meant for the dashboard.
595	     * UiManager_OpenSongSelect re-enables them. */
596	    songsel_set_input(LE_FALSE);
597	}
598	
599	/* Paint every layer-screen surface once, behind the splash. Legato renders into a
600	 * canvas surface independent of whether that canvas is shown or bound to a hardware
601	 * layer, so a full paint here leaves every surface complete — after which showing a
602	 * screen is a pure layer bind with no repaint. Each panel is VISIBLE by now (its
603	 * *_Setup set it) and its canvas window is full-surface sized, so one invalidate
604	 * lands the whole surface; wait_render_idle then confirms it drained. Relied upon so
605	 * the drawer/dialog need never invalidate on open — MGS builds the nav panel
606	 * setVisible(FALSE), so its boot root-damage paints nothing until this runs. */
607	static void paint_all_screens_once(void)
608	{
609	    Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD);
610	    Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION);
611	    Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT);
612	    Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART);
613	}
614	
615	/* Block until the Legato render task has painted all pending damage. We don't
616	 * drive leUpdate — LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task render correctly when they run;
617	 * we just yield and poll the public idle flag, requiring it to hold continuously
618	 * (a lone idle sample is an inter-frame gap, not a finished paint). Bounded. */
619	static void wait_render_idle(void)
620	{
621	    TickType_t deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
622	    TickType_t idle_since = 0;
623	    bool       idle_run   = false;
624	
625	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
626	    {
627	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
628	        {
629	            if (!idle_run)
630	            {
631	                idle_run   = true;
632	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
633	            }
634	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
635	            {
636	                return;
637	            }
638	        }
639	        else
640	        {
641	            idle_run = false;
642	        }
643	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
644	    }
645	    LOG_WARN("UI: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
646	}
647	
648	/* ── boot sequence ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
649	
650	static void ui_boot_task(void *param)
651	{
652	    (void)param;
653	
654	    /* PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work, as fast as the SD allows. */
655	    (void)ScreenSplash_Load();   /* loads the image, or fills the fallback colour */
656	    ScreenSplash_Show(xlcdc_layer(SPLASH_HW_LAYER));
657	    enable_backlight();
658	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
659	
660	    /* Splash is up — let the app start everything else (services + camera) now,
661	     * in parallel with the screen painting below, so it's all warm at reveal. */
662	    if (s_splash_shown_cb != NULL) { s_splash_shown_cb(); }
663	
664	    /* Decode all album art into the RGB888 caches *before* building the screens,
665	     * so the song-select panel's initial selection (ScreenSongSelect_Setup ->
666	     * song_detail_show(0)) finds its cover already cached. Storage mounts here;
667	     * Legato's image decoders are up from SYS_Initialize. All behind the splash;
668	     * the ~1-3 s decode just extends the splash hold. See game/art.h. */
669	    (void)Art_LoadAll();
670	
671	    /* PHASE 2 — build the Marvin screen + per-panel setup behind the splash.
672	     * Scene-graph edits (screenInit_Marvin's leAddRootWidget calls) are guarded
673	     * against the render tasks; the canvas/layer binds after are GFX-canvas only
674	     * (no root-list mutation) so they need no guard. */
675	    scene_edit_begin();
676	    init_screens();
677	    scene_edit_end();
678	
679	    /* Dashboard live on BASE (covered by the splash until reveal). Nav and
680	     * song-select are built and painting into their own canvases but not bound to
681	     * a layer yet — they take their layers at reveal, once the splash vacates. */
682	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
683	
684	    /* Park HEO off (video hidden) so the dashboard owns the full panel until video
685	     * is shown at reveal. BASE discard is off by reset default and stays off until
686	     * the reconcile arms it. Was video.c's job at task start; the compositor owns HEO
687	     * now. Safe as a one-shot here — the video task's reconcile is a no-op while
688	     * video is hidden, so this is the only HEO writer at boot. */
689	    heo_unbind();
690	
691	    /* Paint all screens once now, behind the splash, then wait for it to drain.
692	     * Every surface is complete before it's ever shown; screens are event-driven
693	     * from here — showing one is a pure layer bind, no repaint. */
694	    paint_all_screens_once();
695	    wait_render_idle();
696	
697	    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
698	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
699	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
700	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
701	
702	    /* REVEAL — cut over to the (painted) dashboard. The song-select dialog starts
703	     * closed: it and its OVR2 cover strip are painted into their canvases but not
704	     * shown; UiManager_OpenSongSelect() binds + shows the pair on demand (header tap).
705	     * OVR1/OVR2 colour modes are set by their users when shown (video frame → ARGB_4444,
706	     * dialog → RGB565, nav/album-art on OVR2), so no preemptive poke is needed here. */
707	    ScreenSplash_Hide(xlcdc_layer(SPLASH_HW_LAYER));
708	
709	    /* Bring the live video up (windowed) on HEO over the dashboard, and its OVR1
710	     * frame overlay. Video is intent only — the video task binds HEO on its next
711	     * reconcile once the source is locked. */
712	    ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed();
713	
714	    /* Arm capture LAST — after the display is up and the boot-time task/SD/paint
715	     * contention has drained. The CSI-2 D-PHY RX is timing-sensitive at bring-up
716	     * (it must catch the source's LP11→HS transition); arming it earlier, during the
717	     * splash, makes it lock marginally and the lanes sit in stop-state (~0 fps). This
718	     * is the one ordering that must hold — see the journal (2026-06-30). */
719	    Video_CaptureEnable();
720	
721	    /* Boot sequence done — arm the health monitor now (it stays idle until this
722	     * so its card I/O + task-list walks never perturb the reveal window). */
723	    HealthMonitor_NotifyReady();
724	
725	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
726	}
727	
728	/* ── public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
729

732	    /* Assign the per-screen canvas surfaces, then drive the canvas state machine
733	     * to RUNNING so a blit isn't dropped by the RUNNING gate, then set the Legato
734	     * string table the screens need. All pre-scheduler config — no screen built
735	     * or shown here; the boot task does the sequence. */

737	    ScreenNavigation_InitSurface();
738	    ScreenSongSelect_InitSurface();
739	    ScreenAlbumArt_InitSurface();
740	    GFX_CANVAS_Task();
741	
742	    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);
743	    initializeStrings();
744	
745	    /* Register the compositor's HEO display hooks with the capture producer before
746	     * the video task starts (Video_Initialize runs later, in APP_Tasks). The video
747	     * task then drives heo_reconcile each tick and the ISC IRQ drives heo_frame_latch. */
748	    Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(heo_frame_latch);
749	    Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(heo_reconcile);
750	
751	    /* Load the HEO levels-expansion gamma CLUT now, while GAM/CLUTEN are clear
752	     * (post XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer, pre any HEO bind). heo_bind enables GAM. */
753	    heo_gamma_load();
754	
755	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(ui_boot_task, "UiBoot", BOOT_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
756	                            NULL, BOOT_TASK_PRIORITY, s_boot_stack, &s_boot_tcb);
757	}

170	    memcpy(&s_hb_frame[0], s_coord_mac, 6u);   /* dst = coordinator */
171	    memcpy(&s_hb_frame[6], s_mac, 6u);         /* src = this node   */
172	    s_hb_frame[12] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB >> 8);
173	    s_hb_frame[13] = (uint8_t)(T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB & 0xFFu);
174	    s_hb_frame[14] = T1S_HB_VERSION;
175	    s_hb_frame[15] = T1S_HB_TYPE_GUITAR;
176	    s_hb_frame[16] = (uint8_t)T1S_NODE_ID;
177	    s_hb_frame[17] = synced ? 0x01u : 0x00u;   /* flags: bit0 = synced */
178	    s_hb_seq++;
179	    s_hb_frame[18] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq);
180	    s_hb_frame[19] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 8);
181	    s_hb_frame[20] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 16);
182	    s_hb_frame[21] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 24);
183	
184	    s_hb_busy = true;
185	    if (!TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_hb_frame, T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + T1S_HB_LEN,
186	                                   0u, hb_tx_done, NULL)) {
187	        s_hb_busy = false;
188	    }
189	}
190	
191	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  Public API  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
192	
193	void T1SFollower_Initialize(void)
194	{
195	    SYSTICK_TimerStart();    /* MCC inits the timer; the app enables it */
196	
197	    log_str("guitar: boot - t1s follower + cli\r\n");  /* one-time banner */
198	
199	    buttons_release_all();   /* pins boot Out/Low (asserted) — release first */
200	
201	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST active-low, idle high). */
202	    T1S_CS_Set();
203	    T1S_RST_Clear();
204	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
205	    T1S_RST_Set();
206	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
207	
208	    SERCOM0_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);  /* Mode 0 set by MCC init */
209	
210	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
211	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
212	        log_str("guitar: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
213	        return;
214	    }
215	
216	    EIC_CallbackRegister(EIC_PIN_13, irq_cb, 0u);   /* EXTINT13 enabled in EIC_Initialize */
217	
218	    /* Configure the LAN8651 + PLCA as follower id 2. Not promiscuous — the
219	     * MAC-PHY filters to this node's MAC + broadcast. Non-blocking: the
220	     * register sequence finishes in the background via T1SFollower_Tasks, so
221	     * the CLI is never gated behind the link coming up. */
222	    if (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, true, T1S_NODE_ID, T1S_NODE_COUNT,
223	                      0u, 0u, false, false, false)) {
224	        log_str("guitar: TC6Regs_Init rejected\r\n");
225	    }
226	}
227	
228	void T1SFollower_Tasks(void)
229	{
230	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
231	        return;
232	    }
233	    service_pump();
234	    if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
235	        s_link_up = true;
236	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
237	        char buf[80];
238	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
239	                       "guitar: LAN8651 up - chipRev=%u, MAC=02:00:00:00:00:%02X, "
240	                       "PLCA follower id=%u/%u\r\n",
241	                       (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
242	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID,
243	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
244	        log_str(buf);
245	    }
246	
247	    /* Periodic presence heartbeat to the coordinator. */
248	    if (s_link_up) {
249	        uint32_t now = SYSTICK_GetTickCounter();
250	        if ((now - s_hb_last_ms) >= T1S_HB_INTERVAL_MS) {
251	            s_hb_last_ms = now;
252	            send_heartbeat();
253	        }
254	    }
255	}
256

259	    return s_link_up;
260	}

292	/* Diagnostic: log the raw value of a control register (async — the result
293	 * prints from the service loop a moment later). */
294	static void on_id_read(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint32_t addr, uint32_t value,
295	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
296	{
297	    (void)pInst;
298	    (void)pTag;
299	    (void)pGlobalTag;
300	    char buf[88];
301	    if (addr == 0x00000001u) {
302	        /* PHY id register — oui/model are meaningful here (lib wants 0x1F0/0x1B). */
303	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
304	                       "guitar: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d, oui=0x%03lX model=0x%02lX)\r\n",
305	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success,
306	                       (unsigned long)(value >> 10), (unsigned long)((value >> 4) & 0x3FFu));
307	    } else {
308	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "guitar: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d)\r\n",
309	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success);
310	    }
311	    log_str(buf);
312	}
313	
314	void T1SFollower_ReadId(void)
315	{
316	    /* 0x00 = OA IDVER, 0x01 = PHY id (lib expects oui 0x1F0 / model 0x1B),
317	     * 0x000A0094 = chip rev. */
318	    static const uint32_t addrs[3] = { 0x00000000u, 0x00000001u, 0x000A0094u };
319	
320	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
321	        log_str("guitar: t1s not initialized\r\n");
322	        return;
323	    }
324	    /* Just enqueue; the main service loop completes the reads and on_id_read
325	     * logs each result a moment later. Don't hammer TC6_Service here — doing so
326	     * while the link is live can trip a transient Loss_of_Framing. */
327	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 3u; i++) {
328	        (void)TC6_ReadRegister(s_tc6, addrs[i], false, on_id_read, NULL);
329	    }
330	}
331	
332	void T1SFollower_GetState(bool *synced, uint8_t *txCredit, uint8_t *rxCredit)
333	{
334	    uint8_t tx = 0u, rx = 0u;
335	    bool    sy = false;
336	    if (s_tc6 != NULL) {
337	        TC6_GetState(s_tc6, &tx, &rx, &sy);
338	    }
339	    if (synced   != NULL) { *synced   = sy; }
340	    if (txCredit != NULL) { *txCredit = tx; }
341	    if (rxCredit != NULL) { *rxCredit = rx; }
342	}

347	/* Async read of the PLCA status register (bit 15 = plca_status). Result logs
348	 * from the service loop a moment later. */
349	static void on_plca_read(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint32_t addr, uint32_t value,
350	                         void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
351	{
352	    (void)pInst;
353	    (void)addr;
354	    (void)pTag;
355	    (void)pGlobalTag;
356	    char buf[72];
357	    (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
358	                   "guitar: PLCA status = 0x%08lX (plca_status=%d)\r\n",
359	                   (unsigned long)value,
360	                   (int)(success && ((value & (1uL << 15)) != 0u)));
361	    log_str(buf);
362	}

364	void T1SFollower_ReadPlca(void)
365	{
366	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
367	        log_str("guitar: t1s not initialized\r\n");
368	        return;
369	    }
370	    /* Enqueue only; the main service loop completes it (see T1SFollower_ReadId). */
371	    (void)TC6_ReadRegister(s_tc6, 0x0004CA03u, true, on_plca_read, NULL);
372	}

374	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6 driver callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
375	
376	bool TC6_CB_OnSpiTransaction(uint8_t tc6instance, uint8_t *pTx, uint8_t *pRx,
377	                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
378	{
379	    (void)tc6instance;
380	    (void)pGlobalTag;
381	    if (s_spi_busy) {
382	        return false;
383	    }
384	    s_spi_busy = true;
385	    T1S_CS_Clear();          /* CS low — start of transaction (held across the chunk) */
386	    if (!SERCOM0_SPI_WriteRead(pTx, len, pRx, len)) {
387	        T1S_CS_Set();
388	        s_spi_busy = false;
389	        return false;
390	    }
391	    return true;
392	}
393	
394	void TC6_CB_OnNeedService(TC6_t *pInst, void *pGlobalTag)
395	{
396	    (void)pInst;
397	    (void)pGlobalTag;
398	    s_need_service = true;
399	}
400	
401	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetSlice(TC6_t *pInst, const uint8_t *pRx, uint16_t offset,
402	                              uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)
403	{
404	    (void)pInst;
405	    (void)pGlobalTag;
406	    if (((uint32_t)offset + len) <= sizeof(s_rx_buf)) {
407	        memcpy(&s_rx_buf[offset], pRx, len);
408	    }
409	}
410	
411	void TC6_CB_OnRxEthernetPacket(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint16_t len,
412	                               uint64_t *rxTimestamp, void *pGlobalTag)
413	{
414	    (void)pInst;
415	    (void)rxTimestamp;
416	    (void)pGlobalTag;
417	
418	    if (!success || (len < (T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + 1u))) {
419	        return;
420	    }
421	    uint16_t ethertype = (uint16_t)((s_rx_buf[12] << 8) | s_rx_buf[13]);
422	    if (ethertype != T1S_ETHERTYPE) {
423	        return;
424	    }
425	    /* Command byte is the first payload octet; trailing min-frame padding is
426	     * ignored. Apply directly (latest-wins). */
427	    uint8_t mask = (uint8_t)(s_rx_buf[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN] & T1S_CMD_BIT_MASK);
428	    s_last_cmd = mask;
429	    s_rx_count++;
430	    buttons_apply_mask(mask);
431	}
432	
433	void TC6_CB_OnError(TC6_t *pInst, TC6_Error_t err, void *pGlobalTag)
434	{
435	    (void)pGlobalTag;
436	    s_err_count++;
437	    diag_log("guitar: t1s error: ", TC6_GetErrorStr(err));
438	    switch (err) {
439	        case TC6Error_NoHardware:
440	        case TC6Error_BadChecksum:
441	        case TC6Error_UnexpectedCtrl:
442	        case TC6Error_BadTxData:
443	        case TC6Error_SyncLost:
444	        case TC6Error_SpiError:
445	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
446	            break;
447	        default:
448	            break;
449	    }
450	}
451	
452	/*>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>  TC6Regs callbacks (integrator)  >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>*/
453	
454	uint32_t TC6Regs_CB_GetTicksMs(void)
455	{
456	    return SYSTICK_GetTickCounter();
457	}
458	
459	void TC6Regs_CB_OnEvent(TC6_t *pInst, TC6Regs_Event_t event, void *pTag)
460	{
461	    (void)pTag;
462	    diag_log("guitar: t1s event: ", TC6Regs_GetEventStr(event));
463	    switch (event) {
464	        case TC6Regs_Event_Loss_of_Framing_Error:
465	        case TC6Regs_Event_RX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
466	        case TC6Regs_Event_TX_Non_Recoverable_Error:
467	            TC6Regs_Reinit(pInst);
468	            break;
469	        default:
470	            break;
471	    }
472	}

7	/* 10BASE-T1S follower for the guitar node (LAN8651 MAC-PHY on SERCOM0 SPI).
8	 *
9	 * marvin is the PLCA coordinator (node 0); this node is follower id 2. It
10	 * receives marvin's 1-byte button bitmask (ethertype 0x88B5) over T1S and
11	 * drives the 7 Wii-guitar GPIOs. Transport is the vendored OPEN Alliance TC6
12	 * driver (third_party/oa-tc6-lib) wrapped with the SERCOM0 SPI PLib, a
13	 * GPIO chip-select held across each transfer, the T1S_RST / T1S_IRQ_N pins
14	 * (EIC EXTINT15), and a SysTick-based millisecond clock. Bare-metal: the
15	 * protocol is serviced from the main loop, woken by IRQ_N. See
16	 * firmware/guitar/SPEC.md and docs/t1s-podl-link.md.
17	 *
18	 * Call T1SFollower_Initialize() once after SYS_Initialize (SERCOM0_SPI/EIC
19	 * brought up by MCC), then T1SFollower_Tasks() repeatedly from the main loop. */
20	
21	void T1SFollower_Initialize(void);
22	void T1SFollower_Tasks(void);
23

New `fauxmote` console command drives it for bring-up (`status`/`pair`/`stop`/`reconnect`/`unlink`/`ext`/`btn <mask>`). **Constraint:** owns FLEXCOM1, so it's mutually exclusive with a `TRANSPORT=UART` guitar build (compile-guarded). **Code-complete; pending MPLAB build + on-hardware bring-up** with the ESP32 wired (marvin TX PA28→ESP RX GPIO7, ESP TX GPIO8→marvin RX PA29, common GND). Protocol spec: [`../../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`](../../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:127:| 2026-07-02 | **fauxmote link on marvin uses FLEXCOM1 (PA28/PA29) and mirrors the gameplay mask to both sinks.** New `net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c` reuses the fretboard UART-transport peripheral (free while the guitar rides T1S); `FretboardLink_Send()` taps `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask()` so the T1S guitar node and the ESP32 Wiimote move in lock-step. Shared `mf_proto.h` (byte-identical both sides); 1 Mbaud via `SerialSetup`. Compile-guarded to the T1S build (owns FLEXCOM1). | Zero MCC work — FLEXCOM1's USART PLIB already exists and is idle in the T1S build, so no new peripheral/pin generation. "Mirror to both" (Greg's call) keeps the real guitar and the Wii driven by the one existing choke point without a runtime multi-sink layer, and matches the spec's bit-identical `GUITAR` byte 0 == T1S mask. Latched-state TX task with a 50 ms floor gives low-latency-on-change plus dropped-frame self-heal and keeps fauxmote's watchdog fed. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:149:| 2026-06-17 | **T1S actuator command now targets the guitar node (id 2), not the fretboard (id 1).** `net/t1s/t1s_link.c`: added `T1S_NODE_GUITAR` (id 2, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:02`, `detector_id = T1S_NO_DETECTOR`) to the node table; the service-task command flush now sends to `node_for_type(T1S_NODE_GUITAR)`. Renamed `T1SLink_SendToFretboard` → `T1SLink_SendToGuitar` (one caller, `fretboard_link.c`). The fretboard node (id 1) stays in the table as the **detector/RX** source for when it moves to T1S; only the actuator TX target moved. | The actuation role split out to the dedicated `guitar` node, which is now proven on the bus (guitar G1: `LAN8651 up … PLCA follower id=2/8`). marvin was still addressing its 1-byte command to the fretboard node; with the guitar running non-promiscuous (MAC-filtered), commands had to be re-pointed at `02:..:02` to actuate it. Single guitar today, so the target is `node_for_type(T1S_NODE_GUITAR)`; an **active-guitar selector** (mirror of `Detector_SetActive`) is deferred until multiple guitar nodes share the bus. RX/ADC over T1S is unaffected (no T1S detector node exists yet — the real fretboard is still UART). The "FretboardLink" module keeps its name for now (broader rename deferred). |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:172:| 2026-05-21 | `manual_control` lands as the second producer of `fretboard_link`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Mode-level arbitration is two-mode (`timing_pipeline` vs `manual_control`) and embedded in `ManualControl_SetEnabled`: entering manual mode calls `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false)` then takes the wire; exiting reverses. | First concrete validation of the 2026-05-20 multi-producer `fretboard_link` design — `FretboardLink_Send` stays the only entry point; arbitration lives one layer up. Embedded toggle is enough for two producers; refactor to a dedicated `actuator_mode` arbiter when a third producer (game-state controller §4.8) arrives. `timing_pipeline.publish_mask` keeps updating internal state when gated so the next ≤5 ms tick after re-enable republishes a correct mask without a stale frame. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:214:| 2026-05-20 | Fretboard-link submit queue belongs to `fretboard_link`, not `timing_pipeline`; producers call `FretboardLink_Send(mask)` | Game menu control (spec §4.8) needs to drive the actuator without going through the chord-window scheduler — its inputs are "navigate menu, press start", not gameplay notes. If the queue lives in `timing_pipeline`, the controller has to either reach across modules or duplicate transport. Moving ownership down to `fretboard_link` makes timing_pipeline one of N producers; the menu controller and any manual-test path call the same `Send` API. Latest-wins (depth-1 + xQueueOverwrite) already gives the right behavior — newest submitter wins on the wire. **Mode-level arbitration** (which producer is allowed to submit when, e.g. timing-only during gameplay vs controller-only in menus) lives one layer up; the link stays dumb. |

50	static bool    s_sw_pressed;          /* debounced button state */
51	static uint8_t s_sw_stable;           /* consecutive reads pushing toward a flip */
52	
53	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
54	/* SPSC sample queue: the ISR pushes one scan/tick, the main loop steps the
55	 * stateful streaming model once per sample (it must consume every sample in
56	 * order). Stays near-empty while inference keeps up (>240 Hz). */
57	static volatile uint16_t s_adc_q[ADC_Q_LEN][FRET_COUNT];
58	static volatile uint16_t s_q_wr;      /* ISR-advanced write index */
59	static volatile uint16_t s_q_rd;      /* main-advanced read index */
60	#endif
61	
62	static bool actuation_armed(void)
63	{
64	    bool raw = SW0_PRESSED();
65	    if (raw == s_sw_pressed)
66	    {
67	        s_sw_stable = 0u;
68	    }
69	    else if (++s_sw_stable >= ENABLE_DEBOUNCE_TICKS)
70	    {
71	        s_sw_pressed = raw;
72	        s_sw_stable = 0u;
73	        if (s_sw_pressed)             /* toggle on a confirmed press edge */
74	        {
75	            s_armed = !s_armed;
76	            if (s_armed) { LED0_ON(); } else { LED0_OFF(); }
77	        }
78	    }
79	    return s_armed;
80	}
81	
82	void Callback_TC0 (TC_TIMER_STATUS status, uintptr_t context)
83	{
84	    fret_scan_all();
85	
86	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
87	    uint16_t wi = s_q_wr;
88	    for (int c = 0; c < FRET_COUNT; c++)
89	    {
90	        s_adc_q[wi % ADC_Q_LEN][c] = fret_scan_result((fret_channel_t)c);
91	    }
92	    s_q_wr = (uint16_t)(wi + 1u);   /* publish the sample to the main loop */
93	#else
94	    uint16_t scan[FRET_COUNT] = {
95	        fret_scan_result(FRET_GREEN),
96	        fret_scan_result(FRET_RED),
97	        fret_scan_result(FRET_YELLOW),
98	        fret_scan_result(FRET_BLUE),
99	        fret_scan_result(FRET_ORANGE),
100	    };
101	    model_infer_push(scan);   /* sample the window at a clean 240 Hz */
102	#endif
103	
104	    /* The heavy inference runs in the main loop; here we just gate the most
105	     * recent result and stream the (ADC + driven mask) frame to the coordinator.
106	     * The main loop forwards s_current_cmd to the guitar. */
107	    uint8_t cmd = actuation_armed() ? s_latest_cmd : 0u;
108	    s_current_cmd = cmd;
109	    data_stream_send(cmd);
110	}
111	
112	int main(void)
113	{
114	    SYS_Initialize(NULL);
115	
116	    fret_scan_init();
117	    data_stream_init();
118	    T1SDetector_Initialize();
119	    CLI_Initialize();
120	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
121	    model_infer_stream_init();
122	#else
123	    model_infer_init();
124	#endif
125	    LED0_OFF();   /* boot disarmed: LED off */
126	
127	    TC0_TimerCallbackRegister( Callback_TC0, NULL );
128	    TC0_TimerStart();
129	
130	    while (true) {
131	#if MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
132	        /* Drain the sample queue: one streaming step per sample, in order. */
133	        while (s_q_rd != s_q_wr)
134	        {
135	            uint16_t ri = s_q_rd;
136	            uint16_t s[FRET_COUNT];
137	            for (int c = 0; c < FRET_COUNT; c++) { s[c] = s_adc_q[ri % ADC_Q_LEN][c]; }
138	            s_latest_cmd = model_infer_stream_step(s);
139	            s_q_rd = (uint16_t)(ri + 1u);
140	        }
141	#else
142	        s_latest_cmd = model_infer_run();
143	#endif
144	        /* Forward the gated command to the guitar (edge-triggered + refreshed) and
145	         * service the MAC-PHY / data-frame flush / heartbeat, then the CLI. */
146	        T1SDetector_SetCommand(s_current_cmd);
147	        T1SDetector_Tasks();
148	        CLI_Tasks();
149	    }
150	
151	    return EXIT_FAILURE;
152	}
153

30	     * host as a sample_seq discontinuity. */

14	void fret_scan_init(void)
15	{
16	    ADC0_Enable();
17	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
18	        results[i] = 0;
19	}
20	
21	void fret_scan_all(void)
22	{
23	    for (uint8_t i = 0; i < FRET_COUNT; i++) {
24	        ADC0_ChannelSelect(channel_ain[i], ADC_NEGINPUT_GND);
25	        ADC0_ConversionStart();
26	        while (!ADC0_ResultReadyStatusGet())
27	            ;
28	        results[i] = (uint16_t)ADC0_ConversionResultGet();
29	    }
30	}
31	
32	uint16_t fret_scan_result(fret_channel_t ch)
33	{
34	    return results[ch];
35	}

112	static void spi_done_cb(uintptr_t context)
113	{
114	    (void)context;
115	    T1S_CS_Set();            /* CS high — end of transaction */
116	    s_spi_busy = false;
117	    s_need_service = true;

128	/* One service pass: drive the protocol stack once and check its timers. Do NOT
129	 * loop here on s_need_service — with hardware that never syncs the lib re-
130	 * requests service every pass, which would spin forever. IRQ_N is active-low;
131	 * TC6_Service treats a false interruptLevel as "interrupt active". */
132	static void service_pump(void)
133	{
134	    s_need_service = false;
135	    bool no_int = (T1S_IRQ_N_Get() != 0u);

166	/* Flush the most recent staged data frame to the coordinator. Main loop only. */
167	static void flush_data_frame(void)
168	{
169	    if (!s_frame_ready || s_tx_busy) {
170	        return;
171	    }
172	    /* Snapshot the ISR-staged payload (the scan tick may overwrite s_pending). */
173	    __disable_irq();
174	    uint16_t len = s_pending_len;
175	    if (len > (uint16_t)(sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN)) {
176	        len = (uint16_t)(sizeof(s_tx_frame) - T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN);
177	    }
178	    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN], (const void *)s_pending, len);
179	    s_frame_ready = false;
180	    __enable_irq();
181	
182	    s_tx_busy = true;
183	    if (TC6_SendRawEthernetPacket(s_tc6, s_tx_frame, (uint16_t)(T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN + len),
184	                                  0u, tx_done, NULL)) {
185	        s_tx_count++;
186	    } else {
187	        s_tx_busy = false;
188	    }
189	}

196	    }

198	    s_cmd_frame[T1S_ETH_HDR_LEN] = mask;

202	                                  0u, cmd_tx_done, NULL)) {
203	        s_cmd_dirty = false;
204	        s_last_cmd  = mask;
205	        s_cmd_count++;
206	    } else {
207	        s_cmd_busy = false;   /* retry next pass */

209	}

218	    TC6_GetState(s_tc6, NULL, NULL, &synced);

226	    s_hb_frame[19] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 8);
227	    s_hb_frame[20] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 16);
228	    s_hb_frame[21] = (uint8_t)(s_hb_seq >> 24);

230	    s_hb_busy = true;

239	void T1SDetector_Initialize(void)
240	{
241	    SYSTICK_TimerStart();    /* MCC inits the timer; the app enables it */
242	
243	    log_str("fretboard: boot - t1s detector + actuator\r\n");  /* one-time banner */
244	
245	    /* Prebuild the constant Ethernet headers (payload filled per send). */
246	    fill_eth_header(s_tx_frame,  s_coord_mac,  T1S_ETHERTYPE);
247	    fill_eth_header(s_cmd_frame, s_guitar_mac, T1S_ETHERTYPE);
248	    fill_eth_header(s_hb_frame,  s_coord_mac,  T1S_ETHERTYPE_HB);
249	
250	    /* Hardware reset pulse (T1S_RST active-low, idle high). */
251	    T1S_CS_Set();
252	    T1S_RST_Clear();
253	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
254	    T1S_RST_Set();
255	    SYSTICK_DelayMs(10u);
256	
257	    SERCOM0_SPI_CallbackRegister(spi_done_cb, 0u);  /* Mode 0 set by MCC init */
258	
259	    s_tc6 = TC6_Init(NULL);
260	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
261	        log_str("fretboard: TC6_Init failed\r\n");
262	        return;
263	    }
264	
265	    EIC_CallbackRegister(T1S_IRQ_EIC_PIN, irq_cb, 0u);  /* enabled in EIC_Initialize */
266	
267	    /* Configure the LAN8651 + PLCA as follower id 1. Not promiscuous — the
268	     * MAC-PHY filters to this node's MAC + broadcast. Non-blocking: the
269	     * register sequence finishes in the background via T1SDetector_Tasks. */
270	    if (!TC6Regs_Init(s_tc6, NULL, s_mac, true, T1S_NODE_ID, T1S_NODE_COUNT,
271	                      0u, 0u, false, false, false)) {
272	        log_str("fretboard: TC6Regs_Init rejected\r\n");
273	    }
274	}
275	
276	void T1SDetector_Tasks(void)
277	{
278	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
279	        return;
280	    }
281	    service_pump();
282	    if (!s_link_up && TC6Regs_GetInitDone(s_tc6)) {
283	        s_link_up = true;
284	        TC6_EnableData(s_tc6, true);
285	        char buf[80];
286	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
287	                       "fretboard: LAN8651 up - chipRev=%u, MAC=02:00:00:00:00:%02X, "
288	                       "PLCA follower id=%u/%u\r\n",
289	                       (unsigned)TC6Regs_GetChipRevision(s_tc6),
290	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID, (unsigned)T1S_NODE_ID,
291	                       (unsigned)T1S_NODE_COUNT);
292	        log_str(buf);
293	    }
294	
295	    if (s_link_up) {
296	        flush_data_frame();
297	
298	        /* Periodic command refresh so a dropped command frame self-heals. */
299	        uint32_t now = SYSTICK_GetTickCounter();
300	        if ((now - s_cmd_refresh_ms) >= T1S_CMD_REFRESH_MS) {
301	            s_cmd_refresh_ms = now;
302	            s_cmd_dirty = true;
303	        }
304	        flush_command();
305	
306	        if ((now - s_hb_last_ms) >= T1S_HB_INTERVAL_MS) {
307	            s_hb_last_ms = now;
308	            send_heartbeat();
309	        }
310	    }
311	}
312	
313	bool T1SDetector_IsConnected(void)
314	{
315	    return s_link_up;

318	bool T1SDetector_SendFrame(const uint8_t *payload, uint16_t len)

321	        return false;
322	    }

327	     * wins: overwrite any frame not yet flushed (shows as a sample_seq gap). */
328	    memcpy((void *)s_pending, payload, len);
329	    s_pending_len = len;
330	    s_frame_ready = true;
331	    return true;

364	/* Diagnostic: log the raw value of a control register (async — the result

366	static void on_id_read(TC6_t *pInst, bool success, uint32_t addr, uint32_t value,
367	                       void *pTag, void *pGlobalTag)
368	{
369	    (void)pInst; (void)pTag; (void)pGlobalTag;
370	    char buf[88];
371	    if (addr == 0x00000001u) {
372	        /* PHY id register — oui/model are meaningful here (lib wants 0x1F0/0x1B). */
373	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf),
374	                       "fretboard: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d, oui=0x%03lX model=0x%02lX)\r\n",
375	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success,
376	                       (unsigned long)(value >> 10), (unsigned long)((value >> 4) & 0x3FFu));
377	    } else {
378	        (void)snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "fretboard: reg 0x%08lX = 0x%08lX (ok=%d)\r\n",
379	                       (unsigned long)addr, (unsigned long)value, (int)success);
380	    }
381	    log_str(buf);
382	}

387	     * 0x000A0094 = chip rev. */
388	    static const uint32_t addrs[3] = { 0x00000000u, 0x00000001u, 0x000A0094u };
389	
390	    if (s_tc6 == NULL) {
391	        log_str("fretboard: t1s not initialized\r\n");
392	        return;
393	    }
394	    /* Enqueue only; the main service loop completes the reads and on_id_read
395	     * logs each result. Don't hammer TC6_Service here — doing so while the link
396	     * is live can trip a transient Loss_of_Framing. */
397	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 3u; i++) {
398	        (void)TC6_ReadRegister(s_tc6, addrs[i], false, on_id_read, NULL);
399	    }
400	}

427	                             uint16_t len, void *pGlobalTag)

34	/* Advertise as a Wiimote: Class of Device 0x002504 (peripheral/joystick, with the
35	 * limited-discoverable service bit) + limited-discoverable scan mode. The Wii's

37	static void set_wiimote_discoverable(void)

42	    cod.service = 0x01;

75	#define HID_LINK_MAX  4
76	#define HID_RX_LEN    64
77	#define HID_RX_STACK  3072
78	
79	typedef struct {
80	    bool          in_use;
81	    volatile bool stop;     /* set by the CLOSE handler to make this reader exit */
82	    int           fd;
83	    uint32_t      handle;   /* L2CAP connection handle, matched against CLOSE events */
84	    StaticTask_t  tcb;
85	    StackType_t   stack[HID_RX_STACK];
86	    uint8_t       rx[HID_RX_LEN];
87	} hid_link_t;
88	
89	static hid_link_t s_links[HID_LINK_MAX];
90	
91	/* Read HIDP frames from one HID channel and dispatch them to the Wiimote module.
92	 * Exits when its CLOSE handler sets `stop` — not by watching read() return codes,
93	 * since re-armed servers can recycle this fd number out from under us. */
94	static void hid_reader_task(void *arg)
95	{
96	    hid_link_t *l = (hid_link_t *)arg;
97	    while (!l->stop) {
98	        int n = read(l->fd, l->rx, sizeof(l->rx));
99	        if (l->stop) break;
100	        if (n > 0) {
101	            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "fd %d RX report 0x%02x (%d B)", l->fd,
102	                     n > 1 ? l->rx[1] : 0, n);
103	            Wiimote_HandleRx(l->fd, l->rx, n);
104	        } else if (n < 0) {
105	            break;                          /* genuine close of our fd */
106	        } else {
107	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));  /* non-blocking VFS: 0 = no data yet */
108	        }
109	    }
110	    l->in_use = false;
111	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
112	}
113	
114	static void hid_link_start(int fd, uint32_t handle)
115	{
116	    for (int i = 0; i < HID_LINK_MAX; i++) {
117	        if (!s_links[i].in_use) {
118	            s_links[i].in_use = true;
119	            s_links[i].stop = false;
120	            s_links[i].fd = fd;
121	            s_links[i].handle = handle;
122	            xTaskCreateStatic(hid_reader_task, "hid_rx", HID_RX_STACK,
123	                              &s_links[i], 5, s_links[i].stack, &s_links[i].tcb);
124	            return;
125	        }
126	    }
127	    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "no free HID link slot for fd %d", fd);
128	}
129	
130	static void hid_link_stop(uint32_t handle)
131	{
132	    for (int i = 0; i < HID_LINK_MAX; i++) {
133	        if (s_links[i].in_use && s_links[i].handle == handle) {
134	            s_links[i].stop = true;
135	            return;
136	        }
137	    }
138	}

140	/* Bluedroid consumes the listening server slot when a connection opens, so the
141	 * HID PSMs are armed per pairing window (EnterPairing) and torn down in StopPairing
142	 * — re-arming on every disconnect leaks slots when reconnect uses client connects. */
143	static void start_hid_servers(void)
144	{
145	    esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_CONTROL);
146	    esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT);
147	}

149	static void l2cap_cb(esp_bt_l2cap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_l2cap_cb_param_t *param)
150	{
151	    switch (event) {
152	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_INIT_EVT:
153	        /* The L2CAP data path is fd-based; the VFS must be registered before a
154	         * server can allocate a slot/fd. */
155	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP init status=%d; registering VFS", param->init.status);
156	        esp_bt_l2cap_vfs_register();
157	        break;
158	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_VFS_REGISTER_EVT:
159	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP VFS registered status=%d", param->vfs_register.status);
160	        break;
161	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_START_EVT:
162	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP server up status=%d handle=%u",
163	                 param->start.status, (unsigned)param->start.handle);
164	        break;
165	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT:
166	        log_bda("L2CAP OPEN from", param->open.rem_bda);
167	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "  status=%d handle=%u fd=%d mtu=%d",
168	                 param->open.status, (unsigned)param->open.handle,
169	                 param->open.fd, (int)param->open.tx_mtu);
170	        hid_link_start(param->open.fd, param->open.handle);
171	        /* Connected — stop being discoverable (stay connectable for reconnects),
172	         * matching a real Wiimote which doesn't advertise once connected. */
173	        esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
174	        s_discoverable = false;
175	        if (s_reconnecting) {
176	            /* control channel re-opened — now open the interrupt channel. */
177	            s_reconnecting = false;
178	            esp_bt_l2cap_connect(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT, s_wii_bda);
179	        }
180	        break;
181	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_CLOSE_EVT:
182	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "L2CAP CLOSE handle=%u async=%d",
183	                 (unsigned)param->close.handle, param->close.async);
184	        /* Signal this channel's reader to exit (by handle, robust to fd reuse). */
185	        hid_link_stop(param->close.handle);
186	        /* Stop streaming + reset controller state immediately so the sender
187	         * doesn't write into the dying channel and the LED returns to idle.
188	         * Recovery is via the `reconnect` command — no automatic reconnect. */
189	        Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected();
190	        break;
191	    default:
192	        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "l2cap event %d", event);
193	        break;
194	    }
195	}

197	void Fauxmote_BtStart(void)
198	{
199	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_mem_release(ESP_BT_MODE_BLE));
200	    esp_bt_controller_config_t cfg = BT_CONTROLLER_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
201	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_init(&cfg));
202	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_enable(ESP_BT_MODE_CLASSIC_BT));
203	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_init());
204	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_enable());
205	
206	    const uint8_t *bda = esp_bt_dev_get_address();
207	    if (bda) {
208	        /* Our BD_ADDR — also the 1+2 temporary-pairing PIN (this, reversed). */
209	        log_bda("BD_ADDR", bda);
210	    }
211	
212	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_register_callback(gap_cb));
213	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_set_device_name(FAUXMOTE_BT_NAME));
214	
215	    /* Legacy PIN pairing (SSP disabled in sdkconfig): we answer each PIN request. */
216	    esp_bt_gap_set_pin(ESP_BT_PIN_TYPE_VARIABLE, 0, NULL);
217	
218	    /* Serve the exact Wiimote SDP record, then listen for the Wii's HID L2CAP
219	     * connections on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). */
220	    if (!WiimoteSdp_Register()) {
221	        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Wiimote SDP registration failed");
222	    }
223	    Wiimote_Start();
224	
225	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_register_callback(l2cap_cb));
226	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_init());
227	
228	    /* The stack persists the bond (link key) in NVS and reloads it at boot — recall
229	     * the bonded Wii's address so `reconnect` works after a power cycle. */
230	    int bonded = esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_num();
231	    if (bonded > 0) {
232	        esp_bd_addr_t devs[8];
233	        int n = bonded > 8 ? 8 : bonded;
234	        if (esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list(&n, devs) == ESP_OK && n > 0) {
235	            memcpy(s_wii_bda, devs[0], sizeof(s_wii_bda));
236	            s_have_wii = true;
237	            log_bda("recalled bonded Wii", s_wii_bda);
238	        }
239	    }
240	
241	    /* Stay idle (not discoverable/connectable) until the operator runs `pair`. */
242	    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_NON_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
243	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "fauxmote up (idle). Use the `pair` console command to sync with a Wii.");
244	}

246	void Fauxmote_EnterPairing(void)
247	{

252	    start_hid_servers();          /* arm the HID listeners for this sync window */
253	    set_wiimote_discoverable();
254	    s_discoverable = true;
255	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "pairing mode ON — limited-discoverable as a Wiimote (sync the Wii now)");

1	#include "ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h"
2	
3	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
4	#include "task.h"
5	
6	#include "definitions.h"            /* DRV_SST26_*, XLCDC_* */
7	#include "log.h"
8	#include "flash/qspi_layout.h"      /* QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET */
9	#include "ui/ui_manager.h"          /* BASE_W, BASE_H */
10	
11	/* Fallback fill: opaque black. The layer is RGBA_8888 (packs 0xRRGGBBAA), so a
12	 * little-endian pixel word of 0x000000FF is R=G=B=0, A=0xFF. */
13	#define SPLASH_FILL        0x000000FFu
14	
15	/* The splash pixels, also the buffer the splash layer scans out. Non-cached so
16	 * the QSPI read (CPU copy from the memory-mapped flash) and the LCDC scan-out are
17	 * coherent without cache maintenance; 32-byte aligned. */
18	static uint32_t s_fb[BASE_W * BASE_H]
19	    __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned(32)));
20	
21	void ScreenSplash_Show(XLCDC_LAYER layer)
22	{
23	    /* Drive the overlay layer directly — no GFX canvas. Set every attribute
24	     * deferred (update=false) then enable with update=true so they latch together
25	     * at the next vsync. Mirrors the XLCDC GFX driver's own layer-commit sequence
26	     * (drv_gfx_xlcdc.c): opaque (alpha 255), DMA enabled, full-screen, zero stride
27	     * (the buffer width equals the window width). */
28	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(layer, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, false);
29	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(layer, (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)s_fb, false);
30	    XLCDC_SetLayerOpts(layer, 255u, true, false);
31	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(layer, 0u, 0u, false);
32	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize(layer, BASE_W, BASE_H, false);
33	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(layer, 0u, false);
34	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(layer, true, true);
35	}
36	
37	void ScreenSplash_Hide(XLCDC_LAYER layer)
38	{
39	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(layer, false, true);
40	}
41	
42	static void fill_fallback(void)
43	{
44	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < (BASE_W * BASE_H); i++) { s_fb[i] = SPLASH_FILL; }
45	}
46	
47	bool ScreenSplash_Load(void)
48	{
49	    /* Read the raw splash straight from QSPI NOR into the framebuffer the splash
50	     * layer scans out — no SD mount, no decode (the blob is provisioned via
51	     * openocd/program-qspi.sh). The DRV_SST26 read sets up the QSPI memory-read
52	     * frame itself and completes synchronously; the poll is a bounded backstop. */
53	    DRV_HANDLE h = DRV_SST26_Open(DRV_SST26_INDEX, DRV_IO_INTENT_READ);
54	    if (h == DRV_HANDLE_INVALID)
55	    {
56	        LOG_WARN("SPLASH: QSPI open failed\r\n");
57	        fill_fallback();
58	        return false;
59	    }
60	
61	    TickType_t t0 = xTaskGetTickCount();
62	    bool ok = DRV_SST26_Read(h, s_fb, sizeof s_fb, QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET);
63	    if (ok)
64	    {
65	        DRV_SST26_TRANSFER_STATUS st;
66	        uint32_t guard = 0u;
67	        do { st = DRV_SST26_TransferStatusGet(h); }
68	        while ((st == DRV_SST26_TRANSFER_BUSY) && (++guard < 4000000u));
69	        ok = (st == DRV_SST26_TRANSFER_COMPLETED);
70	    }
71	    DRV_SST26_Close(h);
72	
73	    if (!ok)
74	    {
75	        LOG_WARN("SPLASH: QSPI read failed\r\n");
76	        fill_fallback();
77	        return false;
78	    }
79	
80	    uint32_t ms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - t0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
81	    LOG_INFO("SPLASH: %u B from QSPI in %lu ms\r\n", (unsigned)sizeof s_fb, (unsigned long)ms);
82	    return true;
83	}
84

=== aa_corners.h ===
#ifndef UI_GFX_AA_CORNERS_H
#define UI_GFX_AA_CORNERS_H

#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"   /* leRect, leColor, leColorMode */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Anti-alias the four rounded corners of a rect that a classic skin just drew with
 * a stepped arc. For each corner it repaints a radius×radius box: the backdrop
 * outside the arc (sampled once from the box's outer pixel — assumes a solid
 * backdrop behind the corner, true for our panels), an optional borderWidth-px
 * ring in `border`, then `fill` inside, with 1px anti-aliased bands at the arc
 * edges. borderWidth 0 → no border (backdrop↔fill).
 *
 * Coverage is computed analytically per pixel, so `radius` is arbitrary (bounded
 * by half the rect's smaller side). `mode` is the active render colour mode
 * (leRenderer_CurrentColorMode()). Call from a widget's paint override after the
 * normal draw; it only touches the corner boxes, so the straight edges the skin
 * drew (and any centred text) are left intact. Cheap, and runs only when the
 * widget repaints (state change) — not per frame.
 *
 * Widget-agnostic: the caller extracts fill/border/radius from its own widget +
 * scheme (see widget_button_aa.c). */
void AaCorners_Render(const leRect *rect, uint32_t radius, uint32_t borderWidth,
                      leColor fill, leColor border, leColorMode mode);

/* Round the corners of content already drawn into `rect` (e.g. an album-art image)
 * by AA-blending the corner wedges toward `bg`, a KNOWN solid backdrop colour.
 * Unlike AaCorners_Render, the inside of the arc is left untouched — only pixels
 * outside the arc are replaced (fully → bg) with a 1px anti-aliased band, so the
 * image keeps every interior pixel and only its square corners are eaten back to
 * `bg`. Use when the backdrop behind the rounded shape is a solid colour you can
 * name (here the dialog's 0x18181B); a varying backdrop would have to be sampled
 * per pixel instead. `mode` is leRenderer_CurrentColorMode(). */
void AaCorners_RenderRoundImage(const leRect *rect, uint32_t radius,
                                leColor bg, leColorMode mode);

#ifdef __cplusplus

# edge-ai documentation staleness audit

The Python package (`edge_ai/*`, `pyproject.toml`, tests) is **accurately documented** — model architecture, feature/label schema, CLI, hyperparameters, and quantisation all match the code. The drift is concentrated in the **firmware-integration docs** (`runtime.md`, `architecture.md`, and one line of `rollout.md`), which still describe a local-GPIO / mode-gated fretboard that the firmware has since replaced with T1S transport to a separate guitar node. This move is recorded in the edge-ai *journal* (2026-06-17 decision) but the design docs were never updated.

## Findings (most important first)

- **[runtime.md:33,42 · architecture.md:42-46]** — Command output path (`cmd_receive_apply_mask` / local open-drain GPIOs) no longer exists; the command is now sent to the guitar node over T1S.
  - Doc says: the driven byte goes through `cmd_receive_apply_mask()` in `cmd_receive.c` — "bits 0..4 fret GPIOs, bit 5 strum-down"; architecture.md §2 diagram shows `cmd_receive_apply_mask(enabled ? cmd : 0)` → "(open-drain fret GPIOs + strum)".
  - Code shows: no `cmd_receive_apply_mask` symbol and no `cmd_receive.c` file exist anywhere in `firmware/fretboard/` (grep returns nothing). The gated command is forwarded to the guitar over T1S: `T1SDetector_SetCommand(s_current_cmd)` (`firmware/fretboard/main.c:146`), and `data_stream_send(cmd)` (`main.c:109`). The fretboard no longer actuates locally.
  - Suggested fix: replace the `cmd_receive_apply_mask`/open-drain wording with the T1S path (`T1SDetector_SetCommand` in `main.c`); align with the journal's 2026-06-17 T1S decision.
  - Confidence: high

- **[runtime.md:48 · rollout.md:32 · architecture.md:46]** — The `FRETBOARD_MODE` (`MODEL_DRIVEN`/`MARVIN_DRIVEN`) build-time gate no longer exists.
  - Doc says: "Build-time `FRETBOARD_MODE` (`MODEL_DRIVEN` default, `MARVIN_DRIVEN` to restore the marvin-driven path) in `main.c`" (runtime.md §4); rollout.md Phase 5: "Build-time `FRETBOARD_MODE=MODEL_DRIVEN` + SW0 runtime toggle flips wire ownership from `cmd_receive` to the model"; architecture.md §2: "bypassed when fretboard is in `MODEL_DRIVEN` mode".
  - Code shows: `FRETBOARD_MODE`/`MODEL_DRIVEN`/`MARVIN_DRIVEN` appear only in `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md` and its journal — not in any `.c`/`.h`. `main.c` is unconditionally model-driven; the only runtime gate is the SW0 "armed" toggle (`main.c:62-80,107`).
  - Suggested fix: drop the `FRETBOARD_MODE` mode-gate description; the runtime enable is SW0-arm only (`s_armed`), with the compile-time choice being `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING`, not a marvin/model mode.
  - Confidence: high

- **[architecture.md:37-44 · runtime.md:13,20-21]** — Streaming inference no longer runs inline in the TC0 ISR; it runs in the main loop via an SPSC sample queue.
  - Doc says: architecture.md §2 diagram places `model_infer_stream_step(scan)` inside the "fretboard TC0 ISR @ 240 Hz" block ("streaming … runs inline"); runtime.md §3: "The streaming path is cheap enough (~3 k MACs/tick) to run inline; this section is why the recompute path can't."
  - Code shows: the ISR only samples and publishes to a ring queue (`s_adc_q`, `s_q_wr`) — `main.c:86-92`; the main loop drains it and calls `model_infer_stream_step()` per sample (`main.c:131-140`). Both streaming and recompute now run in the main loop; the ISR runs neither.
  - Suggested fix: move the streaming step out of the ISR block in both docs; describe the ISR→main-loop SPSC `s_adc_q` queue and that inference (either module) runs best-effort in the main loop.
  - Confidence: high

- **[architecture.md:6-32]** — The training-time data-flow diagram shows only the cross-stream `frame_epoch`/`ts_counter` join (the `actuator` mode), but the shipped corpus/model uses the atomic `actuator-fb` schema (no join).
  - Doc says: "Both record streams already flow through perf-log keyed by `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`. The exporter joins them offline." Diagram shows `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` + `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` joined.
  - Code shows: the deployed path is `actuator-fb`, where the fretboard frame carries `applied_mask` + `fb_seq` and is paired on-device with no cross-stream join (`tools/marvin-perf/.../sensiml_csv.py:19-26,71-74`; `edge_ai/data.py:30-35`). training.md §2 documents this correctly; architecture.md §1 lags it.
  - Suggested fix: note the atomic `actuator-fb` flow (in-frame `applied_mask` + `fb_seq`) as the deployed path, with the `frame_epoch` join as the legacy `actuator` mode.
  - Confidence: medium

- **[README.md:43]** — Comment overstates the default `viz` output.
  - Doc says: "visualise the model (summary + RF cone always; graph needs the graphviz binary)".
  - Code shows: the RF cone is only written when `--rf-cone OUT.png` is passed (`cli.py:175-179`); the summary is the default (unless `--no-summary`). "RF cone always" is wrong.
  - Suggested fix: "summary by default; RF cone with `--rf-cone`, graph with `--graph` (needs graphviz)."
  - Confidence: high

## Verified accurate (no drift)

- Model architecture: `StrumNet` 3 dilated causal conv layers `(1,4,16)`, kernel 5, last-timestep linear head, 6 logits — matches `model.py:35-59`. Param counts (918 @ 8ch, 3110 @ 16ch) and MAC table (50k/71k/252k) verified by arithmetic. RF=85 formula correct.
- Feature/label schema (`ph_*`/`fret_*`/`strum`, `fb_seq`), `FRET_COUNT=5`, `N_LABELS=6`, 240 Hz — match `data.py:30-35`, `__init__.py:9-11`, and the exporter `sensiml_csv.py`. Strum-collapse formula `((mask>>5)|(mask>>6))&1` matches `sensiml_csv.py:98`.
- CLI `edge-ai {lag,train,eval,quantize,viz}` and entry point — match `pyproject.toml:9` and `cli.py`. Hyperparameter defaults (8ch train / 16ch deploy, kernel 5, `--strum-weight`, `--label-lead`, `--no-holdout`, 30/50 epochs) — match `cli.py`/`train.py`.
- int8 PTQ scheme (per-tensor symmetric int8, int32 accum, int64 requant, integer input affine, head-accumulator compare, no sigmoid) — matches `quantize.py`.
- Runtime firmware facts that ARE correct: `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING` default 1 (`fretboard_config.h:28-29`); `_Static_assert(MODEL_WINDOW >= 85)` (`model_infer_stream.c:20`); ring depths 5/17/65 and memory budget (25B / 272B / 1040B) (`model_infer_stream.c:28-38`); both `test_bitexact.py` and `test_stream_bitexact.py` exist; SW0=PB03 / LED0=PB02 active-low (`main.c:25-40`); 64 KB Flash / 8 KB SRAM.

## Aspirational (not stale — correctly flagged as future)

- runtime.md §7 "Programmable weights over serial (future)" and §4 "marvin commands difficulty/enable over serial" — explicitly labelled future; no code expected.
- rollout.md Phase 5 gameplay-scoring gate and Phase 4 `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` — correctly marked "In progress"/"Subsumed".
- review.md open questions (Q1–Q5, 2-sensor HW, scroll-speed sensor) — design forks, correctly framed as undecided.

Summary: 3 high, 1 medium, 1 low (plus one high-confidence README wording nit). The Python package docs are accurate; the staleness is confined to the firmware-integration docs (`runtime.md`, `architecture.md`, one `rollout.md` line), which describe a pre-T1S, mode-gated, ISR-streaming fretboard that the firmware has since superseded — stale (code diverged), not aspirational.
